title: News Quiz Oct. 10 | In the hot seat
content:
Are you ready for this week’s news quiz? Get ready, get set, go!




1.

 Why is a group of elders being relocated from Kuujjuaq to Montreal?




A.

 Sewage issues at 

Tusaajiapik elders home forced the relocation of the elders to Montreal.




B.

 There are heating issues at the home.




C.

 There was a problem, and it was technical. That’s all we really know.




2.

 Iqaluit’s Northern store got a facelift recently. What merchandise has a new display with a digital catalogue?




A.

 Furniture




B.

 Appliances




C.

 All-terrain vehicles




3.

 What is Hudson Bay MLA Jason Iqaluq doing now that he’s been elected to represent Sanikiluaq in last month’s byelection?




A.

 Travelling to Iqaluit for orientation.




B.

 Canvassing residents about their needs and priorities.




C.

 Reading up on 

Robert’s Rules of Order

.
















4.

 The federal government has released a new report that predicts what warming temperatures could mean for Canada, including the Arctic. Melting permafrost is one major challenge, but what is particular about this issue?




A.

 Melting permafrost could unearth some spectacular prehistoric finds — a possibility that has paleontologists excited for more trips north.




B.

 Permafrost melt is wreaking havoc now but the problem is expected to stabilize once the permafrost melt is finished and the ground hardens again.




C.

 Researchers are exploring how melting permafrost could be a major source of untapped energy.




5.

 Baffinland Iron Mines Corp., which filed for creditor protection in May, is now seeking approval for a possible sale of company assets. The sale could include the Mary River Mine, but what detail does a judge need to decide?




A.

 How much the mine is worth.




B.

 Who has final say over a potential deal — a court-appointed monitor or group of shareholders.




C.

 How to proceed if nobody comes forward with an offer to buy the mine.




A road once used by ATVs in Pond Inlet, seen here on Sept. 5, collapsed after heavy rain. (Photo courtesy Andrew Tagak)




Answers:
















1.

 C — The problem is 

technical

, but those in charge did not specify. The elders home did experience heating issues in April, though it’s unclear if these same problems led to this month’s relocation of elders.




2.

 A — The new Northern has a 

furniture display

 complete with a digital catalogue for all your chesterfield needs.




3.

 A — Hudson Bay MLA Jason Iqaluq was 

planning a trip

 to Iqaluit last week to participate in orientation for his new job at the legislative assembly. “I’m a bit anxious, but overall, I’m feeling that I can do this,” he said about his new gig.




4.

 B — Permafrost melt is causing coastal erosion, infrastructure damage, flooding and other “catastrophic” problems, said Daniel Fortier, a University of Montreal geography professor. But it’s a 

short-term problem

, he said, because the ground should stabilize again.




5.

 B — A judge 

must consider

 who will have final say over any potential deals to sell Baffinland’s assets or any plan to restructure the company. The next court date was set for Friday in Ontario Superior Court.

title: Geschichte von unten: Jeden Monat ein neues, faires T-Shirt von „Working Class History“ – für LeserInnen des LabourNet Germany zum reduzierten Preis, der zudem auch uns unterstützt!
content:
Dossier




Seit November 2021 ist das neue Projekt „T-Shirt of the Month“ von 

dna merch

 

 in Zusammenarbeit mit der Bildungsinitiative 

Working Class History

 

 online. LabourNet ist Teil des Projekts und kann die Shirts Euch daher mit dem Discount-Code etwas günstiger anbieten. Jeden Monat gibt es ein faires, genossenschaftlich genähtes T-Shirt, das einer Geschichte oder einer Persönlichkeit aus dem Archiv von Working Class History gewidmet ist. Es kann einen Monat lang weltweit vorbestellt werden und wird dann in der jeweiligen Auflage produziert und verschickt. Mit den Shirts werden die Forschungs- und Bildungsarbeit von Working Class History, eine Näherinnen-Kooperative in Kroatien sowie Basisgewerkschafter*innen in Südasien unterstützt. Die Designs kommen von Künstler*innen und Aktivist*innen aus der ganzen Welt. LabourNet-Leser*innen können beim Kauf der Shirts sparen und gleichzeitig unsere redaktionelle Arbeit unterstützen. Für jedes mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code gekaufte Shirt bekommt ihr 5% Rabatt und wir eine Vermittlungsgebühr bzw. Spende. Siehe weitere Infos und die Shirts/Hoodies/Pullover:







[Mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das Oktober-2026-Shirt von Working Class History/dna: La Revolution Est Femme (Frankreich 1789) 

 




„

Das Design dieses Monats ist den Tausenden von Frauen in Paris gewidmet, die am 5. Oktober 1789 einen entscheidenden Wendepunkt der Französischen Revolution herbeiführten. Verärgert über die hohen Brotpreise und den Brotmangel, plünderten sie das städtische Waffenlager und belagerten das Schloss von Versailles. Eine Augenzeugin hörte die Frauen sagen: „Die Männer hatten nicht genug Kraft, sich zu rächen, und sie würden beweisen, dass sie besser seien als die Männer.“ Die Frauen verlangten eine Zusammenkunft mit König Ludwig XVI., um Brot und Fortschritte bei der Ausarbeitung einer neuen, überarbeiteten Verfassung zu fordern, welche die Macht der Monarchie einschränken und neue Rechte für die Bevölkerung festschreiben sollte. (…) Wieder einmal hatten wir das Glück, die italienische Tätowierkünstlerin Fede Borgia für die Gestaltung eines Motivs zu gewinnen, das diese inspirierende Geschichte weiblicher Stärke einfängt. Sie gab ihrem Werk den französischen Titel „La Révolution est femme“, was auf Deutsch „Die Revolution ist weiblich“ bedeutet. Auf dem Schild im Hintergrund ist „Du Pain“ zu lesen – „Etwas Brot“, ein Verweis darauf, dass die hohen Brotpreise und der Brotmangel der Auslöser für die revolutionären Aktionen der Frauen waren

…“ Siehe mehr 

Informationen und Bestellung in verschiedenen Versionen bei dna merch

 

 – den Code „LN20XX“ für 5 Prozent weniger und dennoch auch zur Unterstützung unserer Arbeit nicht vergessen!




[Mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das September-2026-Shirt von Working Class History/dna: Mehr Als 108 (Paraguay 1959) 




„

In der Nacht zum 1. September 1959 stirbt der Radiomoderator und Tänzer Bernardo Aranda bei einem Brand in seinem Zimmer im Asunción Stadtteil Barrio Obrero. Der Fall wird nie aufgeklärt. Die von den USA unterstützte Militärdiktatur Alfredo Stroessners zieht trotzdem einen Schluss: Weil auch schwule Männer bei Aranda verkehrten, muss einer von ihnen verantwortlich sein. In den folgenden Tagen verhaftet und foltert die Polizei gezielt Männer, die als homosexuell gelten. Die regierungstreue Zeitung El País nennt schließlich die Zahl der Festgenommenen: 108. Angeklagt wird niemand, weder für Arandas Tod noch für das, was den Verhafteten angetan wurde. Bis heute wird „108″ in Paraguay als abwertender Begriff für queere Menschen verwendet. Zugleich entstand aus dieser Geschichte auch Widerstand. : Bereits Ende September 1959 erschien ein anonymer Protestbrief in derselben Zeitung, heute anerkannt als erster dokumentierter Akt queeren Widerstands im Land. [Mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das November-2024-Shirt von Working Class History/dna: Penn Sardin (Sardine Workers‘ Strike) 




„

Das November 2024 Design greift den hundertsten Jahrestag eines der bedeutendsten Ereignisse in der europäischen Arbeiterinnengeschichte auf, nämlich den großen Streik der Sardinenarbeiterinnen in Douarnenez an der bretonischen Finistère-Küste im November 1924. ‚Penn Sardin‘ bedeutet wörtlich „Sardinenkopf“ und war ein Name, der den Arbeiterinnen in den örtlichen Sardinenkonservenfabriken gegeben wurde.


Douarnenez war der erste Sardinenhafen Frankreichs. Die ganze Stadt lebte von Sardinen. 1924 gab es Konservenfabriken im Überfluss, 22 davon, dazu eine Konservenfabrik, 2.000 Arbeiter, 5.000 Fischer. Unter dem Impuls des Kapitalismus von Nantes, der zum Teil aus dem Sklavenhandel stammte, ließ sich eine neue Klasse von Industriellen in Douarnenez nieder. Zwei Welten standen sich gegenüber. Die schwierigen Lebensbedingungen der ‚Penn Sardins‘ verschlechterten sich. Konservenfabrikarbeiterinnen wurden in Frankreich am schlechtesten bezahlt.


Trotz eines 1919 verabschiedeten Gesetzes arbeiteten die Frauen 10 Stunden am Tag, erhielten keinen Überstundenzuschlag und arbeiteten zudem auch nachts, was wohl eigentlich illegal war. Im Winter 1924 demonstrierten dann 2.100 Menschen, darunter 600 Frauen, gegen ihren Stundenlohn von nur 80 Cent und die Tatsache, dass sie zu jeder Tages- und Nachtzeit in die Fabrik gehen mussten, wenn eine Ladung Sardinen geliefert wurde.


Der Streik der Sardinenarbeiterinnen von Douarnenez im November 1924 zur Forderung nach einer Lohnerhöhung war der Beginn einer Mobilisierung, die in der Region mehrere Monate andauerte. Die Streikenden, hauptsächlich Frauen, marschierten mit dem Slogan „Pemp real a vo!“ (Fünf Reals werden es sein!). Auch Joséphine Pencalet, die der Metallarbeitergewerkschaft von Douarnenez angehörte, nahm an dem Streik teil. Ihr Name auf Bretonisch, Penn kalet, bedeutet „Hitzkopf“ oder „Stur“.


Die Gendarmen unterdrückten die Streikenden und riefen Streikbrecher herbei, und der Bürgermeister Daniel Le Flanchec, der den Aufstand öffentlich unterstützt hatte, wurde von seinem Amt suspendiert. Der Arbeitsminister schlug eine Schlichtung vor, doch der Kampf ging weiter. Die Arbeiterinnen wurden von Matrosen unterstützt und besetzten die Straßen, die Stadt wurde blockiert und der Konflikt wurde aufmerksam von den Medien verfolgt.


Am 5. Dezember 1924 berichtete die Zeitung L’Humanité in einem Artikel mit dem Titel „Le sang ouvrier a coulé à Douarnenez“ („In Douarnenez ist Arbeiterblut geflossen“) über die im Auftrag des Innenministeriums gegen die Demonstranten erhobene Anklage. Auch das Protokoll der Suspendierung von Le Flanchec wurde veröffentlicht. Der Bericht über die Suspendierung von Daniel Le Flanchec wegen Rebellion provozierte eine landesweite Berichterstattung über den Streik in den Tageszeitungen, darunter Paris Soir und La Dépêche de l’Aube, die von „der provokativen Unnachgiebigkeit der Sardinenkonservenfabrikbesitzer“ bewegt war. Am 6. Januar 1925 gaben die Fabrikbesitzer dann endlich den Forderungen der Arbeiter*innen nach.

Wir brauchen einen Zeitplan, der nicht so voll ist.“ Laut Pogue wollten sie mehr Zeit haben, um „die Sterne, die Erde und uns selbst zu studieren“. In der Folge begann die Bodenkontrolle damit, die Besatzung als „lethargisch und negativ“ zu beschreiben.

Es kam zum Bürgerkrieg, in dem die Arbeiter*innen den von Nazideutschland und dem faschistischen Italien unterstützten spanischen Kapitalisten und Machteliten gegenüberstanden. In den revolutionären Gebieten übernahmen anarchistische und sozialistische Arbeiter und Bauern Arbeitsplätze und Ländereien und begannen, diese kollektiv zu verwalten. Tausende von Menschen aus der ganzen Welt kamen ins Land, um die spanische Revolution zu unterstützen. Einer von ihnen war der berühmte britische sozialistische Schriftsteller George Orwell, der die Situation in Barcelona wie folgt beschrieb: “Es war das erste Mal, dass ich in einer Stadt war, in der die Arbeiterklasse im Sattel saß.” Die westlichen Demokratien, darunter Großbritannien und Frankreich, ließen die Spanische Republik nach Francos Putsch im Stich und verhängten eine Blockade gegen Spanien. Dieser stoppte de facto den Fluss von Hilfsgütern und Waffen an die Antifaschisten. Italien und Deutschland ignorierten die Blockade und setzten ihre Unterstützung von Francos Truppen offen fort. Der US-Ölgigant Texaco versorgte die Nationalisten sogar mit Öl und anderen Gütern, ohne dafür auch nur eine Zahlung zu verlangen, während er jegliche Lieferungen an die Republik und ihre Verteidiger stoppte. Nach fast drei Jahren erbitterten und blutigen Krieges waren die Nationalisten mit ihren überlegenen Waffen und Ausrüstungen schließlich siegreich…

Nachdem Gott die Klapperschlange, die Kröte und den Vampir erschaffen hatte, hatte er eine schreckliche Substanz übrig, aus der er einen Scab machte

.“ Und weiter: „

Wo andere Herzen haben, trägt er [der Streikbrecher] einen Tumor fauler Prinzipien

.“ Das Working Class History T-Shirt des Monats Juli ist

[Wieder mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das Juni-T-Shirt von “Working Class History”: In memory of Katerina Gogou: „Go little comrade, go“  




Das 

Working Class History T-Shirt des Monats Juni

 

 feiert die großartige griechische Dichterin Katerina Gogou. Katerina wurde am 1. Juni 1940 in Athen geboren und war dort insbesondere für die radikale politische und kulturelle Szene der 80er Jahre im anarchistisch geprägten Stadtteil Exarchia ein wichtiger Einfluss. Katerinas erste Lebensjahre waren geprägt von Hunger und Nazi-Besatzung, Widerstand und Bürgerkrieg. 1978 veröffentlichte sie ihre erste Gedichtsammlung „Three Clicks Left“, welche auch auf Englisch übersetzt wurde. Inspiriert von ihrer unvollendeten poetischen Autobiographie und insbesondere vom darin enthaltenen Stück „Civil War“, spiegelt das Juni-Design eine Kindheitserinnerung von Katerina wider. Der Teil des Gedichts, auf dem das Design basiert, bezieht sich auf die Begegnung mit einem Widerstandskämpfer und lautet wie folgt:




I saw through the glass a bullet hitting my left hand palm, blood and the trash breathing. My mother was in the kitchen and my father I don’t even know where, I open the door and I go to the trash. And there I saw, and I don’t give a dime if you don’t believe me, the most beautiful boy I had seen in my life. He was covered there, holding a machine gun, he had a short blond beard and long blond hair. His eyes…I don’t know to tell their colour. He looked like or was the Christ. “Go little girl, go”, he told me, “away from here. They will kill me”. I took a deep breath to run fast. “Bend so I can kiss you”, he told me. I was already home. The first man and the last I ever loved was an urban guerrilla.




Das Design wurde von der in Berlin lebenden italienischen Illustratorin Anna Piera Di Silvestre umgesetzt und ist in weiß und schwarz

[Wieder mit dem LabourNet-Discount-Code] Das Mai-T-Shirt und Hoodie von “Working Class History”: Beer Riots – Münchner Bieraufstände 1844 




Das neue Monats-Shirt ist den sogenannten Münchner Bieraufständen gewidmet. Als es im Mai 1844 zu einer Bierpreiserhöhung kommt, gehen die Münchner für mehrere Tage auf die Barrikaden und schlagen ihre geliebten Brauhäuser kurz und klein. Wegen mieser Ernten und Tierseuchen war das Getreide teurer geworden und König Ludwig I. persönlich veranlasste die satte Erhöhung um 22 Prozent. Diese Frechheit, ausgerechnet zu Beginn des traditionellen Sommerbierausschanks, entfachte am 1. Mai den Zorn der Massen und brachte buchstäblich alle Fässer zum Überlaufen; mit Erfolg, denn am 5. Mai wurde die Erhöhung zurückgenommen. Friedrich Engels, damals als Journalist für die englische Presse tätig, schlussfolgerte in seinem Augenzeugenbericht erwartungsvoll: „Wenn die Leute erst einmal wissen, dass sie die Regierung dazu bringen können, Steuern zurückzunehmen, werden sie bald lernen, dass es genauso einfach ist, sie auch in Bezug auf ernstere Angelegenheiten das Fürchten zu lehren.“


Das Design stammt dieses Mal vom Künstlerrebell Torsten Mühlbach, der in München lebt. Gefragt nach seinem umgestalteten Bierdeckel, auf dem u.a. der Zeitraum der Aufstände in Bierstrichen angezeigt und das Reinheitsgebot zum Freiheitsgebot wird, antwortete Torsten:


„

Nach der Revolution ist vor der Revolution.




Nach dem Rausch ist vor dem Rausch.




Jede große Geschichte beginnt mit:




‚Halt mal kurz mein Bier‘




In diesem Sinne, Prost

 …“

Das 

Working Class History T-Shirt des Monats April 2022

 

, hergestellt aus 100% Bio-Baumwolle von einer Näherinnen-Kooperative in Kroatien, ist zurück. Das Design dieses Monats erinnert an den Kampf der Bergbaugemeinden in Großbritannien gegen die konservative Regierung von Margaret Thatcher in den Jahren 1984-1985. Die Bergleute streikten gegen die Schließung von Gruben, während eine große Anzahl von Frauen, insbesondere Ehefrauen von Bergleuten, eine aktive Rolle bei der Unterstützung des Streiks spielten und es ermöglichten, dass er fast ein Jahr lang andauerte, bis er schließlich niedergeschlagen wurde. Als Thatcher im April 2013 starb, brachen im ganzen Land Straßenfeste aus, insbesondere in ehemaligen Bergbaugemeinden. Der Song „Ding-Dong The Witch Is Dead“ erreichte Platz 1 der Charts. Das 

Working Class History T-Shirt des Monats März

 

 ist den sogenannten Märzstreiks gegen die faschistische deutsche Besatzung in Italien im März 1944 gewidmet. Für eine Woche legten die Arbeiter*innen in den norditalienischen Industriezentren wie Mailand und Turin die Produktion lahm und leisteten so wichtigen Widerstand auf dem Weg zur Befreiung von den Nazis. Das Design stammt von Dekorateurin und Tätowiererin Cinzia Argazzi aus Bologna und enthält ein Wortspiel, bei dem die Wörter „widerstehen/resistere“ und „existieren/esistere“ auf italienisch verwendet werden. Das 

Februar Working Class History Monats-Shirt

 

 ist einer Geschichte indigenen Widerstands gegen den spanischen Kolonialismus gewidmet. Als Hernandez de Cordova im Februar 1517 von Kuba nach Mexiko aufbrach, um Indigene für die Arbeit in Minen zu versklaven, gefiel dies den Maya überhaupt nicht. Cordova wurde von Maya-Kämpfern besiegt und zum Rückzug gezwungen. Bald darauf verstarb er an seinen Wunden. Das hervorragende Design wurde von dem jungen mexikanischen Künstler Julio Mendoza entworfen. Die Rückseite des Shirts stellt einen Maya-Krieger dar, der einen Jaguarhelm trägt. Für die Maya repräsentierte der Jaguar Kraft und Tapferkeit; die Verkörperung von Aggressivität. Das Maya-Wort

fuerza

Es heißt, dass als spanische Invasoren einen Boten schickten, um von Nachán Can Tribut zu fordern, er eine Nachricht zurück schickte, in der er sagte, dass der einzige Tribut, den er den Spaniern geben würde, Truthähne in Form von Speeren und Maiskolben in Form von Pfeilen wären. Der Pfeil beinhaltet auch das Jahr der Schlacht gegen Cordova. Ein Teil der Erlöse gehen diesen Monat zusätzlich an Projekte, die die indigene Autonomie der Maya unterstützen.

title: Smart işçilerinin direnişi 4. gününde: ‘Smart işçileri gidilmesi gereken yolu işaret ediyor’
content:
İzmir Aliağa’da bulunan Smart Solar’da işten atmalara karşı işçilerin fabrika önünü terk etmeden sürdürdükleri çadır nöbeti 4. gününde devam ediyor. Önceki günlerde olduğu gibi yine Aliağa Organize Sanayi Bölgesi (ALOSBİ) içerisinde yürüyüş gerçekleştiren işçiler “Birleşe birleşe kazanacağız”, “İşçilerin birliği sermayeyi yenecek”, “Yaşasın sınıf dayanışması”, “Ölmek var dönmek yok” sloganları attı.

Patronun çoğunluk tespiti öncesi tüm hamleleri, işçilerin birlik ve kararlılığıyla bertaraf edildi. İşçilerin çadır nöbetine geçeceği gün bir haftalık duruş ilan edip, 74 işçiyi daha işten çıkaran patron bu hamleleriyle Enerji-Sen’den Tes-İş’e geçişleri tehditle yapmayı hedeflemişti. Dün gece yarısı işyeri çoğunluk tespitine dair sürecin tamamlanmasıyla işçiler geceyi meşalelerle kutlama yaparak geçirdi. İşten atılan işçiler geri alınana, sözleşme hakları verilene kadar mücadeleyi sürdüreceklerini söyleyen işçiler “Ne olursa olsun burayı terk etmeyeceğiz haklarımızı alana kadar devam edeceğiz” dedi.

İşçilerin yürüyüşüne Emek Partisi İzmir İl Örgütü dayanışma ziyaretiyle destek verdi. Emek Partisi İzmir İl Başkanı Elif Çuhadar yaptığı açıklamada, Smart işçilerinin kararlı mücadelesine vurgu yaparak “Smart işçileri dosta güven düşmana korku verecek bir kararlılıkla mücadelesini sürdürüyor. Patronun tüm hamlelerine birlik ve mücadele ile cevap veriyorlar. Bu cevap yalnızca Smart işçilerinin değil, ALOSBİ işçileri başta olmak üzere Türkiye işçi sınıfının gitmesi gereken yola işaret ediyor. Bu mücadele emekten yana tüm güçlerin desteğiyle büyütülmeli, işçiler bulundukları her yerde kendi talepleri için Smart işçilerinin açtığı yoldan gitmelidir” ifadelerini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Fındıklı Belediye Başkanı Çervatoğlu'ndan kaymakama mezarlık tepkisi
content:
Rize - Fındıklı Belediye Başkanı Ercüment Şahin Çervatoğlu, belediyenin yetki ve sorumluluğundaki mezarlıkların, belediyenin bilgisi ve izni dışında taşınmak istenmesine tepki gösterdi. Çervatoğlu, Fındıklı Kaymakamlığı’nın yürüttüğü çalışmaya ilişkin, "Şu anda Türkiye Cumhuriyeti Kaymakamlık makamı suç işliyor. Bu da yaratılan AKP düzeninin kendisidir" dedi.

Rize’nin Fındıklı ilçesine bağlı Aksu Mahallesi Kavak Dibi mevkisinde, belediyenin yetki ve sorumluluğunda bulunan mezarlıkların kaymakamlığa ait iş makineleriyle taşınmak istendiğini belirten Belediye Başkanı Ercüment Şahin Çervatoğlu, çalışma yapılan alana giderek tepki gösterdi. Çervatoğlu, belediyenin ve mezar sahiplerinin izni olmadan yürütüldüğünü söylediği çalışmaya ilişkin, kaymakamlık görevlilerinin belediyenin yetki alanına müdahale ettiğini söyledi.

Çervatoğlu, 5393 sayılı Belediye Kanunu’nun 14’üncü maddesinde mezarlık hizmetlerinin belediyelerin görev ve sorumlulukları arasında sayıldığını, ilgili yönetmelikte de mezar nakli için belediyeden izin alınmasının öngörüldüğünü belirterek, "Belediyenin izni yok, ailelerin izni yok, kaymakamlık belediyecilik yapmaya çalışıyor. Gelinen noktada bu siyasal rejimin tam da kendisidir. Kolluk kuvvetleriyle bizi karşı karşıya getirmek isteyen bu kaymakamlık anlayışını protesto ediyoruz. Cenazelerimizi bile rahat bırakmıyorsunuz, mezarlarımızı bile rahat bırakmıyorsunuz. Müslümanlığınız nerede" diye konuştu.

Çalışmanın hangi amaçla yapıldığının belli olduğunu öne süren Çervatoğlu, "Kaymakamlık belediyecilik yapacaksa, bize gerek yoktur. Mezara kadar indiyseniz, bizim bu ülkede yaşayacak halimiz yok" dedi.

Çervatoğlu, Kaymakam Mücahit Aydoğdu’ya tepki göstererek, "Yasa dışı bir şekilde kolluk kuvvetleriyle bizi karşı karşıya getiriyor. Biraz utanma olacak. Bu mudur devlet insanı olmak. Ne amaçla kaldırılıyor, belirsiz. Şu anda Türkiye Cumhuriyeti kaymakamlık makamı suç işliyor. Bu da yaratılan AKP düzeninin kendisidir" dedi.

Çervatoğlu, "İlçede yenildiğiniz halde nasıl yeniliyoruz buna diyerek kolluk kuvvetleriyle bizi karşı karşıya getirerek iş yapmaya çalışıyorsunuz. 'Belediyeden izin alınmasının gerekli olduğu hüküm altına alınmıştır' deniyor. Sana izin veren oldu mu? Yasayı tanımıyorum mu diyorsun? Nasıl güveneceğiz bu kaymakama?” ifadesini kullandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: “Okulda ölmek istemiyoruz” diyen öğretmene disiplin cezası
content:
Okullarda art arda yaşanan şiddet olayları eğitim emekçilerinin tepkisine neden olurken okulların güvenli hale getirilmesini isteyen öğretmenler de disiplin yaptırımlarıyla karşı karşıya kalıyor.




Bunun son örneği, Eğitim-İş Genel Özlük-Hukuk ve TİS Sekreteri Yeliz Toy’a verilen disiplin cezası oldu.




Nisan 2026’da Maraş’ta İ.A.M.’nin düzenlediği ve 10 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiği okul saldırısının ardından “Okulda ölmek istemiyoruz” açıklaması yapan Toy hakkında kademe ilerlemesinin durdurulması cezası istendi.




Açıklamayı sendikal faaliyetleri kapsamında yaptığını söyleyen Toy, bu gerekçeyle savunma vermeyi reddetti. Toy’un cezaya yönelik itirazlarını Bursa İl Milli Eğitim Müdürlüğü İl Disiplin Kurulu kabul etti. Ancak Bursa Valisi Erol Ayyıldız, Toy’a disiplin cezası verdi.




“Bu neyin husumeti?”




Disiplin cezasına tepki gösteren Toy, Bursa Valisi Erol Ayyıldız’a seslenerek kararın gerekçesini sorguladı. Öğretmenlerin ve öğrencilerin yaşam hakkını savunmanın cezalandırılmak istendiğini söyleyen Toy, laik ve bilimsel eğitim mücadelesinden vazgeçmeyeceğini belirtti.




Toy, açıklamasında şu ifadeleri kullandı:




“‘Okulda ölmek istemiyoruz!’ sözlerime gösterdiğiniz idari hassasiyet ile makamınızda ağırladığınız cübbeli sarıklı tarikatçılara gösterdiğiniz kabul arasındaki fark, kamuoyunun dikkatinden kaçmayacaktır. Gerçi Sayın Vali, biz sizi bu tercihlerinizden de tanıyoruz! Ama bugün meselemiz kimi makamınıza buyur ettiğiniz değil, hangi gerekçeyle disiplin cezası verdiğinizdir.




Yoksa asıl meseleniz, laik, bilimsel, kamusal ve Cumhuriyetçi eğitim konusundaki tavizsiz duruşumuz mu? Cumhuriyetin öğretmenleri olarak tarikatlara teslim edilmeyen, bilimin rehberliğinde bir eğitim sisteminde ısrar etmemiz mi cezalandırılmak isteniyor?”




“Cumhuriyetin öğretmenleri susmaz”




BirGün'deki habere göre, Toy, disiplin cezasının kendisini savunduğu değerlerden vazgeçiremeyeceğini vurgulayarak şöyle devam etti:




“Şunu da çok iyi bilin. Dün neyi savunduysam bugün de aynı yerdeyim! Cumhuriyetin okullarını, laik ve bilimsel eğitimi, öğretmenlerin onurunu, çocukların yaşam hakkını savunmaya devam edeceğim.




Ne disiplin cezalarınız ne soruşturmalarınız ne de makamlarınızın gücü, beni inandığım değerlerden bir adım geri attırabilir! Çünkü ben gücümü Cumhuriyetin değerlerinden, öğretmenlerin haklı mücadelesinden alıyorum.




Cumhuriyetin öğretmenleri susmaz, laik eğitim mücadelesinden vazgeçmez, çocukların geleceğini karanlığa teslim etmez!”

title: Spot doğal gaz piyasasında referans fiyat 19 bin 48 lira oldu
content:

Duygu Ayber Gültekin [email protected]

«Η Αλληλεγγύη δεν ποινικοποιείται» | Φεστιβάλ Αλληλεγγύης στην Παλαιστίνη

title: Il settore agricolo in crisi: voci da Campania e Piemonte
content:
Da diversi giorni gli agricoltori sono tornati a mobilitarsi. Come ribadiscono con forza dal 2024, il settore primario è in crisi: costi di produzione che eccedono il guadagno, indebitamento, squilibri di potere lungo le filiere della GDO, difficoltà climatiche, politiche agricole inadeguate ai più, assenza di ricambio intergenerazionale. 




Oggi, il lievitare del costo del carburante si inserisce in un contesto di aumento dei costi di produzione (es. fertilizzanti e concime), mettendo particolarmente in crisi il settore cerealicolo, determinato dai conflitti in corso. 




Le risposte di questi giorni consistono in blocchi stradali  e di autocisterne di carburante (in particolare in Calabria e Sicilia, dove sono coinvolti anche i pescatori), latte versato sulla Via Aurelia (Lazio), cortei di trattori, presidi (in Puglia, dove si denuncia l’olivicoltura in crisi)  e sit-in a Roma, in piazza Santi Apostoli. Non mancano i tavoli di confronto con le autorità (come in Calabria), ma le misure promesse vengono generalmente giudicate insufficienti. 




Come sottolineano spesso le organizzazioni nate dalle proteste dei trattori del 2024, che cercano di interfacciarsi direttamente con l’opinione pubblica, mentre il margine degli agricoltori è ridotto all’osso, i prezzi dei prodotti sugli scaffali continuano a salire. Più in generale, nelle mobilitazioni si parla tanto di carovita, e questo sta portando altre categorie di lavoratori e lavoratrici ad unirsi. 




Ne parliamo con Gabriele Forte, agricoltore in Campania e membro di Agricoltori Italiani, e Ivo Pittavino, allevatore in Piemonte. Ivo fa parte della realtà Agricoltori Autonomi Italiani Piemonte.

title: Malgré la répression le mouvement continue
content:
Deuxième semaine, qu'est-ce qui se passe ? Les flics tapent de partout. Et ça court de partout. Les enfants donnent des belles leçons aux adultes, de courage et de révolte.




Lundi 5 octobre ça continue malgré la violence de la réponse étatique et les stratégies de division... Les blocages se mettent en place malgré les fermetures annoncées des lycées et la mise en place des cours en présentiel (tout pour que les enfants restent sages à la maison, seuls devant leur écran, comme les aiment l'État et le capitalisme). Et les cours en visio sont perturbés avec classe :)


Certains profs refusent aussi de jouer le jeu. (vont-ils lutter aussi contre les conseils de discipline qui s'abattent contre leurs élèves ?!)




Et la date de manif c'est demain. Mardi 6 octobre. Gros rendez-vous annoncé par les syndicats, et discuté tout au long du week-end, et qu'attendent tout ceux qui ont loupé jeudi et vendredi dans la rue. Bref tout le monde attend, et boomla manif a duré longtemps, joyeuse et déterminéé et inarrêtable. (voir un récit de la journée en bas de la page)




La réponse de l'État reste la même : les CRS, la CSI et la Brigade AntiCriminalité. On compte 3 arrestations à Réformés, puis 3-4autres plus tard. Et on ne peut compter le nombre de gens gazés, intoxiqués, frappés, insulté, bousculés par la police.




On a vu les CRS utiliser leurs lanceurs PennArms 40 mm, des lanceurs multi-coups (18 palets en 6coups à 100m de distance) produits par l'entreprise américaine Combined Systems.




 

 

 

 

 

CRS et penn arm


 

 




Quant on parle d'interpellations, d'arrestations, de gav : ça veut souvent dire que des gens se sont fait attraper violemment par des flics, frappés, menotté, insulté. Que ces personnes vont être conduites vers le commissariat pour 24 ou 48h, sous la pression. Dans la malnutrition, le mauvais sommeil et la pression psychologique. Lisez 

nos textes et brochures pour mieux se préparer à cette épreuve

, et n'oubliez pas que le droit au silence est un refuge :)


Les flics accusent les manifestant.e.s de tout un tas de délits : participation à un attroupement, outrage, dissimulation du visage, violence sur flic, résistance avec violence à son arrestation, etc.


Selon les personnes et les dossiers, les procureurs décident de relâcher sans suite ou de convoquer plus tard.


Les personnes majeurs peuvent aussi être présenté dès la fin de la garde à vue devant des juges, en « comparution immédiate ». Mais il est possible pour la personne de refuser cette procédure dès le début de l'audience. Ce que nous conseillons de faire, la date sera repoussé de quelques semaines, ce qui nous laisse du temps pour préparer la défense et au mieux démonter les mensonges des flics :)




 

 

 

 

 

en GAV c'est un nom d'avocat.e qu'il te faut. Le numero de la LT c'est pour plus tard, ou pour les proches.


 

 




On parle des manifs mais les blocages continuent le matin. Et les flics continuent de venir en force.


C'est dans beaucoup de lycées : st-exupery, marie curie, st joseph, marseilleveyre, florida, don bosco, le chatelier, thiers, jean perrin, montgrand, etc.




Et chaque jour des manif lycéennes ont lieu l'après midi.




La nouvelle date de manif syndicale est annoncée le jeudi.




Jeudi 8 octobre ça marche ça crie de Réformés à la Pref, porte d'aix, joliette, réformés, parc longchamp, jusqu'à boulevard de plombières. Education physique et sportive ! Les drones policiers essaient de suivre la foule inarrêtable, et guider les flics à bout de souffle.




 

 

 

 

 

utilisation de drone contre les manifestant.e.s, place du tribunal


 

 




La fac se soulève aussi : le campus st Charles bloqué, occupé puis expulsé par les flics. Campus Schuman à Aix bloqué. Mais ça reste difficile de s'organiser dans les locaux universitaires, les chefs/patrons d'université appellent les flics et ils entrent à l'intérieur des bâtiments !




RDV à la Plaine dimanche pour une collecte de matos masque ffp2, serum phy, maalox, etc.




Et on rappelle les initiatives de soutien psy face à la violence policière : Spaam 

8750




et la nouvelle équipe de psy pro « psychoteam13 »




Merci à l'équipe de cuisinier.e.s qui vendredi a préparé de la soupe pour les lieux de blocage.




SVP pour le soutien juridique des personnes interpellés faites un don sur notre cagnotte !!! merci




https://www.helloasso.com/associations/liberte-toujours-soutien-juridique-et-defense-collective/collectes/legalteam




***




Récit du mardi 6 octobre 2026 à Marseille : « Mardi tôt le matin. On est beaucoup à naviguer dans la ville pour chercher les lycées bloqués mais la grande majorité sont fermés. Alala les proviseurs les recteurs tout ce monde là a bien peur et se retranche derrière la fermeture administrative des lycées. Pas grave en vrai, il semble pas que ça empêche les lycéens de se retrouver, d'échanger sur les téls et les réseaux et de se retrouver en manif ensuite.


À voir qu'est-ce qu'on fait de ces fermetures administratives à plus long terme, comment s'adapter par rapport à ça.




Réformés 10h. Plus tôt une équipe de camarades s'est activée pour poser quelques tables vers le kiosque, avec des boissons chaudes et un p'tit déj. Et puis sur une table, des conseils en manif, une fiche sur le matériel de protection, des tracts anti-répression et d'auto-défense contre la police... ça ramène du monde, on discute de ce qu'il y a sur les tracts, ça échange des infos sur les blocages des derniers jours. Les lycéen·nes ont vu déjà bien tourner les conseils d'auto-défense face à la police sur les réseaux sociaux !


On est un peu surpris de voir finalement pas si grand-monde aux réformés, on marche aisément sur la place bon, on se dit que ça arriver après.




10h30/11h, réformés toujours, les gens.tes arrivent en masse. Ça commence à ressembler à une grosse grosse manif, en mode des dizaines de milliers de personnes et tout. Y'a de la joie dans l'air, on se retrouve entre copaines et camarades, y'a des têtes qu'on avait pas vu depuis un p'tit moment. Vers 11h un truc comme ça, la CGT installe son cortège avec son cordon ridicule à ne pas franchir blabla ça serait la sécurité des manifestants. Au même moment, plusieurs cortèges de lycéen·nes arrivent en masse sur le haut de la canebière et prennent la tête de la manif, ce qui fera quelques tensions avec la CGT mais au bout de 2 minutes les syndicalistes voient bien que leur cordon sert à rien donc ils laissent tomber. La Gen Z qui renvoie Jean jaurès et son encadrement des manifestations (instauré pour impressionner la bourgeoisie) aux oubliettes de l'histoire des luttes, ça fait plaisir.




Le cortège s'élance progressivement, y'a énormément de monde, ça descend la canebière. La CGT avec son camion change le parcours à la dernière minute (parce qu'ils se sont faits déborder ils veulent reprendre la main ??). On remonte vers la porte d'Aix, gros slogans, surtout méga énergie de fou, les lycéen·nes chauffent toute la manif y'a vraiment une belle énergie.


On arrive Porte d'Aix. Y'a tellement de monde c'est une dinguerie, pendant plus de 45 minutes les gens continuent d'arriver sur la place. C'est la fin de la manif officielle avec la CGT qui fait son blabla sur le camion. Oh les syndicats là annoncez des dates de mobilisation qui sont pas dans un mois au lieu de raconter votre blabla habituel !! En tout cas sur le moment y'a plein de monde qui préfère regarder les battle d'aura sur la place que de les écoutez parler !


Heureusement, des lycéen·nes arrivent à monter sur le camion et à parler dans le mégaphone. Ça lance l'appel à continuer la manif en direction de la préfecture (sans dire explicitement que c'est une manif sauvage hihi) !! Et paf 10 minutes après, une masse immense de personnes s'engouffrent rue d'Aix vers Belsunce et la préfecture. C'est immense, y'a trop de monde, on est plusieurs à se dire qu'on n'a rarement vu une manif comme ça à marseille. Ça prend des airs de 30 000/40 000 personnes à vue de nez.




On arrive devant la préf, ça s'échauffe un peu dans les esprits, ça se rapproche des keufs, puis ça repart. Y'a beaucoup de monde, des lycéen·es et d'autres, beaucoup de personnes en noir, puis ça prend Lieutaud, Castellane, on s'arrête un p'tit moment sur la place sans trop savoir quoi faire. Puis une banderole lycéenne se replace en tête de manif et lance l'appel à poursuivre ! Let's go du coup ! Rue de rome, lieutaud encore puis cours Julien (là ça lance des appels à bloquer la gare), puis la plaine où y'a pas mal de personnes qui vont rester sur la place alors que y'a un appel au mégaphone à descendre sur réformés.




Aux réformés, y toujours beaucoup beaucoup de monde, les flics sont pas loin. Ça s'active un peu, ça s'équipe ça se masque. Des feux de poubelles et les flics lancent les premières lacrymos. C'est le début du zbeul et visiblement y'a beaucoup de monde équipé qui a envie de continuer. Après les lacrymos des flics, 3 cortèges se forment, un sur le cours longchamp, l'autre sur libération et l'autre au niveau de rue Thiers/rue Barbaroux. Malheureusement 3 arrestations ont lieu à ce moment-là, au niveau du cours joseph thierry.




C'est parti pour 2 heures de zbeul dans la ville avec des p'tits feux, des poubelles des barrières des tuyaux, tout ce qu'on trouve sous la main quoi (et faut dire que la ville de marseille avec tous ses travaux dans tous les coins nous régale dans ces moments-là). Les bacqueux se montrent et foutent la press mais bon après que leurs collègues aient gazés ils se retouvent bloqués dans les petites rues de longchamp.


Les cortèges deviennent plus petits, ça donne des infos à voix haute à partir des boucles signal, on essaie de se rejoindre.


Ça continue un long moment comme ça, une belle déter qui passera par Sébastopol et la rue Monte Cristo avant de revenir aux réformés et que les flics ne gazent une autre fois.


Ça remontera ensuite à la plaine, puis un beau p'tit cortège descendra tout chave pour bloquer Sakakini pendant 30 minutes, beau jeu, on a encore de l'énergie alors qu'il est 16h et qu'on a marché de fou aujourd'hui mais on est heureux d'être là !!


On se quitte en fin d'aprem, ça se donne rendez-vous sur des blocages de lycée, on se tiendra au jus le soir pour le prochain matin et surtout on se dit qu'on est heureux de ce qu'il se passe et d'être là, c'est fou c'est fou !!


Hâte de la suite et force aux lycéen·nes !!! »

author: Craig Brittain
title: Lessons from jail: Barry York’s 'A Pentridge Memoir'
content:
A Pentridge Memoir: A political prisoner's story, including a history of the Victorian Prisoners' Action Committee 1973–1976 By Barry York Self-published Sept, 2026 RRP $34.95

In 1972, three student radicals from Melbourne’s La Trobe University — Barry York, Fergus Robinson and Brian Pola — were sent to Pentridge Prison for being in contempt of the Supreme Court of Victoria.

The three were seen as ringleaders of one of the radical student groups causing major problems for the authorities in the late 1960s and early ‘70s, during the Vietnam War.

There had been no trial, they’d been given no chance to defend themselves, and there’d been no sentencing. As far as they knew they were going to jail forever. A Pentridge Memoir: A political prisoner’s story is York’s personal account of this harrowing experience: what it was like to be sent to a high security prison for the “crime” of being an effective political activist on a university campus.

York, Robinson and Pola had been instrumental in organising mass meetings and protests against Australia’s involvement in the war. They staged anti-Apartheid protests against the all-white South African Springbok rugby team's tour, and contributed to the resignation of La Trobe University Chancellor, Sir Archibald Glenn, after he was exposed as being the managing director of Imperial Chemicals Industries (ICI). ICI was directly connected to Australia’s Vietnam War effort, and the Apartheid regime in South Africa.

La Trobe came up with a novel way of dealing with objectionable left-wing student leaders. “The La Trobe Three”, as they came to be known, were suspended from the university, but, on top of this, the University Council took out an injunction against them in the Supreme Court, barring them from setting foot on campus.

There were meetings and protests in support of the banned students. Even political enemies thought they’d been unfairly treated, and the Council was seen as interfering with students’ right to freedom of speech and assembly.

Naturally the La Trobe Three ignored the injunction, and were eventually arrested and incarcerated.

However, the administration’s bright idea of locking them up and throwing away the key backfired spectacularly. Against all odds, they stuck it out, and weren’t broken.

York vividly describes what prison was like for a young student who’d never even been in trouble with the police, let alone been in jail before:

“What stays with me most were the nights in A Division, locked in my cell, lights out, no escape — and the sounds echoing from H Division, the prison’s maximum security wing. Thuds. Kicks. Fists. Screams. The screws in H didn’t merely enforce discipline. They enjoyed inflicting pain on men who couldn’t fight back. They beat defenceless men — unarmed, caged.

“Then there was the crying. A prisoner in an observation cell in our own division, just wailing. Not weeping — wailing. Hour after hour, this long haunted howl of anguish that cut through everything. I couldn’t block it out; it became part of the atmosphere, the texture of the night.

“And I can’t forget the young man in the cell beside mine. He died during the night. Alone.”

York spent 44 days in prison; Robinson, 4 months; and Pola, 3 months.

York and Robinson were Maoists, members of the Communist Party of Australia (Marxist-Leninist), while Pola was a member of the Moscow-aligned Communist Party of Australia (CPA).

They came out stronger for the experience and were fortunate in being committed communists with knowledge of history and Marxist theory to support them. They understood jail was just another part of the class struggle.

They had a sense of identity and purpose that other prisoners didn’t have. They knew they were political prisoners and, as such, had something to live up to. They had committed no crime. They were in jail for protesting the crimes Australia was committing in an imperialist war; and the crimes of the university, as they saw it, denying freedom of speech and assembly to its students.

They didn’t give in. They never “purged” their contempt by apologising to the Supreme Court.

Eventually, La Trobe backed down. The Vice-Chancellor made an offer — which Ted Hill, their Communist lawyer, recommended they accept. They agreed to renounce violence (they’d never been in favour of violence and hadn’t committed any) on condition that the university also renounced violence — such as its use of police against protesting students. The university then approached the court and requested their release.

As Marxists they understood their task was to continue the struggle wherever they found it — even in prison. They collected information from prisoners and identified tensions within the prison, and between the prison and the outside world. They listened to prisoners’ grievances and then collectively worked out what could be done about them.

When they were eventually released, they didn’t just continue protesting about university regulations and structure, or the war in Vietnam. They set up support groups for prisoners and became active spokespeople for prison reform and prisoners’ rights.

They took on the minister responsible for prisons and had him removed from the University Council. They made the public aware of what was going on in Pentridge, and arranged jobs for former prisoners.

What York describes is a perfect example of dialectics at work. He and his comrades were jailed for their activism against the Vietnam War and La Trobe University's connection to it. They had overwhelming support from the student population and the Student Representative Council, but the University Council decided to make an example of them. They suffered the barbaric conditions at Pentridge and brutal treatment by prison wardens, and they met and learned from ordinary prisoners.

But, most importantly, once released from jail, their activism changed direction and they formed prisoner support groups, both on campus and in the broader community, getting support and publicity from some of the country’s most powerful trade unions — especially, the Builders Labourers Federation (which went on to become part of the CFMEU).

Their activism was taken to a new level. The negative prison experience was transformed into something new — and wouldn't have happened if they had not been jailed. This is a good example of the negation of the negation; quantitative experiences making the leap into a qualitative change.

Maoism had also taught them an important thing: theory without practice is worthless.

Hill gave York some useful advice: If you’re ever arrested by the police for political activism the best response to questioning is “I’ve done nothing wrong” and “I’ve got nothing more to say”.

Readers can order York’s prison memoir directly by emailing: [email protected].

York also wrote an account of his student activism at La Trobe University in Student Revolt: La Trobe University 1967-73, which he has made available for free at: c21stleft.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/09/student-revolt-by-barry-york.pdf.

How one old cottonwood tree became a symbol for border wall protesters

Some activists are doing a tree sit to save cottonwood trees from being taken down for border wall expansion.

These activists have had someone consistently tree sitting for more than 60 days now. (

As of checking the activists’ instagram on Sept. 28, 2026.

)

Most press on the matter outside of social media, that I can find, has died down, but they continue providing on the ground footage and documentation of what is happening at the US/Mexico “border” wall.

And they are making a difference.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

View this post on Instagram

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 




The Tohono O'odham Nation also had set up a prayer camp in resistance to border wall expansion, having had the buried remains of their ancestors at sacred sites blown apart by border wall expansion.

Some quotes from an

 article on the Tohono O'odham’s experience with the efforts of expansion:

“I have been here because of this border wall that’s going up and the Trump administration,” he said.  “I really dislike it because it’s dividing our people and that really hurts,” he told ICT. “They can’t see their families, they can’t visit their families, they can’t go home. Just the other day, we went to our neighbors right across (the border) to invite them over for breakfast and we got stopped … and we got carded and they never did that before. They wouldn’t let us cross until we gave them our tribal IDs.”

- Davy Cross, Tohono O’odham

Later in the article:

The chairman [of the Tohono O'odham Nation, Verlon Jose] explained that Tohono O’odam citizens in Mexico would have to apply for a special permit to come into the United States for a day or a couple of days. 

But he said there would be real problems with those.

“The 

president of the United States put out an executive order and they said that anybody with those permits would have to pay $1,000 for it

,” he said while standing this month at one of the traditional tribal border gates. 

“

We don’t have $1,000

,” he said, shaking his head. 

“It is even hard for our members … in Mexico, to even have $100. So it’s very difficult.”

Since many tribal members wouldn’t be able to pay for a visa, they would lose the ability to access Indian Health Service and other tribal benefits on the U.S. side of the border, he said.

“As it is right now, 

they won’t have health care. The public health care in Mexico is zero-to-none. People die in the waiting rooms,”

 Jose said.

author: Secretariat
title: Semana Internacional Contra el Impago de Salarios
content:
Del 12 al 18 de octubre se celebra la Semana de la Asociación Internacional de los Trabajadores (AIT) contra el impago de salarios. La lucha contra el impago de salarios es una campaña permanente de la AIT, y esta semana es el momento en que animamos a los sindicatos y otras organizaciones a alzar la voz sobre este tema.

Señalamos que el impago de salarios puede adoptar diversas formas:

- falta total de pago por el trabajo realizado - pago insuficiente de diversa índole, incluyendo obligar a las personas a realizar horas extra sin remuneración adicional, pagar menos de la tarifa acordada, pagar menos de la tarifa legal o de lo estipulado en un convenio colectivo, etc. - obligar a las personas a trabajar bajo contratos inadecuados para privarlas de prestaciones legales, como vacaciones pagadas o baja por enfermedad - deducciones injustificadas del salario - periodos de prueba, de formación o prácticas no remunerados e ilegales

… por citar solo algunas de las formas en que los patrones roban a los trabajadores el dinero que han ganado.

Puedes participar en esta semana de diferentes maneras: desde republicar nuestros artículos o escribir uno propio, hasta emprender acciones directas contra una empresa donde se hayan producido estos problemas o contactar a los trabajadores de dicho lugar para animarles a actuar.

Asimismo, si aún no lo has leído, te recomendamos un artículo escrito por compañeros de Corea del Sur que aborda algunos de los problemas relacionados con el impago de salarios en ese país: https://iwa-ait.org/content/iwa-campaign-against-wage-theft-korea. Suponemos que muchas personas en todo el mundo verán que lo que allí se describe ocurre en muchos otros lugares. Puede que los detalles varíen, pero nuestros problemas con la explotación capitalista son esencialmente los mismos.

¡Luchemos por crear un movimiento internacional y fomentar la acción directa de los trabajadores!

author: Secretariat
title: IWA Week Against Unpaid Wages
content:
October 12-18 is the International Workers' Association Week Against Unpaid Wages. The fight against unpaid wages is a permanent campaign of the IWA and the week is when we encourage the unions and other organizations to make some noise about this topic.

We point out that unpaid wages can take various forms:

- complete lack of payment for work performed - underpayment of different kinds including forcing people to work overtime without extra payment, paying less than the agreed rate, paying less than the legal rate or less than required by a collective agreement, etc. - forcing people to work on the wrong kind of contract so they are ineligible for statutory benefits, such as paid vacation or sick leave - unjustified deductions from the salary - illegal unpaid probationary periods, training periods and internships

… just to name a few of the ways that bosses rob the workers of the money they have earned.

You can participate in this Week in different ways – ranging from republishing our articles, to writing one of your own, from taking direct against a business where problems have occured to contacting workers in such a place and encouraging them to take action.

And, if you haven't read this yet, we recommend an article written by comrades from South Korea which talks about some of the issues with unpaid wages in that country. https://iwa-ait.org/content/iwa-campaign-against-wage-theft-korea We suppose a lot of people around the world will see that what they talk about occurs in many places. Our issues may sometimes differ in some details, but our problems with capitalist exploitation are very much the same.

Let's fight to create an international movement and encourage workers' direct action!

author: Chinedu Akpa
title: Marketing GLP-1 Drugs for Addiction: Why Critics Are Skeptical
content:
T

he enthusiasm surrounding glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) has moved beyond diabetes and obesity. Scientists are now investigating whether drugs such as semaglutide and tirzepatide could help treat addiction by reducing cravings and altering the brain circuits involved in reward.




There is a 

biological rationale

 for this idea. GLP-1 receptors are present in brain regions involved in reward, motivation, learning, and behavior. Early research suggests that GLP-1RAs may influence some of the same pathways implicated in addictive behavior.




But addiction is more than a biological process. It also has psychological and social dimensions. People may use substances or engage in compulsive behaviors to cope with trauma, loneliness, shame, anxiety, stress, or difficult environments. Recovery can therefore require more than suppressing a craving: it can involve developing new coping mechanisms, rebuilding relationships, changing one’s environment, and learning to live without the behavior that once served a psychological function.




That raises a question that has received less attention amid the excitement over GLP-1 drugs: if a medication reduces the biological urge to use a substance, does that necessarily mean it has treated the addiction? Or has it simply created an opportunity for the person to begin addressing the deeper psychological and social factors underlying the behavior?




There are also unresolved questions about the long-term effects of manipulating neural pathways involved not only in reward and craving, but also in motivation, pleasure, and affect. While current regulatory assessments and randomized trials have not established a causal link between GLP-1RAs and serious psychiatric harms, observational and pharmacovigilance studies have generated signals that warrant further investigation.




Image created with AI




A long-running debate




That tension is reflected in a long-running debate over the role of willpower and personal agency in addiction. If addiction is driven largely by changes in brain circuitry, then framing recovery in terms of choice, discipline, or self-control can seem simplistic. But clinicians who work with people in recovery argue that acknowledging addiction’s biological basis does not eliminate the need for personal agency or the psychological work of recovery.




“It is not a matter of willpower or discipline” has become the rallying cry of advocates of prescribing glucagon-like peptide receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) for addiction. The argument is that these drugs act on the neurobiology of hunger, satiety, cravings, and reward—processes that may operate beyond deliberate self-control.




But 

Brook McKenzie

 does not quite agree with this notion. The licensed chemical dependency counselor who has spent over a decade with families and individuals struggling with substance use disorder is convinced that willpower and discipline have a role to play in recovery. The counselor believes the real question isn’t whether willpower or discipline matter, but what they can accomplish. While he notes that these human traits are essential, he adds that “it is not all that is required, but they could open the door to recovery.”




Dr. Lauren Grawert

, a double board-certified addiction psychiatrist, similarly argues that recovery requires repeated acts of commitment and accountability.




“It takes discipline and willpower to repeat many of the same challenging decisions: attending therapy sessions, adhering to the medication regimen as ordered by their doctor, avoiding risky behaviors, mending damaged relationships and practicing coping mechanisms to avoid giving into cravings. These types of decision-making require commitment and accountability. There is a need for a middle ground to exist in addiction treatment.”




The debate over willpower, however, is only one part of a larger disagreement about how addiction should be understood. If addiction is viewed primarily through a biological lens, it follows that changing the brain’s reward circuitry could be seen as a powerful way to treat it. But research on addiction has long suggested that biology is only part of the story.




The biological rationale: Why GLP-1s are being studied for addiction




It is not surprising that GLP-1RAs are being investigated for use in addiction. Over the years, this class of medication’s therapeutic use has expanded beyond its initial indication for diabetes to areas such as obesity, renal disease, and cardiovascular disease.




GLP-1 receptors are abundant in the body and are expressed in the kidney, lungs, heart, pancreatic cells, gastrointestinal tract, and the brain. Their presence in the brain has attracted particular interest because addiction involves neural systems responsible for reward, motivation, and behavior.




One of the pharmacological drivers of the research into novel treatments for addiction is the limitations that have been observed with conventional treatments. Pharmacological approaches such as opioid antagonists, dopamine reuptake inhibitors, and nicotinic partial agonists target only specific neurotransmitter pathways involved in reinforcement and craving. However, important gaps in long-term treatment response and relapse prevention remain, highlighting the need to investigate approaches that may address the complex interplay of neurobiological, behavioral, and metabolic processes involved in addiction.




Another major motivation for developing novel treatments for addiction is the high rate of relapse seen with conventional therapies. Current pharmacological treatments are highly effective for many people and work by relieving withdrawal symptoms, reducing cravings, or blocking the rewarding effects of addictive substances. However, addiction is driven by many neurobiological processes, including reward, stress, learning, memory, and executive control, and no existing medication fully addresses all of these mechanisms.




GLP-1 receptor agonists offer a different therapeutic approach. Rather than acting on a single receptor system associated with a specific substance, these drugs appear to influence multiple brain circuits involved in addiction through the gut-brain axis and the mesocorticolimbic reward system. The gut-brain axis is a bidirectional communication network linking the gastrointestinal tract and the central nervous system. It plays a key role in regulating reward processing, motivation, and feeding behavior. Signals from the gut are transmitted to the brain primarily via the vagus nerve, where they are integrated in the nucleus tractus solitarii (NTS), a part of the brain rich in GLP-1-producing neurons and GLP-1 receptors. From the NTS, these signals are relayed to downstream brain regions involved in appetite regulation, energy homeostasis, and behavior.




On the other hand, the mesocorticolimbic system comprises a network of brain parts such as the ventral tegmental area(VTA), nucleus accumbens (NAc), and prefrontal cortex (PFC). These parts play a key role in mediating reward, reinforcement learning, and compulsive drug-seeking. GLP-1RAs are expressed across this circuitry, where their activation modulates dopaminergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic neurotransmission.




This biological rationale helps explain why researchers are interested in GLP-1RAs. But it does not answer a different question: what happens to the psychological and social dimensions of recovery when treatment focuses primarily on reducing biological urges?




The psychological components of recovery




Before U.S. Army personnel departed Vietnam for home in September 1971, they underwent urine drug screening amid growing concerns that many servicemen had become addicted to heroin during the war. Of the approximately 13,760 enlisted soldiers returning to the United States that month, around 1,400 tested positive for drugs such as opiates, amphetamines, or barbiturates. These screenings laid the foundation for what would become one of the most influential studies on addiction and recovery.




To carry out the 

study

, Lee N. Robins and his colleagues divided the returning soldiers into two groups. The first was a “general” sample of 470 men randomly selected to represent all Army enlisted men returning from Vietnam. The second consisted of 495 men whose urine had tested positive for opiates when they left Vietnam, making them a drug-positive group at higher risk of continued drug use. The researchers attempted to locate and interview participants in both groups after their return to the United States.




Among the 470 men in the general sample, the researchers found that hard-drug use before Vietnam had been uncommon, and less than 1% had ever been addicted to narcotics. During their service in Vietnam, however, nearly half reported using narcotics, and about one-fifth developed physical or psychological dependence. After returning to the United States, about 10% reported some experience with opiates during the following 8 to 12 months, but less than 1% showed signs of opiate dependence.




The findings were different among the 495 men in the drug-positive group. About three-quarters reported that they had been addicted to narcotics while in Vietnam. Yet after returning home, only about one-third reported any experience with opiates, and 7% showed signs of dependence. Many shifted from heroin to other drugs, including amphetamines and barbiturates.




Put together, the results showed a striking decline in heroin use and dependence after the soldiers returned to the United States, even among men who had been using opiates heavily in Vietnam.




The results suggested that environmental change contributed significantly to recovery from addiction. The researchers posited that the decrease in drug intake after Vietnam may be a function of a decline in the drug epidemic in the United States, the men getting old, or the effect of the extraordinary ease of obtaining such drugs in Vietnam. However, they also pointed to the fact that environmental change alone was not responsible for recovery. Other factors such as family support, reduced drug availability, lower heroin purity, higher cost, and the end of wartime stress likely played a role as well.




Robins’ findings underscore an often overlooked factor in addiction treatment: the environment’s influence on both initiation and recovery. This doesn’t diminish the important biological contributions to the disorder, but defining addiction solely through a biological lens is misleading. That nuance helps explain why some critics remain skeptical about positioning GLP-1 receptor agonists as a primary treatment for addiction.




When Robins asked the soldiers whether they had personally known heroin or opium users before Vietnam, 91% knew none, yet 43% eventually used narcotics in Vietnam. The finding highlights once more the important role that the environment can play in shaping addictive behavior. McKenzie explains it this way: “I think there is a tendency to assume that if we can change the brain’s reward system, we’ve solved addiction—I’m not convinced that’s the right framework”.




The licensed therapist believes that the reward pathway matters, but argues that it is one piece of a much larger picture that includes trauma, loneliness, shame, relationships, habits, identity, and environment.




“Recovery isn’t simply the absence of an urge. It’s the presence of new ways to live,” McKenzie added. He explained that if a medication reduces cravings but a person never develops healthier coping skills, relationships, purpose, or accountability, “we’ve treated an important symptom without fully addressing the life that existed around it.”




Therefore, the question is not whether GLP-1RAs might have a role in addiction treatment, but how large that role should be and what other components of recovery must accompany it.




Why GLP-1 drugs might hinder psychosocial recovery




From a psychological perspective, 

Wildaliz Caro, PhD

, believes that treating addiction is more than suppressing cravings. The medical contributor at the Healing Center Cherry Hill, a drug and alcohol rehabilitation center, says treatment must also address what people do with the emotions, thoughts, and circumstances that have contributed to their addictive behaviors. “The primary purpose of most addictions is to serve a psychological function,” Caro explained.




Addictive substances or behaviors can provide temporary relief from distress, distract from anxiety, block memories of trauma, provide comfort, or create a sense of escape. “Reducing the desire to consume a particular substance doesn’t mean removing the need that was being met by consuming that substance,” Caro said.




The licensed clinical psychologist believes this distinction is particularly important when addiction is viewed through a trauma-informed lens. For people who have used drugs, alcohol or other compulsive behaviors to manage overwhelming emotions, reducing the urge to use may be beneficial, but it could also bring long-unaddressed feelings to the surface.




“I would not view this as a failure on behalf of the medication,” Caro said. “Instead, I would view it as a reason to incorporate psychotherapy into the treatment plan, rather than expecting that reducing urges alone will lead to complete recovery.”




Melanie Johnson’s

 experience with binge eating also points to a deeper question about what may drive compulsive behavior in the first place and why the use of GLP-1RAs might not fully address the issue of addiction. Johnson was diagnosed with binge eating disorder but was initially prescribed Zepbound for obesity and sleep apnea. When asked whether GLP-1 treatment helped her binge eating disorder, she said the effect was almost immediate: “It decreased the food noise, regulated my appetite.”




This happened within a couple of days, she said, and she became more intentional about the type of food she ate and her portion sizes. Before Zepbound, she said, “I was so out of control.”




Her experience seems to align with what some individuals report on forums such as Reddit. Personal accounts from people taking GLP-1RAs for diabetes and obesity describe drinking less, losing interest in alcohol, experiencing fewer cravings or becoming abstinent, and eating less.




“Even if all these effects are attributed to GLP-1RAs, we don’t yet know whether they’ll rebound after discontinuation,” said 

Phil Smyth

, a behavioral health executive at Milestone Treatment Center.




Johnson’s story, however, also illustrates why reducing a behavior may not be the same thing as understanding it. She grew up in America in the 1980s, when she described the prevailing messaging around food and weight as “unhealthy,” much of it coming from both parents and society. Such messages made her think she was fat when, in reality, her weight was normal. As she put it, “gaining weight was a self-fulfilling prophecy.” She said childhood trauma and her need to be in control also contributed.




Her account is a reminder that loss of control over a behavior does not necessarily tell us what is driving it. And that distinction matters when considering GLP-1RAs as potential treatments for addiction.




Even if these drugs can dampen cravings or reduce the urge to engage in addictive behavior, they may not address the psychological, emotional, and environmental factors that helped sustain the behavior in the first place.




The concern is not limited to what researchers and clinicians say about GLP-1RAs. The way these drugs are discussed in the media can also shape how the public understands addiction and what recovery is supposed to look like.




Amid growing enthusiasm for the potential use of GLP-1RAs in addiction treatment, some headlines have framed the drugs in ways that may give readers the impression that their effectiveness is already established. Examples include:







“Ozempic for addiction: how an elite rehab center is using GLP-1s to ‘obliterate’ all kinds of craving”




“Can Ozempic Cure Addiction?”




“Ozempic ‘Significantly’ Lowered ‘Alcohol Craving’ in First Clinical Trial, with Those Taking The Drug Drinking 40% less”







Such headlines can reduce a complicated question to a simple narrative: addiction produces cravings, GLP-1RAs reduce cravings, therefore GLP-1RAs treat addiction. But that framing risks obscuring the other components of recovery. If public discussion focuses heavily on a drug’s ability to suppress cravings, people may come to view recovery primarily as the elimination of an unwanted biological signal rather than a process that can also involve psychotherapy, behavioral change, social support, accountability, relationships, and changes in environment.




This matters because the 

evidence for GLP-1RAs

 in addiction remains preliminary. Much of it is observational, anecdotal or at an early stage. Even where randomized evidence is emerging, studies remain relatively small in size and scope and do not yet establish the effectiveness of GLP-1RAs across different substance use disorders.




The danger, then, may not simply be that people overestimate what the drugs can do. A single-story narrative about addiction can also make the biological component appear to be the whole story. That is precisely why behavioral and psychosocial interventions remain important.




As Grawert explains, “There are instances where behavioral therapy is sufficient, especially for those with less severe cases, high levels of motivation, and a stable/positive environment.”




Behavioral therapies such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT), motivational approaches and contingency management can help individuals identify personal triggers, tolerate cravings, and establish new habits. She cautions, however, that this should never be viewed as a universal solution for all patients.




The broader point is not that medication and behavioral therapy should compete. Rather, addiction may require a combination of interventions tailored to the individual. A medication may help create the biological space in which recovery becomes more achievable, while psychotherapy, social support, behavioral interventions, and changes in the person’s environment may help make that recovery sustainable.




Long-term neuropsychiatric concerns




Because GLP-1RAs are being investigated for addiction treatment based on their nervous system activity, concerns have emerged about their potential long-term effects on the human psyche. Available data are limited owing to small sample sizes and short follow-up in human trials. Moreover, the same neural pathways through which GLP-1RAs may attenuate addictive behaviors—reward, motivation, and affective processing—are also involved in experiences of sexual desire, pleasure, and meaning. This raises the question of whether chronic GLP-1RA exposure could affect one’s psychological state long term. To explore this issue, we examined the US Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) 

database

. The FAERS is a database that contains postmarketing reports of adverse drug events received from manufacturers, consumers, and healthcare professionals.




One FDA pharmacovigilance report concerns a purported link between GLP-1RA use and 

suicidal ideation.

 Although the agency’s current assessment concluded that there is no clear causal relationship, citing limited information on many reports and the potential influence of confounding factors, it cautions that a small risk cannot be excluded. This uncertainty stems from the low number of suicidal thoughts or behaviors observed in both GLP-1RAs users and comparator groups. Consequently, the FDA continues to monitor and investigate this safety signal. Similarly, a 

systematic review

 and meta-analysis involving more than 107,000 patients found no association when compared to placebo.




Contrary to the FDA conclusion and the systematic review and meta-analysis, a separate observational study by 

Jisu Park

 et al. found that GLP-1RAs, when used for weight loss, were associated with higher risks of certain psychiatric and gastrointestinal outcomes when compared with non-users. The psychiatric outcomes included depression and anxiety. This was corroborated by another study by 

Wei Chen

 et al. in which 8,240 reports of psychiatric adverse events were analyzed among individuals on GLP-1RA treatment. Findings showed a significant association between GLP-1RAs and the development of specific psychiatric adverse events.




Taken together, the evidence concerning the neuropsychiatric effects of GLP-1RAs remains inconsistent. While randomized clinical trials and regulatory assessments have not demonstrated an increased risk of psychiatric adverse events or suicidality, pharmacovigilance and observational studies have identified signals involving depression, anxiety, and other psychiatric outcomes. Differences in study design, population, follow-up duration, and potential confounding may partly explain these discrepancies. More important, relatively little is known about the consequences of prolonged pharmacological modulation of the neural circuits involved in reward, motivation, and affect. As GLP-1RAs move into investigations for addiction, understanding whether their effects on these circuits remain therapeutically selective, which will be an important area for long-term research.




How independent is the GLP-1 addiction research?




Since researchers first hypothesized that GLP-1RAs might reduce addiction-related cravings, pharmaceutical companies, independent researchers, and government-funded bodies have all become involved in testing the hypothesis.




The 

SEMALCO study

 is an example of how, even when a study is not 

directly

 funded by industry, the influence of pharmaceutical money often remains. The study was an investigator-initiated trial, funded in part by the Mental Health Services of Copenhagen. In the 

study,

 108 Danish patients were investigated in a 26-week, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind clinical trial in an effort to determine if semaglutide would reduce alcohol intake among those with alcohol use disorder and comorbid obesity. The results showed that semaglutide was associated with a reduction in heavy drinking days compared with placebo.




While there was public funding for the study, funding also came from the Novo Nordisk Foundation and Novavi Foundation, two foundations funded by Norvo Nordisk, the pharmaceutical company that markets semaglutide under the names of Ozempic and Wegovy. In addition, some of the investigators on this study, such as Anders Fink-Jensen, had received an unrestricted Novo Nordisk grant for a different study and served on a Novo Nordisk randomized controlled trial advisory panel. Another investigator, Thomas Vilsboll, disclosed advisory/speaker/consulting relationships with both Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly, which is the other major pharmaceutical company with a GLP-1 product.




However, there is important research being done that is free of such industry influence. A study by the US Department of Veterans Affairs is an example of this. This was a large, 

prospective observational study

 involving 606,434 US veterans that investigated whether the initiation of GLP-1RA is linked to lower rates of new alcohol, cannabis, cocaine, nicotine, opioid, and other substance use disorders in people without prior substance use disorders, and to fewer substance use disorder-related adverse clinical outcomes in people who already have a substance use disorder. Among 606,434 US veterans with type 2 diabetes, participants were followed up for up to three years and split into two protocols. Protocol 1 included 524,817 people starting GLP-1RA or sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT-2) inhibitors, while protocol 2 included 81,617 such initiators.




Their findings suggested that GLP-1RA use was linked to a lower risk of new substance use disorders and fewer adverse outcomes in people who already had one, suggesting possible roles in both prevention and treatment. The researchers declared that there was no financial relationship between the funders and any organization that may have a financial interest in the submitted work, and no relationships or activities that may have influenced the submitted work within the three-year period of the research.




What would success actually look like?




For 

Patricia Freebery

, a psychotherapist with more than 20 years of experience, specializing in addiction, trauma and emotion-focused somatic therapy, the question of what constitutes successful treatment is just as important as whether a drug would reduce cravings. Recovery in her view, is not just the absence of cravings or substance use, but the restoration of someone’s ability to live a meaningful and self-directed life.




“A successful treatment would result in a return to my authentic self,” she said, describing recovery as being “fully present in mind, body, and spirit,” and connected to oneself, family, and community. It would involve self-agency and accountability, with a person’s behaviors and intentions aligned rather than aligning with external people or substances to maintain emotional and chemical sobriety.




She also described recovery in practical and relational terms: being physically responsive to one’s body, becoming competent in adulthood, and becoming emotionally capable of engaging with others with “curious compassion, clarity, and confidence.” It means being able to tolerate uncertainty, resist becoming consumed by obsessive thoughts, experience joy and creativity, and remain connected to the present.




Ultimately, Freebery said, recovery should leave a person able to honestly say, “I am free”—not merely free from the substance or behavior, but capable of fully appreciating and engaging with their life.




Conclusion




Perhaps this is the central question that should accompany the excitement surrounding GLP-1 drugs and addiction: if we can reduce the urge, have we necessarily treated the addiction?




The answer may not be either medication or the human dimensions of recovery. It may be both. GLP-1RAs could eventually become another useful tool in the treatment of addiction. But their success should ultimately be measured by more than how effectively they suppress a craving.




A successful treatment may also need to help people regain agency, rebuild relationships, develop healthier ways of coping, address the psychological functions that addictive behaviors once served, and return to a meaningful life.




That is why the question surrounding GLP-1RAs is not simply whether they can change the brain. They may be able to. The harder question is whether changing the brain is enough to change the life around it.




***
