title: "The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist": Daniel Roher, Tristan Harris Discuss New Film
content:
As the development of artificial intelligence accelerates, more voices inside and outside the industry are warning that the technology poses major risks to humanity. The new film, 

The AI Doc: Or How I Became an Apocaloptimist

, features interviews with leading AI executives, researchers, as well as critics, who all voice similar concerns. Since the film’s release earlier this year, a number of AI-driven hacks and other incidents have further alarmed people studying this topic.




“I’m really scared, and I’m struggling in my own life to sort of compartmentalize what I learned, what I know, what I understand, what I see happening around me,” says filmmaker Daniel Roher. He began work on 

The AI Doc

 as he was about to become a father and wondered what kind of world his children would inherit.




We also speak with Tristan Harris, co-founder of the Center for Humane Technology, a leading AI safety advocate who is featured in the film. He says part of the risk of AI development is that it has the logic of an “arms race,” with companies and countries racing to gain supremacy rather than building guardrails.




“The race changes as soon as the fear of all of us losing becomes bigger than the fear of me losing to you,” he says.

title: Urgente: nueva amenaza de desalojo para el Lof Melo
content:
El lonko de la comunidad, Lucas Melo, alertó por una nueva orden de desalojo para este viernes 9 de octubre. Ocurre a pocos días del fallo de la Corte Suprema que habilita la extranjerización ilimitada de tierras. Convocan “a todas las comunidades mapuche, las organizaciones sociales, los partidos políticos y los sindicatos a varias manifestaciones pacíficas en toda la provincia del Neuquén desde las 8 a 11 de la mañana de este viernes”. 

Por La Izquierda Diario Neuquén.







Una comunicación urgente del Lof Melo informa sobre una 

nueva orden de desalojo para la comunidad mapuche

, habitante del lote 42 en el paraje Pedregoso del 

Parque Nacional Nahuel Huapi

. La orden tiene fecha para el próximo viernes.




En su comunicado, convocaron “a todas las comunidades mapuche, las organizaciones sociales, los partidos políticos, los sindicatos a varias manifestaciones pacíficas en toda la provincia del Neuquén desde las 8 a 11 hs. de la mañana de este viernes 9”.




En agosto la comunidad resistió un intento de desalojo, en ocasión del desalojo efectivo del Lof Kinxikew de una porción de su territorio.




Para quienes habitan cerca de la zona, la convocatoria es a las 8 hs. del viernes 9 en el Lof. En Neuquén capital la convocatoria es en la puerta de la Gobernación.




El 6 de agosto, cientos de miles de personas se movilizaron en todo el país contra la extranjerización ilimitada de tierras, que derrotó el intento del gobierno de aprobarla por ley. Para el próximo 15 de octubre se espera una nueva movilización masiva, luego del fallo de la Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación en el mismo sentido.




En el caso del Lof Melo, 

la justicia provincial actúa como agente de los grupos inmobiliarios

, y en particular de una 

familia de origen belga

. Para defender el territorio hay que rodear de solidaridad a las comunidades amenazadas.




Noticia en desarrollo.




Fuente: 

https://www.laizquierdadiario.com/Nueva-amenaza-de-desalojo-para-el-Lof-Melo

title: "She Put Her Body on the Line": Maricarmen, 87, Dies; Her Eviction Sparked Spain Housing Protests
content:
The 87-year-old pensioner in Spain whose eviction from her lifelong home sparked nationwide protests has died. María del Carmen Abascal, better known as Maricarmen, died on Wednesday just hours before she was set to sign a new rental agreement. She was forcibly removed from her Madrid apartment last month on a stretcher after the private investment company that owns the building hiked her rent. After massive public outcry, the landlord had agreed to allow her back into her apartment.




Independent Spanish journalist María Carrión says that although Maricarmen’s story galvanized much of the country, evictions like hers are “a daily occurrence” in Spain.




“Rents have gone up 80% in the last 10 years, while salaries have not kept up,” Carrión says. “Young people cannot leave their homes. They cannot become independent or start families. And this is what people are trying to change from the street.”

author: heinhtetkyaw
title: An Anarchist Perspective on Israel, Palestine, and the Endless Cycle of Violence
content:
From October 7 to the Present: States at War with Human Beings The Israeli–Palestinian conflict cannot be said to have begun on October 7, 2023, just as it cannot simply be reduced to a war between “two nations.”

The roots of this catastrophe go back decades: to the end of the British Mandate, the 1948 war, the establishment of the State of Israel, the displacement and expulsion of more than 700,000 Palestinians, and the emergence of what Palestinians call the Nakba — the catastrophe. Following the 1967 war, the occupation of the West Bank, East Jerusalem, and Gaza, the expansion of Israeli settlements, and extensive restrictions on Palestinians’ lives and freedom of movement further entrenched structures of inequality and domination. Today, nearly 5.9 million Palestinian refugees are eligible for services provided by UNRWA.From an anarchist perspective, the question is not simply: “Which state has the right to govern which territory?” The more fundamental question is: Why should human beings have to submit to states, armies, borders, and military institutions in order to live, enjoy freedom, and secure their safety? October 7: A Crime That Cannot Be Justified On October 7, 2023, Hamas forces and several other Palestinian armed groups attacked southern Israel. Approximately 1,200 people were killed, and 251 were abducted and taken to Gaza. Civilians were among those targeted in the assault. According to the findings of the United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry, hostage-taking, murder, torture, and other acts against civilians constituted war crimes. From an anarchist standpoint, no occupation, repression, or historical injustice can justify the deliberate killing of civilians or the taking of hostages. But this principle must be applied consistently, without exception. If killing an Israeli child is a crime, killing a Palestinian child is equally a crime. If taking an Israeli civilian hostage is a crime, depriving an entire civilian population of water, food, medicine, and security cannot be justified as a “right to self-defence” either. From “Revenge” to Collective Punishment Following October 7, the Israeli government launched a large-scale war in Gaza. The scale of killing, destruction, displacement, and deprivation of basic necessities went far beyond a limited military operation against armed groups.In 2024, the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry reported that Israeli operations in Gaza involved war crimes and crimes against humanity, including murder, extermination, forcible transfer, torture, and the use of starvation as a method of warfare. The same Commission also identified Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups as responsible for war crimes committed during the October 7 attack. In September 2025, the same Commission went a step further, concluding that, based on its investigation, Israel had committed genocide in Gaza. This is a finding by a UN Commission of Inquiry; it is not the same as a final ruling by the International Court of Justice in the genocide case, and the two should not be conflated. South Africa's case against Israel remains before the International Court of Justice. In November 2024, the International Criminal Court also issued arrest warrants for Benjamin Netanyahu and Yoav Gallant on charges of war crimes and crimes against humanity. These decisions, however, do not constitute final convictions; they are part of an ongoing international judicial process. An Anarchist Is Neither a Supporter of the Israeli State nor of a Palestinian State This is where the difference between an anarchist perspective and many prevailing narratives becomes clear. Anarchism fundamentally opposes turning human beings into soldiers serving a state. From this perspective:

The State of Israel, even if it regards the protection of its citizens as its responsibility, has no right to pursue security through mass killing and military domination over another people.

Hamas, even if it describes itself as a resistance movement, has no right to kill civilians or take hostages in the name of the Palestinian people. No state, army, or armed organization owns human lives.

“National security” cannot be used to justify depriving millions of people of their freedom and dignity.

The suffering of one community must never become an excuse for repressing another.

Victims must not be turned into soldiers serving state ideologies.From this perspective, the binary choice between “Israel or Hamas” is fundamentally incomplete.

What does an Israeli living in fear of rockets and attacks want?

What does a Palestinian living under siege, occupation, and displacement want?

Before belonging to any community, both are human beings. After the Ceasefire: Has the War Really Ended? The October 2025 ceasefire brought an end to the large-scale war, but it did not put an end to violence. A September 2026 UN report states that the ceasefire remains fragile, Israeli attacks continue, large parts of Gaza remain subject to severe access restrictions, and reconstruction is proceeding on a scale far below what the population needs. According to the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), between the announcement of the ceasefire on October 10, 2025, and September 2026, at least 1,402 Palestinians were killed and 4,881 injured in Gaza. These figures are attributed to Gaza's Ministry of Health and do not encompass all the consequences of the war and the destruction it has caused. The situation in the West Bank is no different. Settler violence, home demolitions, restrictions on movement, settlement expansion, and the forced displacement of Palestinians continue. The United Nations has reported that in 2026, an average of approximately 17 Palestinians were displaced every day as a result of settler violence and demolitions — twice the average recorded in previous years. Therefore, a “ceasefire” does not necessarily mean “freedom” or “peace.” The sound of bombardment may diminish, but as long as domination, occupation, discrimination, siege, settlement expansion, imprisonment, military borders, and structural poverty remain in place, the conditions that reproduce violence will remain as well. The Problem Is Not Just War; It Is the Structure of PowerAnarchism compels us to take a step back and examine the bigger picture. States usually say:

“We need an army to protect your security.”

“We need more weapons to defend you.”

“You must give the state more power to confront the enemy.”

And ultimately, ordinary people, both Israeli and Palestinian, pay the price of this cycle with their lives, homes, freedom, and future. Under such circumstances, each side can present the other side’s crimes as evidence that it needs even more power.Hamas says: Occupation and repression exist; therefore, armed resistance is necessary.The Israeli government says: Hamas and other armed groups exist; therefore, a military and military control are necessary.And this cycle can continue for generations. Power justifies its own violence through the violence of the opposing side.This is one of the most fundamental lessons that an anarchist perspective can draw from this catastrophe. A Third Way: Beyond StatesAnarchism does not necessarily mean indifference to the security of Israelis or the rights of Palestinians. On the contrary, it can demand security for both, but a form of security that is not built upon the domination of one group by another.The path that deserves serious consideration is one based on direct cooperation among people, democratic local councils, trade unions, mutual-aid networks, women's groups, peace activists, human rights defenders, anti-war movements, and all those who refuse to reduce human beings merely to “Israeli,” “Palestinian,” “Jewish,” “Muslim,” or “enemy.”Movements for Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions — BDS — can also be examined from this perspective: as efforts to exert pressure from below rather than send human beings onto battlefields. However, even these movements are compatible with anarchist ethics only as long as they do not turn into hatred of Jews, Palestinians, or any ethnic or religious group.If the cycle of violence is ever to be genuinely broken, the demand must go beyond “Israel's victory” or “Palestine's victory.” It must be something much deeper:

An end to the killing of civilians.

The release of hostages and prisoners, with their rights respected.

An end to occupation and military domination.

An end to the siege and collective punishment.

An end to settlement expansion and forced displacement.

The right of return or fair compensation for displaced people, within a framework that recognizes the rights of all inhabitants.

Full legal and political equality for all human beings, regardless of ethnicity or religion.

The right of people to determine their own destiny, without states, armies, or armed organizations deciding that destiny on their behalf.

From an anarchist perspective, the issue is not to prove that “these people are good and those people are bad.” The issue is to understand how states, armies, nationalist ideologies, and armed organizations trap ordinary people in a cycle in which every death becomes an excuse for the next. October 7 cannot be separated from the history of occupation, displacement, and repression. But the history of occupation cannot justify the deliberate killing of civilians or hostage-taking either. Likewise, the crimes of October 7 cannot justify the killing, starvation, displacement, and collective punishment of millions of Palestinians. If we are to escape the cycle of revenge, we must also move beyond the logic of “the enemy of my enemy is my friend.” A peace achieved solely through the victory of one army over another is not the peace of the people. Real peace begins when no child has to be sacrificed so that another can live freely. And perhaps the fundamental question here is this:

How can we build a society in which people's security comes not from the barrels of state guns, but from freedom, equality, mutual aid, solidarity, and the organized collective power of the people themselves?

Conclusion: No to States, Yes to Human Beings From an anarchist perspective, choosing between Israel and Hamas means choosing between two armed powers; it does not necessarily mean choosing between two paths to liberation. We can:

Condemn the killing of civilians on October 7.

Condemn occupation and settlement expansion.

Condemn the collective punishment of Gaza's population.

Condemn violence against Palestinian and Israeli civilians.

And, at the same time, refuse to turn any state or armed organization into an idol.

No to apartheid and discrimination.

No to the glorification of armies and war.

Freedom, equality, solidarity, self-determination, and the equal dignity of all human beings.

Anarchism has never sought to replace one flag with another. Instead, it asks us to consider: Why should a human being have to possess a state in order to be free? Perhaps the way out of this cycle is not the victory of one community over another, but the creation of a society in which no state, army, armed organization, or ideology can turn human beings into instruments of its own power.

An Israeli life lost is no less human than a Palestinian life lost.

And as long as human lives are not valued equally, no victory can truly be a victory for humanity.

title: Vom Protest zum Widerstand: Vernetzungskonferenz in Kassel „gewerkschaftlicher Widerstand gegen Sozialabbau und Aufrüstung“ 16.–17. Oktober 2026
content:
„… 

In den vergangenen Monaten ist zwischen 

´Sagt NEIN!´

 

, der 

Gewerkschaftslinken Hamburg

 

 und der 

VKG – Vernetzung für Kämpferische Gewerkschaften

 

 die Idee entstanden, eine gemeinsame Diskussion über den Aufbau einer bundesweiten Koordinierung klassenorientierter Gewerkschaftsarbeit zu eröffnen.

 

Wir wollen Erfahrungen, Konflikte und Fragen aus dem antimilitaristischen Widerstand miteinander teilen. Nicht übereinander reden, sondern miteinander. Nicht nur analysieren, sondern voneinander lernen, Kontakte knüpfen und gemeinsame Perspektiven entwickeln

…“ Aus der 

Einladung zur Eröffnung einer Diskussion bei der VKG

 

 und mehr Informationen:







Vernetzungskonferenz in Kassel: »Aus einzelnen Kämpfen koordinierten Widerstand machen« 

 


„

Antimilitaristische Vernetzungskonferenz am 16. und 17. Oktober in Kassel: Es soll nicht bei Appellen gegen Aufrüstung bleiben. (…)


In den vergangenen Monaten und Jahren sind an vielen Orten antimilitaristische Initiativen entstanden – in Betrieben, Gewerkschaften, Friedensgruppen und anderen gesellschaftlichen Zusammenhängen. Kolleginnen und Kollegen organisieren sich gegen Militarisierung und Rüstungsproduktion, gegen Sozialabbau und die Unterordnung gewerkschaftlicher Interessen unter die sogenannte Kriegstüchtigkeit. Aber vieles findet noch nebeneinander statt. Unser Ausgangspunkt ist deshalb die Frage: Wie bekommen wir diese Erfahrungen zusammen? Zudem wollen wir verhindern, dass die jüngsten Massenmobilisierungen, also der Aktionstag der Automobilindustrie und die Sozialproteste am 26. September, seitens des Gewerkschaftsapparats in konzertierte Aktionen überführt werden.




[Es gibt Initiativen dieser Art. Was wollen Sie anders machen?]




Uns interessiert vor allem die konkrete Praxis: Was passiert in den Betrieben? Welche Auseinandersetzungen gibt es dort und innerhalb der Gewerkschaften? Wo gelingt es Kolleginnen und Kollegen, sich zu organisieren? Wo stoßen sie auf Widerstände? Und was können andere daraus lernen? Dabei wollen wir betriebliche und gewerkschaftliche Initiativen ausdrücklich mit der zivilgesellschaftlichen antimilitaristischen Bewegung zusammenbringen. Nicht übereinander reden, sondern miteinander. Nicht nur analysieren, was gerade geschieht, sondern diskutieren, was wir praktisch tun können. Auch muss niemand mit fertigen Antworten kommen, und wir müssen auch nicht in jeder Frage derselben Meinung sein. Entscheidend ist die Bereitschaft, Erfahrungen zu teilen und darüber zu reden, wo gemeinsames Handeln möglich ist. (…) Wir wollen nicht den nächsten Apparat gründen und auch niemandem ein fertiges Programm vorsetzen. Es geht, wie der Name nahelegt, zunächst darum, Menschen und Initiativen zusammenzubringen. Unterschiede dürfen dabei sichtbar bleiben. Eine tragfähige Vernetzung entsteht nicht dadurch, dass man Differenzen zukleistert. Wir wollen herausfinden, was wir gemeinsam tun können: Wo können Aktionen miteinander verbunden werden? Wo können wir uns gegenseitig unterstützen? Welche Formen kontinuierlicher Zusammenarbeit brauchen wir? Und wie kann aus Protest tatsächlicher Widerstand entstehen? Ob daraus anschließend eine dauerhafte Koordinierung entsteht und welche Form sie haben könnte, müssen die Beteiligten gemeinsam entscheiden. (…)


Ein besonderer Programmpunkt wird eine Liveschaltung nach Vigo in Spanien sein. Dort tagt die Generalversammlung des European Dockworkers’ Council. Die Hafenarbeiter bereiten derzeit ihren nächsten europäischen Hafenaktionstag am 30. Oktober vor. Das ist für uns wichtig, weil antimilitaristischer Widerstand international gedacht werden muss. Häfen, Logistik, Produktion – Kriegsmaterial bewegt sich nicht von selbst. Überall stehen Beschäftigte an entscheidenden Stellen

…“ 

Gespräch mit Andreas Buderus von Niki Uhlmann in der jungen Welt vom 08.10.2026

 

 – Andreas Buderus ist Mitglied der koorganisierenden Initiative »Sagt NEIN!«







Grundinfos:







Beginn: Freitag, 16.10., 13:00 Uhr Ende: Samstag, 17.10., 15:00 Uhr Ort: Kassel, Stadtteilzentrum „Vorderer Westen“




Das Programm

 

 

 bietet kurze Erfahrungsberichte, Podiumsgespräche, Arbeitsgruppen, einen ´Markt der Möglichkeiten´ und vor allem viel Raum für persönlichen Austausch und Vernetzung.




Mit dabei sind bereits Aktive unter anderem von SNOP Automotive, Ford Köln, Mercedes Bremen, VW ´Wir wollen nicht den Tod produzieren´, Zukunftswerk Osnabrück, FU Berlin, IPPNW, Anwaltskollektiv der ´Ulm 5´ und weiteren betrieblichen und zivilgesellschaftlichen Initiativen.

Gewerkschaften, Sozialabbau und Widerstand: Fast 25 Jahre Theorie und Praxis




Dossier: 

Wird der „Herbst der Gegenwehr – Sozialabbau verhindern“ im Sommer 2026 nachgeholt?

Vom Protest zum Widerstand: Vernetzungskonferenz in Kassel „gewerkschaftlicher Widerstand gegen Sozialabbau und Aufrüstung“ 16.–17. Oktober 2026

 erschien zuerst auf 

LabourNet Germany

.

author: John Mullen
title: France: Workers mobilise to support inspiring school student revolt
content:
There were vibrant mass demonstrations in dozens of French towns, on October 6, as five of the nation's six main trade union confederations mobilised in support of the escalating school student movement.

Entering its third week, the historic uprising against years of cuts in school budgets continues to gain momentum in the face of brutal police violence and state panic.

The movement has involved far more high schools than the last comparable movement eight years back. More than 1000 high schools (for 15 to 18-year-olds) and more than 100 middle schools (for 11 to 15-year-olds) have been blockaded.

Thirty universities have joined the movement in the past few days.

Daily student mass meetings in every establishment decide on the day’s actions. On the demonstrations you can see thousands of home-made placards with imaginative slogans. They range from quoting the 1793 Declaration of the Rights of Man (on the duty of insurrection) to quoting popular rap artists; from “Generation X, Generation Z, one struggle!” to “The 6-7 generation is aiming at 68” (referring to the uprising of May-June 1968).

Desperate to extinguish the flames of revolt, authorities resorted to mass lockouts, preemptively closing hundreds of schools and several university campuses this week.

Macron’s minority government, eager to pass its austerity budget before the end of the year, has reacted in three ways:

First, with violence and intimidation. In the hope of scaring away as many young protesters as possible, they ensured that the police repression was extreme. A couple of hundred teenagers have been injured by cops, and some of the examples are heartbreaking.

In the Paris region, an officer fired a tear gas canister point-blank into the face of a 14-year-old boy, shattering his jaw in two places and knocking out all his teeth; his family is now suing for attempted murder. In Tours, a 16-year-old lost an eye to a rubber bullet fired directly at him — on video, police can be heard boasting about blinding protesters.

Elsewhere, multiple students suffered severe eye injuries. A viral video captured an officer pinning a young girl in a violent chokehold, while in Lens, a bystander schoolchild lost a hand to an exploding crowd-dispersal grenade (he did not “pick it up” as the media have claimed).

In a further attempt to intimidate, more than 5000 young people have been arrested — only 1800 were subsequently charged with an offence. Even now, the government refuses to rein in the police thugs. Interior minister Laurent Nuñez spoke on October 6 of “supposed excesses” in police action, while former minister Bruno Retailleau demanded loudly that the age of criminal responsibility be lowered.

Secondly, the government has offered tiny concessions, which are only cosmetic. Proposals to hike some higher education tuition fees were abruptly shelved, and school student union leaders have been invited to talks with the education minister. The regime has also launched a token online portal for grievances and they have scheduled managed "consultation sessions" in all schools for the end of the week.

Finally, a propaganda offensive is trying to paint the young people as manipulated by the radical left organisation la France Insoumise (France in Revolt, FI). The old lie of “outside agitators” is being mobilised, because the FI is playing an excellent role in the movement.

Even previously sceptical far-left commentators have written that the young protestors consider the FI to be their party. Its leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon insisted that FI Members of Parliament and local elected councillors position themselves between the police and students to help protect them. All of them were present and vocal in denouncing police violence.

In parliament, Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said one could not speak of “police violence” and complained that the FI “were implying that the police forces of the Republic … were racist”!

School student leaders are not fooled by the cosmetic concessions, and are showing their confidence by announcing a new day of action, only two days after the previous one. Trade union leaders could learn from the youngsters, but are dragging their feet, suggesting a strike in November.

The establishment media are working hard at slandering the movement and twisting the truth.

Media watchdog, Acrimed, measured the time spent discussing the events on the prime-time national public news channel, France 2, this week. It found that 75% of the time was spent speaking about the alleged damage caused by the protesters, 8% spent on the movement’s demands and 12% on government accusations of FI manipulation.

This uprising is taking place against a backdrop of severe political polarisation, ahead of next May’s presidential election. Polls show the fascist candidate, Marine Le Pen leading the field, with FI candidate Mélenchon running second.

The prominence of antifascist placards and banners across student marches reflects the fact that young people recognise that their struggle against austerity and police violence is directly linked to the broader fight against the far right.

The most recent opinion polls show that 62% of the population support the school students’ movement. The next week will show whether much-needed escalation will come.

[John Mullen is a Marxist activist living in the Paris area and a supporter of the France Insoumise. Visit his website at randombolshevik.org.]

title: Comunidad Temulemu vuelve a la Corte Interamericana de Derechos Humanos por el caso de su werken Rafael Pichun Collonao
content:
La comunidad Temulemu interpondrá una demanda ante la Comisión Interamericana de Derechos Humanos, por el caso de su werken Rafael Pichun Collonao, privado de libertad en la cárcel de Angol desde abril del 2024, condenado a 7 y 8 años de cárcel por su supuesta “participación organizativa” en el llamado caso Quilleco.




Según el Lonco Juan Pichun, el estado de Chile vulnera su propia legislación y lo que hoy vive su hermano Rafael repite lo que vivió su padre en la CIDH por el caso lonkos, en el año 2013:







“Hoy en día no sólo se vulneran los derechos Mapuches, el mismo estado a través de los poderes judiciales, a través de los persecutores, están vulnerando los mismos derechos que el estado ha impulsado y legislado, y en ese marco creemos que es importante llevar el caso de Rafael como un caso donde se vulneran varios derechos, como por ejemplo los derechos a la defensa, con el uso de testigos secretos, sin rostro.










Es una discriminación por parte del estado, dentro de sus mismos contextos jurídicos, ellos mismos han vulnerado su propia legislación.










Esta es la segunda vez que llevaremos un caso de la familia a un contexto internacional. Ya el estado de Chile fue condenado, y Rafael es parte de ese fallo de la CIDH, en el llamado caso lonkos, donde mi padre pudo lograr su inocencia a través de este tribunal internacional y eso mismo queremos acreditar, que en la acusación que le hacen a Rafael se vulneran también los derechos a una defensa”.







El werken rafael Pichun fue condenado en el denominado caso Quilleco, proceso judicial donde se presentó como única prueba un mensaje de whatsapp que el Werkén recibe, lo que la comunidad y los abogados defensores consideran insuficiente para mantenerlo hoy en la cárcel.




“Si hoy día ponemos a un Mapuche y a un no Mapuche en las mismas condiciones, en un mismo juicio, el que no es mapuche va a salir libre y nuestra gente va a ser condenada a una alta condena”.

author: cnt.es
title: El sindicato de inquilinas consigue una confluencia sindical histórica
content:
«

Ha sido una reunión histórica

». Así ha calificado Nieves Román, secretaria general de la CNT, la asamblea celebrada este miércoles, 7 de octubre, entre los sindicatos de toda la geografía nacional. Sindicatos como CNT, CGT, Solidaridad Obrera, LAB, CCOO, UGT, Co.bas, Confederación Intersindical, Intersindical Alternativa de Catalunya, Intersindical Valenciana, o la Unión de actores y actrices han confluido ante el llamamiento del Sindicato de Inquilinas para la organización de «una huelga general de verdad, en la que se detenga la producción y lo paremos todo».




Las reivindicaciones de la huelga general pasan por «

obtener reformas avanzadas en favor de la clase trabajadora con respecto al problema de la vivienda

» y «

abrir un nuevo período de luchas de cara a los próximos meses y años, con el sindicalismo en el centro y con capacidad de frenar a la reacción

». La decisión de la fecha para la huelga, 11 de noviembre como proponían Inquilinas, fue celebrada con aplausos por las personas asistentes. Lamentablemente, momentos después contrastó con la triste noticia del fallecimiento de Mari Carmen, apoyada por el Sindicato de Inquilinas y personalmente por algunas de las personas asistentes al acto.




«

Podríamos decir que nunca se celebró una cumbre como ésta

»- nos confirma el historiador Juan Pablo Calero. «

Podemos congratularnos de estar más cerca de conseguir una unidad más amplia del movimiento obrero. Queremos que el sindicalismo llegue a todos los sectores, incluyendo juventud, población migrante y otros que tradicionalmente han estado oprimidos.

» – ha señalado Román.




El sindicato CNT se encuentra actualmente manteniendo reuniones, tanto a nivel interno como externo, para la preparación de la huelga, y, previsiblemente, la anunciará en unos días. «

Tenemos que medir muy bien el encaje legal, contactar con otras organizaciones y, lo más importante, consultar a nuestras bases y tomar una decisión democrática, como mandan nuestros principios anarcosindicalistas

» – concluyó Román.

El sindicato de inquilinas consigue una confluencia sindical histórica

Confederación Nacional del Trabajo

author: ABC-Belarus
title: The reality of released Belarusian anarchist prisoners: Why our support doesn’t stop at prison doorstep
content:
In the last two years, quite a few of our comrades left prison: some after completing their sentences, others were released as a result of pardons negotiated between the dictator and US diplomats in exchange of easing sanctions. We are preparing a longer analysis on this kind of trading and how it enables dictatorship, but today, we wanted to focus on what awaits released political prisoners on the outside and why they need even more support than before.

As a reminder, all imprisoned anarchists are put on a list of extremists and some additionally end up on the terrorist list. What is means is that once they are released in Belarus, they can’t open a bank account, can’t register a phone number, can’t register as self-employed. Of course, most employers would refuse hiring them as they can’t even transfer salary to the ex-prisoner, saying nothing of them being scared of engaging with an “extremist”. People on the extremist list can’t engage in publishing activity or teaching. Combined, this effectively pushes the released to the grey economy zone and makes them dependent on external support.

Moreover, every released person usually falls under police supervision for a period of up to 2 years. This means they have to check-in with local police weekly, be at home at specified hours, ask for permission to leave town and can’t leave the country. Most ex-prisoners feel like they were just moved to a prison with a milder security and prefer to move abroad illegally, meaning they then have a criminal case opened in Belarus resulting from violation of the supervision.

In the last two years, about 850 prisoners have been released on pardon, many of them were expelled from Belarus right from prison and ended up in Lithuania, Poland and Ukraine. These people don’t have their passports, so they need to ask for international protection or a similar humanitarian status. While they are waiting for decision, they can’t work, travel but need to be able to pay the rent and support themselves. The majority of ex-prisoners don’t speak the language of the host country or English, which limits their employment opportunities. Many experience depression and anxiety over losing access to homeland and family, the need to start from scratch in an unfamiliar place, and PTSD resulting from years of isolation. According to our in-depth interviews with released comrades, it takes over a year to regain the agency and become more independent in a new country.

There are multiple organisations and projects that try to meet the most urgent needs of the expelled prisoners. We at ABC Belarus also assign a part of our budget to the immediate or ongoing support of the ex-prisoners. Your donations are greatly appreciated and can be made at abc-belarus.org/donate

Garstka przestraszonych chłopaczków, wspierana przez kilku napinaczy jest dowodem na to, że hasła “White power” są cały czas obecne w publicznej przestrzeni.




I, mimo że wykrzykuje je banda sfrustrowanych neonazistów, to nie możemy zapominać, że są oni użytecznym narzędziem w ręku władzy, antagonizującym społeczeństwo. Społeczeństwo, które ma uwierzyć w to, iż osoby z doświadczeniem migracji są realnym zagrożeniem dla naszej pracy, dla marnej polityki socjalnej, zaś każda osoba w drodze stanowi bezpośrednie ryzyko dla naszego życia i bezpieczeństwa.




Skrajna prawica buduje swój kapitał polityczny na strachu i ten strach chciały narzucić nam osoby “kontrmanifestujące”. Oczywiście bezskutecznie – ponieważ demonstracja ruszyła i nie daliśmy się zablokować!













Idąc ulicami Torunia, w obecności Samba Rythms of Resistance, kierowaliśmy do mieszkańców i mieszkanek przekaz “Mamy tylko siebie, tu nie ważne są korzenie” “Bez granic, bez nacji, stop deportacji” “Solidarność naszą bronią” “Otwarte serca, otwarte granice”. 







Jako ruch anarchistyczny sprzeciwiamy się dzieleniu ludzi na równych i równiejszych, sprzeciwiamy się tworzeniu gett dla osób innego pochodzenia, sprzeciwiamy się ograniczaniu swobody przemieszczania się i dostępu do rynku pracy, sprzeciwiamy się traktowaniu osób migrujących jako tanią siłę roboczą, która zdana jest na łaskę barbarzyńskich agencji pracy!













Demonstracja zakończyła się w Forcie Jakuba gdzie odbył się koncert zaangażowanego HH:




Profesor Ulicy, NMCP, Erick Havok oraz punkowa załoga z Torunia z trąbką – 8Kaw.













Zarówno sobotnia demonstracja jak i cała Kampania są dowodem na to, że nasza siła tkwi we wspólnocie, kulturze oporu i pomocy wzajemnej. Pokazaliśmy i pokazałyśmy, że na próby siania nienawiści odpowiadamy jeszcze donośniejszym głosem sprzeciwu.













Nasze ulice pozostaną wolne od ksenofobii, dopóki będziemy tworzyć je razem!










Do zobaczenia na kolejnych akcjach.







Nasze ulice – wasze granice!




#naszeulicewaszegranice







Artykuł 

Relacja z demonstracji w Toruniu – Nasze ulice, wasze granice!

 pochodzi z serwisu 

FEDERACJA ANARCHISTYCZNA - wolność, równość, pomoc wzajemna

title: MKG: Di Îlonê de 2 rojnamegerên jin hatin girtin û 3 jî hatin desteserkirin
content:
Komeleya Rojnamegerên Jin a Mezopotamyayê (MKG) rapora xwe ya binpêkirina mafên jinên rojnameger a meha Îlona 2026an aşkere kir.




MKGê, di raporê de bal kişand ser astengiyên li qadê, şert û mercên xebatê yên ji bo rojnamegerên jin û sansura li ser çapemeniyê.




MKGê diyar kir ku di meha Îlonê de zext bi awayên cûr bi cûr li ser rojnamegerên jin berdewam kirin û wiha got: 







“Lêpirsîn û dozên li dijî çalakiyên rojnamegeriyê, astengiyên li pêşiya nûçeyan, binçavkirin û girtin, gef û êrîş û sansura dîjîtal qada xebatê ji bo rojnamegeran teng kir. Geşedanên di tevahiya mehê de nîşan dan, raporên nûçeyan û çalakiyên rojnamegeriyê wekî bingehek ji bo tawanbarkirinê têne bikaranîn. Darizandinên bi salane berdewam dikin, dozên nû tên vekirin û berdewama biryarên girtinê nîşan dide ku zexta darazê ya li ser rojnamegeran domdar bûye. Astengiyên li qadê şert û mercên xebatê ji bo rojnamegeran jî dijwar kirin. Destwerdana li ser nûçeyan, dûrxistina rojnamegeran a ji qadê, gef û êrîşan nîşan dan ku gihiştina nûçeyan her diçe bi sînordar dibe. Di meha Îlonê de, qada dîjîtal jî yek ji wan deveran bû ku zext lê zêde bûn. Xwegihandina platformên medya dîjîtal ên gelek koman, rojnameger, sazî û dezgehên medyayê, rêxistinên jinan û parêzvanên mafên mirovan, hate astengkirin. Bi vê yekê di heman demê de xwegihandina raya giştî ya dezgehên agahdariyê jî hatin sînordarkirin.”







“Divê astengiyên li pêşiya rojnamegeran werin rakirin”




MKGê di berdewamiya raporê de bi lêv kir ku zextên li ser rojnamegeran li cihên kar jî berdewam kir. MKGê da zanîn ku ji kar derxistin, mobîng û şert û mercên bêewle zêde bûne û hebûna jinan a di qada çapemeniyê de zehmet bûye û wiha hate gotin: 







“Bûyerên meha Îlonê nîşan didin ku dema rojnameger nûçeyan çêdikin, li qadê dixebitin, di pêvajoyên darazê de û li qada dîjîtal di bin zextê de ne. Binpêkirinên mafên mirovan ên li dijî rojnamegeran nikarin ji azadiya çapemeniyê û mafê raya giştî yê agahdarkirinê cûdatir bên nirxandin. Divê darizandin û çavtirsandina rojnamegeran a ji ber çalakiyên wan ên pîşeyî, astengkirina weşana nûçeyên wan û girtina platformên wan ên dîjîtal bi dawî bibe. Divê rojnamegerên girtî werin berdan û hemû astengiyên li pêşiya xebatên rojnamegeran werin rakirin.”







Daneyên Rapora Binpêkirina Mafên Jinên Rojnameger a Îlona 2026an ev in:







Rojnamegerên êriş li wan hatine kirin: 3

Rojnamegerên bi ser mala wan de hat girtin: 2

Rojnamegerên hatin binçavkirin: 3

Rojnamegerên hatin girtin: 2

Rojnamegerên bi muameleya ne baş rû bi rû man: 1

Rojnamegerên gef li wan hat xwarin: 1

Rojnamegerên şopandina nûçeyan wan hatin astengkirin: 3

Binpêkirina mafên rojnamegeran ên li girtîgehan: 1




Binpêkirina maf û azadiya ramanê ya rojnamegeran




Rojnamegerên derbarê wan de doz hat vekirin: 3

Rojnamegerên hatin cezakirin: 2

Cezayê hepsê: 6 sal û 5 meh 24 roj

Rojnamegerên darizandina wan didomin: Hejmara dosyayê 14

Hejmara kesan 36

Hejmara rojnamegrên girtî: (Ji 1ê Îlona 2026an heta niha) 9




Binpêkirina mafên aborî/civakî ya jinên rojnameger




Rojnamegerên karê wan hatin bidawîkirin: 3




Astengiyên li ser înternet/medyaya dîjîtal




Sîteyên hatine girtin: 4

Platfromên Medyaya Dîjîtal ên Hatine Astengkirin: Herî kêm 810

Nûçeyên hatine astengkirin: 15




Lîsteya rojnamegerên girtî:




1. Derya Okatan – Rojnameger




2. Hatice Duman – Midûra Karên Nivîsê û Xwediya Rojnameya Atilimê




3. Nadiye Gurbuz – Edîtora Ajansa Nûçeyan a Etkînê (ETHA)




4. Ozden Kinik – Xebatkara TRTyê




5. Oya Lale Ozan Arslan – Rojnameger




6. Yelis Ayaz – Xwediya Sîteya Înternetê ya Aydinpostê




7. Songul Yucel – Gerînendeya Weşana Giştî ya Kovara Onsozê




8. Fatma Sibel Gurcihan – Rojnameger




9. Îrem Delice – Nûçegîhana Rojnameya Dengeyê ya Aydinê




10. Tugba Tekerek – Rojnameger







Her weha di nava meha îlonê de Pinar Gayip û Elif Bayburt tehliye bûn, Oya Lale Ozan Arslan, Tugba Tekerek jî hatin girtin. Derya Okatan jî di 2ê Cotmehê de hate girtin.

title: EDRi-gram, 8 October 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Turning up the heat – Commission backs social media bans, Apple held accountable, summer to-dos, & more!

This EDRi-gram edition includes a real snapshot of the disconnect between the kind of technology and protections people and communities around the world need, and the kind that are being pushed at us by lawmakers and companies either for the sake of profits, as easy fixes to structural societal issues or more sinister reasons.

Take the EU’s recently announced KIDS ACT. We unpack the many shortcomings of the proposal which is a missed opportunity to address the root cause of why online platforms are harmful to children – and everyone else. We also look at the Cloud and AI Development (CADA) Act, a part of the EU’s Tech Sovereignty Package announced earlier this year. What was sold as a way to jumpstart the EU’s “sovereign AI” ambitions seems to be set to hurt digital rights and environmental protections instead, while also imposing an unreliable technology onto us.

Elsewhere, Austria will soon get to find out what happens when AI systems are allowed to issue legally binding government decisions without any human oversight. EDRi-member epicenter.works detail the draft proposal and all the ways it could backfire.

None of the above is without resistance from those of us working to protect your rights. Dutch EDRi-member Bits of Freedom have launched a new campaign demanding a ban on Meta’s “pervert glasses”, aka, AI glasses which can be used to film people without them knowing. Meta was clearly paying attention – their viral satirical video on these glasses was removed from Instagram.

From critical campaigns, and urging EU countries to not treat data protection and “competitiveness” as opposing goals as they discuss the Digital Omnibus, to legal action against Big Tech corporations preying on our minds – we’re fighting back.

Next week, at our flagship annual event #PrivacyCamp26, we’ll be asking the real questions – where does technology come from? Who shapes it? And what would self-determination look like if it were defined by the people, not dictated by profits or a state’s agenda? We hope to see some of you attending!

author: bert
title: Konto bleibt: Rote Hilfe gewinnt Hauptsacheverfahren
content:
Konto bleibt: Rote Hilfe gewinnt Hauptsacheverfahren




Die Rote Hilfe 

e. V.

 hat heute auch das Hauptsacheverfahren gegen die Sparkasse Göttingen gewonnen. Das Landgericht Göttingen hat entschieden, dass die Kündigung des Kontos der bundesweiten linken Solidaritätsorganisation vom 9. Dezember 2025 keinen Bestand hat.

Bereits im Eilverfahren war die Sparkasse gescheitert. Darin 

verpflichtete zunächst das Landgericht die Sparkasse das Konto weiterzuführen

. Im Anschluss stellte das Oberlandesgericht Braunschweig fest, dass eine öffentlich-rechtliche Sparkasse ein Konto nicht ohne sachlichen Grund kündigen darf. Die von der Sparkasse vorgebrachten Gründe, dass ein erhöhter Prüfaufwand bestehe und ein Reputationsschaden bei Führung des Kontos des antifaschistischen Vereins bestehe, überzeugten das Gericht nicht.

Ein zusätzliches Risiko durch die 

US

-Listung der sogenannten „Antifa Ost“ als Terrororganisation  konnte die Sparkasse nicht plausibel machen. Das 

OLG

 stellte zudem klar, dass die Rote Hilfe nicht eine Organisation „Antifa Ost“ finanziert, sondern gemäß ihrer Satzung Beschuldigte und Angeklagte in den entsprechenden Verfahren unterstützt. Die 

US

-Einstufung selbst entfaltet keine unmittelbare rechtliche Wirkung in Deutschland. Dieser Beurteilung des 

OLG

 schloss sich das Landgericht heute »vollumfänglich« an.

Damit hat die Rote Hilfe nach den Erfolgen im Eilverfahren nun auch in der Hauptsache Recht bekommen.

Für die Rote Hilfe geht es über den eigenen Fall hinaus auch um die Frage, wie weit politische Entscheidungen und Sanktionslisten aus Drittstaaten auf zivilgesellschaftliche Strukturen in Deutschland durchschlagen können.

Hartmut Brückner vom Bundesvorstand der Roten Hilfe 

e. V.

, erklärt: „Das ist ein wichtiger Erfolg für die Rote Hilfe und für alle, die sich gegen politisch motiviertes Debanking wehren. Einer Organisation die finanzielle Infrastruktur zu entziehen kann ihre Arbeit faktisch lahmlegen. Genau deshalb war es notwendig, diese Kündigung nicht einfach hinzunehmen.«

Brückner weiter: „Besonders problematisch bleibt, dass politische Entscheidungen und Sanktionslisten aus den 

USA

 überhaupt solchen Druck auf zivilgesellschaftliche Strukturen in Deutschland entfalten können. Solidaritätsarbeit für Beschuldigte und Angeklagte ist keine verdächtige oder illegale Tätigkeit. Das Recht auf Verteidigung und ein faires Verfahren muss auch und gerade dann gelten, wenn Verfahren politisch aufgeladen sind.“

Die Rote Hilfe dankt der Gesellschaft für Freiheitsrechte, den beteiligten Anwält*innen, dem Netzwerk Debanking Stoppen und allen Menschen, die den Verein seit Bekanntwerden der Kontokündigung solidarisch unterstützt haben.
