author: Unknown
title: Once again on Kurdish democratic unity
content:
The creation of Kurdish democratic unity continues to be a matter of urgent importance. The stage reached by the Third World War, which is spreading and deepening across the Middle East, makes this an immediate necessity. The process initiated by Abdullah Öcalan’s Call for Peace and Democratic Society on 27 February 2025 has made Kurdish democratic unity an urgent task.




Although some collaborationist-nationalist circles continue to create obstacles, the forces supporting national democratic unity are growing by the day. Kurdish intellectuals and politicians are placing greater emphasis on democratic unity than ever before. Politicians are speaking about democratic unity, while intellectuals are writing about it. There is a demand both for unity and for that unity to be democratic, because the Kurds need both unity and democracy. At present, there is neither sufficient national unity nor sufficient democracy. Yet developments in the region and the struggle in Kurdistan need democratic unity more than bread and water.




The stage reached by the Third World War in the region is creating both significant opportunities for the Kurds and very serious dangers. To seize these opportunities and avert these dangers, the Kurds need to unite and develop their democracy. With Kurdish politics fragmented, lacking unity and democracy, it does not appear possible to seize these opportunities or avert the dangers. Almost everyone now sees and expresses this. More importantly, all of us have a responsibility to fulfil such a task for the success of the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated and led by Abdullah Öcalan.




The process initiated by the Call for Peace and Democratic Society on 27 February 2025 is clearly pushing both the Kurds and Turkey as a whole, including the state and society, towards change and democratization. The steps taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement in this direction are prompting everyone to reassess their current position and move towards democratic change and transformation. This is undoubtedly not easy in one respect; it requires greater courage and sacrifice, as well as more courageous criticism and self-criticism. In another respect, it places new and greater responsibilities before everyone, requiring a more organized and creative struggle. The tasks of the new process cannot be accomplished through the fragmented, excessively centralized approaches and structures of the past that placed only one’s own party at the centre. In short, the Peace and Democratic Society Process is compelling all Kurds to create democratic unity.




The approach of the Turkish side, namely the state and the government, to the Peace and Democratic Society Process makes Kurdish democratic unity even more important and urgent. For example, the final statement issued after the National Security Council meeting on 30 September clearly shows that there is nothing new on the Turkish side. In both content and tone, the statement is identical to National Security Council statements from two years ago. Despite a new process having been underway in Turkey for two years, it still refers to the “Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK)-Kurdistan Communities Union (KCK) terrorist organization” and places it in the same category as ISIS. Naturally, when the National Security Council uses such language, the special warfare media uses the same language and content. But what will happen if the Kurdish side and Kurdish media also continue to speak of the “fascist Turkish Republic”? The National Security Council statement is entirely anti-Kurdish and makes the elimination of Kurdish gains and Kurdish existence a central political objective. What, then, remains of the discourse of Turkish-Kurdish brotherhood?




The final statement of the National Security Council meeting on 30 September makes it very clear that there has been no change in the anti-Kurdish mentality and policies of the Republic of Turkey. With the state maintaining this position, the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government is also implementing the same mentality and policies on a daily basis. In this context, we should look at what the AKP government is doing. Has there been any democratic change compared with two years ago? Not only is it clear that there has been no such change, but it can even be said that repression and exploitation have increased. Most importantly, there has been no change in the conditions of Abdullah Öcalan. Even the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) delegation is unable to visit as frequently as it did last year, and the isolation on Imrali essentially continues.




The AKP government continues to disregard law and legal norms. Pressure and manoeuvres against political activity continue in an effort to leave no alternative. New detention operations targeting opposition parties are carried out every day. The appointment of trustees to municipalities continues. Prisons are overcrowded, and dozens of prisoners who have completed 30 years, and in some cases as many as 35 years, are being arbitrarily held in prison as hostages. Every day, another “unsolved murder” case is allowed to expire under the statute of limitations. Hunger and poverty have reached extreme levels, with people living below the hunger threshold. A full-fledged police state and special warfare system prevails; protests against the government cannot be held, and even criticism of the government is not tolerated. Violence and killings targeting women continue to increase.




Such practices are undoubtedly too numerous to list. The situation has reached a point where people cannot even bear to watch television news bulletins. Those with marginalized identities naturally face the harshest repression and persecution, with Kurds foremost among them. Some officials repeatedly speak of the process and brotherhood, yet the special warfare attacks against Kurds continue unabated. Kurdish families cannot even find the bodies of their children who lost their lives in the war. Could there be anything more painful than this?




The Kurdish side, however, has fulfilled the requirements of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Mustafa Karasu, one of the spokespersons of the Kurdish Freedom Movement, clearly expressed this during a special programme broadcast on Medya Haber TV on the evening of 5 October. He said that disarmament with regard to Turkey had been carried out and that there were no longer any weapons posing a threat to Turkey. Despite this, the Turkish state and the AKP government continue their anti-Kurdish policies and practices. Anti-Kurdish policies and efforts to eliminate Kurdish gains, for example, remain at the centre of their policies towards Syria, Iraq and Iran. Their sole objective in relations with these states is to dismantle and eliminate existing Kurdish organizations. Turkish diplomacy operates on this basis towards Rojava, Shengal, Southern Kurdistan (Başur) and Eastern Kurdistan (Rojhilat).




Deceptive statements and false claims on this issue should not be believed. In reality, a policy aimed at eliminating Kurdish gains and existence is being pursued. The failure to take the steps required by the process in Northern Kurdistan (Bakur), the efforts to completely eliminate the gains in Rojava and the pressure placed on the Iraqi government over Shengal are all manifestations of this policy. This is also the main policy threatening the existence and security of Southern Kurdistan. Politicians from Southern Kurdistan, including Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) President Masoud Barzani, have said that “the withdrawal of US military forces is putting our security at risk.” If that is the case, what should be done? First of all, the connection between this situation and Turkey must be clearly understood. Second, rather than relying on the United States or any other power, Kurds must trust and rely on their own strength. It is clear that this strength lies in Kurdish democratic unity.




The mentality and policies of the Turkish Republic that deny Kurdish existence and envisage its elimination continue to pose the greatest threat and danger to all Kurds. How, then, can this danger be averted? Clearly, by uniting and creating Kurdish democratic unity; by organizing a democratic unity that encompasses all Kurds in every region, including Southern Kurdistan. This is how the opportunities created by current developments can be seized and how the dangers arising from those developments can be averted. Democratic unity is the only solution. History will never forgive those who stand in its way.




Source: Yeni Özgür Politika

author: Unknown
title: Çetintepe: Constitutional Court ruling may leave women more helpless
content:
The Constitutional Court annulled on 4 June 2026 the provision in Article 175 of the Turkish Civil Code that allowed a spouse who would fall into poverty as a result of divorce to claim alimony from the other spouse “indefinitely,” finding it unconstitutional. The reasoning for the annulment was published in the Official Gazette on 30 September. The ruling will take effect nine months later, on 30 June 2027.




Gamze Çetintepe of the Women’s Defence Network spoke to ANF about the Constitutional Court’s ruling and drew attention to how the reasoning portrays men who pay alimony as “victims.” Çetintepe said women’s acquired rights were being taken away and women’s labour was being rendered invisible.




Çetintepe said the ruling was based on a narrative suggesting that women were trying to “take away” something that rightfully belonged to men and that this created a grievance for men.




Çetintepe described the ruling as part of propaganda aimed at trapping women in families marked by exploitation and violence, in line with the “Decade of the Family” policies of making divorce more difficult, encouraging marriage and increasing birth rates. She said the reasoning behind the ruling states:“The reasoning states: ‘Due to the contested provision, the obligation to pay poverty alimony may continue until the end of a person’s life, which could prevent that person from remarrying, acquiring property and providing for future children, and therefore the provision imposes a disproportionate restriction on the person’s right to respect for private and family life and their right to property…’




The so-called disproportionate restriction is alimony averaging 2,000 lira a month. If there is to be a debate about alimony, it should be about why it is so inadequate and why it fails to prevent women from falling into poverty after divorce.”




‘Women are forced to give up even their existing rights’




Çetintepe said the reality of how alimony works in practice is very different from the picture presented by the ruling. She said, “Apart from the inadequacy of alimony payments, it is also very common for even these amounts not to be paid, or for men to tell women, ‘If you don’t ask for alimony, I won’t cause trouble and I’ll agree to the divorce,’ forcing women to give up even their existing rights so that they can escape households of exploitation and violence as quickly as possible.”




Çetintepe said that many men also fail to pay child support, the financial contribution paid by the parent who does not have custody to cover expenses such as the child’s care, education, healthcare and housing in proportion to their financial means.




Çetintepe said, “Many men do not even pay the child support they are required to provide for the care of their children, continuing to place the burden of shared responsibilities on women even after the marriage ends. The same concern shown for men’s private lives and their ability to acquire property is not shown when it comes to monitoring whether the alimony women are entitled to receive is actually paid and ensuring that those payments are made.”




‘Men’s “victimhood” is that they can no longer exploit women’




Çetintepe said the law approaches marriage and divorce in a way that disregards women’s unpaid labour and is implemented in a misogynistic manner. She explained the actual purpose of the ruling and its possible impact on divorce rates as follows: “If women are nevertheless divorcing at increasingly higher rates, it may not be accurate to say that this ruling will change that. But that is certainly the intention. What they call men’s victimhood is precisely this: that they can no longer exploit women.




Still, if we consider this ruling together with all the pro-family policies of which it is a part, as well as the country’s deepening poverty and persistent sexism, it could make women feel more helpless about how they would survive on their own if they divorced.”




‘Women are expected to find work while caring for their children alone’




Asked about claims that ending alimony after a certain period would encourage women to enter the workforce, Çetintepe described this discourse as another part of the propaganda portraying men as victims of women. She explained why women fall into poverty after divorce: “It is not because women can live on monthly alimony payments of 2,000 lira that they do not take paid jobs. The reason women fall into poverty after marriage is the exploitation of their paid and unpaid labour, yet this discourse seeks to conceal that reality and blame women. Women are unable to take paid jobs, or work in flexible, part-time and insecure jobs, so that they can provide years of unpaid labour within marriage.




After divorce, women who have been unable to work full-time for years are expected to find jobs that will support both themselves and their children while caring for their children alone, as though there were no unemployment in the country and no sexism in recruitment, workplaces or wages.”




‘Restricting alimony is not the way to bring women into employment’




Çetintepe stressed that restricting women’s alimony is not the way to increase women’s participation in employment: “Women’s participation in employment cannot be achieved by restricting alimony. It can be achieved by ensuring that girls continue their education instead of being married off, promoting an equal division of labour within marriage instead of unpaid labour, adopting policies to prevent sexism in employment and wage inequality instead of viewing women as servants whose role is to give birth to and care for children, and ensuring that women do not become afraid even to leave their homes because of death threats from their former husbands after divorce or get killed despite having protection orders.”




Çetintepe said, “We see the hostility that is trying to strip us of all our rights step by step,” and adding: “We will continue to struggle against attacks that seek to oppress women and LGBTI+ people in the name of ‘protecting the family’ and confine our lives within patriarchal structures and norms.”

content:

author: Kalundi Serumaga
title: As Long as You Don’t Say Nothing, You Can Say Anything at All
content:
In Uganda, censorship is a reality, and in fact, a governance necessity. Once those governing us came to the realization that they cannot give the population what it needs, either because they don’t want to, or because they are not able, then they have got to try to stop the conversation about governing. Why permit or encourage talk about something you know is not going to change? Why raise hope?




That becomes step one, the usual result of which is to then see the discourse migrate to creative spaces, where it operates in a much more multi-layered and subliminal way. This requires a different kind of management of that arts scene, as step two.




With political censorship, matters have been very clear for some time now. Vocal activists who say things that those in power find offensive now have a standard playbook against them. They get barred from as many media outlets as they can. In extreme cases, landlords can be persuaded to evict them from their homes and business premises. Media houses themselves can be banned, or their troublesome journalists harassed or dismissed. There have been reports of even the tax authorities being sent after the records of businesses owned by such critics. Social media influencers are brought on board to cast the predictable aspersions.




Social media platforms themselves can be shut down as a whole. During the contentious 2021 general election, there was a shutdown across the board. Up to today, Facebook remains banned. Then there are the abductions.




This is not to say it comes easy. The human is designed to see, reflect and speak. So political censorship has it challenges. Recently, some laws seeking to make digital democracy more punishable were thwarted. But in the end, it gets done. Of late, there has been a steady stream of convictions of simple users of X (formerly Twitter) for making posts critical of important government figures. The longest sentence has been six years for the offence of insulting the president via TikTok.




The arts are a different kind of problem, requiring a different set of tools. Art is nebulous. It defies time and form. The key thing to understand is that there is a difference between freedom of speech, and freedom of expression. The Uganda arts sector has suffered over a two decades of deliberate sabotage in my view, and this is why I argue that arts censorship has thus been historically approached in a structural way.




In terms of practical implementation of immediate measures, the lines between politics, art, media and morality are very blurred. Many personalities wear more than one hat, with prominent journalists also being politicians, musicians being opinion leaders, and politicians becoming entertainers.




So the goal has been to create an entirely plastic and artificial practice of noisy, energetic, colourful, but ultimately very hollow forms of “African” expression.




This is actually the best form of arts censorship; creative voices must be monitored, and then led astray.




The transformation of the singer Bobi Wine into the major opposition politician known as Robert Kyagulanyi was not the origin of this process, but became the occasion for its intensification.




There had been other political musicians, like Ronald Mayinja whose themes had become a source of quiet nervousness among the authorities. Various theories exist as to how he vanished from prominence, amid a flurry of mixed messaging.




The closest analogy I can think of is the analyses I have seen by and about certain pioneers of old-school Hip Hop in the United States, such as Wise Intelligent, KRS-One, Chuck D and others, who say that the art form was hijacked.




Citing examples from original rap groups such as Roc Nation, they argue that the wider American power structure and society became worried about the political impact of rap music due to its articulation of Black political concerns about racism, imperialism, and poverty. 




They say that the strategic response to this was to encourage the emergence of a new kind of Hip Hop practice, which was mainstreamed and made the dominant and more accessible kind. This was done through the manipulation and encouragement of entertainers more concerned with hedonistic themes in the way those in charge of the major recording companies signed up, curated, distributed and marketed them. The result is largely what became known as “Gangsta Rap”. 




They argue that this process was aimed at depoliticizing, or corrupting a valid art form with the purpose of derailing the radicalizing effect it was having on a new generation of, especially, Black American youth.




My title phrase, “As long as you don’t say nothing, you can say anything at all,” is an American expression (possibly from the singer Bob Dylan) to reflect this. 




Apart from the usual lack of funding and deliberate appointment of unskilled people to manage the lead state institutions, censorship has also been done through the building of ignorance and falsehoods into our cultural discourse and historical memory. Because in the end, the absolutely certain way to ensure that people do not talk about the things that matter is to not let them know of the existence of those things to begin with. Or, failing that, not know about their significance in the wider scheme of things. Ignorance is a pre-emption. Co-option is a method.




Freedom of artistic expression in Uganda therefore depends on who the particular artist is, and what they are expressing. Some are extremely free; others are silenced. 




My last personal experience of censorship was when I was asked to direct the one-man play 

For My Negativity,

 written and performed by Kgayi Ngobi, during the 2022 edition of the Kampala International Theatre Festival. Ngobi is a well-known performance poet with a number of works that excoriate the way we live now and the role of the government in creating it. I, for my part,  just seem stuck with a name that appears on many an official blacklist going all the way back to 2009. Various stratagems were brought into effect to discourage either the venue, or the festival owners, or the festival sponsors from staging the play. In the end, and with not a little irony, it was the decision of the ambassador of one of the European Union countries that was among the event sponsors to be physically present at the performance that seemed to have kept at bay the scores of not very well-disguised undercover intelligence cops mobilized to the venue. 




The emergence of Bobi Wine into political visibility led the regime and its associates to seek to build a counter-industry to match his youth appeal. For a while, this literally created a busy marketplace among the creatives in which singers, in the main, chose which side they would sing for, or switch to. Concerts and counter-concerts, songs and counter-songs, and imagery and counter-imagery became the order of the day. 




New bodies were hurriedly set up to “represent” these wiser artists, and at least one was granted office space at the National Cultural Centre. Some singers were even officially appointed “Presidential Advisors”.




So the real censorship has been strategic and structural. This is actually very wise. Because a “fire-fighting” approach is much costlier, destabilizing, and does not cover as many targets.




It has also been long-standing. Uganda, a country of fifty million people, has one public-owned art gallery and one public-owned theatre, both of which are based in the capital, with no real upcountry sites. This builds exclusion and discourages innovation. Arts programmes are essentially driven by some schools, or by embassies and their cultural institutes.




Whatever other facilities do exist are essentially private enterprises set up by heroic and dedicated individuals. Access and exposure require money. The various national awards that were given out for the arts basically no longer exist. The only exception is a “national” film award, which is owned and managed by the Uganda Communications Commission. And that was largely to do to the film sector what the other initiatives have done to the music sector, at least.




But we persist. We will still talk.




The post 

As Long as You Don’t Say Nothing, You Can Say Anything at All

 first appeared on 

The Elephant

.

author: Yuanyi Tham
title: Mega Anthropic data centre to blight Queensland
content:
Queensland is set to become home to Australia’s largest AI data centre. Last month, Liberal National Party Premier David Crisafulli announced a landmark deal with Anthropic to develop the Western Downs Digital Park, near the town of Dalby, about 250 kilometres northwest of Brisbane. Led by Singaporean developer Zerra DC, the site will be constructed in four phases, with the first building expected to be operational next year.

The data centre will occupy 725.5 hectares, an area twice the size of New York’s Central Park. Its estimated value is $32 billion, nearly five times the 2032 Brisbane Olympics infrastructure budget.

Data centres suck up huge amounts of power, driving up energy prices and accelerating climate change. When fully constructed, electro-mechanical engineer Dr Andreas Helwig told the ABC it would use the equivalent of 25 to 30 percent of Queensland’s total energy consumption.

The data centre will run primarily on electricity generated by coal and gas, drawn from the state’s electricity grid. Greenpeace estimates that the data centre would raise the grid’s emissions by 6.6 million tonnes, the equivalent of two million extra cars on the road.

Last month, Crisafulli wrestled with the federal government and eventually won a state exemption from the requirement that data centres run on renewable energy. The exemption, Crisafulli argued, was simply “common sense”; according to him (and now the Labor cabinet), environmental protections shouldn’t get in the way of AI investment opportunities.

While workers worry about AI’s impact on their jobs, power bills and the environment, Crisafulli has never been happier. He celebrated the data centre deal as the fruits of his five-day trip to the US in early September, where he met with the CEOs of OpenAI and Anthropic. On the same trip, he met with US Vice President J.D. Vance and discussed Queensland’s potential to become the next link in the American critical minerals supply chain.

Crisafulli’s MAGA meetings highlight that this data centre is a story of more than just environmental degradation and corporate greed. Attracting investment in areas like AI and critical minerals is a part of a broader mission to strengthen Australia’s alliance with the US. The data centre boom is driven in part by the AI arms race between the US and China. In this context, striking a deal with the US’s largest AI corporation is not just a step towards turning Queensland as an AI investment hub. It also further integrates the Australian and US economies, so both countries are better placed to outpace competitors in the global tech arena.

Anthropic’s new project adds to the 225 other data centres currently in development in Australia and supported by both major parties. Politicians and tech billionaires have no compunction about the impact of their actions on people or the environment, so long as they are making money and moving up the imperialist pecking order. We need a political alternative that will fight for an immediate moratorium on data centres and a socialist society where we can all have a say in the future of our lives and the planet.

author: webadmin
title: The Law Catches up with the Lauderdale: Huntswoman Convicted of Illegal Fox Hunting
content:
Claire Bellamy, 51, veteran huntswoman for the Lauderdale Hunt, became the first fox hunter convicted under Scotland’s new hunting laws, following a case in which footage captured by Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs exposed illegal hunting taking place beyond the boundaries of licensed operation.




Claire Bellamy after the incident. Image: Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs




On Monday, 5 October 2026, Bellamy, the former master and huntsman was found guilty at Paisley Sheriff Court of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs during an outing at Kirkton Wood, between Houston and Kilmacolm in January, 2025.




The hunt had been granted a licence by NatureScot, allowing dogs to be used under controlled circumstances. But the footage, which was played to the court, showed the hounds pursuing a fox outside the area covered by that licence.




Under the Hunting with Dogs (Scotland) Act 2023, NatureScot can licence more than two dogs to search for, stalk or flush a fox from cover, where this is necessary to prevent serious damage and where an alternative control is not available – it is not a licence to hunt foxes in any traditional sense.




This fox was hunted as hounds were allowed to hunt in the open. Image: Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs




Dogs can be used to search for and flush a fox from cover, but the dogs must remain under control. The fox can be flushed towards waiting guns and shot as soon as possible. The hounds are not allowed to pursue or kill the fox.




The hounds in pursuit of the hunted fox. Image: Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs




Licences are also geographically restricted, specifying exactly where the activity is permitted to take place.




So, the legal model is that dogs can enter the cover, flush the fox, and the waiting guns shoot the fox. What is not allowed is that dogs find the fox, and then pursue the fox across the country.




Sabs warned when the new legislation was introduced that licensing created a loophole, through which traditional fox hunting could continue under the guise of wildlife management and Bellamy’s conviction shows those warnings were well founded.




WATCH THE VIDEO










The footage was filmed by hunt saboteurs and shown in court. It shows the hunt spread out across the countryside with hounds moving over open ground along the edge of the woodland.




Bellamy argued that the hounds had got away from her and that she was attempting to regain control. However, the terms of the licence state that the dogs must be under control, but more importantly, the court rejected that this was an accidental loss of control.




After viewing the footage, Sheriff Sukhwinder Gill found Bellamy guilty of deliberately hunting a fox with dogs outside the area in which the licensed activity was permitted.




The old “whoopsie my dogs were out of control” is not a defence under the Scottish Hunting Act.




Terrier-men with quads stuffed with terriers follow behind. Image: Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs




Bellamy’s conviction vindicates sabs concerns that hunts would turn the licences into loopholes to continue with traditional fox hunting.




Naturally, Bellamy was not operating in isolation; behind her stands an organised network of dedicated wildlife killers, eagerly searching for any loophole to carry on traditional fox hunting just as they always have.




In 2023, following the passing of the new Scottish hunting laws, another hunt – the Lanarkshire & Renfrewshire announced that it was folding after 252 years.




At their final meet

, the hunt gave thanks to riders and supporters who had followed the hunt, and to the farms and landowners who had allowed them to cross their land over the years.




The Lanarkshire & Renfrewshire meet for the last time ever in March 2023. Image: Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs




The foxhound pack was disbanded, with the hunt saying that the hounds would be rehomed. But the organisation itself did not disappear. Instead, it announced that it would continue to operate as a ‘hunt club’.




A hunt club can maintain the social network of riders and hunt supporters, organise events such as Point-2-Points, and preserve the relationships with landowners and farmers within the countryside where the hunt previously operated.




It was on the former Lanarkshire & Renfrewshire country that Bellamy and the Lauderdale hounds were operating on the day of the illegal hunt.




The Lauderdale packing up under the watchful eyes of Glasgow sabs. Image: Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs




Bellamy’s conviction is important not just because she is the first fox hunter to be convicted under the new Act, but because it demonstrates that licensing hunts has not prevented illegal hunting from taking place, and without observers on the ground, what happens during a hunt, would rarely ever make a courtroom.




As the government is currently considering a new law for hunting in England and Wales, Bellamy’s case serves as a warning about how exemptions or permitted hunting activities work in practice.




Given the opportunity, hunts will sniff out a loophole or opportunity to hunt foxes from a thousand paces. The government must ensure, this time, a ban means a ban.




A spokesperson for Glasgow Hunt Saboteurs said:







“We welcome the outcome of this case, particularly as it is the first of its kind under the new Scottish law. The blatant illegal hunting and sheer audacity of those involved shows what we are up against. Those who want to kill wildlife clearly believe they are above the law. Not this time.




With more of Scotland’s hunting community due in court over the coming months, we will continue to be out there in all weathers, working tirelessly until the day comes when fox hunting is cleansed entirely from Scotland’s beautiful countryside.”







You can support Glasgow Hunt Sabs 

here

 and follow them 

here

 
















The post 

The Law Catches up with the Lauderdale: Huntswoman Convicted of Illegal Fox Hunting

 appeared first on 

Hunt Saboteurs Association

.

author: Mary Ellen Murphy
title: Hospital doctors strike for wages, safe hours and public health
content:
In July, Victorian public hospital doctors voted 97 percent in favour of taking industrial action for the first time in 20 years. The reason is simple: the healthcare system is unsafe for patients and staff.

The Victorian healthcare system is in crisis. Systemic failures at every level compound one another. Limited access to primary care and community services leaves people more unwell and reliant on emergency departments for care. This results in long wait times, overcrowding and unsafe workloads.

Bed shortages, often caused by delays in discharging patients due to the lack of support services, are also an issue. For example, recent data from the Victorian Health Department shows that nineteen of 21 mental health units fail to admit acutely unwell patients from the emergency department within eight hours. This results in staff attempting to care for patients in under-resourced and unsuitable environments in which they are at greater risk of violence. The lack of suitable facilities for mental health patients and adequate staffing also contributes to the ongoing failures to meet goals for the reduction in use of restrictive interventions such as seclusion and restraint.

It is no wonder then that burnout is endemic among public hospital doctors like me working in this broken system. We are expected to be machines and cope with unsafe workloads, under-resourcing and excessive hours without complaint. The system relies on unpaid overtime, guilt and obligation to keep going.

Our industrial claims highlight the punishing hours and minimal protections Victorian doctors currently face. They include a pay rise in line with what the nurses won in 2024, better guarantees of overtime for all non-rostered hours worked, permanent employment as a default model (instead of many thousands of “junior” hospital doctors, many with over a decade of experience, being given only yearly contracts), maximum shift lengths of 12.5 hours (rather than the 14 hours commonly worked at the moment), at least four rostered days off per fortnight including two consecutive days, a maximum of four consecutive night shifts, minimum doctor-to-patient ratios for safe care and mandatory 30-minute paid rest breaks every five hours.

During the fourteen months of unsuccessful bargaining discussions, the Victorian Hospitals Industrial Association (the association of employers in the public health industry) backpedalled on its previous agreement to simplify overtime payments, arguing it would cost too much to pay doctors the hours they actually work.

It is not only at work that public hospital employees are coming under attack. Over the last few months, we have seen our regulator, AHPRA, conflate antisemitism with anti-Zionism to silence healthcare workers speaking up about Palestine, including outside of work and on social media. This violates democratic rights and sets a terrible precedent for other professions. Many healthcare workers feel particularly obliged to advocate for Palestinians based on our roles as health workers. We suffer moral injury when we are prevented from speaking out about the atrocities committed against our colleagues in Gaza and against the Palestinian people as a whole.

When confronted about the lack of a public response to this attack on our freedom of speech, the Victorian branch of the Australian Medical Association admitted it was scared to address it publicly for fear of backlash, and that the federal organisation was engaged in back-room discussions with AHPRA. This approach aligns more with a lobby organisation than a trade union.

A union’s strength comes from its members’ involvement and activity. This also protects unions when they want to speak out about political issues important to their members. There is a reason that the Australian Salaried Medical Officers Federation (the part of the Australian Medical Association that is engaged in bargaining) in New South Wales—the branch involved most recently in prolonged industrial action with an active rank and file—was the only branch of our union that put out a statement condemning the AHPRA adoption of the pro-Israel International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance definition of antisemitism.

Turning to the current campaign for a better agreement in Victoria, we have so far had multiple four-hour stop-works across different sites and services on different days. At these rallies, workers were asked to vote on whether they supported a statewide strike on 14 September. The response was almost unanimous—doctors voted for a statewide strike.

Despite this, on 14 September, thousands of other public hospital doctors went to work with even less enthusiasm than usual. Our statewide strike did not go ahead after a legal challenge about patient safety by the state government led our union to withdraw the notice. It seems that the state government cares about patient safety only when it comes to preventing doctors from taking industrial action, not when hospitals are chronically understaffed and overstretched day in and day out.

Under sustained pressure from the membership, a four-hour statewide stop work took place on 1 October and hundreds of doctors rallied outside state parliament. Our union leaders called a meeting the previous evening and suggested there could be an offer and that we should consider cancelling the rally. The membership made it clear that we would not back down again and that we are tired of tactics aimed at impeding industrial action.

We are now being told that we have run out of time prior to the government entering caretaker mode to secure a four-year agreement and have been presented with a one-year interim offer, our first offer in fourteen months. This is very convenient for the state government, as it would prevent us from taking action in the lead-up to the election. The situation is developing, but I will vote “No” and support the demand for a twelve-hour statewide strike.

There has been little indication that the union leaders are considering another statewide strike. This is despite the members giving a clear mandate for one. It can be done. Other healthcare unions have pulled it off before. This is where solidarity between workers is essential, and we need to talk to other unions about how they organise to stand up in Fair Work rather than tossing the idea of a statewide strike into the too-hard basket. After all, our fight is relevant to other healthcare workers. If we can achieve significant gains and improve the system that we all work in, everyone will benefit. If we get a significant pay increase, then other workers are better positioned to demand the same.

Hospitals are massive workplaces with real industrial power. We need to rebuild a socialist current within healthcare to revive rank-and-file trade unionism and overcome sectionalism with real solidarity. Together, we can win the system we deserve.

author: Ya puso la puerka radio
title: Ya puso la puerka Radio Episodio 33
content:
¡Amigos y enemigos! ¡Amargopunks y no amargopunks!


Presentamos una entrega más de temas de anarquismo, punk y actualidad que nos somete.  Actualidad a la que estamos obligados — Sí o Sí — a pensar, recuérdese que como Zoon politikón que somos y que como todo indica; no podemos escapar como arte de magia (A menos que te entregues a las drogas —cualquiera— y el embrutecimiento para olvidar y escapar de la realidad.  Bueeeenooo. También a nosotros nos gusta el escapismo, ¿A quién no? Pero breve, si no, no se disfruta) a los vaivenes y estertores de la historia.  Si no ¿Para qué chingados estas de punk?  Es más. Es un puto imperativo vital y existencial el enterarte de todo, cuestionarlo, regurgitarlo, vomitarlo, y cambiar desde tu existencia hasta nuestro entorno próximo y lejano.  A ser un agente de cambio.




Los sucesos nos avasallan, pasan las guerras, el hambre, las ideas, los gobernantes, la violencia y con todo esto tenemos que lidiar con nuestras tragedias individuales, con nuestra pesada existencia, importante mencionar que nuestras tragedias vienen en buena medida de las decisiones y acontecimientos que hicieron otros, a los que no les importamos, a los que les importa mas el prestigio y/o el dinero.  Hijosdeputa!  Y ante este alud de acontecimientos nos damos el tiempo de escoger algunos que nos parecen interesantes y pensarlos, ya saben, desde la mirada del anarquismo y el punk.




De qué hablamos.




La patética visita de Angela Davis y Gina Dent en la UNAM




Patética, porque como dice la palabra Patético= pathētikós. = pathos= sentimiento.   Nos provoca o nos mueve a pensarlo urgentemente.  Sugerimos que pueda ser un punto de quiebre del feminismo, un cisma, y nos proyecte a análisis conectados con lo que ha perseguido el anarquismo y el punk desde su génesis: La destrucción de moldes viejos y construir nuevos basados en la libertad del individuo y la sociedad.  Estuvo chido porque mostró en una forma cagadisima de contradicción de lo que trataba el coloquio y la durísima realidad insultante, no sólo en la UNAM, sino en otros ámbitos, como el antipunitivismo.    Nuestra resolución: Patético hastasuputamadreeee. Ja, ja, ja.




Reflexiones sobre la violencia. Así nomás.




Aquí partimos del nombre de nuestra banda de punk —Descripción muy pretenciosa, para dos Weyes que osaron agarrar unos ruidosos instrumentos y “hacer” música— llamada Radikal Violencia. Como individuos pertenecientes al género humano, nos asumimos como cómplices del odio y la violencia…hacia el opresor, obvio.  Incluso aventuramos una brújula moral para toda la banda: “La violencia hacia abajo, ejercerla con alguien más débil que tú, es cobarde.  La violencia horizontal, con tu igual, es estúpida.  La violencia hacia arriba, con el opresor, es necesaria” ¡¡¡¡Ahhhh perrrroooo!!!




Dos antípodas. Luigi Mangione y Charlie Kirk.




“Comenzamos por el final” ¡Vete a la verga Charlie Kirk!     Aquí comparamos estas vidas paralelas, Luigi, Charlie y nosotros, y hablando de violencia este tema se conecta de una manera muy fluida.  Destacamos a Luigi y reflexionamos sobre Charlie. Uno de los tópicos: El esquema político gringo y mundial ya nos rebasó, ya lo hemos dicho, el simple izquierda y derecha se amplía y ahora hasta tenemos unos weyes llamados Groypers, el internet y los memes ya son parte de el escenario. Para complicar más las cosas.




Bares “culturales” El Alicia por decir uno solamente.




Otro tema para pensar el significado de activista, y activista gestor cultural, y activista depositario de ayudas y comodatos, y activista cantinero. Se desdibuja el significado y las palabras y la semántica sí que importa.   La neta el tema del Alicia ya está muy masticado, pero conviene aterrizar las ideas.




Israhell. El David triunfante y pernicioso desde tiempo bíblicos.




¡Mierda!  Por culpa de estos pendejos y sus aliados, la gente de todo el mundo lo está pasando mal.  Sube el petróleo, el comercio se ralentiza y la gente de a pie en todo el mundo paga los platos rotos.  Sabemos que no estamos descubriendo el agua tibia.  Pero es que si nos da un chingo de dolor de panza del coraje.




Inteligencia Artificial,




La I.A. llegó para quedarse, aunque no lo queramos. Es la batalla tecnológica que se está desarrollando en estos momentos.  Conviene ir agarrando el hilo, aunque no seamos usuarios ni tengamos nuestra ingeniería en Machine Learning.   Hay mucho ruido. Revisamos la noticia de que hay un 10% de probabilidad de que la I.A. destruya la humanidad.




Nuestras secciones de siempre.




Cartas y saludines.


Recomendaciones.




Invitamos a todos a escuchar, vomitar y pensar en conjunto.   ¡Saludos perrunos y amargosos!




Búho y Kaio.  Septiembre 2026

author: Rachel Evans, Mark Gillespie
title: Inquest into Jesse Deacon’s shooting by NSW Police ends
content:
Jesse Deacon’s coronial inquest, which ended on October 2, heard details about the actions of NSW Police in July 2023 which led to his death.

A coronial inquest aims to establish what happened in the lead up to the death of a person, and the people involved in the incident.

Police forcibly entered the 43-year old’s home, ostensibly for a welfare check, on July 20 of that year. Jesse was kettled by three police, with one tasering him and another fatally shooting him in the back.

Judy Deacon, Jesse’s mother, represented herself and questioned the witnesses. She was supported by Leesa Topic, the mother of 22-year-old Courtney Topic, who was shot dead by police in 2015.

Deacon has led a successful campaign for health providers to supply mental health responders to replace police in mental health emergencies.

Jesse was a well-read, talented artist and musician, who struggled with “treatment resistant” schizophrenia. He had spent time in inpatient mental health facilities. A shy person, he also had an illicit drug and alcohol addiction.

In 2023, a neighbour called 000 for an ambulance after Jesse asked them for a cigarette. He had a knife and was using it to cut himself.

Three police officers, Constable Riley Avery, Sergeant Hugo James and Officer A*, arrived before the ambulance. The inquest heard that they saw blood near Jesse’s apartment, but did not discuss an approach plan. Their only attempt to communicate with Jesse was Avery asking Jesse to open the door before he kicked it in.

None of the three officers had undertaken training in how to undertake mental health call-outs.

Jesse was still holding the knife when the police intruded. Still, none of the officers attempted to deescalate the situation. Jesse became trapped between two officers.

Barrister Donna Ward, senior legal counsel assisting the coroner summarised the situation as: “Riley Avery shot a taser into Jesse’s front torso. Simultaneously, Officer A* fired into Jesse’s back, which killed him.”

It took less than eight seconds from Avery kicking Jesse’s door down, to Officer A* shooting Jesse in the back. None of the three officers took up a medical first aid kit to the unit.

Deputy state coroner David O’Neil conducted the inquest over a week in July, hearing from NDIS care workers, hospital workers and police officers, and a further week over September-October.

In the second week, the inquest heard expert medical witnesses, a General Practitioner, a boarding house manager and methadone clinic witnesses.

The Deacon family, including Jesse’s father Michael Deacon and Jesse’s sister, Lucinda Deacon, also gave testimony. An accomplished soprano singer, Lucinda had compiled photos and videos of Jesse’s life and the campaign for justice with a soundtrack “Creep” by Radiohead, covered by Avie Sheck and his mother who sang in Hindi. Lucinda finished her video statement by singing “Traum”.

Deacon and the Ward put forward their recommendations for changes to policing practices, housing and mental health to the coroner, and requested that Jesse’s case be heard in court.

If the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions and the Attorney-General agree, the case could go to trial. This has only happened twice in recent history, both times under NSW Coroner Teresa O’Sullivan.

Deacon said she wants “real changes to stop these things happening again”. She has been leading a three-year fight to replace NSW Police with trained mental health responders in cases of mental health emergencies. Some $270 million over 10 years was announced for a Virtual Mental Health Hub within NSW Ambulance and eight Mental Health Acute Assessment Teams on July 30. One hundred mental health responders will replace police in parts of NSW.

“The mental health responders program is Jesse’s legacy and will save lives,” Deacon told Green Left. “There is no justice when someone dies, but at least we have this legacy. It is only a first step and needs refining and a funding boost. We also need supported accommodation.

“Jesse’s death could have been prevented if there had been enough supported accommodation for people with schizophrenia.”

Crown counsel assisting Ward admitted to the inquiry that there was “little behind the media release” of the mental health responder program. “To date, there’s no further details of the roll-out of the new initiative to have mental health trained responders attend call outs through NSW Ambulance.”

The coroner’s report is due in the next few months.

[Non-publication orders mean that Green Left cannot print Officer A*’s full name, nor can we print Judy Deacon’s final request to the coroner.]

author: Unknown
title: Küçükçekmece'de eğlence mekanında silahlı saldırı: 1'i polis, 2 kişi hayatını kaybetti
content:
İstanbul - Küçükçekmece'de bir eğlence mekanında silahlı saldırı yaşandı. Çıkan çatışmada 1’i polis, 2 kişi hayatını kaybetti, 2 kişi de yaralandı.

DHA'da yer alan habere göre silahlı saldırı, Atatürk Mahallesi İkitelli Caddesi’nde saat 03.40 sularında meydana geldi. Müzikhole gelen bir kişi henüz bilinmeyen nedenle çevreye ateş açtı. Bu sırada içeride olan ve izinli olduğu öğrenilen polis, ateş açan kişiye karşılık verdi. Çıkan çatışmada polis ile ateş açan kişi ağır yaralandı. Çalışanların ihbarı üzerine olay yerine ekipler sevk edildi. Sağlık ekiplerinin yaptığı kontrolde polis ile saldırganın hayatını kaybettiği belirlendi. Çatışmada 2 kişinin de yaralandığı öğrenildi.

İş yerine ait güvenlik kamera görüntülerini inceleyen ekipler, çalışanların da bilgisine başvurdu. İncelemelerin ardından hayatını kaybeden polis ile saldırganın cansız bedeni Adli Tıp Kurumu morguna kaldırıldı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: CHP’de butlan yönetiminin işçi kıyımı sürüyor: 3 çalışanın daha işine son verildi
content:
CHP’de mahkemenin mutlak butlan kararıyla göreve gelen yönetimin 85’i aşkın genel merkez çalışanını işten çıkarmasının ardından 3 kişinin daha işine son verildi. İşten çıkarılanların eşlerinin daha önce CHP’de çalıştığı, ardından Yeni Parti’de işe başladığı öğrenildi.

CHP’de Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu’nun mahkemenin mutlak butlan kararıyla yeniden genel başkanlık görevine gelmesinin ardından başlayan işten çıkarmalar devam ediyor. Genel merkezde çalışan 85’i aşkın kişinin işine son veren yönetimin, son olarak eşleri Yeni Parti’de çalışmaya başlayan 3 çalışanı daha işten çıkardığı belirtildi.

Cumhuriyet’in haberine göre, işine son verilen Hasan Demirhan’ın eşi Yeni Parti’de büro personeli, Ozan Çiftçi’nin eşi kat görevlisi, Simge Cansu’nun nişanlısı ise büro personeli olarak çalışıyor. Söz konusu kişilerin daha önce CHP’de görev yaptığı, işten çıkarılmalarının ardından Yeni Parti’de işe başladıkları öğrenildi.

CHP’nin 7. Genel Başkanı Kemal Kılıçdaroğlu, 21 Mayıs’ta mahkemenin mutlak butlan kararıyla yeniden genel başkanlık görevine gelmişti. Kararın ardından genel merkez çalışanlarına yönelik işten çıkarmalar 26 Mayıs’ta, Kurban Bayramı arifesinde başlamıştı. İşine son verilen 85’i aşkın çalışan arasında sekreterler, fotoğrafçılar, kameramanlar, temizlik görevlileri ve çay ocağı emekçileri de bulunuyordu.

İşten çıkarmaların bir bölümünde, SGK’ye yapılan bildirimlerde Kod-48'in kullanıldığı belirtilmişti. İşçinin devamsızlığı, işverene veya ailesine yönelik hakaret gibi gerekçelerle iş sözleşmesinin feshedilmesinde kullanılan bu kod nedeniyle çalışanlar kıdem ve ihbar tazminatları ile işsizlik ödeneğinden yararlanamadı. İşten çıkarılan bazı çalışanlar, haklarını aramak için CHP yönetimine karşı dava açmıştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: 10. Çanakkale Bienali 10 Ekim’de başlıyor: 9 ülkeden 60’tan fazla sanatçı
content:
Gözde Tüzer Korkmaz [email protected]

“Metcezir // Ebb & Flow” başlığıyla düzenlenen 10. Çanakkale Bienali, 10 Ekim-20 Kasım 2026 tarihleri arasında gerçekleştirilecek. Bienalin sergi ve etkinlikleri Çanakkale kent merkezinin yanı sıra Troya, Ayvacık, Assos ve Küçükkuyu’daki 15 farklı mekâna yayılacak.

2006 yılında başlayan ve ilk edisyonunu 2008’de gerçekleştiren Çanakkale Bienali, 10. edisyonunda 9 ülkeden 60’tan fazla sanatçının çalışmalarını bir araya getirecek.

Bienalin bu yılki programı “Metcezir // Ebb & Flow” başlığı altında suyun çekilmesi ve yükselmesinden hareketle hafıza, coğrafya ve zamanın dönüşümünü ele alıyor. Su, toprak, hafıza ve dönüşüm kavramları etrafında şekillenen programda yeni üretimlerin yanı sıra farklı disiplinlerden çalışmalar ve uluslararası iş birlikleri yer alacak.

Bienal kapsamında Çanakkale’nin tarihî yapılarının yanı sıra gündelik yaşamın parçası olan farklı mekânlar da sanat çalışmalarına ev sahipliği yapacak.

Eski palamut depoları bölgesindeki MAHAL, StudioMAHAL ve DemirHAN, Troia Vakfı Korfmann Kütüphanesi ve Troya Müzesi bienalin ana mekânları arasında bulunuyor.

Çarşı içindeki Mavi Ev de programda yer alırken, Cuma Pazarı'nın yanındaki bir park kalıcı bir kamusal sanat çalışmasına ev sahipliği yapacak. Yeni kuşak sanatçı ve tasarımcıların çalışmalarını sürdürdüğü sanayi bölgesindeki ASTİM de bienal kapsamında kullanılacak.

Çanakkale’nin denizle ilişkisine odaklanan özel seçkinin adresi ise Balıkhane olacak.

Program kent merkeziyle sınırlı kalmayacak. Ayvacık’ın Yukarı Tartışık Köyü, Küçükkuyu’daki Adatepe Zeytinyağı Müzesi, Assos’taki Güneşane Vakfı ve İda Blue Adatepe de bienal kapsamındaki mekânlar arasında yer alacak.

Çanakkale Bienali programında Çanakkale’nin seramik mirasına odaklanan “Özel Odak: Seramik” seçkisi de yer alıyor.

Seramiği yalnızca bir üretim tekniği olarak değil, hafıza, arkeoloji, tarih, coğrafya ve dönüşümle ilişkili bir malzeme olarak ele alan seçkide farklı kuşaklardan sanatçıların çalışmaları bir araya getirilecek.

Troya Müzesi başta olmak üzere MAHAL, Korfmann Kütüphanesi ve Mavi Ev’de gösterilecek çalışmalar, Çanakkale’nin tarihsel üretim geleneği ile çağdaş sanat pratikleri arasındaki ilişkiye odaklanacak.

Bienal, Çanakkale’deki kurumların yanı sıra uluslararası kültür kurumlarının destekleriyle gerçekleştiriliyor.

Dardanel ile Kale Grubu-Kale Tasarım ve Sanat Merkezi’nin ana destekçiliğini üstlendiği bienal, Çanakkale İl Kültür ve Turizm Müdürlüğü, Çanakkale Onsekiz Mart Üniversitesi ve Çanakkale Belediyesi iş birliğiyle düzenleniyor. Troya Kazı Başkanlığı, ÇATKAV ve Troia Vakfı yerel paydaşlar arasında yer alırken, 1915 Çanakkale Köprüsü ve Otoyolu da kurumsal destekçiler arasında bulunuyor.

“Metcezir // Ebb & Flow” başlıklı 10. Çanakkale Bienali, 10 Ekim’de başlayacak ve 20 Kasım’a kadar devam edecek.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Yıldız Teknik Üniversitesi'nde siber saldırı duyurusu: 140 bin öğrencinin verisi çalınmış olabilir
content:
Yıldız Teknik Üniversitesi'nde (YTÜ) 1 Ekim'den bu yana yaşanan sistem aksaklıklarının arkasından siber saldırı çıktı. Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurulu'nun (KVKK) 7 Ekim tarihli kararıyla üniversitedeki veri ihlali resmi olarak kamuoyuna duyuruldu. Yaşanan siber saldırı ve veri ihlalinden yaklaşık 140 bin öğrenci ile 4 bin 500 personelin etkilendiği belirtildi.

Yıldız Teknik Üniversitesi'nde altyapı sorunu: Öğrenciler çevrimiçi derslere erişemiyor

Üniversitenin resmi internet sitesi, Öğrenci Bilgi Sistemi (OBS), Online Yıldız ve çeşitli başvuru sistemlerine günlerce erişim sağlanamazken, üniversite yönetiminin yaşanan aksaklıklara ilişkin ilk etapta kapsamlı bir açıklama yapmadığı görüldü. Yönetim, 3 Ekim'de yaptığı ilk duyuruda süreci yalnızca "teknik çalışma" olarak nitelendirmişti. Ancak KVKK'nın devreye girmesiyle birlikte sistem kesintilerinin arkasında bir fidye yazılımı saldırısının olduğu netlik kazandı.

Kişisel Verileri Koruma Kurulu’nun yayımladığı duyuruda "Veri sorumlusu sıfatını haiz Yıldız Teknik Üniversitesi tarafından Kurula iletilen veri ihlal bildiriminde özetle; ihlalin 01.10.2026 tarihinde başladığı ve aynı gün tespit edildiği, veri sorumlusunun sanallaştırma altyapısı ve üzerinde çalışan sunucuların fidye yazılımı saldırısından etkilendiği, ihlalden etkilenen ilgili kişi grubunun öğrenci, personel ve ziyaretçiler olduğu, mevcut kayıtlara göre ihlalden etkilenmiş olabilecek ilgili kişi sayısının yaklaşık 140.000 öğrenci ve 4.500 personel olduğu, ziyaretçilere ilişkin sayının henüz belirlenemediği, ihlalden etkilenen kişisel veri kategorilerinin belirlenemediği bilgilerine yer verilmiştir" ifadeleri kullanıldı.

Öğrencilerin hangi kişisel verilerinin siber saldırıdan etkilendiği ve dışarı sızdırıldığı konusundaki belirsizlikler ise hâlâ devam ediyor.

author: anonerror
title: Crónica de Naada en Ceuta
content:
Van a cumplirse un par de semanas desde que volví de Ceuta, y el panorama está cada vez más calentito en nuestro país. Es difícil hablar de cualquier tema político o social sin que surja enemistad… Primero la crisis de Ceuta. Manifestaciones en defensa de España. Mari Carmen. La acampada en Sol y en otras ciudades. Más manifestaciones. El rechazo de los dos decretos. Las elecciones anticipadas…

Me demoré en escribir estas líneas porque me parecía que en este momento podría juzgarse de frivolidad. Que hablar de Ceuta en la actualidad, con otros muchos problemas, sería tachado de inoportuno. Pero me doy cuenta de que ha sido, sigue siendo y será imprescindible no silenciar su voz. Especialmente tras mi visita a la ciudad autónoma, donde pude despertar y ser consciente de que vivimos una gran desinformación desde fuera. Como si a las noticias; las publicaciones en redes sociales y los reportajes les costara cruzar el estrecho sin deformarse, tergiversarse o manipularse en el intento.

Un pueblo mal informado es un pueblo manipulable. Y un pueblo además dividido es un pueblo controlable. Ya lo decía Julio César.

Por eso no es de extrañar que haya una buena campaña de desinformación en marcha desde la entrada masiva de migrantes el 30 y 31 de julio en Ceuta. Existen unos creadores de contenido en redes sociales que buscan, precisamente, la polarización de la sociedad en pensamientos realmente radicales. Hay bulos por todas partes que siembran y alimentan los pensamientos retorcidos llenos de racismo, odio y, a fin de cuentas, miedo. Mientras organizaciones humanitarias, vecinos y vecinas ceutíes y grupos autogestionados se organizan en terreno para responder a contrarreloj y sin medios a todas las necesidades humanitarias de los migrantes que el Gobierno no cubre, otros seres a los que no quiero poner nombre, pero defensores de pensamientos fascistas, se dedican patrullar las calles para “cazarlos a todos”, como un diputado de Vox animaba a hacer. Organizados por redes sociales, se dividen los barrios marginales para dar ueltas en sus coches, amenazar, violentar y perturbar tanto a los dadores de ayuda como a sus receptores.

Es real el descontento de los ceutíes. Hay críticas sobre la situación de la ciudad; sobre la intervención- o su ausencia-, su alcance, su demora, y el modo de ejecutarla del Gobierno y las instituciones. Hay quejas y más quejas. Sin embargo se ven pocas manos tendidas a ayudar. Lo fácil es colgar la bandera del balcón, sacarla al escaparate de tu negocio, o ponérsela en la muñeca, solicitando que tu ciudad vuelva a ser la misma. Más difícil y valiente es jugársela a ser apartado e ir contracorriente de tus vecinos odiadores por acoger en tu casa a unas cuantas personas. Esos casos también los hay y me llenan de emoción, dándome todavía algo de esperanza en la humanidad. Hay estos vecinos y vecinas, que son los que están levantando Ceuta a pasitos pequeños pero constantes.

Sin embargo, lamentablemente, hay un discurso que nos venden como el predominante, porque es lo que interesa que España vea. El de odio y de racismo que están calando en estratos de la sociedad que no deberían hacer manitas con dichas ideologías. Básicamente por puros principios.

Pero creo que ya no sabemos ni qué quiere decir esa palabra. Porque antes que crisis política o social estratégicamente buscada por los hilos invisibles de los poderes fácticos americanos y sionistas, esto es una grandísima crisis humanitaria. Y lo que más está escaseando es la humanidad. Lo que estamos viviendo en Ceuta no es casual y, como vemos, tampoco será inocuo. Pero en este texto no me quiero extender en el análisis de sus orígenes y consecuencias geopolíticas. Eso se lo dejo a los expertos.

Yo tan solo soy una enfermera que ha estado en terreno y que necesita sacar de las entrañas toda la frustración acumulada en mi paso por Ceuta. Así que hablemos de lo que pude experimentar allí, de todo aquello que fui testigo y que contrasta fuertemente con lo que se difunde en redes. Hablemos de lo que realmente está sucediendo a los migrantes y a las vecinas ceutíes.

El día 20 de septiembre celebraron en Ceuta una manifestación en la frontera, a la que acudieron según los reportes 200 personas, con nuestra bandera de España ondeando al grito de “¡invasores fuera! Expulsión”. Bandera que siguen haciendo suya y con la que defienden lo indefendible; la segregación, el maltrato, la violencia. Hablan de defender España y a los Españoles, a los ceutíes, mientras lanzan improperios e insultos a niñas racializadas dentro de la protesta por ser, simplemente, racializadas. Mientras gritan a mis compañeras “Depílate el sobaco, puta”. Entonces no va a defender a todos y todas las personas españolas, con o sin vello corporal. Parece que va de defender cierta raza… Supremacismo blanco.

Esa misma noche tuvimos que soportar una noche de continuas patrullas en las naves de Tarajal, complejo industrial donde se concentra gran cantidad de chabolas donde sobreviven unos 300 migrantes, entre ellos familias y menores. En esas patrullas, realizadas por militares, mayoritariamente legionarios, los tanques pasaban haciendo ruidos innecesarios, con el himno de la legión a todo volumen. Los militares a pie silbaban al avanzar por los callejones, de forma espeluznante para asustar a los menores a los que iban a aporrear para celebrar su día; 20 de septiembre, día de la legión. Forzaron las puertas de varios coches y gasearon a los ocupantes, que dormían, con gas lacrimógeno.

Y no es un hecho aislado. Varias organizaciones, colectivos y personas a título individual, están grabando como prueba las “cacerías”, la violencia, las palizas y las devoluciones que han pactado llamar “retornos voluntarios”. Alivia pensar que todos estos casos han llegado ya a la fiscalía, tras la denuncia de estos colectivos, que ha abierto una investigación sobre presuntos malos tratos de los militares en Ceuta. La investigación tiene como fin esclarecer si ha habido comportamientos constitutivos de delito por parte del Ejército. Independientemente del veredicto, si estás leyendo mis palabras, aquí y ahora puedes irte con la clara respuesta: Sí. No son presuntos. Suceden cada día y hay pruebas. Tenemos vídeos, testimonios de menores llenos de porrazos, brechas, heridas… contando cómo les acorralan, les pillan por sorpresa y se ensañan con ellos.

Luego están los desalojos de las zonas con asentamientos temporales más hacinados, como las playas de Trampolín y de Benítez. La policía aparece allí con órdenes de desalojo y destruyen todo lo que pueda quedar en pie. Servicios de limpieza pasan a continuación a su recogida.Miles de personas reciben órdenes en una lengua que no hablan. Presas del pánico, puesto que no comprenden qué sucede, huyen. Imagen que los medios luego califican como “estampida y caos”. En lo segundo no les falta razón. Se les pide sentarse en ocasiones, hacer filas en otras, y son conducidas a las nuevas carpas habilitadas para la acogida. En esas carpas no hay espacio para todos y no se hace un conteo previo para no movilizar a personas que finalmente no entrarán. Tampoco se valora caso por caso el grado de vulnerabilidad para priorizar las plazas. La consecución o no de plaza depende del orden de llegada. Los juegos del hambre. A todas aquellas personas heridas en estas carreras o en las noches de porrazos, deshidratadas, a las que tienen gastroenteritis aguda por las malas condiciones de vida, por el no acceso a agua y saneamiento. A todas las que desarrollan enfermedades de la piel como sarna, hongos, heridas sobreinfectadas, abscesos en la piel; gripes, neumonías, etc. ¿Qué les espera cuando acuden a centros para que cuiden de su salud? Nótese que tan solo he citado problemas físicos. Los problemas de salud mental también están presentes y al mismo nivel de importancia. Sin embargo, por mucho que duela decirlo, no existe una manera de abordarlos en estos contextos. O de hacerlo bien.

Pero la manera de dar atención a la salud física sí. Existe.

Según la Ley 16/2003 , de 28 de mayo, de cohesión y calidad del Sistema Nacional de Salud, las personas extranjeras no registradas ni autorizadas como residentes en España tienen derecho a la protección de la salud y a la atención sanitaria en las mismas condiciones que las personas con nacionalidad española.

Dicha asistencia será con cargo a los fondos públicos de las administraciones competentes – y dice también- “El reconocimiento del derecho a la asistencia sanitaria corresponde a las CCAA/Servicios Públicos de Salud.”

Es decir, es competencia del servicio de salud de la ciudad de Ceuta brindar esta atención en las mismas condiciones que se brinda a los ciudadanos españoles. Muy lejos de cumplir, y violando además otras leyes y derechos fundamentales, el personal sanitario y auxiliar de servicios (como por ejemplo los guardas de seguridad), bajo la permanente presencia de militares, están llevando a cabo una macabra estrategia de segregación racial, un apartheid. En España, año 2026.

Una mañana de domingo llevando al hospital de Ceuta a un chico que llamaremos Mohamed, con vómitos incontrolables, deshidratado, con fiebre muy alta y casi desfallecido, me encontré ante tal circo, indignante y degradante para todos aquellos que esperaban en lo que ellos fallan a llamar sala de espera. Una sala que no es sala. El área en cuestión está fuera del edificio del hospital; a la intemperie llueva, haga viento o un sol abrasador. Tienen colocados unos bancos donde los pacientes se ganan su nombre más que nunca puesto que, ya que sólo han asignado a un sólo sanitario para todos ellos, la clasificación según gravedad (triage) es insoportable e inaceptablemente lenta.

Indicadores de calidad dicen que el tiempo hasta que te evalúan rápidamente y clasifican debe ser inferior a los 10 minutos. En su caso, y en el de todos aquellos que esperaban con Mohamed, una hora después de llegar todavía no le habían llamado. A pesar de estar acompañado por una enfermera. A pesar de que insistí en que su condición de salud se estaba deteriorando y que tenía fiebre muy alta. A pesar de que tiritaba y suplicaba. Nadie le miró. Nadie le sacó una manta. Y ahora me doy cuenta de que eligieron voluntariamente no oírle, ni verle. Él y todos los sentados a su lado son invisibles. El lugar parece una cárcel más que un hospital. La presencia de militares en la puerta; de policía nacional de cuando en cuando; de la empresa subcontratada de seguridad, que realiza un trato vejatorio tanto a los migrantes como a los que acompañamos. Las normas, que se han inventado, son estrictas. No permiten el acompañamiento del paciente de puertas para dentro. Sin intérpretes. Sin una mano que poderles tender. Tras el enorme y desmedido tiempo de espera entran en esas consultas y lo que pasa allí es un misterio.

Pero tenemos documentos gráficos que demuestran la gravedad del maltrato de este servicio de salud en Ceuta. Administrativos y médicos manipulando las fechas de nacimiento para convertirlos en mayores de edad; haciendo juicios irrelevantes para la historia clínica del paciente con frases del tipo “migrante ilegal/ migrante de la invasión”; pruebas necesarias y no realizadas; tratamientos vitales que son escritos pero no recetados, sin garantía de que los pacientes los vayan a conseguir por carecer de la financiación de la que nos beneficiamos con las recetas. Ese día que acompañaba a Mohamed encontré en la puerta, cabizbajo y esperando ser visto o escuchado, al borde de las lágrimas, a otro chico. Mismas edades, rondando la veintena, y misma invisibilidad. Le llamaremos Karim. Karim estaba siendo rechazado porque según los trabajadores de urgencias “no disponían de la medicación que necesitaba” en el hospital. Su problema de salud era muy grave, potencialmente mortal. Le habían diagnosticado hacía dos días de una trombosis venosa profunda. El tratamiento que Karim necesitaba eran inyecciones de heparina, una cada doce horas, durante diez días.

No sé qué eslabón de la cadena que forma la atención recibida en urgencias del hospital de Ceuta me perturba más. Si los militares, con su continua presencia haciendo del lugar un escenario bélico totalmente innecesario. O los trabajadores de seguridad de la puerta llevando rigurosamente guantes y mascarilla N95 (¿Os acordáis? Las que nos faltaban en el COVID) no vaya a ser que los migrantes traigan una plaga contagiosa y letal. Seguridad que trata a los pacientes a gritos, despreciando y siendo explícitamente violentos. Amenazándome a mí y a mi compañera con llamar a la policía y denunciarnos si utilizamos el teléfono móvil para grabar. O no se si me perturba la profesional administrativa de la ventanilla en recepción, que miró con desprecio esa carta escrita por Médicos del Mundo que le enseñe según llegamos, ilusa de mí, pensando que serían rápidos en atender a Mohamed, dado el contenido del documento. Le derivaban a urgencias del hospital por necesidad de terapia intravenosa. La ONG le había atendido hacía ya tres horas en su caravana ambulante en las naves industriales del Tarajal, sin que mejorase tras la primera medicación que le administraron. Llamaron a la ambulancia, que no apareció. Explicando esto en la recepción me preguntó “¿Es un inmigrante? Pues a esperar fuera”. O será que quien me perturba es el facultativo que diagnosticó a Karim de trombosis, y que fue capaz de darle un informe con su número de colegiado en el pie de página, con su firma de médico que obliga al cumplimiento del código deontológico que juró cuando se licenció. Código que incluye tener respeto a la vida, no discriminar, no causar daño. Básicamente, no dejar a Karim a su suerte, con la expectativa de que compre por sus medios una heparina que sin financiación cuesta 150 euros la caja para cinco días. Básicamente dejar a Karim, sin haberle hecho una traducción, sin haberle explicado la importancia de sus inyecciones para no tener complicaciones y no morir a sus veintipocos años. Básicamente no decirle que esos trombos en sus piernas, si no desaparecen, podrían desprenderse, viajar a los pulmones y acabar con él. Sin haberle recomendado buscar a otra organización en caso de escasez de medios, haberse encargado de que pudiera acceder a lo que su problema de salud requería. Pero no puedo elegir entre tanta perturbación. Porque aún me ha faltado listar a la enfermera que me gritó retóricamente ¿Me estás llamando tonta? por insistirle que leyera el informe de Karim otra vez; insistir en que su deber era ponerle una inyección de heparina, teniendo total certeza de su disponibilidad en el hospital. Por pedirle que nos hicieran ese favor por ser domingo, ya que los dos días previos le habían inyectado allí mismo, cuando le diagnosticaron y le hicieron las pruebas. Se negó. Nos mandó a un SUAP (Un centro de salud que permanece abierto para urgencias durante el fin de semana), y resultó que allí tienen abierto un centro que es plenamente de atención al migrante. Otra vez militarizado. Otra vez con sala de espera en el exterior. No obstante, el trato es bastante más correcto. Sólo dos trabajadores atienden, un(a) médico/a y un(a) enfermero/a, pero lo hacen con más agilidad y con profesionalidad. Esos trabajadores, como los/as vecino/as humanas y valientes, me hacen mantener mi esperanza en el mundo. Trataron a Mohamed, que mejoró. Ayudaron como pudieron a Karim. Y ambos están muy bien. La única trabajadora que me perturbó en este centro de atención al migrante, llamado Otero II, fue una médica que tuvo el cuajo de preguntarme “¿Vosotros, entonces, sois los que

estáis repartiendo los spray pimienta?”. No la culpo. Ha habido tremendos bulos sobre el reparto de dichos sprays entre migrantes para que se protejan de los ataques de los militares y la policía. Aunque mi opinión fuera que de verdad necesitan una protección, esta no es la manera. Y por supuesto que son rumores y bulos creados, una vez más, para fomentar el miedo, el odio, el rechazo de los ceutíes y de todos los españoles en general. Lo que sí es cierto es que hubo un reparto de cientos de estos sprays para mujeres españolas, “para defenderse de los invasores”, por parte del creador de contenido Juan Ruíz, responsable del bulo anterior y de otros tantos. El 2 de septiembre aparecía mostrando su cara, sin vergüenza ninguna, haciendo este reparto en las calles de Ceuta en el marco de una campaña de promoción de un grupo de ultraderecha, escindido de Vox, llamado Revuelta. Aparecía después en cadenas públicas de televisión, alimentando esa idea de que es una medida necesaria, que está justificado y que él se ha hecho cargo de forma voluntaria ya que el Gobierno no lo ha hecho. Y son este tipo de eventos los que hacen más ruido, crean revuelo, inyectan miedo y odio en una Ceuta en la que hacer vida normal es una tarea muy sencilla, por mucho que un pequeño círculo intente hacernos pensar lo contrario. Y quiero traer unos pocos ejemplos para ilustrar el ambiente de la ciudad. He paseado por las playas con asentamientos, por las calles y naves industriales, incluso de madrugada, sin sentir ninguna amenaza por parte de los migrantes. La única amenaza que sentí fue por parte de los grupos que patrullan y cazan invasores. Una noche un coche negro hizo el amago de venir a atropellarnos a unos migrantes menores y a mi, mientras hablábamos, tras haberles hecho una cura en la zona aledaña al supermercado Mercadona. Al compartir la matrícula y modelo con mis compañer@s resultó ser un coche que ya teníamos anotado en la lista de “vehículos agresivos”, o que nos persiguen. He visto a niños yendo al colegio con normalidad; las calles de Ceuta respiran calma. Los comercios funcionan sin interrupción, sin masificación, sin inseguridad. De hecho, el responsable de Mercadona en Ceuta ya se ha encargado de hacer otra política de segregación racial. Con militares custodiando las puertas, el personal de seguridad privada va decidiendo a quién se permite o no el paso, basándose en aspecto y morfología racial. Tuve conversaciones con much@s vecin@s. Pregunté si las imágenes de barricadas en las calles, quema de contenedores o destrucción de mobiliario público o escaparates habían sido una realidad. La respuesta fue negativa.

Entiendo el descontento ceutí. Entiendo la incomodidad y es legítimo el miedo a lo desconocido. Puedo entender, incluso, esa nostalgia de aquellos días cuando los ceutíes bajaban a la playa de su ciudad. No obstante, hace falta empatizar y ser consciente de que estamos hablando de problemas de diferente graduación. En esas playas hay seres humanos buscándose la vida y soñando con un futuro mejor, con poder llegar a Europa. Problema mayor, creo yo, que no poder tomar el sol este septiembre. Lamento todos los inconvenientes que esta situación pueda causar a nuestros vecinos del norte global, con sus privilegios europeos.

Sin embargo, nada justifica ni va a justificar en el futuro el uso de la violencia y la violación sistemática de los derechos humanos. El odio, el racismo, el fascismo y la violencia nunca son la respuesta. Invisibilizar al vulnerable y poner el foco en el opresor, tampoco. Ser humanos, tender la mano y tratar el tema con responsabilidad, rigurosa legalidad y pensando en que podríamos ser nosotros mismos mañana, viviendo una circunstancia similar, sí que es un buen camino.

Que podamos decirle al mundo entero que se puede hacer bien.
