title: Marche des Fiertés de Lyon 2026
content:
“Canicule et fascismes nous butent

 

! Pour les putes, pour les trans rentrons en résistance

 

!”




Cette année la Marche des Fiertés de Lyon aura lieu le 10 Octobre 2026. On se donne rendez-vous pour 

13h à l'arrêt “Gratte-Ciel” du Métro A 

 (Villeurbanne) pour revendiquer et célébrer nos luttes dans l'espace public

 

!




Les discours commenceront à 

13h

 et la Marche partira à 

14h

.




Le Parcours




Nous partirons de Gratte-Ciel à Villeurbanne pour suivre le Cours Emile Zola, puis le Cours Vitton et le Cours Franklin Roosevelt jusqu'à Foch. Nous remontrons ensuite le long du Rhône pour finir sur au parc de la Tête d'Or à la Porte des Enfants du Rhône.




Le parcours total fait 3.8km et se déroule sur route goudronnée tout le long. Nous avons noté très peu d'ombre jusqu'à Charpennes ainsi que peu de sanitaires publique tout le long du parcours.


Le parcours deviendra moins large après Masséna jusqu'au début du cours Franklin Roosevelt.




Un village associatif vous accueillera en fin de parcours sur la place.




Pour les participant·e·s




Accessibilité




 Un cortège Handi : revendicatif avec moins de bruit et port du masque obligatoire.

 Un cortège Calme avec peu de bruit et port du masque conseillé.

 Un véhicule accessible 

PMR

 mais pas 

UFR

, dans chacun de ces cortèges.

 Des casques anti-bruit, des bouchons d'oreilles et des masques 

FFP2

 seront à disposition dans ces cortèges et par les bénévoles.

 Les prises de parole seront interprétées en Langue des Signes Française et un·e interprète en 

LSF

 sera présent·e dans le cortège Handi durant toute la manifestation.




S'organiser




La matos classique à compléter en fonction de vos besoins

 

!




 de l'eau en bonne quantité

 

!

 de quoi grignoter.

 de quoi se protéger du soleil : chapeaux et crème solaire.

 vos meilleure tenues, maquillages et pancartes

 

!

 un masque 

FFP2

 

; le 

COVID

 est toujours là, prenons soin des un·e·s des autres

 

!




Sécurité




Tout au long du parcours, des personnes de l'organisation seront présentes pour encadrer la Marche. Elles seront identifiables par les manifestant.es en cas de besoin par un brassard de couleur et leur visuel.
















 




 













 




 













 







Une vingtaine de secouristes de la Croix-Rouge française ainsi que plusieurs streets médics suivront également le parcours et seront présent.es au départ et à l'arrivée. N'hésitez pas à crier “médic

 

!” en cas de besoin d'assistance médicale immédiate pour vous ou quelqu'un d'autre.


Évitez de rester seul·e et repartez accompagné·e du rassemblement si possible.




Bienséance




 On ne touche pas une personne (ni ses cheveux, ses vêtements,ses aides à la mobilité…) sans autorisation explicite de sa part.

 Ne prenez pas en photo ou vidéo les personnes sans autorisation de leur part. A défaut, floutez les visages avant de partager des images en ligne.

 Respectez l'autodétermination des personnes qui vous entourent, n'hésitez pas à demandez les pronoms qu'une personne utilise ou de faire attention à comment elle se genre.

 La Marche n'est pas le lieu pour les questions indiscrètes sur les pratiques sexuelles, les opérations ou les handicaps des personnes.




La non-mixité




Certains cortèges dans la Marche peuvent être en “non-mixité”.




La non-mixité est une pratique couramment employée par les groupes militants 

LGBTQ

+, anti-racistes, féministes ou syndicaux depuis les années 70. Elle permet de réserver ponctuellement des espaces spécifiques à des personnes concernées par un certain type d'oppression et de discrimination.


Dans le cadre de la Marche, la non-mixité sert notamment à visibiliser certaines revendications et groupes souvent invisibilisé·es.




Lorsque l'on fait partie de groupes opprimés, il peut parfois être difficile d'accéder à certains lieux et de s'y sentir à l'aise et en sécurité. De plus, Les comportements oppressifs ne sont pas forcément volontaires et conscients. Lorsque l'on est en situation de privilège, on ne perçoit pas le monde de la même manière. Il existe ainsi un besoin de la part des personnes concernées d'avoir des espaces réservés pour se sentir libres de parler, d'organiser des actions, de revendiquer des droits.




Il est donc important de savoir respecter les espaces dédiés à la non-mixité, et d'éviter d'y aller, même si vous estimez être bienveillant·e et déconstruit·e sur certains sujets. Il peut exister des exceptions, par exemple quand une personne concernée vous demande de l'accompagner pour ne pas se rendre seule dans un cortège. Dans ce cas, contactez les organisateur·trices pour en savoir plus et assurez-vous de respecter le fonctionnement du groupe.




Le mot clé ici : autodétermination




Nous vous faisons confiance pour savoir si vous pouvez, ou non, participer à l'un ou plusieurs des cortèges. Des rappels seront faits pour souligner quels endroits sont en mixité ou non et nous comptons sur vous pour y être attentif·ves et pour vous tourner vers nos bénévoles si vous avez le moindre doute. Iels sauront vous renseigner

 

! Enfin, ce n'est pas parce qu'une personne est concernée par l'une des non-mixité qu'elle est obligée de la rejoindre

 

! Elle le 

PEUT

 si cela lui fait plaisir mais elle peut aussi marcher dans le cortège mixte.




“Mais c'est de la discrimination inversée, non

 

?”




Non. Lorsque l'on est en situation de privilège sur un ou plusieurs critères, on ne rencontre pas les obstacles dénoncés par les personnes concernées, qui, elles, vivent une exclusion et des violences quotidiennes

 

!


Il n'est donc pas correct de parler de discrimination inversée.




La non-mixité n'est pas une fin en soi, mais une solution ponctuelle pour s'organiser afin de trouver le meilleur moyen d'abolir les discriminations vécues. De plus, il existe une grande majorité d'événements et d'espaces mixtes qui restent accessibles à toustes.




Consulter le site du collectif fierté en lutte : 

https://www.fierte.net/marche-des-fiertes-lyon-2026/

author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Mulheres são maioria das vítimas de violência política, mesmo sendo minoria das candidatas
content:
O primeiro turno da campanha eleitoral de 2026 durou 50 dias e registrou 134 episódios de violência política contra candidatos e candidatas, além de agentes políticos.

Um aumento de 11% em relação aos 121 casos registrados no mesmo período da eleição municipal de 2022.




Os 134 episódios representam um caso de violência política a cada nove horas de campanha.

 E apesar das mulheres serem apenas 35% do total de candidatos, elas foram a maioria (52%) das vítimas do primeiro turno, segundo o levantamento.




Os dados integram a 4ª edição da pesquisa Violência Política e Eleitoral no Brasil, realizada pelas organizações de direitos humanos Terra de Direitos e Justiça Global, que pesquisa o tema desde 2016. O levantamento foi divulgado nesta quarta, dia 7 de outubro.




A porcentagem de 

vítimas mulheres aumenta

 mais ainda quando a pesquisa separa apenas os casos envolvendo candidatas e candidatos. Dos 134 episódios de violência política durante o primeiro turno, 102 foram dirigidos a pessoas que disputavam o pleito. Desse total, 60 eram mulheres, quase 59% do total.




Para a coordenadora do Setor de Incidência da Terra de Direitos, Gisele Barbieri, “os dados trazem importantes achados para identificar os ambientes em que agentes políticos estão mais vulneráveis e pensar medidas de proteção. Quando eleitas, essas pessoas passam a ser vítimas de violências nos seus locais de atuação, seja no Parlamento ou no Executivo”, afirma.



















Machismo e misoginia se misturam nos casos de violência política




A pesquisa mostra que a violência política é marcada pela discriminação de gênero e raça. 

Quando se considera o universo completo de 70 casos de violência política contra mulheres, 45 casos envolveram machismo ou misoginia, nove envolveram racismo e cinco envolveram transfobia. Mulheres pretas foram vítimas de 25% dos casos de violência política medidos nesse primeiro turno.




A ameaça foi o tipo de violência política mais recorrente no período, com 64 casos registrados. Na sequência, aparecem 33 episódios de ofensa e 19 de agressão física. Também foram registrados 11 atentados, cinco casos de criminalização e dois assassinatos.




Mais da metade dos casos (71 ocorrências) aconteceu nas ruas, durante atividades públicas de campanha. O ambiente virtual concentrou 31,3% dos episódios.




Além disso, apenas candidatas sofreram ameaças de violência sexual. Em todos os sete casos, as vítimas eram mulheres.




“Enquanto os homens são atacados por sua atuação política, mulheres, pessoas negras e pessoas trans enfrentam também o racismo, o machismo e a transfobia que estruturam a sociedade brasileira”, afirmou em nota Glaucia Marinho, diretora-executiva da Justiça Global.




Policiais e outros agentes públicos foram a maioria dos autores




Em quase 20% dos casos o autor identificado da violência política era um agente público, incluindo parlamentares e forças de segurança. 

Até o encerramento da coleta de dados pelas organizações autoras da pesquisa, nenhum dos 134 episódios havia resultado em alguma punição efetiva, limitando-se a medidas cautelares de urgência determinadas pela Justiça Eleitoral.




A região Nordeste liderou o número de casos (48), seguido pelo Sudeste (38). Entre os estados, São Paulo lidera com 16 casos, seguido por Rio Grande do Norte (13), Minas Gerais (12) e Rio Grande do Sul (10).




A presença de policiais entre os autores de violência política já havia sido detectada também em 

levantamento

 realizado pela 

Agência Pública

 durante o primeiro turno.

author: anred
title: Los sepultureros de Gaza de Norman Finkelstein es una obra maestra
content:
Hay hechos sin consecuencias, libros sin seguimiento. ¿Qué haremos de esta monumental investigación y razonamiento que apela a nuestra conciencia y debería impulsarnos a la acción? Lo que está en juego es la esencia misma de la existencia civilizada, los valores de la Declaración Universal de los Derechos Humanos, los propósitos y principios de las Naciones Unidas. El genocidio en Gaza no es solo otro Holocausto monstruoso, es un espectáculo público. 

[1]

 El fracaso de las Naciones Unidas para detenerlo y la inacción de la mayoría de los estadounidenses y europeos nos hacen a todos cómplices del crimen, porque 

qui tacet consentire videtur 

. Si solo somos 

voyeurs 

de esta masacre en curso, tenemos, como mínimo, responsabilidad moral. Por Alfred de Zayas 




En los últimos 30 años, Norman Finkelstein nos ha brindado muchos libros brillantes, entre ellos 

Método y locura, Acuso, Saber demasiado, 

Gaza 

, 

Más allá de la desfachatez 

y 

La industria del Holocausto.




Este libro de más de 400 páginas documenta el colapso civilizatorio de las clases dominantes en Occidente, la traición a todos los valores humanistas, el rechazo demasiado público por parte de Israel del derecho internacional y la moral, con la complicidad, 

entre otros 

, de Estados Unidos, Reino Unido, Francia, Alemania y la Unión Europea.




Todo esto se ve acompañado por la cacofonía de los medios de comunicación convencionales orwellianos, que difunden noticias falsas, historia falsa y leyes falsas, especialmente con respecto a los palestinos como pueblo, a quienes se les representa erróneamente como “terroristas”, cuando poseen el derecho, reconocido en el derecho internacional, a resistir la colonización y la ocupación. 

[2]







Nelson Mandela también fue tildado de «terrorista», pero fue fundamental en la lucha por la liberación de su pueblo. Hoy todos reconocen que el fin del apartheid en Sudáfrica era algo que debió haberse hecho hace mucho tiempo. ¿Cuándo veremos el fin del apartheid en Israel y los Territorios Ocupados? Esto es lo que Jimmy Carter exigió en su libro 

Palestina: Paz, no apartheid 

. 

[3]




Los políticos occidentales y los principales medios de comunicación han invertido los papeles y han culpado a la víctima de su desgracia. Israel es el terrorista que practica el terrorismo de Estado y coloca trampas explosivas en los buscapersonas, como demostró de forma obscena el primer ministro israelí Benjamin Netanyahu durante su diatriba en la Asamblea General de la ONU el 24 de septiembre de 2026. 

[4]




Israel nació del terrorismo 

[5]

 contra británicos y palestinos, ha sido un Estado agresor desde su creación, en un sentido muy real un 

Estado fallido 

, porque no ha aprendido a vivir en paz con sus vecinos.




Israel ha atacado Líbano, Siria, Irak, Irán, Egipto, etc. En una infame operación de falsa bandera, incluso atacó el buque de inteligencia de la Armada de los Estados Unidos USS 

Liberty 

[6]

 en junio de 1967, matando a 34 marineros estadounidenses, en un intento fallido de involucrar a los Estados Unidos en la guerra de agresión de Israel.




Israel ha sido un estado paria desde su creación en 1948, e incluso antes.




El genocidio de Gaza no es más que una continuación de la intención criminal de establecer un «Gran Israel» anacrónico e imperialista en medio del mundo árabe y musulmán.




[Fuente: 

cartooningforpeace.org 

]




Sin duda, los gobiernos de Israel, Estados Unidos y la UE están moralmente en bancarrota. 

[7]




Lamentablemente, la 

percepción 

de la realidad es más determinante que la realidad misma. Dado que nuestras acciones están condicionadas por la información de la que disponemos, nuestro juicio se ve influenciado —e incluso subvertido— por las narrativas odiosas que recibimos de los principales medios de comunicación, y nuestras opiniones se distorsionan por el incesante discurso de odio y la propaganda contra los palestinos. Esto constituye una incitación al odio y a la violencia, en contravención del artículo 20 del Pacto Internacional de Derechos Civiles y Políticos. 

[8]




Los principales medios de comunicación difunden la versión israelí y suprimen las opiniones disidentes. No solo nos mienten, sino que nos privan de información crucial que cambia radicalmente la situación.




El público es manipulado, pero muchos se dejan manipular. Como escribió Julio César en 

De Bello Civili (II, 27, 2): «quae volumus, ea credimus libenter» 

(Creemos lo que queremos creer). O peor aún, como decían los romanos: 

«mundus vult decipi 

» (El mundo quiere que le mientan).




Precisamente porque nos han hecho creer que los israelíes son los «buenos» y los palestinos los terroristas, no hemos actuado con la suficiente rapidez contra las atrocidades cometidas contra los palestinos, los libaneses, los sirios, los iraníes, y no solo por Netanyahu, sino por todos los gobiernos israelíes desde 1948.




Los principales medios de comunicación no solo han influido, sino que han fabricado nuestro consentimiento cualificado 

[9]

 para el genocidio en curso contra los palestinos.




[Fuente: 

newyorkwarcrimes.com 

]




El nuevo libro de Finkelstein pretende ser una «llamada de atención», con la esperanza de que una nueva conciencia entre los jóvenes de muchos países conduzca a una enérgica resistencia contra el genocidio en curso y a la rendición de cuentas ante tribunales nacionales e internacionales.




Finkelstein nos impacta al hacernos comprender la magnitud de los crímenes y la responsabilidad ineludible de nuestros líderes, que han brindado y continúan brindando apoyo militar, político, económico, diplomático y propagandístico a un estado genocida.




Finkelstein demuestra la inacción de las Naciones Unidas, la corrupción de algunos funcionarios de la ONU que se han plegado a la narrativa israelí y han inventado excusas para los crímenes más graves.




Documenta la falta de profesionalismo de los «asesores especiales» del Secretario General, las «comisiones independientes» y muchos jueces politizados de la Corte Internacional de Justicia y la Corte Penal Internacional.




[Fuente: 

lemonde.fr 

]




La estructura del libro




Los historiadores menos conocidos, los académicos politizados y los periodistas suelen aplicar un enfoque deductivo a la escritura de la historia, partiendo de la conclusión deseada y trabajando hacia atrás para encontrar justificaciones.




Finkelstein se basa en el razonamiento inductivo, guiando al lector paso a paso a través de las causas profundas del conflicto palestino-israelí, la dialéctica del racismo y el apartheid.




Recopila y evalúa hechos irrefutables que conducen necesariamente a conclusiones bien fundamentadas: que Israel ha cometido y está cometiendo genocidio, que muchos países son cómplices de los crímenes, que los medios de comunicación han engañado al público y que las Naciones Unidas no solo han fallado a los palestinos, sino que han fallado al mundo.




El lector no tendrá dificultad alguna en seguir la lógica de Finkelstein, respaldada por hechos y argumentos irrefutables.




Avanza paso a paso desde un prólogo exhaustivo, seguido de una necesaria refutación de las “fantasías de violación” asociadas con la narrativa israelí de lo sucedido el 7 de octubre de 2023, 

[10]

 una dialéctica entre “Leyes de la guerra o lógica del genocidio”, el análisis perspicaz “¿Agente libre o agente extranjero?” y la manipulación de la opinión pública a través de “Reescritura del presente”, un epílogo inquietante sobre el significado de todo ello y un epílogo final y desgarrador.




En el apéndice, añade un análisis exhaustivo del fracaso de la Corte Penal Internacional a la hora de investigar los crímenes israelíes relacionados con el secuestro ilegal reiterado en aguas internacionales de las flotillas humanitarias que transportaban medicamentos y alimentos esenciales a la población asediada de Gaza.




Como profesor de derecho internacional durante más de 30 años, puedo confirmar que las acciones de Israel constituyeron el delito de piratería, así como múltiples violaciones de la Convención de las Naciones Unidas sobre el Derecho del Mar y el uso ilícito de la fuerza, en contravención del artículo 2(4) de la Carta de la ONU. Resulta difícil creer que la entonces Fiscal Jefe de la CPI, Fatou Bensouda, se negara en tres ocasiones a iniciar una investigación sobre los asesinatos ocurridos durante el abordaje de la flotilla, lo que implica violaciones de los artículos 7 y 8 del Estatuto de Roma. ¿Fue chantajeada por Israel? Ella y otros funcionarios de la ONU tienen muchos trapos sucios.




Fatou Bensouda [Fuente: 

icc-cpi.int 

]




A lo largo del libro, Finkelstein utiliza hábilmente tablas en las que contrasta la ley con su interpretación, contrasta los hallazgos fácticos de las comisiones con sus evaluaciones a veces incomprensibles, contrasta los informes con su mal uso por parte de los tribunales y contrasta las narrativas israelíes con el lenguaje utilizado, por ejemplo, por la jueza Julia Sebutinde 

[11]

 (p. 103) en la CIJ y la fiscal jefe Fatou Bensouda 

[12]

 en la CPI.




A veces las tablas constan de tres columnas, por ejemplo, contrastando las fuentes citadas por el juez Sebutinde con las presentadas por Israel y Sudáfrica (pág. 109), contrastando la solicitud de Sudáfrica con la respuesta de Israel y los comentarios del juez Sebutinde (pág. 119), y contrastando las medidas indicadas por el tribunal con la respuesta del juez Barak y las observaciones del juez Sebutinde (122).




También incluye tablas que resumen las conclusiones principales de las sentencias y opiniones consultivas (p. 169). Este método es sumamente revelador del nivel de disfunción en la CPI y la CIJ. Se puede concluir con seguridad: 

quod erat demonstrandum 

.




El análisis que hace Finkelstein de los diversos informes de las comisiones especiales, las opiniones consultivas pertinentes de la Corte Internacional de Justicia y los argumentos presentados por Sudáfrica en el caso pendiente 

Sudáfrica contra 

Israel 

son invaluables para comprender lo que está sucediendo en la corte y por qué la CIJ está demorando el proceso y no emite un fallo expedito que determine que Israel ha cometido y está cometiendo genocidio.




Cabe recordar que la Convención para la Prevención y la Sanción del Delito de Genocidio de 1948 tenía como objetivo principal 

prevenir 

el genocidio. A pesar de la enorme cantidad de documentación sobre el genocidio y las declaraciones públicas de numerosos funcionarios y militares israelíes, la CIJ sigue demorando su resolución. No cabe duda de que se han cumplido los criterios de los artículos 1 a 3 de la Convención. Sin embargo, la CIJ permite que el genocidio continúe.




Finkelstein también nos recuerda que, hace 15 años, el juez sudafricano Richard Goldstone (judío y sionista) emitió un informe sobre la Operación Plomo Fundido de Israel (2008-2009) y concluyó que las acciones de Israel constituían crímenes de guerra y crímenes de lesa humanidad.




Como suele ocurrir en el pasado, los jueces que expresan opiniones incómodas son acosados ​​por turbas. Esto lo sabemos por los jueces antimafia en Italia, algunos de los cuales han sido asesinados.




Goldstone también fue amenazado y, el 1 de abril de 2011, lanzó una bomba al retractarse del informe en un artículo de opinión publicado en 

el Washington Post 

. No consultó con sus colegas de la comisión de investigación de la ONU, sino que optó por un artículo de opinión para intentar distanciarse unilateralmente de las bien fundamentadas conclusiones de la Comisión. Finkelstein concluye acertadamente que Goldstone «deshonró su profesión y a sí mismo» (p. 295).




Juez Richard Goldstone [Fuente: 

theguardian.com 

]




La observación de Finkelstein en el epílogo titulado 

“Réquiem: una declaración de guerra contra Gaza. Resolución 2803 (2025 

) del Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas” 

[13]

 en la página 299 y siguientes puede sorprender a algunos lectores.




Como veterano con 50 años de experiencia trabajando en las Naciones Unidas en diversas funciones —como abogado sénior, secretario del Comité de Derechos Humanos, jefe del Departamento de Peticiones, consultor, experto independiente, relator, presidente de organizaciones no gubernamentales con estatus consultivo ante la ONU— comprendo plenamente la conclusión de Finkelstein, aunque la habría expresado de forma menos tajante, porque sigo aferrándome a mi optimismo inveterado y a la esperanza inquebrantable de que la ONU pueda reformarse y que, algún día, cumpla con los principios y propósitos establecidos en la Carta de las Naciones Unidas.




Alfred de Zayas (izquierda) y Norman Finkelstein (derecha) en Nueva York. [Fuente: Foto cortesía de Alfred de Zayas]




En la página 308, Finkelstein señala: «La Resolución 2803 implicó directamente al Consejo de Seguridad en el genocidio en curso. También condenó al martirio eterno a los atormentados y torturados habitantes de Gaza, o a aquellos que no fueron asesinados… Las manos alzadas en silencio para ratificar la resolución anunciaron su fin. De ahora en adelante, la causa de la Justicia deberá reconstituirse sobre una nueva base. Hay que decirlo sin rehuir —porque es la Verdad—, pero también conscientes de la gravedad del veredicto: Después del 17 de noviembre de 2025, la ONU es un cadáver en descomposición» (p. 308).




Palabras duras. De hecho, el Consejo de Seguridad, al dar la bienvenida a la absurda “Junta de Paz” para Gaza del presidente Donald Trump, le dio la espalda a cientos de resoluciones del Consejo de Seguridad (incluida la Resolución 242 del 22 de noviembre de 1967), 

[14]

 la Asamblea General, el ECOSOC, la Comisión de Derechos Humanos, el Consejo de Derechos Humanos y numerosos fallos de la Corte Internacional de Justicia, incluidas tres opiniones consultivas sobre cuestiones israelí-palestinas.




[Fuente: 

newyorker.com 

]




Resulta inconcebible cómo se propuso y aprobó semejante resolución. La pregunta sigue siendo por qué China y Rusia no vetaron esta aberración. La resolución es claramente incompatible con la Carta de las Naciones Unidas y debería considerarse nula 

desde su origen 

, pues traiciona los propósitos y principios de la Carta y pretende subcontratar y delegar el proceso de paz al presidente Trump, una función que corresponde exclusivamente al Consejo de Seguridad. ¿Acaso la ONU está cometiendo deliberadamente un suicidio político?




Cualquier Estado miembro de las Naciones Unidas puede solicitar a la Corte Internacional de Justicia que emita una opinión consultiva sobre la ilegalidad de la Resolución 2803. Lamentablemente, al momento de redactar esta reseña, ningún Estado ha tenido el valor de hacerlo. Sin embargo, el 19 de noviembre de 2025, la Relatora Especial del Consejo de Derechos Humanos sobre Palestina, la profesora Francesca Albanese, 

[15]

 emitió una contundente declaración en los medios de comunicación rechazando la resolución por 

contraria a la ley 

y afirmando: «Este es un momento crucial… La comunidad internacional no debe permitir que el futuro de Gaza —ni el futuro del pueblo palestino— se decida sin su participación ni consentimiento. Solo un enfoque basado en la justicia, la legalidad y la autodeterminación puede conducir a una paz genuina».




Francesca Albanese [Fuente: 

thenation.com 

]




En su epílogo, Finkelstein nos dice: «Este libro fue escrito para desenmascarar las mentiras y restaurar la verdad. No salvará vidas. El genocidio en Gaza es demasiado avanzado. ¿Es entonces inútil el libro? Para los muertos, sí. Pero para los vivos, no. La exigencia planteada en el prólogo del libro sigue vigente: no solo los perpetradores en Israel, sino también sus cómplices en las altas esferas —todos ellos manchados de sangre— deben rendir cuentas» (p. 297).




Observaciones generales




Una y otra vez, tuve que coincidir con la descripción de Finkelstein sobre el malestar crónico en la Secretaría de la ONU, la Asamblea General, el Consejo de Seguridad y otros órganos de la ONU. Por mi propia experiencia en la ONU, puedo confirmar que «es imposible ignorar que la política siempre se interpone en las investigaciones de la ONU. Cuanto más cerca del poder se encuentra una facción, más lejos está de la verdad; mientras que cuanto más lejos del poder, más independiente es y más cerca puede estar de la verdad». (p. 89)




El abuso de poder por parte de la Secretaría de la ONU 

, que excede sus facultades legales, 

siempre resulta inquietante, a veces incluso escandaloso. Como Experto Independiente de la ONU, puedo confirmar los intentos de la Secretaría de manipular mis informes, banalizarlos y dictar lo que debía escribir. Rechacé todos estos intentos y escribí sobre algunos de ellos en mi libro 

La industria de los derechos humanos 

.




Sí, Occidente ha instrumentalizado a la ONU. Tarde o temprano, la Mayoría Global se asegurará de que la ONU sea finalmente descolonizada. En una docena de casos, ideólogos de la Secretaría de la ONU se negaron a publicar algunos de mis comunicados de prensa, 

[16]

 los cuales luego publiqué en mi blog indicando que la Secretaría de la ONU los había censurado.




Por desgracia, la situación es así de grave. Como escribió Juvenal en su Sexta Sátira: « ¿Quién vigilará a los guardianes? 

» 

(versículos 347-348). ¿Qué hacemos cuando las instituciones creadas para defender nuestros derechos nos traicionan?




Con frecuencia, Finkelstein tiene que recordarnos artículos pertinentes del Estatuto de la Corte Internacional de Justicia. El artículo 19 estipula: “Cada miembro de la Corte, antes de asumir sus funciones, hará una declaración solemne en audiencia pública en la que manifestará que ejercerá sus poderes con imparcialidad y conciencia” (p. 97).




Esto resulta necesario ante la conducta poco profesional de algunos magistrados de la CIJ, entre ellos Thomas Buergenthal, Georg Nolte, Julia Sebutinde y Joan Donoghue. La falta de ética del magistrado alemán y las acrobacias lógicas que emplea en sus opiniones y declaraciones individuales perjudican a la Corte, independientemente de su elegancia estilística.




Decir que 

Gravediggers 

es una 

obra maestra 

es quedarse corto. Los hechos son fascinantes, la metodología rigurosa, las fuentes impecables, el análisis implacable y los argumentos convincentes.




Con frecuencia, tenía que dejar el libro a un lado, porque los hechos eran demasiado perturbadores, las implicaciones morales demasiado inquietantes. Me invadió una profunda indignación, una frustración ante la hipocresía de nuestros líderes, la convicción de que debemos ganar la guerra de la información.




Una víctima de los crímenes israelíes.

title: Ticaret Bakanı Bolat'tan "Fondan 360 milyon lira kazandı" iddiasına yalanlama
content:
Gazeteci Murat Ağırel, Yeni Parti İzmir Milletvekili Ümit Özlale'nin gündeme getirdiği "babasının fon hesabına 470 milyon lira yatırıp 830 milyon lira çeken bakan"ın Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat olduğunu iddia etti. Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat, iddiayı yalanladı.

Yeni Parti İzmir Milletvekili Ümit Özlale, TBMM Genel Kurulu'nda Cumhurbaşkanı Yardımcısı Cevdet Yılmaz'a fon vurgununa ilişkin bir bakanın babasının hesabına 470 milyon lira yatırıp 830 milyon lirayla fondan çıkıp çıkmadığını ve Özel Kalemi Fatih Kılınç'ın kapalı fonda parası olup olmadığını sormuştu.

Yılmaz ise Özlale'nin gündeme getirdiği iddialara ilişkin, özel kalem müdürü Fatih Kılınç'ın 7 milyon lira yatırdığı fonda büyük kayıp yaşadığını belirterek, "Yatırım yapan herkes suçluysa, hepsini birden mahkemeye gönderelim. Böyle şey olmaz" yanıtını vermişti.

Cumhuriyet yazarı Murat Ağırel, Sözcü TV'de fon satın alan bakanın Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat olduğunu iddia ederek "Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat’ın fon satın aldığı ve kriz patlamadan önce sattığı ortaya çıktı" dedi.

Ticaret Bakanı Ömer Bolat, fon soruşturmaları başlamadan önce yatırım hesabını kapatarak parasını çektiği iddiasını reddetti ve iddiayı dile getirenler hakkında hukuki yollara başvuracağını açıkladı.

Bolat, sosyal medya açıklamasında, ailesine ait 37,8 milyon liralık tasarrufun 26 Şubat 2024’te Hedef Yatırım Portföy bünyesinde kira sertifikası niteliğindeki bir yatırım aracına yatırıldığını ve halen aynı hesapta bulunduğunu söyledi.

Sözcü TV yayınında gazeteci Murat Ağırel’in dile getirdiği iddiaları “iftira” olarak nitelendiren Bolat, 16 Eylül 2026’da başlayan soruşturmalar öncesinde veya sonrasında hesabın kapatılmadığını, hesap üzerinden hisse senedi alım satımı yapılmadığını belirtti. Bolat, yatırımın mal beyanında kayıtlı olduğunu ve yetkili kurumların denetimine açık bulunduğunu ifade etti.

Bu akşam Sözcü TV yayınında 16 Eylül’den beri yürütülen 7 kuruluşa ait fon soruşturmaları ile alakalı olarak şahsımı hedef alan ve “fonda parası olup, krizden önce çekti, hesabı kapattı”, “fona 400 koydu, krizden önce çekti, 800 aldı” şeklinde başta Murat Ağırel’in haysiyetsizce iftirasına konu olan açıklamalar konusunda, kamuoyunun doğru bilgilendirilmesi ve tümüyle mesnetsiz, yalan yanlış iddialara açıklık getirilmesi amacıyla aşağıdaki hususları ifade etmek istiyorum:

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Çeşme Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı 16 aydır tutukluydu: Tahliye edildiği gün yine gözaltına alındı
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesine (İBB) yönelik yürütülen soruşturma kapsamında yaklaşık 16 aydır Silivri Cezaevi’nde iddianamesiz tutuklu bulunan Çeşme Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Onur Gülin, hakim karşısına çıktığı ilk duruşmada tahliye edildi. Ancak Gülin, aynı gün Çeşme Belediyesine düzenlenen eş zamanlı operasyonda hakkında verilen yeni gözaltı kararı nedeniyle özgürlüğüne kavuşamadan İzmir İl Jandarma Komutanlığı’na sevk edilecek.

Onur Gülin, 20 Mayıs 2025 tarihinde eşi Yelda Gülin’in ameliyatı için bulunduğu hastaneden gözaltına alınarak tutuklanmıştı. Kasım 2025’te hazırlanan yaklaşık 4 bin sayfalık ana İBB iddianamesinde yer almayan Gülin, süreç içerisinde kısa süreli bir tahliye kararı alsa da savcılığın itirazı üzerine Silivri Cezaevi’nde kalmaya devam etti. İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nın ana dosyadan ayırarak 21 Temmuz 2026’da hazırladığı ek iddianamede, Gülin ve beraberindeki sanıklara İBB Basın Yayın ve Halkla İlişkiler Daire Başkanlığı ihalelerine ilişkin "ihaleye fesat karıştırma", "rüşvet" ve "kamu zararından dolandırıcılık" suçlamaları yöneltildi.

İstanbul 7. Ağır Ceza Mahkesi’nde dün görülen davanın ilk duruşmasında mahkeme heyeti, aralarında Onur Gülin’in de bulunduğu 5 sanığın tahliyesine karar verirken bir sanığın tutukluluğunun devamına hükmetti.

İzmir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Cemil Tugay'ın AKP'ye geçtiği günün sabahında dün Çeşme Belediyesine yönelik 12 kişi hakkında "suç örgütü kurma", "rüşvet", "irtikap" ve "resmi belgede sahtecilik" suçlamalarıyla başlatılan soruşturmanın ihbarla başladığı öğrenildi.

Onur Gülin'in yarım kalan tahliye sevinci ise ilk değil. 4 Aralık’taki aylık tutukluluk incelemesinde aralarında Ekrem İmamoğlu’nun şoförlerinin de bulunduğu 21 kişilik gruptan Gülin dahil 19 kişi hakkında tahliye kararı verildi.

İzmir’den gelen ailesi ve iki küçük kızıyla cezaevi kapısında buluşmayı bekleyen Gülin, savcılığın jet hızıyla yaptığı itiraz üzerine cezaevinden çıkamadan, gece yarısı jandarma karakoluna götürülerek 9 saat içinde yeniden tutuklandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Man injured after shooting in Pangnirtung, deputy mayor says
content:
Pangnirtung is in shock after a shooting Tuesday afternoon injured a man, says deputy Mayor Markus Wilcke.




Wilcke said he heard shots Tuesday at around 4 p.m. and that the RCMP has since made an arrest.




“A lot of people were impacted, many of them children,” the deputy mayor said in an interview. “Pretty well everybody was impacted, directly or indirectly.”




He said the shots came from near the harbour. The suspect then entered residential streets and the area near the hamlet office.




“The RCMP did a good job and everyone is safe now,” Wilcke said.




Nunatsiaq News asked the RCMP about the incident but was told information about it would be available Thursday.




Wilcke says the hamlet will update the community through public statements and that counselling services will be available.
















He also said the community can expect a public meeting within the next few days to discuss what actions are needed to respond and prevent similar incidents in the future.

title: La transphobie de l'empire Křetínský avec l'association « Toutes des Femmes » dans Médias et antifascisme
content:
Texte d'annonce de l'épisode du vendredi 9 octobre 2026 de l'émission «

 

Médias et antifascisme

 

» diffusé tous les deuxièmes vendredis du mois sur la station Radio Libertaire (89.4 

FM

 en Île-de-France et anarchiste.info/radio/libertaire).




Nous recevons vendredi 9 octobre prochain à 11h30 l'association «

 

Toutes des Femmes

 

» (

https://toutesdesfemmes.fr/

) pour évoquer notamment le colloque de «

 

l'Observatoire de la Petite Sirène

 

» le 16 octobre au Palais du Luxembourg à Paris : 

https://www.observatoirepetitesirene.org/colloque-2026

. Il devait se tenir initialement le 22 juin dernier au Collège de France mais a été annulé par la direction de cet établissement.




La «

 

Haute-Commissaire à l'Enfance de la République

 

» Sarah El-Haïry devait d'ailleurs y participer. Cet événement est finalement rendu possible par la sénatrice Jacqueline Eustache-Brinio du parti «

 

Les Républicains

 

» qui chapeaute son déroulement.




Eustache-Brinio est de plus l'auteure de la proposition de loi sur la «

 

prise en charge des mineurs en questionnement de genre

 

». Cette loi est actuellement bloquée en commission des affaires sociales à l'Assemblée Nationale en attendant les recommandations à son sujet de la Haute Autorité de Santé (

HAS

) dont nous parlions dans notre épisode du 12 décembre dernier : 

https://www.anarchiste.info/radio/libertaire/emission/medias-et-antifascisme/2025/12/12/

.




Ce climat nous préoccupe du fait par exemple de son instrumentalisation par le magazine hebdomadaire Marianne acheté en 2018 par le milliardaire tchèque Daniel Křetínský. L'empire Křetínský s'évertue en effet à s'acharner sur des associations comme le Planning Familial ou OUTrans.




Accusations d'islamisme, d'entrisme, de transgenrisme, de sécessionnisme, de séparatisme ou de radicalisme, tout est bon pour les dénoncer. L'une des toiles de fond de ces attaques est l'obligation pour Marianne de surmonter un redressement judiciaire comme nous l'abordons dans notre texte sorti dans le numéro 1885 du journal mensuel de la Fédération Anarchiste «

 

Le Monde Libertaire

 

» : 

https://paris-luttes.info/l-institut-iliade-bollore-sterin-21023

.




Křetínský constitue d'autant plus un danger qu'il possède la Fnac et le groupe Editis qui comprend en tout 55 maisons d'édition. Il dirige aussi les «

author: Unknown
title: AKP, Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya’ya kapıyı gösterdi
content:
AKP, fon soruşturmasında adı gündeme geldikten sonra Genel Başkan Yardımcılığı görevinden ayrılan eski Aile ve Sosyal Politikalar Bakanı Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya’yı partiden uzaklaştırdığını açıkladı. 




AKP Genel Sekreteri Eyyüp Kadir İnan, Kaya’nın artık parti üyesi ve mensubu olmadığını açıkladı. İnan, kararın parti yönetiminin iradesiyle alındığını da açıkça ortaya koydu:




“AK Parti olarak Cumhurbaşkanımızın talimatları doğrultusunda, yetkili kurullarımızın tespiti doğrultusunda zaten gereken işlemleri yaptık. Bugün Fatma Betül Hanım partimizin üyesi değildir, partimizin mensubu da değildir.”




İnan’ın açıklaması, Kaya’nın eşi İlyas Kaya ile birlikte aynı gün İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı’nda “şüpheli” sıfatıyla ifade vermesinden birkaç saat sonra geldi.




İhraç mı, zorunlu istifa mı?




AKP yönetimi, Kaya’nın parti üyeliğinin hangi usulle sona erdiğini açıklamadı.




İnan’ın “Cumhurbaşkanımızın talimatları” ve “gereken işlemleri yaptık” sözleri, ayrılığın Kaya’nın kendi tercihiyle gerçekleşmediğini gösteriyor. Ancak Kaya hakkında disiplin kurulu tarafından kesin çıkarma kararı verilip verilmediği ya da kendisinden üyelikten istifa etmesinin istenip istenmediği de kamuoyuna açıklanmadı. 




AKP’ye yakın Star gazetesi dahil çok sayıda yayın, gelişmeyi “Kaya AKP’den ihraç edildi” diye duyurdu. Star da haberini İnan’ın aynı açıklamasına dayandırdı; ayrıca bir disiplin kurulu kararına göndermede bulunmadı. 




Kaya’nın AKP üyeliğinin parti yönetiminin müdahalesinden sonra sona erdiği yönetim açısından netleşmiş görünse de, bunun AKP tüzüğünün ve disiplin yönetmeliğinin hangi hükmünün ihlali nedeniyle gerçekleştirildiği açık değil. 




11 gün önce yalnızca görevlerinden ayrılmıştı




Kaya 26 Eylül’de AKP’de yürüttüğü görevlerden “affını” istemişti.




Kaya açıklamasında, hakkındaki iddiaların araştırılması sırasında bulunduğu makamın tartışmaya konu edilmemesi gerektiğini söylemiş ve “yürütmekte olduğum tüm görevlerimden affımı Sayın Genel Başkanımızdan istedim” demişti. AA ve TRT de gelişmeyi “partideki tüm görevlerinden affını istedi” şeklinde duyurmuştu.




Böylece Kaya, 26 Eylül’de AKP yönetimindeki görevlerini bırakmasına rağmen parti üyesi olarak kalmıştı.




AKP Genel Sekreteri’nin 7 Ekim’deki açıklaması bu statünün de sona erdiği anlamına geliyor.




Önce TMSF’ye ödeme, ardından savcılık




Partinin Kaya’ya kapıyı göstermesine giden süreç son üç günde hızlandı.




Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya ile eşi İlyas Kaya’nın dondurulan hesaplarındaki yatırımlarının anapara dışındaki bölümünü, 5 Ekim’de Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu’nun (TMSF) “isteğe bağlı iade hesabına” gönderdikleri açıklandı.




İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı, SPK’nın “gönüllü ödeme” yöntemi kapsamında Kaya çiftinin yaptığı başvuru üzerine transferin gerçekleştirilmesine izin verdi. Kamuoyuna açıklanan bilgilerde ne kadar para iade edildiği belirtilmedi.




İki gün sonra Kaya ve eşi İstanbul Adliyesi’ne çağrıldı.




İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı Terörizmin Finansmanı ve Aklama Suçları Soruşturma Bürosu tarafından yürütülen sermaye piyasası soruşturması kapsamında Betül Kayan Saya ve eşi savcıya “şüpheli” sıfatıyla ifade verdi. Yaklaşık bir saat süren işlemlerin ardından Kaya çifti adliyeden ayrıldı.




Reuters da Adalet Bakanlığı kaynaklarına dayanarak Kaya ile eşinin soruşturmada şüpheli olarak yer aldığını ve Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu’nun (SPK) haklarında Sermaye Piyasası Kanunu kapsamında suç duyurusunda bulunmasının beklendiğini bildirdi.




AKP’nin siyasi mesafesi büyüdü




AKP Genel Sekreteri, Kaya’nın artık parti mensubu olmadığını duyurduktan sonra soruşturmayla ilgili siyasi değerlendirme yapmaktan da kaçındı:







“Geri kalan konu hukuki bir konudur, ona da yargı karar verir.”







(AEK)

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Has Granted $6B in Contracts to Arms Makers His Sons Have Invested In
content:
Trump has previously said that his children have “inside information” about government actions.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Military contractors with investments from President Donald Trump’s sons have raked in billions of dollars in government deals and contracts since June 2025, when their venture capital company first obtained a major stake in military technology company Anduril, new reporting finds.

Last year, 1789 Capital, of which Donald Trump Jr. is a partner, invested $2.5 billion into Anduril. According to an analysis of the government’s public contracts by ABC, since then, Anduril has been awarded 135 contracts from the U.S. government, with $1.8 billion of it having been paid out thus far.

In all, military contractors with backing from Donald Trump Jr. or Eric Trump have gotten $6 billion in “active or promised government contracts,” the analysis found.

The Pentagon and a spokesperson for the two brothers denied any impropriety. “No company receives preferential treatment. The War Department always looks for solutions to benefit the warfighter, not any pre-selected entity. Outside affiliations, investors, or political connections play absolutely no role in the Department’s funding decisions,” a Pentagon official said.

However, ABC uncovered several instances in which companies were granted Pentagon contracts for the first time after Donald Trump Jr. or Eric Trump joined their teams.

A drone manufacturer named Unusual Machines was granted a contract for 3,500 motors, and potentially 20,000 more, in 2025, months after Donald Trump Jr. was named an adviser for the company. And another drone company, Powerus, got its first Pentagon contract just one month after the two brothers were listed as “notable investors” for the company in March 2026.

A Pentagon spokesperson defended the contracts, saying that “defense procurement is merit-based” and that “neither Donald Trump Jr. nor Eric Trump is an advisor to Powerus, and neither is involved in the company’s day-to-day business.”

“Their interest is indirect, held through American Ventures, an investor in the company,” the spokesperson told the outlet.

Previous reports have found instances of companies being granted large investments after receiving backing from 1789 Capital.

At an event in Maryland on Tuesday, Trump announced a new partnership with Anduril, billionaire Palmer Luckey’s autonomous military technology company, in its project to build a new shipyard called “Arsenal- 2.” The company will be providing a $3.7 billion investment into building the factory in Maryland, while the Navy will contribute $2.9 billion, he announced.

Bizarrely, Trump said that the public will be receiving “a 40 percent stake” in the shipyard, which he called “proof to our commitment to ensuring the shipyard’s enduring success.” It’s unclear what he meant by this, as the shipyard is being paid for by public money — and the $2.9 billion contributed by the Navy is actually more than 40 percent of the project’s $6.6 billion price tag.

At the event, Trump praised Luckey as a friend and a “brilliant guy.” Last week, Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth announced that Luckey will help lead a new military task force called “Project Meridian,” which is tasked with shaping the future of warfare.

Democrats have previously launched efforts to probe potentially corrupt deals involving 1789 Capital’s investments. In August, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Maryland), ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee, opened an investigation into the firm, pointing out that it grew from managing $150 million in investment capital to over $3 billion since Donald Trump Jr. was named a partner just days after his dad was elected president.

“Whether government decisions and contracts are being manipulated to ensure that your firm and the President’s family get a cut of the action or your firm and the President’s family are being given advance insider information about those forthcoming decisions and contracts (or more likely both), these practices constitute clear violations of laws banning governmental conflicts of interest, political insider trading, exploitation of public office for financial gain and fraud,” Raskin said.

In July, Trump openly bragged that his status as the president gives his children access to “inside information.”

“Almost anything they do, if they want to buy a truck, if they want to buy, you know, they buy an energy efficient truck, they have inside information,” he said.

We now have three full months of data since Google changed its search to feature AI results. The numbers are worse than we anticipated. Overall readership that comes to Truthout through Google is down 54 percent against last year. The number of new readers who discover Truthout via Google searches is down 49 percent, and returning users from Google are down 51 percent.

We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We anticipate a loss of roughly $500,000 in online revenue as a result of this massive traffic plunge in the next year alone.

The only way we can keep publishing is with strong reader support. We are asking you to start a monthly donation to Truthout today — anything you can do, whether $5 or $25, makes a difference.

author: Lilli Akpaleeapik
title: Boil water advisory issued for Taloyoak
content:
Nunavut’s Health Department issued a boil water advisory for Taloyoak due to the mechanical failure of a pump at the water treatment plant.




Any water used for consumption must be brought to a rolling boil for a minimum of one minute, either on the stove or with a kettle that does not have an automatic shut off, according to the advisory.




The advisory applies to water for drinking, preparing infant formulas, making juice or ice cubes, washing produce, cooking and brushing teeth.




Residents are also reminded that a camp stove should be used outdoors to avoid the risk of carbon monoxide poisoning.




The Health Department will notify community members when the boil advisory has been lifted.

author: Unknown
title: Palestinian Arts Workers Call for Solidarity
content:
Palestinian cultural workers living through apartheid, occupation, and genocide are 

calling for solidarity

 from their counterparts abroad.




Not every artist has as large a platform as rapper Macklemore, children’s TV star Miss Rachel, or country singer Zach Bryan—who wore a “Free Palestine” shirt last weekend while playing a packed show at the same stadium where billionaire Robert Kraft had barred Macklemore for saying those words—but there’s plenty that artists and art workers can do to end complicity in Israel’s ongoing atrocities.




We as Palestinians have long decried Israel’s war crimes and crimes against humanity. Now the 

Palestinian Performing Arts Network

 (PPAN), representing hundreds of Palestinian dancers, actors, musicians, playwrights, and circus performers, has 

outlined

 four ways that U.S. arts unions can lend solidarity:




1. Reject the blacklisting and censorship of members who speak out on behalf of Palestinian rights.




For example, British Actors’ Equity 

passed a motion in the UK’s Trade Union Congress

, representing 5 million workers, affirming the right of artists to “critique institutions and bring attention to issues through overtly political art without fear of censorship or losing their public funding.”




In the U.S., over 700 entertainment industry union members signed a 2024 

open letter calling on SAG-AFTRA

 to back a ceasefire, protect members from blacklisting, and condemn the targeting of journalists.




2. Refuse to work with institutions and corporations—such as venues, festivals, publishers, broadcasters, and foundations—that are verifiably complicit in Israel’s crimes against Palestinians, and divest union funds from such corporations.




In fall 2025, over 5,500 film industry workers 

signed such a pledge

. Earlier that year, Norway’s actors union Norsk Skuespillerforbund (NSF) 

recommended that its members

 “reject work and collaboration with Israeli cultural institutions that operate in violation of the Palestinian cultural boycott.”




3. Exclude Israel from international labor federations

 such as the International Federation of Actors (FIA) and International Federation of Musicians (FIM).




4. Pressure governments to compel Israel to end its genocide and apartheid through lawful sanctions.




“Historically, including in the struggle that ended apartheid in South Africa, organized labor has been the working person’s leverage,” the PPAN said. “[Unions are] a powerful force for peace and justice when governments fail.” 




UNION MOVES




Drawing inspiration from the global movement to end South African apartheid, Palestinian unions and workers have consistently 

called on unions worldwide

 to use sanctions, boycotts, and divestment (BDS) campaigns as pressure points to end Israel’s genocide and occupation.




The United Auto Workers has 

endorsed divestment

 from Israel bonds and acted on it. Since 2023, a smattering of Palestine solidarity groups across unions have pushed for pension fund divestment, joined other unions abroad to 

block arms to Israel

 at international docks, and 

protested complicit corporations>

.




The United Auto Workers, the United Electrical Workers (UE), National Nurses United, and the Painters have also thrown their support behind an 

end to military funding

 to Israel and 

divestment

. UE also became the first national union to endorse the BDS movement.




Some rank and filers have been forming loose solidarity networks like 

Entertainment Labor for Palestine

, 

Purple Up for Palestine

 (SEIU), 

CWA4Palestine

, and 

IATSE Members for Palestine

.




Union members can find resources like 

Ethical Investment

 and 

Ethical Procurement Policies

 to keep union pension funds and vendor contracts out of companies complicit in human rights abuses anywhere, including Palestine.




In the UK, on September 8, British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called illegal settlements in the West Bank “ethnic cleansing,” as part of the announcement of sanctions against Israel. Shortly thereafter, the UK’s Trade Union Congress, representing 5 million workers, 

endorsed the Palestinian-led BDS movement

.




ATROCITIES ONGOING




The calls come as Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza reaches horrifying numbers. At least 

80,000 Palestinians had been killed by Israel

 as of January 2025, which is likely an undercount as Israel’s destruction in Gaza is so extensive that it has obstructed our ability to even count our dead. Israeli settlers’ land theft in the West Bank has 

drawn condemnation from 12 countries

 including Canada, France, and Britain. 




Over the past few years international human rights organizations and institutions from the United Nations and the International Court of Justice to 

Amnesty International

 and Israeli human rights organization 

B’Tselem

 have corroborated what Palestinians have been saying for years—determining that Israel is committing the crimes of apartheid, illegal occupation, and genocide. 




Since 2023, a majority of the U.S. public has consistently 

supported ending military aid to Israel

. Yet tens of billions of our taxpayer dollars continue to flow to Israel to fund its military actions, instead of being used to meet workers’ needs. Meanwhile working families in the U.S. face cuts to education, health care, and housing.




This is one practical basis for solidarity between workers here and in Palestine. Our tax dollars shouldn’t enable Israel’s war crimes. They should go to ensuring a dignified life for all, through more funding for social services, community needs, affordable housing, and accessible health care. 




Mona Abhari is the North America labor organizer for the Boycott, Sanctions and Divestment Movement.

author: Rizomatica
title: Escuela Popular Campesina José Bengoa Cabello: Diez años sembrando educación popular desde Curaco de Vélez
content:
La Escuela Popular Campesina José Bengoa Cabello de Curaco de Vélez, Chiloé, celebró sus diez años de vida con dos jornadas que reunieron a estudiantes, profesoras y profesores, organizaciones sociales, artistas, artesanas y artesanos, voluntariado y comunidad, marcando además la inauguración oficial de esta nueva etapa que lleva el nombre de José Bengoa Cabello, manteniendo viva una memoria que no queremos solamente recordar, sino proyectar desde nuestros territorios.




El encuentro comenzó reuniendo a estudiantes y profesorado de la Escuela Popular Campesina José Bengoa Cabello de Curaco de Vélez (Chiloé) y de la Escuela Ismenia Ortiz Lizama de Palquibudis (Curicó), compartiendo una asamblea entre ambas experiencias campesinas, para continuar con Saberes del Mar, junto al profesor Constantino Contreras, y el conversatorio de Género y Ruralidad con Ximena Valdés, «porque hablar del mundo rural es también reconocer a las mujeres, sus trabajos, aquello que históricamente ha permanecido invisibilizado y las transformaciones que aún necesitamos impulsar», destacaron en la presentación.




Seguidamente, el 29 de agosto, el Gimnasio Bordemar de la Población Vista Hermosa de Curaco de Vélez acogió una extensa jornada. Desde la organización, se señaló: «Quisimos expresar aquello que somos y en lo que creemos, uniendo cultura, formación, organización y autogestión, con puestos de artesanía de nuestras ferias, organizaciones sociales, estudiantes, voluntariado y productos de ambas escuelas, haciendo posible que una parte importante de la actividad se financiara desde nuestro propio trabajo colectivo».







La organización del festival de la Escuela, también resaltó: 

«Para nosotros la autonomía y la autogestión no son solamente principios escritos, son prácticas que se aprenden haciendo, compartiendo responsabilidades y poniendo cada cual algo de sí para sostener lo que hemos decidido construir en común».







Como señala Janett Cárdenas, esta trayectoria también nos invita a preguntarnos para qué educamos y desde dónde lo hacemos:







«Seguimos apostando a que la educación es una acción transformadora y una herramienta política que ponemos a disposición de quienes queremos transformar este modelo de injusticia, porque educarnos es también organizarnos, recuperar nuestra memoria y reconocernos en nuestros propios saberes, comprendiendo que desde el campo, el mar, las semillas, la artesanía, la cultura y la experiencia de quienes nos antecedieron se construye conocimiento para transformar nuestra realidad.»







La jornada permitió también reconocer a personas que han acompañado ese andar: Ximena Valdés, en memoria de José Bengoa; Sergio Faumangaun, director de la Escuela Campesina Águila Sur; la familia Gamin, en memoria de don Enrique Gamin; Mirian Alarcón, voluntaria y profesora de Agricultura Campesina desde el comienzo de este camino en 2016; y Patricio Larco, profesor de Acuicultura.




La cultura, inseparable de la manera de comprender la formación y la vida comunitaria, estuvo presente con Patricio Guerrero, Raíces Curacanas, Amaranto, Maribel Manquecoy, Javier Chandía, el bloque infantil integrado por Luis Soussi y Natali, Daniela Reyes, Aliwen, Nancy San Martín y su banda, Los Pirulonkos, Almas Chilotas y Rancheritos Vientos del Sur, quienes generosamente acompañaron esta celebración con música, voces y expresiones nacidas también desde nuestros territorios.







«Mirar estos diez años es reconocer que la Escuela ha podido sostenerse gracias a estudiantes, profesoras y profesores voluntarios, campesinas y campesinos, artistas, organizaciones y familias que han compartido conocimientos, trabajo, semillas, alimentos, música, tiempo y afectos, haciendo posible una experiencia que no pretende enseñar desde arriba, sino construir conocimiento desde aquello que cada una y cada uno sabe y aporta»

, señaló la declaración de la Escuela.










Agregan en su declaratoria: 

«Cumplir una década no significa cerrar una historia, sino mirar lo caminado para continuar, ahora llevando el nombre de José Bengoa Cabello y recogiendo esa invitación a SER, HACER y PENSAR, desde Chiloé, desde nuestras insularidades y desde el mundo campesino, convencidos de que mientras existan saberes que compartir y comunidades dispuestas a organizarse, existirán también posibilidades de transformación»

.







Finalizaron con la consigna: 

«Seguiremos sembrando esperanza desde la educación popular, porque educarnos, organizarnos y transformar nuestra realidad son parte de un mismo camino».

author: Tareq S. Hajjaj
title: Children Born in Gaza Over Last 3 Years Have No Memory of World Before Genocide
content:
Israel’s genocide has narrowed Palestinian children’s expectations of life’s possibilities.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

When I left Gaza in 2024, after six months of living through genocide, I wanted one thing above all else: to spare my only child a life spent permanently at war. I did not want him to grow up believing that the whole world looked like Gaza.

But I left more than fifteen nieces and nephews behind. Many were still too young to understand the world they had been born into. They were learning what a home was, what a school was, what it meant to be alive, at the very moment those things were being destroyed around them.

I spent the next year and a half in Cairo. It took me a long time to learn how to inhabit ordinary life again. Whenever I saw a garden, a playground, a school, or children playing freely and safely in the street, I could not simply enjoy the sight. Gaza was always there, beneath it.

A garden brought back the rubble. A school brought back the children who no longer had one. Even safety became a reminder of those still denied it.

There was a comparison I could not stop making: why could children elsewhere grow up among their families and the people who loved them, while Gaza’s children remained trapped in this unending cycle of occupation, bombardment, destruction, genocide, and hunger? How could a child starve to death in a world with so much food?

I kept thinking about the children whose first understanding of life was taking shape inside the genocide. My niece, Elaf, was a year and a half old when I left. She was still at the beginning of everything.

Then her life changed entirely. A tent became her home. Missiles and bombs became the sounds she fell asleep to. Rubble shaped the landscape through which she was learning to see the world, and daily death shaped her first knowledge of life.

What could she know of the world beyond Gaza’s walls? What reason did she have to imagine that elsewhere, children slept without bombardment, lived in homes that stood, and went to schools built to shelter them?

I feared she would grow up believing that life in Gaza was simply life.

At first, I thought this was a danger facing mainly the youngest children: those born during the genocide, or too young to remember anything before it. But children who were two or three when it began, and are now five or six, are also learning to see the world as rubble upon rubble.

During a video call with my brother Osama, who has eight children, his six-year-old son, Muhammad, saw me sitting on a sofa in a brightly lit room.

“Uncle, how did your tent fit that sofa?” He asked. I did not know how to answer.

His question took me far from the room where I was sitting. Muhammad had lived in a beautiful home before the genocide. But now, when he looked at his uncle’s home, he was left wondering how such lavish furniture could fit into the only kind of home he had come to expect.

He had more questions. “Is your tent made of fabric pieces, or is it ready-made? Do you have a community kitchen that gives you food?”

These were simply the only frames of reference he had to try to understand my life, asking whether the arrangements that governed his own survival also governed mine. Shelter meant a tent. Food meant waiting for a meal to be distributed.

There was nothing strange about his questions. What was unbearable was how much sense they made within the life imposed on him.

The change reaches older children, too. My nieces, Amira and Heba, respectively 12 and 10, remember life before. Yet I can hear their expectations for ordinary life shrinking.

They no longer ask for much from a school. They hope it might be something more than tents pressed against one another: perhaps a wooden structure with a roof of corrugated steel sheets.

During one call with my brother, Amira sat beside him as we discussed my son starting school.

“Are your schools tents, or are they wooden?” she asked. Those were the possibilities she offered me. I asked what she liked about her own school.

“We leave our cramped tent and go to a bigger one,” she said. “We can play more freely. There is a little space where we can play.”

Her answer stayed with me. Even that small difference — being able to move from one cramped space to another slightly less cramped one — mattered.

Then I asked what she wished her school could have.

“The school is very hot in summer, and in winter the rain gets in,” she told me. “I wish there were a fan in summer and a heater in winter.”

She did not ask to return to a school like the one she had attended before the genocide. She asked for something that might make the tent more bearable.

I cannot know what she has forgotten, or what she has pushed aside because remembering it hurts. But I can hear what has disappeared from the wishes she shares with me.

The genocide has reached into children’s sense of what is possible. The tent remains, and the dream becomes to make it cooler. The rain comes through; the dream is for it to be a little warmer.

What frightens me is how familiar these conditions have become. Children have learned to move through them, to make room for play wherever they can, to ask for improvements within them. Their ability to adapt helps them get through the day. It also reveals the depth of what they have been forced to endure.

A child should not have to learn to dream in terms of a tent.

Arwa Jundiya, 23, has given birth to two daughters during the genocide. One is three years old. The other is one.

Her older daughter is growing up without knowing what it means to live in a house. She has never known the family home that shaped the childhoods of so many of us in Gaza: grandparents, parents, uncles, and their families living on different floors of the same building, sharing their days across one extended household.

Jundiya speaks of that life as something no longer available to her children. “The house was more than a shelter — it held the people among whom a child grew up.”

But there is another deprivation she returns to, something so small that its absence becomes almost impossible to comprehend. “My three-year-old daughter has never held a toy,” she said.

Poverty leaves little room for such purchases, Jundiya explains. “Toys are no longer readily available for parents to buy,” she explained. “My husband spends most of his time trying to secure food for them. The work of keeping them fed consumes what might once have gone toward making them happy.”

Jundiya tells me that her children spend their days lying inside the tent, with little to do and nowhere to go. There are precious few ways of breaking the monotony, and the stones and sand beside the tent are the only things they have to play with.

“Maybe in five years, my children will ask me about their lives,” she says. “I don’t know what I will tell them. I don’t know whether I will say that the whole world is like Gaza, or that Gaza is the only place where children face this fate.”

Her question returns me to the fear that made me leave.

Her children have little connection to the world outside. There is no internet available to them, no television inside the tent. They cannot see the places their mother might compare their lives to. Gaza is the world they know.

I think of my son, and of the life I wanted him to discover beyond war. Then I think of the children I left behind: Elaf falling asleep to bombs, Muhammad trying to fit my sofa inside a tent, Amira wishing for a fan, Arwa’s daughter reaching the age of three without ever holding a toy.

These are some of the ways the genocide continues inside childhood. It takes away the places where children live and learn, then narrows their understanding of what a home or a school can be. It deprives them of ordinary pleasures until those pleasures become things they have never known to ask for.

But the children are still curious. They still want to play. They still ask questions about the world. Yet the world they have been given offers them tents, hunger, and rubble as answers.

When Muhammad asked how my tent could fit a sofa, I heard a child trying to make sense of what he could see. I also heard how far we had allowed his expectations to fall.

title: Υποχρεωτική η καθαρογραφή αθωωτικών αποφάσεων από το Εφετείο Αθηνών
content:
Όπως αναφέρει στο Δελτίο Τύπου που ακολουθεί ο Κώστας Παπαδάκης, μέλος του Δ.Σ. του Δ.Σ.Α. και εισηγητής του σχετικού αιτήματος, στην υποστήριξή του ενώπιον της Ολομέλειας του Εφετείου Αθηνών: “

Το επόμενο βήμα είναι να μην περιοριστεί μόνο στο Εφετείο Αθηνών αλλά να επεκταθεί σε όλα τα δικαστήρια και εν τέλει να νομοθετηθεί με ανάλογη τροποποίηση του άρθρου 142 παρ. 4 Κ.Ποιν.Δ, ώστε να είναι υποχρεωτική παντού η καθαρογραφή όλων των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων χωρίς καμμία προϋπόθεση..”

ου Υπουργού Δικαιοσύνης (επισυνάπτεται) έγινε δεκτή η γνώμη που περιλαμβάνεται στην υπ αριθμ. 1/2026 απόφαση της Ολομέλειας του Εφετείου Αθηνών σχετικά με την καθαρογραφή των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων.




Με την υπ. αριθμ. 61301οικ/30.9.2026 Απόφαση του Υπουργού Δικαιοσύνης (επισυνάπτεται) έγινε δεκτή η γνώμη που περιλαμβάνεται στην υπ αριθμ. 1/2026 απόφαση της Ολομέλειας του Εφετείου Αθηνών σχετικά με την καθαρογραφή των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων.




Η απόφαση είχε ληφθεί από την Ολομέλεια του Εφετείου Αθηνών στις 19.2.2026, όπου είχε κληθεί και παρέστη η αντιπροσωπεία του Δ.Σ. του Δ.Σ.Α. αποτελούμενη από τον πρόεδρό του κ. Ανδρέα Κουτσόλαμπρο και μέλη του Δ.Σ,. του, μεταξύ των οποίων και ο υπογράφων ως εισηγητής που ανέπτυξε τα σχετικά αιτήματα. Ενώ είχε προηγηθεί η διοργάνωση εκδήλωσης στις 11.2.2026 στα γραφεία του Δ.Σ.Α. στις για την προβολή του αιτήματος.




Το αίτημα είχε στηριχθεί πάνδημα από όλους τους δικηγορικούς φορείς και από τις Ενώσεις Ποινικολόγων και πολλά νομικά περιοδικά. Όχι ωστόσο από τις δικαστικές και εισαγγελικές ενώσεις.




Σύμφωνα με την παραπάνω Υ.Α. η καθαρογραφή των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων του Εφετείου Αθηνών καθίσταται η υποχρεωτική εφόσον το ζητήσει ο κατηγορούμενος εντός 6 μηνών από την έκδοση τους χωρίς να απαιτείται η επίκληση εννόμου συμφέροντος.




Ανεξάρτητα από την καθυστέρηση έκδοσής της Υ.Α. πρόκειται για μία μεγάλη νίκη που πιστώνεται σε όσους συνέβαλαν με κάθε τρόπο διότι άρχισε να αποκαθίσταται μια μεγάλη αδικία, της οποίας οι πτυχές έχουν αναλυθεί λεπτομερώς, αλλά και ένα έλλειμα δικαίου που είχε οδηγήσει στην εξαφάνιση της επιτυχούς υπερασπιστικής νομολογίας.




Το επόμενο βήμα είναι να μην περιοριστεί μόνο στο Εφετείο Αθηνών αλλά να επεκταθεί σε όλα τα δικαστήρια και εν τέλει να νομοθετηθεί με ανάλογη τροποποίηση του άρθρου 142 παρ. 4 Κ.Ποιν.Δ, ώστε να είναι υποχρεωτική παντού η καθαρογραφή όλων των αθωωτικών αποφάσεων χωρίς καμμία προϋπόθεση.




Με θερμές ευχαριστίες προς όσους/ες συνέβαλαν.




Αθήνα, 7.10.2026




Κώστας Παπαδάκης




Δικηγόρος, Μέλος του Δ.Σ. του Δ.Σ.Α.

author: Emran Feroz
title: The War on Afghanistan Was Launched 25 Years Ago. It Still Hasn’t Ended.
content:
The war inaugurated a terrible new global order in which armed drones kill civilians who are neither named nor counted.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

“There were nights full of terror. Our village was bombed constantly,” says Zalmay Khan. Afterward, he goes to pray. Because of his wounds, he cannot kneel, so he prays sitting down.

Khan is in his early twenties and now works as a Taliban intelligence officer. As a boy, he says, he learned to read the sky before he learned to read words. His village in Wardak province, near Kabul, was bombed, then bombed again. First came American planes, then NATO’s, then those of the Afghan army the West had built. By night it got worse, when jets and armed foreign contractors hit villages and killed civilians seemingly at random.

“I became a Mujahed [a Taliban fighter] naturally,” Khan tells me.

He is not an outlier. In village after village on my most recent trip to Afghanistan a few weeks ago, I met men who grew up as the so-called war on terror’s raw material. Some wear the Taliban’s turbans, and some do not. Almost all of them say the same thing, with remarkable calm: The American narrative of this war belongs to the past. After two decades of war and destruction, it is their turn to control narratives and to rule the country.

October 7, 2026, marks exactly 25 years since the United States began bombing Afghanistan. The anniversary will pass in Washington with little reflection. In Afghanistan, the reality of it is lived daily.

The war on terror made history in a way few people remember. In its opening weeks, the United States used an armed drone against a target in Afghanistan, one of the first such attacks ever, in an attempt to kill the Taliban’s founder, Mullah Mohammad Omar, in Kandahar. Omar was not hit on October 7, 2001. He survived and reportedly died of natural causes a decade later, which the Taliban kept secret for years.

Who died instead? The record offers almost nothing: no definitive or officially confirmed names, ages, villages. One news report cites unnamed Kandahar residents suggesting the raid killed Omar’s 10-year-old son and the child’s stepfather, but the Taliban’s ambassador to Pakistan declined to confirm or deny this report.

In other words, the first known attempt to kill a man with an armed drone killed people no one has ever definitively identified, and it set the template for the type of warfare that would dominate over the next decades. No one can say who the victims were. But if the pattern of the following years is any guide, many were likely civilians, like the thousands of victims who came after them. During the Obama years, Afghanistan officially became the world’s most drone-bombed country.

That template repeated itself so often that Afghans developed names for the many men who were declared dead after supposed “surgical strikes,” but who then reappeared alive: mord-e zinda (the living dead) in Farsi and khyali marr (the not truly dead) in Pashto. I call them “Taliban ghosts.”

It continued across successive U.S. administrations, even across the bureaucratic, supposedly methodical “kill lists” infamously used by the Obama administration used to mark people for death from the skies.

The first known attempt to kill a man with an armed drone killed people no one has ever definitively identified, and it set the template for the type of warfare that would dominate over the next decades.

The obvious question was almost never asked: If Omar was not the victim, who was killed instead? In the logic of the drone war, a body is a statistic, and a body in a targeted area becomes a militant by default. The dead were not counted, and the stories of their families, who were left to count for themselves, largely continued to go unknown.

Strikes did not only create ghosts. They also created recruits. Researchers, journalists, and Afghan elders have long described the same pattern: A village is hit, a family is destroyed, and the Taliban offer the survivors the only form of justice made available to them. By the end of the war, entire districts had made that choice, not out of ideological conviction but out of grief.

One of the people I talked to on my recent trip was a Taliban official who had been held at Bagram, the American prison north of Kabul, for several years. He told me what the Americans wanted from him. “Accept our democracy or get tortured and rot here. That’s what they told me,” he recalled.

The aim, as he described it, was reeducation by coercion: Accept our system, our ideology, and the pain stops. He refused. By his account, he left more committed than when he arrived. He was freed in 2020 under the prisoner exchange the United States negotiated with the Taliban, part of the same Doha process that handed the country back to the movement the war was purportedly meant to destroy.

Consider the sequence. A man is imprisoned and tortured to make him embrace a political order. He then walks out of the prison and eventually helps govern. The war’s own methods created much of its failure.

I make no argument here that the Taliban’s rule is benign. Women and girls have been shut out of education and public life, and dissent is severely punished. These facts belong in any honest account. But an honest account also includes what the war did, who did it, and whom they harmed; the powers that waged it have shown little interest in reckoning with that part.

Here is the part that does not fit the story that the war on terror ended in August 2021: someone else is still fighting it.

Pakistan is currently bombing Afghanistan. Just a few days ago, Pakistani airstrikes killed at least 10 civilians, most of them children, in the provinces of Helmand and Kunar.

Pakistani authorities say they are targeting militants of the Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, often known as the Pakistani Taliban. Afghans on the ground, and independent reports, repeatedly describe civilians as being among the dead. Islamabad has also forced hundreds of thousands of Afghans, many of them born there, out of Pakistan.

The phrasing used to justify these attacks is familiar: “Terrorists were eliminated.” Anyone who covered the American war has heard that sentence before, and the same pattern follows. The claims are hard to verify, the dead are hard to identify, and the people left behind are not asked.

Pakistan has run this game before, and it has historically done well for itself out of it. In the first days of the war on terror, Islamabad aligned itself with Washington while, according to critics and many former officials, hedging its bets with the Taliban. The United States poured billions into Pakistan in military aid and reimbursements. A double game paid for itself.

For a military establishment that benefits from a war to fight, an enemy is an asset. That helps explain why the army has so little tolerance for those who challenge its role. This pattern goes beyond the foreign policy of one country alone. It is a system — one created by the U.S. but now adopted globally — that requires a threat to warrant its continued expansion and removes the people who question its logic.

If Pakistan again needs an Afghan threat to justify its budgets, its alliances, and its hold on power at home, the logic is the same as in 2001. The war on terror, seen from Islamabad, is a renewable resource.

The TTP itself is not a mystery. It did not appear from nowhere, and it cannot be blamed on Kabul alone. It grew out of Pakistan’s own tribal areas, where decades of military operations, drone strikes with Islamabad’s tacit consent, and brutality under former Pakistani President Pervez Musharraf shattered communities. Many of these massacres have been forgotten outside the region. In the tribal belt they are not.

The result was a generation radicalized by state violence, in much the same process I heard described in Afghan villages. The TTP is, in significant part, a product of the very policies now used to justify the continued bombing of Afghanistan. Without Pakistan’s violence in the tribal areas, the group would not look as it does. Accountability for that history will not come from the same army that carried it out.

The war on terror in Afghanistan was sold as a campaign against a specific enemy. What it produced was a country scarred by airstrikes, night raids, and detention, and an enemy that outlasted the world’s strongest military. It also produced a new precedent: That a state can kill from the sky, in secret, and rarely be asked who died, much less held accountable for its deathmaking.

That precedent traveled. Drones have gone from being an innovation in killing, one shrouded in secrecy, to a mainstay of battlefields on multiple continents.. The language of “surgical” strikes and “militants eliminated” has become standard, notably throughout the genocide in Gaza. And in Afghanistan, the war continues in new hands, with the same justifications and the same result.

On October 7, if this anniversary is marked in the U.S. at all, there will be speeches about sacrifice and lessons supposedly learned. The real lessons are available to anyone who asks the people who lived under the sky, and the most critical question is still the one nobody answered in 2001: Who was killed instead?
