author: webadmin
title: The Rural Connections Behind Illegal Hunting
content:
Thanks to Wiltshire Hunt Sabs for this guest post, who, alongside Cirencester Illegal Hunt Watch, Bristol Hunt Sabs and Bath Hunt Sabs, have been keeping the pressure on the Beaufort Hunt.




The Duke of Beaufort’s Hunt is one of Britain’s most prominent fox hunts and has been terrorising wildlife across the countryside surrounding the Badminton Estate in Gloucestershire for hundreds of years. But the Beaufort Hunt does not exist in isolation. Behind it lies a wider rural network of landowners, estate managers and property professionals.




One of the most striking examples is Rupert Sturgis, Partner and Head of Knight Frank’s Cirencester office.




Rupert Sturgis, Partner and Head of Knight Frank, Cirencester. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs




Knight Frank’s website describes Sturgis as specialising in the sale of town and country property across Gloucestershire and North Wiltshire.




Screenshot: 

Knight Frank




He is also a Field Master of the Beaufort Hunt.




On Saturday we filmed Rupert directing the field riders to surround a covert. This is so foxes become trapped inside, whilst hounds are sent in to kill them. It’s a classic cubbing technique that teaches the new hounds to kill.




Rupert Sturgis directing the field to surround the covert in a classic cubbing formation. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs




Watch the video below




Rupert’s role with the hunt is not recent. In 2015, Horse & Hound described him as an estate agent who was then in his 12th season as a Beaufort Field Master.




Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs




The Field describes him as a Beaufort Field Master, quoting him discussing the hunting country where they were openly hunting foxes just last Saturday, and where our drone was shot down in December 2025: 

“Field Master Rupert Sturgis recommends the Widleys hedges as part of a run west from Common Wood Farm”

.




Beanie Sturgis laying a trail of cigarette ash. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs




His wife, Beanie Sturgis, is also a Beaufort Field Master. Badminton Horse Trials states that she married Rupert in 2007 and describes her as a Beaufort Field Master, as well as an event organiser, show judge and course designer. Beanie accepted a community resolution in respect of a hate crime committed against a hunt sab in October 2024.




Knight Frank and the Badminton Estate




The connection between Knight Frank and the Badminton Estate goes well beyond Rupert Sturgis. In fact, Knight Frank has been involved with the estate for decades, with senior figures from the firm becoming closely involved in the management structure surrounding Badminton.




In its 2015 Rural Report, Knight Frank stated that it had been involved with the Badminton Estate for 15 years. The report featured Simon Dring, then Badminton’s senior resident agent, who said he had worked at the estate for more than 30 years, including 15 years as senior resident agent. He described working closely with the Duke and his family, as well as coordinating the various specialists and advisers involved with the estate.




Dring retired from the Knight Frank LLP partnership on 31 December 2016, but his relationship with Badminton continued for almost another decade. He remained the estate’s senior resident agent until his retirement from Badminton in late 2025.




Dring once hilariously told us, via deluded hunt supporters, that we couldn’t fly our drone in the ‘Duke’s air space’.




Companies House records show that he was secretary of Swangrove Estates Ltd from 31 March 2000 until 9 March 2026. The company is registered at the Estate Office, Badminton, and its stated business is mixed farming. He was also secretary of Swangrove Holdings Ltd from 31 March 2000 until 9 March 2026, another company registered at the Badminton Estate Office.




Both companies show current officers including members of the Somerset family alongside other directors. The records show the overlap between the people managing the estate and the companies through which its interests are held.




And Dring is not the only former Knight Frank figure with a connection to the Badminton Estate.




Christopher Smith, who was a Knight Frank partner heading its rural consultancy, renewables and energy consultancy, is now listed as a person with significant control of Badminton Hospitality Ltd, with ownership and voting rights of 75% or more. His correspondence address is the Badminton Estate Office.




Alexander (Sandy) Douglas provides another link. He has been a director of Swangrove Estates Ltd since 2000, with the company’s records giving his correspondence address as the Badminton Estate Office. Douglas also has a longstanding history with Knight Frank, having previously been an LLP member.




The overlap extends beyond Badminton. Atty Beor-Roberts, whose real name is Alastair Guy White Beor-Roberts, spent more than 30 years with Knight Frank and was chairman of the firm’s central region, retiring in 2018 but continuing as a consultant.




Screenshot: Radley College




At the same time, Beor-Roberts was chairman of the Radley College Beagles, retiring in May 2026. In the same interview, he listed hunting among his preferred weekend activities. Beor-Roberts was chairman of the hunt when 

sabs were arrested

, whilst stopping illegal hare hunting near Radcot.







This provides another example of the close relationship between senior figures in the rural property world and Britain’s traditional hunting networks.




These links show a network of people whose professional careers in rural property have overlapped with the management and corporate interests of one of Britain’s most prominent landed estates.




And the Beaufort Hunt itself is of course closely tied to the Badminton Estate. The hunt’s own contact information lists the Badminton Estate Office alongside the organisations with which it is associated.




The Beaufort Family and Fox Hunting




Just one of the five foxes we saw and helped to safety from the Duke of Beaufort’s Hounds on 19 September 2026. Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs




The Beaufort family’s association with fox hunting dates back to 1762, when the 5th Duke of Beaufort chased a fox into Silk Wood and decided to focus his attention entirely on fox hunting. Since then, successive Dukes of Beaufort have maintained a deep involvement in the hunt. The mastership has traditionally been held by the head of the Beaufort family at Badminton, with the family owning the hunt’s hounds, kennels and stables.




The current Duke’s grandfather, Henry Somerset, the 10th Duke of Beaufort, led the hunt for 60 years and was described as the ‘greatest fox hunter of the 20th century’. A dubious title if ever there was one.




The current Duke’s grandfather, Henry Somerset, the 10th Duke of Beaufort. Image: Fox-Hunting, The Duke of Beaufort, 1980




In 1980, he published ‘Fox-Hunting’, described as a ‘comprehensive examination’ of the ‘sport’ of fox hunting. Its chapters cover the management of hounds, fox coverts, earth-stopping, terriers and digging.




The book provides a detailed and disturbing insight into fox hunting and is particularly relevant given the Beaufort Hunt’s use of artificial earths ‘AEs’, which continued until recently when their use was exposed by sabs.




The AEs are used to encourage foxes to live and breed, therefore keeping them in the area to be hunted. The foxes are flushed on the morning of the hunt, and the entrances then blocked so they can’t return.




One of the artificial earths in use by the Beaufort Hunt, until exposed by sabs. Image Wiltshire Hunt Sabs




Henry ‘Harry’ Somerset, the current 12th Duke of Beaufort, is a director of both Swangrove Estates Ltd and Swangrove Holdings Ltd, as well as a director of Badminton Horse Trials Ltd. He is also the senior Master of the Beaufort Hunt.




A network of rural enablers




These connections show a longstanding overlap between the professional world of rural property management and the institutions surrounding the Badminton Estate.




Knight Frank has itself described its involvement with Badminton as longstanding, while former Knight Frank figure Simon Dring held senior positions within companies connected to the estate. At the same time, Knight Frank’s Cirencester office is headed by Rupert Sturgis, who is a Field Master of the Beaufort Hunt.




These connections raise questions about the extent to which the same people and professional networks operate across the rural property industry, major landed estates and hunting organisations.




Knight Frank & ‘Nature Depletion’




A deer runs from the Duke of Beaufort’s hounds, 3rd October 2026. Image Wiltshire Hunt Sabs




Knight Frank publicly describes itself as a responsible business and says its sustainability plan is intended to address global risks including climate change and nature depletion, while making a positive and measurable difference to the natural environment and communities.




Screenshot: Knight Frank




Meanwhile, Rupert Sturgis – Partner and Head of the Knight Frank Cirencester office – is publicly carrying out illegal hunting in his role as a Field Master of the Beaufort Hunt.




Image: Wiltshire Hunt Sabs




The Beaufort Hunt is part of a much wider rural network in which landowners, estate managers, property professionals and hunting figures are connected through longstanding personal and commercial relationships. By exposing those connections, we can better understand the establishment surrounding illegal hunting and the networks that allow it to continue.




The question is not just who goes hunting. It is who manages the land, who advises those who own it and how closely those worlds are connected.




You can support Wiltshire Hunt Sabs 

here

 and follow them 

here

 
















The post 

The Rural Connections Behind Illegal Hunting

 appeared first on 

Hunt Saboteurs Association

.

author: heinhtetkyaw
title: The Marxist Roots of Spanish Fascism
content:
The political regime of General Francisco Franco, which came about following the conclusion of the Spanish Civil War, is often described as being conservative, clerical, and authoritarian. The distinctive features of the fascist rule under General Francisco Franco are revealed in a curious episode from history – on his death, the very first flowers laid at his coffin came from China, signed by Communist leader Zhou Enlai. It just happened to be about the same period of time when communist Cuba led by Fidel Castro observed three days of national mourning. It’s beyond irony for communist regimes to express such friendliness to a fascist dictator. However, rather than indicating some form of ideological sympathy, this unusual episode reveals another side of Cold War diplomacy, a possible precursor of nowadays campism.

However, looking closer, the earlier movement of the Franco regime before it suffered an internal coup had the rhetoric, symbols, and even some aspects of the organizational structure characteristic of National Syndicalism as the pre-cursor to their Spanish fascism. The earlier Spanish National Syndicalism did not emerge from the typical right-wing Spanish conservatism. Rather, the radical ideology was formed in the early 1930s and the main authors of this movement were Ramiro Ledesma Ramos and Onésimo Redondo Ortega. Being inspired by the revolutionary ideologies that dominated the European left of that period, such as Sorelian Marxism (revolutionary syndicalism), anarchism, and Marxist socialism, National Syndicalism rejected any attempts to preserve the existing capitalist or agrarian order in favor of a total revolution of the working class. Between 1936 and 1937, however, due to the physical elimination of the leadership of the movement and the purely tactical actions of Franco, who managed to seize military and political power, National Syndicalist movement in Spain was thoroughly co-opted by Franco. Having deprived the ideology of its social-revolutionary nature and keeping the symbols and slogans of the movement, Franco transformed the movement of total state transformation into a means of labor control.

In order to see how Franco managed to pervert National Syndicalism, it is necessary to take a look at the ideological origin of the movement. The main ideologist of National Syndicalism, Ramiro Ledesma Ramos, created his political newspaper "La Conquista del Estado" (The Conquest of the State) in March 1931, stating from the very beginning that his purpose was to channel the revolutionary spirit of the Spanish proletariat for the sake of the national project. His paper (The Conquest of the State) even became a subject of debate in a CNT assembly, yet, it did not have the intended impact. Ledesma was well-versed in continental philosophy and embodied what is called the greatest assimilation of Georges Sorel's revolutionary syndicalism in Spain. The syndicalism of Sorel proclaimed direct actions of workers' syndicates to crush bourgeois liberal regime. The key reference point of Ledesma on the left side of Spain was the Confederación Nacional del Trabajo (CNT), a strong anarcho-syndicalist labor union. It was obvious that Ledesma admired the fighting spirit, anti-bourgeois combativeness, and revolutionary passion of the masses of the CNT. In his opinion, anarcho-syndicalists were the best combat forces in Spain, and it was his main aim to "nationalize" the CNT, that means to redirect revolutionary power of CNT from internationalist anti-statism to the national state. It is important to note that this influence was not only theoretical. The early National Syndicalist cells included many former members of anarchist and communist organizations. One of the leaders of CNT, Alvaro de Sotomayor, became the head of National Syndicalist union of taxi drivers in Madrid. Similarly, Dr. Santiago Montero Díaz from Communist Party of Spain also joined them. Both National Syndicalists and anarchists shared the following superficial values: their common hatred of bourgeois democratic system, opposition to gradual reforms, and support of direct action through workers' unions. Similarly, the relations between National Syndicalism and Marxism were also very similar. The movement was defined by structural mimicry and fierce ideological rivalry. First of all, Ledesma admitted Karl Marx as a great philosopher and agreed with the basic ideas of his criticism of bourgeois liberal capitalist system. Even though the ideology of National Syndicalism was also anti-capitalist, condemning the liberalism of the capitalistic economy for making workers economic slaves and making labor a commodity, Ledesma and Redondo sharply denied two fundamental ideas of the Marxism:

Historical materialism, because according to their opinion it was destroying the spirituality, culture, and nationalism of humanity, reducing the history to purely economic interactions;

Class struggle, considering it a destructive civil war that divided the nation and made it vulnerable for foreign domination.

Thus, in order to answer the challenge of Marxism, the JONS (Councils of National-Syndicalist Offensive), formed as a result of the merger of Ledesma and Redondo organizations in October 1931, presented their sixteen-points manifesto including radically leftist economic policies in the frame of nationalist ideology. The document demanded:

The compulsory syndicalization of all production processes and placing of the private enterprises under the control of the state in order to prevent the exploitation of workers;

The nationalization of credit, banks, and transport;

Expropriation of vast semi-feudal estates owned by absentees and their transfer to peasants' syndicates and peasant family farms;

Severe criminal prosecution of the financial speculators and capitalists exploiting the misery of the working class.

With such demands, the JONS claimed to provide the Spanish proletariat with "bread, justice, and dignity".

On February 28th, 1934, because of financial difficulties and lack of electoral success along with the beginning of the attacks from the left, the JONS joined forces with Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera’s Falange Española into FE/JONS. Although the charisma and aristocratic connections of Jose Antonio, the son of the former dictator of Spain General Miguel Primo de Rivera, provided the new organization with the funds and the speaker, his party was lacking a coherent programmatic doctrine. It is Ledesma who formulated the Twenty-Seven Points of the platform of the new alliance based on his Sixteen Points. Nevertheless, ideological conflicts started appearing very soon after the unification of the organizations.

The outbreak of the Spanish Civil War in July 1936 marked the final absorption of the movement into the mainstream. Four months after the beginning of the war, all of the leaders of the National Syndicalist political faction had been liquidated:

Onésimo Redondo was murdered in a roadside clash at Labajos on July 24, 1936.

Ramiro Ledesma Ramos was executed by republican militiamen in Madrid on October 29, 1936.

José Antonio Primo de Rivera was executed in a prison of Alicante on November 20, 1936.

Once the leaders were gone, the burgeoning ranks of Falangist militants, who were primarily composed of newly-recruited young men who were ideologically inexperienced, lacked a leader strong enough to prevent military domination. Realizing the value of the Falange for propaganda purposes, General Francisco Franco decided to take control of the movement. In 1937, on April 19, he issued the Decree of Unification, forcing the merger of the Falangist party (FE/JONS) with the ultra-conservative, religious Carlist monarchists in order to form a unified state party called “Falange Española Tradicionalista y de las Juntas de Ofensiva Nacional Sindicalista (FET/JONS)”. Franco proclaimed himself the undisputed leader (Caudillo) of this fabricated alliance.

The substantive objectives of National Syndicalism were deliberately perverted under Franco. While the idea was for the economy to be controlled by the workers through the use of vertical syndicates that were supposed to end the exploitation of workers, under the “Spanish Syndical Organization” system, vertical syndicates were formed but with the opposite meaning. Rather than giving the workers power, these syndicates served to ensure labor discipline, prohibit strikes, and keep the wages constant so as to increase the profits of the capitalists and landowners. The syndicates membership was compulsory for both the employers and employees. Inversion of the Structural Elements of Syndicalism:

Original Vision of the National Syndicalists: Workers and technicians formed vertical syndicates from the ground up to capture state power and tame the interests of capital for the benefit of the nation.

Francoist Reality: State bureaucrats and capitalists controlled top-down official syndicates to discipline workers, prevent strikes, and ensure their profits.

The true early supporters of the movement—the "old shirts" who had joined before 1936 and who maintained social radicalism—are ignored, jailed, or silenced if they complain. Besides, they had been outvoted by millions of new opportunists and post-war members of the party who saw the party as just a means for bureaucratic advancement. Through his glorification of the dead founders, especially José Antonio, as sacred martyrs, Franco mythologizes them and puts their portraits on streets everywhere and even inscribes their names on the walls of churches throughout Spain. Through this substitution of ritualistic hagiography for radical and activist doctrine, he ensures that their original teachings of “national syndicalism” never become a challenge to the social order.

The hijack against the Spanish National Syndicalism movement by Francisco Franco is one of the great examples of political cooptation in the twentieth century. Beginning as a radical syncretism of revolutionary syndicalism, and Bolshevik influenced state-controlled economy of the kind appropriated by Sorel, National Syndicalism was a militant querfront response to both capitalist liberal democracy and internationalist socialism. By making use of the deaths of Ledesma, Redondo, and José Antonio, Franco took control of the movement's revolutionary symbols, flags, and organizational system. He incorporated it with reactionary monarchism and Roman Catholicism, thus neutralizing the movement's threat to the Spanish landowners and industrialists. He succeeded in transforming the revolutionary anti-bourgeois workers' movement into the ideological facade of an aristocratic and conservative dictatorship. Here, it’s important to state the key differences between the anarcho-syndicalism and National Syndicalism with regards to their ultimate goals concerning the state. Anarcho-Syndicalism required the destruction of the state through general strikes with the creation of the stateless and collectivist global society of free communes of workers. On the other hand, National Syndicalism proclaimed the complete statism. As stated by Ledesma, the workers' syndicates should not destroy the state, but become the state, inspiring the experiences of Bolshevik revolution and their attempt to establish socialism in one country according to National Syndicalism. They believed that it was possible to get it accomplished through "vertical syndicates" which will organize the whole sector of industry from the top to the bottom, and thus parliament will be substituted by functional economic representation of four national classes, ensuring the national unity. As Alexander Reid Ross stated in the book “Against the Fascist Creep”:

The leading three fascist political figures of the interwar period in France were all former leftists: a former member of the inner committee of the Communist Party, a former anarcho-syndicalist, and the leader of the “neo-socialist” faction of the Socialist Party (then called the French Section of the Workers’ International). The movement was led by a host of frustrated and powerful leftists joining with sectors of the nationalist radical right to attack liberalism.

And as Robert O. Paxton stated in the book “The Anatomy of Fascism”:

By 1914, part of the Left’s traditional following had become disillusioned with what they considered the compromises of moderate parliamentary socialists. After the war, looking for something more uncompromisingly revolutionary, they went over to Bolshevism, or, as we have seen, via national syndicalism to fascism.

It’s apparent that anarchism and Marxism to fascism pipeline was via proto-fascist movements like national syndicalism. Thus, to remain genuinely anti-fascist, anarchists and Marxists must ensure that the core principles of internationalism and class struggle are never sidelined or replaced without straying into dogmatism. History shows that when nationalism and anti-imperialism—such as the concept of the "proletarian nation"—superseded these core values, it triggered a pipeline from anarchism and Marxism straight into fascism. This dynamic unfolded across multiple countries through proto-fascist movements like national syndicalism, demonstrating that the trend was structural rather than an isolated anomaly.

title: Başakşehir’de ortaokulda bıçaklı kavga: Beş öğrenci yaralandı
content:
İstanbul’un Başakşehir ilçesindeki Kayaşehir Şeyh Şamil İmam Hatip Ortaokulu’nda öğrenciler arasında çıkan kavga sırasında beş öğrenci bıçakla yaralandı.




Bugün (6 Ekim) sabah saatlerinde öğrenciler arasında henüz bilinmeyen bir nedenle kavga çıktı. İhbar üzerine okula sağlık ekipleri sevk edildi.




Yaralanan öğrenciler ambulanslarla hastaneye kaldırıldı.



















“Çocukları değil, onları bu hale getiren sistemi konuşun”




17 Nisan 2026










Valilikten açıklama




İstanbul Valiliği olayla ilgili yaptığı açıklamada, kavganın saat 08.40 sıralarında meydana geldiğini belirtti.




Valiliğin açıklaması şöyle:




“06.10.2026 Salı günü saat 08.40 sıralarında Başakşehir İlçesi’nde bulunan bir ortaokulda öğrenciler arasında çıkan kavgada 5 öğrenci yaralanmıştır. Olay sonrası yaralılar, bölgeye sevk edilen sağlık ekipleri tarafından hastaneye kaldırılarak tedavi altına alınmıştır.”




(NÖ)

author: Unknown
title: Les flics balancent des grenades assourdissantes GL-304 sur des ados
content:
Cet article a principalement pour but de s'assurer vite fait que cette action ne passe pas sous le tapis et prétend décrypter ni le mouvement lycéen, ni le maintien de l'ordre




Personne ne devrait subir la répression policière. Mais le fait est qu'elle est d'autant plus cruelle quand elle est dirigée contre des enfants et des ados qui luttent pour leurs conditions de vie




Jeudi 1

er

 octobre, alors que les blocus battaient leur plein, un cortège de lycéen se déplace dans le 7

e

 arrondissement, évidemment «

 

accompagné

 

» par la police. Alors qu'iels fuient en direction des quais, les flics balancent un de leur nouveau joujou, encore assez peu vu pour l'instant, la 

GL

-304 Condor

, fabriquée par le brésil.




Théoriquement, c'est une grenade «

 

assourdissante

 

». Elle produit une forte détonation qui a pour but d'incapaciter partiellement et temporairement. Dans les faits, elle sert à remplacer la tristement célèbre grenade double effet lacrymogène & assourdissant «

 

GM2L

 

». Elle est toujours en service, mais elle peut plus être lancée à la main, uniquement au lanceur, 

comme encore vu récemment

. Les flics n'avaient donc plus de quoi mutiler facilement à courte distance, et cette grenade 

GL

-304 tombe à pique.




Pour ce qui est de lyon, c'est une 

vidéo postée par actuFR Lyon

 qui interpelle, de par la détonation importante (qui plus est semble correspondre à la détonation en deux temps qui éjecte le détonateur). L'action se situe à angle rue Lortet et Boulevard Yves Farge dans le 7

e

. Et une fois sur place, les débris confirment qu'il s'agit d'une 

GL

-304.
















 







Cette grenade est extrêment dangereuse malgré tout le discours sur le «

 

détonateur à double étage

 

» et sa coque en caoutchouc : il est fort à parier que la «

 

grenade de désencerclement

 

» qui a 

grièvement blessée un lycéen à Lens ce 05 octobre

 est probablement une de ces grenades au vue des dégâts, et l'

hésitation du procureur

 à confirmer le modèle va en ce sens. Un mutilé dans la première année d'utilisation, c'est la promesse d'un scandale.

title: HSK tarafından açığa alınmıştı: Saruhanlı Cumhuriyet Savcısı tutuklandı
content:
İstanbul’daki bazı dava ve soruşturmalara maddi menfaat karşılığında müdahale edildiği iddialarına ilişkin yürütülen soruşturmada, HSK kararıyla açığa alınan ve hakkında soruşturma izni verilen Manisa Saruhanlı Cumhuriyet Savcısı B.G., ‘rüşvete aracılık’ ve ‘örgüte bilerek yardım etme’ suçlarından sevk edildiği mahkemece tutuklandı.

Bakırköy Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca ‘rüşvet almak’, ‘rüşvet vermek’, ‘rüşvete aracılık etmek’ ile ‘suç örgütü kurmak, yönetmek ve üye olmak’ suçlarından yürütülen soruşturmada, daha önce İstanbul’da görev yapan Manisa Saruhanlı Cumhuriyet Savcısı B.G., HSK kararıyla açığa alınarak hakkında soruşturma izni verilmişti.

B.G.’nin, 2022 yılında Beşiktaş Belediyesi yöneticilerine yönelik yürütülen rüşvet ve irtikap soruşturmasında tutuklanan Belediye Başkan Yardımcısı Hüseyin Avni Sipahi’ye, menfaat karşılığında soruşturmaya ilişkin önceden bilgi verdiği de dosyadaki iddialar arasında yer aldı.

Soruşturma kapsamında adliyeye sevk edilen savcı B.G., ‘rüşvete aracılık’ ve ‘örgüte bilerek yardım etme’ suçlarından sevk edildiği mahkemece tutuklandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: ABD'den Suudi Arabistan'a Husiler karşısında askeri destek: 200 Amerikalı danışman görev yapıyor
content:
Fotoğraf: Suudi Arabistan Kraliyet Divanı

ABD'nin Suudi Arabistan'a Yemen'deki Husilere karşı yürüttüğü operasyonlarda verdiği desteğin kapsamına ilişkin yeni bilgiler ortaya çıktı. Üst düzey bir ABD'li yetkili, Al Jazeera'ya yaptığı açıklamada Washington'ın Riyad'a destek verdiğini söyledi.

Yetkili, Suudi Arabistan'ın hava sahasını savunmak ve Husilere karşı savaşan güçlere destek olmak amacıyla ABD'nin yakıt ikmali kapasitesinden yararlandığını belirtti. Suudi Arabistan'daki planlama merkezlerinde ise yaklaşık 200 Amerikalı danışmanın görev yaptığı ifade edildi. Bu personelin Suudi güçlerine planlama ve hedef belirleme süreçlerinde danışmanlık yaptığı aktarıldı.

ABD'li yetkili, Washington'ın Yemen'deki savaşa doğrudan dahil olmadığını savundu. ABD askerlerinin çatışmalarda doğrudan yer almadığını ve Washington'ın Yemen'de özel bir askeri hedefinin bulunmadığını söyledi.

Ancak ABD'nin istihbarat paylaşımı, hedefleme desteği ve askeri danışmanlık yoluyla Suudi operasyonlarına sağladığı destek, Washington'ın çatışmadaki rolüne ilişkin tartışmaları yeniden gündeme taşıdı. CNN'in daha önce aktardığı bilgilere göre de Suudi Arabistan'da 100'den fazla ABD'li askeri danışman bulunuyor ve toplam Amerikan personelinin yaklaşık 200'e ulaştığı belirtiliyordu.

ABD'li yetkili, açıklamasında İran'a yönelik politikaya da değindi. Washington'ın İran üzerindeki baskıyı artırdığını söyleyen yetkili, “İran'a yönelik kuşatmayı sıkılaştırıyoruz” dedi.

İran'ın ekonomik açıdan zor durumda olduğunu savunan ABD'li yetkili, Washington'ın uyguladığı baskının devam edeceğini belirtti.

ABD Dışişleri Bakanı Marco Rubio da son açıklamasında Washington'ın Suudi Arabistan'a yönelik güvenlik taahhütlerine bağlı olduğunu söyledi. Rubio, Husilerin Suudi Arabistan'a yönelik saldırılarının ardından Riyad'ın kendisini savunma hakkı bulunduğunu savundu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Derbarê rojnameger Rabîa Onverê de lêpirsîn hat despêkirin
content:
Nûçegihana JINNEWSê Rabia Onver, bi tohmeta ku “propagandaya rêxistinê kiriye” ji ber parvekirinên wê yên li ser hesabê wê yê medyaya civakî, ji bo îfadeyê hat gazîkirin.




Rabia Onverê li Şaxa Têkoşîna li dijî Terorê ya Emniyeta Polîsan a Geverê îfadeya xwe da.




Di dema pirsê de, gotinên ku Rabia Onver di parvekirinên wê yên medyaya civakî de bikar aniye jî yek bi yek hatin lêkolînkirin. Ji wê hat pirsîn ka kesên ku di parvekirinan de hatine behskirin kî ne û gelo têkiliyek  wê bi wan re heye.




Her wiha ji Rabia Onverê hat pirsîn ka gelo endamek ji malbata wê bi PKKê re têkiliyek wan heye an na.




Rabia Onver di îfadeya xwe de derbarê pirsên ku jê re hatine kirin de diyar kir ku nivîsên ku behsa wan tê kirin di çarçoveya xebatên rojnamegeriyê de ne.




Piştî pêvajoya îfadeyê, Rabia Onver bi parêzerê xwe re ji emniyetê derket.




(AY)

author: Sebastian Lotzer
title: City of Blood [Part ll]
content:
“Macht kommt nicht von einem Abzeichen oder einer Waffe. Macht entsteht durch Lügen. Groß lügen und die ganze verdammte Welt dazu bringen, mit dir zu spielen. Sobald alle mit dem einverstanden sind, von dem sie in ihrem Herzen wissen, dass es nicht stimmt, hast du sie an den Eiern.”




Senator Roark – Sin City




Jede Stadt hat ihre ganz eigene, persönliche Hölle. Manche sagen, es gäbe keine Hölle, so wie es kein Paradies gäbe. Dem letzteren mag man zustimmen, vielleicht sogar mit einem bedauernden Seufzen, aber die Existenz der Hölle an sich ist nicht wirklich zu bestreiten. Der Ort, an dem sie existiert, ist nicht exakt definiert, im Laufe der Jahre, ja sogar Jahrzehnte, wechseln die Schauplätze, die Protagonisten, aber sie ist immer da, an jedem einzelnen Tag, den diese Stadt gesehen hat. In Berlin ist dieser Ort nun das Kottbusser Tor, der Kotti.




Das war nicht immer so, ganz im Gegenteil. Wenn man früher mit der U-Bahn, die am Nollendorfplatz sich aus der Tiefe erhebt und in eine Hochbahntrasse mündet, am Kotti ankam, wurde das Herz weit. Kein verlogener Glanz wie in der City, die letzten Kontrolleure, die damals noch in uniformierten Gruppen unterwegs waren, hatten spätestens am Gleisdreieck die Segel gestrichen. Das war ein ungeschriebenes Gesetz. In Kreuzberg werden keine Fahrkarten kontrolliert. Wenn die Gegenseite dagegen verstoßen wollte, musste sie immer ein paar Dutzend Bullen mitbringen, die die Kontrolleure in ihren blauen Uniformen beschützen vor der Wut und dem Ärger aufgebrachter Fahrgäste. Das ganze war aber sehr personalintensiv, sorgte jedesmal für einen riesen Heckmeck und wurde deshalb nur ein paar Mal im Jahr und meistens zu Zeiten durchgezogen, wo die notorischen Schwarzfahrer noch im Bett lagen oder gerade ihren ersten Kaffee runterschluckten.




Das Kottbusser Tor war nicht immer hässlich, aber was der Krieg übrig gelassen hatte von seinen alten Häuserzeilen wurde Anfang der 70er großflächig abgerissen um Platz zu schaffen für eine Autobahn und seelenlose Neubauten, im Norden des Platzes entstand das NKZ (das ‘Neue Kreuzberger Zentrum’ wird ohne Widerspruch mitten in Deutschland von wirklich allen nur ‘das NKZ’ genannt), der Hochhauskomplex sollte später den Lärm der Autobahn abschirmen. Schön also war der Kotti eigentlich nie, seitdem ich denken kann, aber er war das Herz von 36. Hier begannen die wichtigsten Demos und Krawalle der Hausbesetzer und wenn am 1. Mai schon lange Schicht war, weil die Bullen alles Kontrolle gebracht hatten, flogen hier noch die Flaschen Richtung Ordnungskräfte und der eine oder andere ehrliche Faustkampf wurde noch mit ihnen ausgetragen. Der Kotti sollte schon immer “befriedet” werden, in den 80er gingen die Bullen immer wieder massiv gegen das Volk vor, was so am Kotti abhing. Daraus entstand u.a. das legendäre “Punkerfrühstück”, das natürlich nicht vor Sonntag 12:00 Uhr begann und zu dem sich nicht nur einige hundert Punker versammelten sondern auch etliche Sympathisanten, was dann zu handfesten Meinungsverschiedenheiten mit den angerückten Einsatzhundertschaften führte.




Und während die Oranienstraße und der Lausitzer Platz schon lange “gefallen” sind, wobei diese Niederlage weniger den Bullen als dem Generalangriff der Gentrifizierung zuzuschreiben ist, blieb der Kotti bis vor wenigen Jahren so etwas wie ein ‚widerständiger Ort”. Noch im Spätherbst des letzten Jahrzehnt machten die Auseinandersetzungen von Einheimischen mit den Bullen Berlinweit Schlagzeilen. Auslöser war die brutale Festnahme eines mutmasslichen Fahrraddiebes, was zu Solidarisierung einer großen Menge, vorwiegend migrantischer Anwohner und Besitzer kleiner Läden führte. Blumenkübel, Flaschen und allerlei andere Gegenstände flogen in Richtung der Bullen, ich war gerade das Wochenende zuvor wieder vom behäbigen 61 zurück nach 36 gezogen und Zeuge der Geschehnisse. “Fein gemacht”, dachte ich mir, “endlich wieder Zuhause angekommen.“ Und auch während der Jahre des Corona Ausnahmezustandes lächelte man sich verschmitzt zu, wenn man den Platz, entgegen der behördlichen Anordnungen, ohne Maske zu tragen querte, was dazu führte, dass die Bullen jeden Abend mehrere Mannschaftswagen am Kotti positionierten, deren Besatzungen die wenigen Passanten belästigten, die es wagten kurz vor Mitternacht noch frische Luft zu schnappen ohne dabei sinnfrei eine FFP2 Maske spazierenzutragen.




Doch Corona ist vorbei und dank der fürsorglichen Einsperrungen der Regierung haben wir es überlebt und nun sind die apokalyptischen Reiter über den Kotti hergefallen. Massen von Touristen, zugezogenen Hipstern und der Partymob wimmeln über den Platz, die Junkies und Obdachlosen gehen in den Massen fast unter, alle schauen über das Elend hinweg, niemand interessiert sich mehr für den anderen und irgendwann werden sie einfach über die Leichen drüber steigen, um den besten Hintergrund für ihre Selfies zu generieren. Der soziale Kannibalismus in Extase. Zu jedem beliebigen Anlass regiert der Ballermann in 36 und dass große Teile der Demo zum 1. Mai stundenlang am Heinrichplatz feststecken, weil die TikTok PdL ihre langweilige Bühnenshow zum “Tag der Arbeit” mit Ikkimel aufwerteten, fast die generelle Entwicklung gut zusammen. In einer Welt der Blasen, die nicht mehr in der Lage sind, über die Grundsätzlichkeiten der Welt miteinander zu kommunizieren, ersetzt der Event die Berührungen, die sozialen Beziehungen. “Wir erleben die Rückkehr der Oberflächenverliebtheit” schrieb Christian Klar schon weitsichtig in den 90er aus dem Knast.




“Seitdem hat ein Jahrhundert der Verwüstung hinreichend veranschaulicht, wie richtig Kafka in allen Dingen lag und das fast als einziger. In allererster Instanz muss jeder den Zugang zu dem, was er denn noch empfindet, gut verbarrikadiert halten. Und man ist gut beraten, sich gegenseitig in diesem rühmlichen Bestreben zu unterstützen – was jedoch keineswegs verhindert, sein Leben in Abhängigkeit von dem Rumor zu führen, die aus dem verbotenen Untergeschoss dringt. Schließlich hat eine Verstümmelung noch nie das Auftreten von Phantomschmerz verhindert. Die herrschende Gesellschaftsordnung ist mehr denn je eine Verschwörung von Verstümmelten – eine objektive, strukturelle, spontane, universelle Verschwörung.”




Konspirationistisches Manifest




In ‘City of Blood’ sind die Vampire nicht mehr die Ausgeburt unserer uneingestanden Urängste und Projektionen, sie sind nur ein Clan mehr, der seine Geschäfte tätigt und nach politischem Einfluss strebt. So wie das gedruckte Geld nach dem Kollaps des Nationalsozialismus keinen wirklichen Wert mehr besaß und mit Zigaretten, Kaffee und Wertgegenständen gehandelt wurde, so ersetzt das Blut in ‘City of Blood’ das bedruckte Papier. Die Blutbank als Fort Knox. Von dort aus ist es kein gewagter Bogenschlag zur marxistischen Analyse der warenförmigen Durchdringung aller Lebensbereiche, ja des Lebens selbst dieser Tage – in der Welt, in der wir leben und überleben. Die Subjekte selbst ahnen darum, wenn sie es nicht sogar wissen. Dieses Wissen und Halbwissen produziert eine unglaubliche Menge von individueller und kollektiver Angst. Und Angst hat, wie alle wissen, eine unglaubliche Macht. Die reife Haltung konfrontiert sich mit dieser Angst, erforscht ihre gesellschaftlichen Ursachen und Zusammenhänge, sucht nach Aufhebung, produziert revolutionäres Denken und Handeln. In der allgegenwärtigen gesellschaftlichen Regression jedoch sucht die erdrückende Mehrheit der Subjekte nach Zuflucht in Projektion und Delegierung. Der Corona Ausnahmezustand war die Generalsstabseinübung dieser Synthese aus paranoider Angst vor der Auslöschung und der Delegierung der Errettung an einen übermächtigen Staat. Das eint auch den Linkspopulismus wie Rechtspopulismus: Die “Eroberung” des Staates als Zielstellung. Dabei spielt es keine wirkliche Rolle, wer den oder die Bürgermeister/in von Berlin stellt, ebenso wie es keine strategische Rolle spielt, dass Italien seit 2022 von Meloni regiert wird. Alle Mitte-Links Regierungen vor ihr haben mehr repressive und arbeitnehmerfeindliche Gesetze und Dekrete erlassen als die Vorsitzende der Nachfolgepartei des MSI. Alles weitere regelt der Markt.




Die medialen Begleitmusiken zur möglichen Regierungsübernahme durch die PdL sind ebenso Nebelkerzen wie die mögliche Regierungsübernahme selbst. Es spielt überhaupt keine Rolle, die Machtverhältnisse im sozialen Antagonismus verändern sich um keinen µ, oder höchstens zu unseren Ungunsten, weil der ganze partizipatorische Blödsinn noch allgemeiner um sich greift. Nach all den Massenmobilisierungen per Unterschriftenliste nun also als letzter Strohhalm die parlamentarische Option. Wir konnten ähnliches schon vor ein paar Jahren in Frankreich beobachten, wo vor dem Horizont eines möglichen Wahlerfolgs von Marie Le Pens ‘Rassemblement National’ die “Volksfront” aus der Mottenkiste der Geschichte gezaubert wurde. Der “Wahlsieg” der “Volksfront” fiel nicht zufällig zusammen mit dem Ende der sozialen Bewegungen, die die letzte Dekade geprägt hatten. Gegen die allgemeine Regression, die auch in nicht unerheblichen Teilen die Überreste antagonistischer Stimmen hierzulande erreicht hat, gilt es sich mit einem Diskurs zu behaupten, der an der Grundsätzlichkeit der Aufhebung der Warenförmigkeit aller gesellschaftlichen Beziehungen als Prämisse festhält. Im Allgemeinen wie in den konkreten Kämpfen und sozialen Konflikten.




„Auf der Basis des Kapitals kann das Ganze nur vom Teil aus verstanden werden. Das Wissen ist an den Kampf gebunden. Wahrhaftig erkennt nur, wer wahrhaftig hasst.“




Mario Tronti




wird fortgesetzt…

title: AFFAIRE DE BUDAPEST PAS UNE EXTRADITION DE PLUS #FREE ZAID
content:
Soyons nombreuses & nombreux dans et autour la salle d'audience de la cour d'appel de Paris (Palais de Justice), à 15h30 le 7 octobre- chambre 5, pôle 7 - pour manifester notre résistance et notre solidarité

 

!




AFFAIRE

 

DE

 

BUDAPEST

 




PAS

 

UNE

 

EXTRADITION

 

DE

 

PLUS


#

FREE

 

ZAID




"On doit refuser cette idée de coupable ou innocent, ce sont des personnes qui se posent comme résistants" 


Zero Calcare




"Si j'avais 30ans ou 40ans de moins j'aurais été aux cotés de Zaid et Gino, des formes de résistances, de manifestations ou de contre manifestations sont tout à fait nécessaires"


Robert Guediguian




Le 7 octobre 2026, la justice française va juger de l'extradition de Zaid A. vers la Hongrie

 à la cour d'appel de 

Paris

. Après des mois de procédure, marqués par plusieurs renvois, 

cette audience - la dernière de plaidoirie - est déterminante pour Zaid

.




Enfant de 

réfugiés palestiniens vivant en Syrie

, Zaid A. s'exile en 

Allemagne

 en 2014 à l'âge de 11 ans avec sa famille pour fuir le régime d'Assad et la guerre meurtrière qu'il livre contre le peuple syrien. En 2024, poursuivi par un 

mandat d'arrêt européen émis par la Hongrie

 dans le cadre de l'affaire dite «

 

de Budapest

 

», il se 

réfugie en France

 en espérant que celle-ci refuse son extradition comme elle l'avait fait pour 

Gino

, un autre inculpé de l'affaire. Cependant, malgré ce précédent juridictionnel, il n'est pas sûr que la justice prenne la même décision. 

Dans ce cas, Zaid A. perdrait à nouveau la vie qu'il a construit activement depuis un an en France en s'engageant dans de nombreuses activités solidaires et associatives

. Il risque en outre un procès inéquitable et des conditions de détention délétères en Hongrie.




En

 2023

, une vague de mesures répressives transfrontalières à l'encontre d'une vingtaine de personnes a été déclenchée : c'est ce qui a été appelé

 “l'affaire de Budapest”.

 La Hongrie les accuse d'avoir participé à des agressions contre des néonazis en marge du 

"Jour de l'honneur"

 à Budapest. Ce défilé annuel rythmé par des saluts nazis, rassemble des nostalgiques du 

III

e

 reich en uniforme 

SS

. Tandis que le régime d'extrême droite de Viktor Orban a autorisé et légitimé ces célébrations, une répression démesurée s'est abattue sur les militant·es venu·es de plusieurs pays pour protester contre cette 

glorification de l'idéologie nazie.







Mais la traque à laquelle se livre la Hongrie ne se cantonne pas à ce pays. 

L'affaire de Budapest est l'affaire d'une collaboration entre les États européens, qui prennent le relais à tour de rôle pour tenter de neutraliser les mouvements de contestation. 

 On peut citer le cas de 

Gino

 : si la France a refusé son extradition vers la Hongrie en septembre 2025, elle vient de l'accepter vers l'Allemagne, où il sera jugé selon les mêmes accusations. A l'heure actuelle il n'est pas possible de savoir si de là-bas il sera extradé vers la Hongrie. Par ailleurs, 

le cas de Maja T., une des autres inculpé·es, est emblématique à ce sujet

 : en 2024, alors qu'iel est incarcéré·e en Allemagne, iel est 

transféré·e illégalement en Hongrie par la police allemande

 quelques heures 

avant que la Cour constitutionnelle statue sur son recours et qu'elle ordonne de ne pas procéder au transfert.

 Cela n'a pas empêché la Hongrie de la placer à l'

isolement

 depuis deux ans, sous vidéo surveillance continue, de la soumettre à des fouilles personnelles constantes et de la condamner le 30 septembre 2026 à sept ans de prison. La peine est sans commune mesure avec les faits reprochés. Précisons ici, que 

la cour ne l'accuse plus d'être co-auteure mais la condamne pour complicité.







Dans ce contexte de collaboration sélective, 

la répression des militants antifascistes semble primer sur la protection des droits fondamentaux.

 La France pourrait aujourd'hui accepter d'extrader Zaid en Hongrie sous prétexte du changement de gouvernement. Cependant l'arrivée au pouvoir d'une droite conservatrice pro-européenne ne trompe personne. 

Les risques élevés d'atteinte aux droits humains n'ont pas disparu avec le changement de gouvernement et la surpopulation carcérale ainsi que les conditions de détention dégradantes ont largement été dénoncées

 par plusieurs rapports du comité Helsinki1 ainsi que du Comité européen pour la prévention de la torture (

CPT

) du conseil de l'Europe. Les 

témoignages de Maja 

 sur les violences qu'iel subit régulièrement encore aujourd'hui montrent que la situation n'a pas changé.




Le cas de Zaïd présente une particularité majeure

. 

Il n'est pas citoyen européen, il a perdu son statut de réfugié et sa demande de naturalisation a été suspendue suite à l'acharnement judiciaire

 dont il est la cible depuis plusieurs années. 

 

Son extradition 

 pose donc non seulement la question de ses conditions de détention et de son droit à un procès équitable en Hongrie, mais également celle de l'absence de protection diplomatique dont il disposerait dans les prisons hongroises 

. En effet, sa nationalité syrienne dans un pays connu pour ses politiques xénophobes et racistes constitue un risque supplémentaire. En outre, il n'a aucune garantie contre un éventuel éloignement ultérieur vers la Syrie, où son statut de militant politique rend sa situation risquée et plus qu'incertaine.


Si Zaid risque aujourd'hui d'être extradé vers la Hongrie, si la Cour de Cassation a confirmé l'extradition de Gino vers l'Allemagne, si Maja reste en prison et que six autres inculpé·es sont jugés en Allemagne à l'heure actuelle, c'est que la criminalisation des militant·es antifascistes s'intensifie. L'affaire de Budapest s'inscrit dans un contexte de montée de l'extrême droite partout dans le monde et démontre de sa normalisation au sein des institutions. En septembre 2025, 

Trump utilise l'assassinat de Charlie Kirk pour publier une circulaire visant à classer «

 

les antifas

 

»

 - terme délibérément flou visant à regrouper tout ce qui l'arrange- d'organisation terroriste.




Orban lui emboîte le pas et le parlement hongrois inscrit dans sa liste nationale antiterroriste les groupes considérés comme «

 

antifascistes

 

».

 

Le nouveau gouvernement n'a pas abrogé cette législation

. Par ailleurs, le

 16 juillet 2026, une conférence organisée par l'administration Trump, rassemble des représentants de 66 pays - parmi lesquels l'Allemagne et la France - pour combattre "les extrémistes de gauche",

 démontrant non seulement que la 

criminalisation du mouvement antifasciste

 risque de s'étendre très rapidement à l'ensemble des mouvements de contestation, mais aussi qu'elle semble essentielle au projet de l'extrême droite mondiale. 




Loin d'être anecdotique, le cas de Zaid doit donc illustrer notre capacité collective à faire front et défendre nos camarades, qu'ils soient militant·es antifascistes, écologistes ou lycéen·nes révoltés.

 Les 

prochains jours seront décisifs 

 : quand des milliers de lycéen·nes sont réprimé·es, que les militant·es révolutionnaires sont traqué·es à travers toute l'Europe, que les personnes migrantes sont systématiquement refoulées et que les prisonnier·es politiques sont réduit·es au silence, 

il nous faut nous faire entendre, nous organiser et riposter.




Soyons nombreuses & nombreux dans et autour la salle d'audience de la cour d'appel de Paris, à 15h30 le 7 octobre- chambre 5, pôle 7 - pour manifester notre résistance et notre solidarité

 

!

title: Colloque « Anarchie, Femmes, Émancipation »
content:
Le samedi 10 octobre, de 9h30 à 18h, Radio Libertaire sera en direct et en public depuis l'

AERI

, 57 rue Etienne Marcel à Montreuil (Métro Croix de Chavaux) pour diffuser et enregistrer les débats du Colloque «

 

Anarchie, Femmes, Émancipation

 

».


Radio Libertaire, sur le 89,4 

FM

 et en streaming sur le site 

https://radio-libertaire.org/accueil.php




Depuis le 150

e

 anniversaire de la Commune de Paris en 2021, groupe Commune de Paris de la Fédération anarchiste consacre annuellement une journée d'étude à un des thèmes majeurs de cette révolution. Ce fut le cas avec l'autogestion, l'art et la culture, la place des idées anarchistes dans la Commune… En 2026, quatre groupes de la région parisienne, les Groupes Louise Michel, Salvador Segui, Pierre Besnard et Commune de Paris organisent une journée destinée aux femmes, à leur rôle pendant la Commune, en projetant leurs revendications dans les luttes actuelles en France et dans le monde. 


Aujourd'hui, comment les luttes des femmes participent à la perspective anarchiste

 

?


Sur tous les continents, les femmes luttent malgré les guerres, les dictatures, les emprisonnements, les déplacements forcés, les violences sexuelles. La situation des femmes relève aussi de l'apartheid de genre et, les féminicides ne cessent. Mais les combats pour le droit à l'avortement, à la scolarisation, à l'accès à l'emploi, à l'égalité des salaires se rejoignent contre le patriarcat et le capitalisme. De même du côté du genre et de la pensée queer, ou dans le champ culturel, apparaissent des revendications contre l'invisibilisation des femmes, sur la liberté du corps, le respect de chacun et chacune, être libre. Il reste à continuer de définir et de faire vivre l'anarcha- féminisme.




Programme




9h : accueil


9h30 : Présentation de la journée, introduction. Hélène Hernandez et Francis Pian


9h45 : Quelle mémoire, qul legs des femmes de la Commune

 

? Sidonie Verhaeghe


10h15 : Des femmes anarchistes : Lucy Parson, Voltairine de Cleyre, Emma Goldman. Alice Béja et Léa Gauthier




Partout, au plan international, des femmes luttent


10h45 : en Amérique latine, Journal des 7-8-9 mars à Santiago du Chili, la révolte libertaire des femmes. Monica Jornet


11h15 : en Afghanistan, Non à la reconnaissance et à la normalisation des Talibans. Shoukria Haidar, association 

NEGAR


11h45 : en Iran, de «

 

Femme Vie Liberté

 

» à «

 

Vive le roi

 

». Assareh Assa


12h15 : en Espagne, anarchistes espagnoles, luttes et émancipation. Ramon Pino


12h45 : en France, le syndicalisme féministe, un projet d'émancipation. Intersyndicale Femmes




Pause méridienne




Genre et Queer


14h30 : se défaire de la pensée hétéronormée. Natacha Chetcuti-Osorovitz


15h : féminisme, anarchisme et transidentités, ne pas se tromper d'ennemi. Karine Snepmac




Dans le monde artistique


15h30 : compositrices, une classique, oui bien sût

 

! Florence Belenfant


16h : une chambre, un lieu à soi pour... la femme endettée et toutes les autres. Mariama Keita


16h30 : le fil des amours. Sandrine-Malika Charlemagne


17h : poesiA. Monica Jornet




Conclusion


17h30 : pour un anarchaféminisme. Hélène Hernandez

title: Thomas More : L'utopie - lecture Anarchiste du 12 octobre 2026
content:
L'Utopie n'a pas attendu les anarchistes. Le mot est créé par Thomas More qui le met en titre de son livre, paru en 1513, et lui donne un contenu toujours aussi brûlant.







u-topie : du grec ‘u' qui signifie ‘sans' et ‘topos' qui signifie ‘lieu'.







Un projet sans lieu, hors sol

 

? Si Thomas More a le mérite d'avoir inventé le mot, son livre a surtout suscité beaucoup d'engouement et provoqué un débat qui s'est prolongé jusqu'à nous, malgré les perplexités qui l'ont accompagné... Mais ce n'était qu'un début

 

!




Les anarchistes ne sont pas des rêveurs, ils veulent donner à l'utopie une dimension concrète : construire une société égalitaire et libertaire.







La question de l'utopie sera au cœur des lectures anarchistes durant l'année 2026/2027.




À une époque qui ne cesse d'en appeler au réalisme, au pragmatisme, voire à un utilitarisme étroit, où le mot «

 

dystopie

 

» s'est imposé au regard des menaces politiques, économiques et écologiques qui hantent les sociétés actuelles, l'utopie a-t-elle encore une place dans les débats politiques

 

? Entendre : une place autre que celle que lui vaut l'usage méprisant de l'adjectif «

 

utopique

 

» dans l'expression «

 

c'est utopique

 

»

 

? Au fil de séances à venir, nous proposons donc la lecture de quelques grands textes consacrés à l'utopie – ou, plus justement, aux utopies rédigées par quelques auteurs marquants – ou aux commentaires critiques qu'ils ont suscités.




Chaque séquence s'appuiera ainsi sur un texte, présenté en ouverture de la causerie, de manière à introduire le débat. Les participants seront ensuite invités à y prendre une part active.




Ci-dessous, le programme de cette année 2026-2027 des lectures anarchistes :




 12 octobre : Thomas More - L'Utopie

 9 novembre : Voltaire - Candide ou l'optimisme, chap. 17 et 18

 14 décembre : Denis Diderot - Supplément au voyage de Bougainville

 11 janvier : Charles Fourrier - Le nouveau monde industriel et sociétal

 8 février : Victor Considérant - Exposé abrégé du système phalanstérien

 8 mars : Étienne Cabet - Voyage en Icarie

 12 avril : Louis Blanc : Organisation du travail

 10 mai : Joseph Dejacque - L'Humanisphère, utopie anarchique

 14 juin : Friedrich Engels - Socialisme utopique et socialisme scientifique




L'objectif de ces causeries, inspirées des causeries du 19

e

 siècle, est de créer un espace social, où l'on peut échanger en dehors du cadre du travail ou du cadre amical/familial, faire société ensemble. C'est un espace où on peut confronter nos idées et nos arguments et y politiser nos vies, face à un système qui nous pousse de plus en plus à en être passif.


Chacun.e y est légitime pour prendre la parole, ou simplement écouter. Chacun.e y est légitime pour modérer la parole, dans une organisation sans hiérarchie, une organisation anarchiste.


Vous pouvez amener quelques victuailles à partager lors des causeries. Aussi bien à manger qu'à boire, même si le bar est ouvert.

author: Einige Eltern
title: An unsere Kinder und Schüler
content:
Danke für alles. Für die Kühnheit, den Mut und die Entschlossenheit.




Danke, dass ihr uns daran erinnert, dass es nichts zu erwarten gibt. Wir selbst haben so lange gewartet, dass wir wissen, was es am Ende kostet.




Auf das Ende des Tages zu warten, auf das Ende der Woche, auf den Monatsanfang, auf die Rückmeldung der CAF. (1) Darauf zu warten, dass sich die Lage beruhigt, auf bessere Tage zu warten, auf die Wahlen zu warten, auf den Bus, auf die U-Bahn zu warten. Darauf zu warten, endlich ins Bett zu gehen. Immer wieder ins Bett zu gehen.




Euch hat man auch gesagt, ihr sollt warten. Auf das Ende des Tages, den Beginn der Ferien, die Ergebnisse von Parcoursup. (2) Auf eine Ausbildung zu warten, warum nicht auf einen Job, darauf, selbstständig zu sein – und dann festzustellen, dass das das Gegenteil von Freiheit ist. Darauf zu warten, dass das Leben genau dort beginnt, wo es endet.


Ihr habt wirklich gut daran getan, mit dem Warten aufzuhören.


Bravo für den Humor, die Verkleidungen, das Feuerwerk, die Solidarität und alles, was wir auf den Straßen gesehen haben.




Die Welt, die wir euch hinterlassen, ist eine Ruine, die Zukunft, die wir für euch vorbereiten, ein Albtraum – und dennoch schafft ihr es, Spaß zu haben. Ihr seid die beste Version von uns selbst, die Summe all dessen, was wir vermasselt haben, all dessen, worauf wir verzichtet haben.


Das wisst ihr zwar, aber es ist wichtig, es euch noch einmal zu sagen. Auch wir sind sehr besorgt. Aber wir wären es noch viel mehr, wenn ihr die Welt so akzeptieren würdet, wie sie ist.




An die Lehrer, Aufsichtspersonen und Schulleiter




Am Dienstag habt ihr gestreikt, um bessere Arbeitsbedingungen zu fordern. Ihr seid marschiert, habt demonstriert und Parolen skandiert – und dann seid ihr wieder nach Hause gegangen. Die Regierung hat sich nicht einmal die Mühe gemacht, Euch zu verachten.


Innerhalb von zwei Tagen haben Eure Schüler mit ihren Blockaden im Élysée-Palast einen Krisenstab ausgelöst, Panik in den Fernsehsendungen verursacht und die Schließung eines Großteils der französischen Oberstufen zur Folge gehabt. Daraus lässt sich eine Lehre ziehen.




All ihre Forderungen kennt Ihr und teilt sie: überfüllte Klassen, nicht ersetzte Kollegen, unhygienische Räumlichkeiten und Rettungsfolien an den Fenstern, um schon ab Mai nicht zu verbrennen. Und natürlich „Parcoursup“ – dessen Missstände und Ungerechtigkeiten kennt Ihr auswendig. Diese fiese kleine Maschine der Selektion und des Drucks, die jeden Tag ebenso auf Eure Schüler wie auf Euch lastet. Pädagogik der Demütigung. Und doch sind eure Schüler gekommen, um euch daran zu erinnern: Nichts von dem, was getan wurde, lässt sich rückgängig machen.




Vielen Dank an alle unter Euch, die sich den Blockaden angeschlossen und ihre Schüler unterstützt haben. Die Gleichung ist einfach: Ihr habt objektiv gesehen nichts zu verlieren und alles zu gewinnen – angefangen damit, dass auch ihr euch nicht länger demütigen lasst.




Wenn ihr aufrichtig Eure gemeinsame Situation ablehnen würdet, wäre das eine andere Geschichte: Für eine Regierung ist es nicht so einfach, einen Mathelehrer zu würgen oder der Französischlehrerin mit einem LBD-Gewehr in den Kopf zu schießen. Vielleicht würden dann alle mitmachen.




An Laurent Nuñez, Edouard Geffray und die Präfekten




Auf Ihren Befehl hin schikaniert die Polizei seit mehreren Tagen Kinder. Auf Ihren Befehl hin wurden sie niedergeschlagen, über den Boden geschleift, gewürgt und aus nächster Nähe mit LBD-Geschossen beschossen. Sie wollten sie nicht nur verletzen, Sie haben alles getan, um sie zu demütigen.


1.949 Schüler wurden festgenommen – wie viele Polizisten wurden zur Rechenschaft gezogen? Welche Lehren sind daraus zu ziehen?


Und dennoch verschanzen Sie sich hinter Lügen und Verantwortungslosigkeit.




Man muss wirklich noch nie einen Fuß vor eine weiterführende Schule gesetzt haben, um zu glauben, dass „La France insoumise“ auch nur die geringste Verantwortung für diesen Ausbruch der Jugend trüge. Man muss besonders schlecht informiert sein, um sich vorzustellen, dass „Stellvertreter der extremen Linken“ heimlich die vor den Schulen aufgestapelten Mülltonnen fernsteuern würden. Einzig und allein, und auf schmutzige Art lügt Ihr.




Während die Schüler Lehrer, Mittel und ein wenig Wertschätzung fordern, rufen Sie die Polizei dazu auf, beim Einsatz von Gewalt „keine Hemmungen zu haben“, und wenn Polizeigewerkschaften fordern, mit LBD-Waffen auf sie schießen zu dürfen, warnen Sie die Präfekten vor jeglicher „entgegenstehender Anweisung vor Ort“. Wir erfinden oder übertreiben nichts, wir zitieren Sie aus „Le Monde“ vom 2. Oktober 2026. Sie fordern und fördern Gewalt gegen unsere Kinder. Eingeschlossen in Ihren vergoldeten Büros lassen Sie die Polizei los und zählen die Festnahmen und Verletzten.




Heute Morgen wurden 400 Gymnasien blockiert. Nicht von den Schülern, sondern durch Ihre Verordnungen. Die während einer Pandemie ausgearbeiteten Hygiene-Maßnahmen werden zur Waffe, mit der Ihr die Jugend einsperrt. Der Trick ist zu durchschaubar: Es ist jedem verboten, sich in der Nähe einer weiterführenden Schule zu versammeln. Wer es wagt, das Haus zu verlassen, kann festgenommen werden. Nachdem ihr die Gewalt inszeniert habt, organisiert ihr nun ihre Freiheitsberaubung.




An uns alle




Wie können wir das, was unsere Kinder – die Kinder – in ihrer Freude und trotz des Tränengases zum Ausdruck bringen, ernst nehmen? From the 1880s through the 1940s tens of thousands of anarchists were active in the United States, the overwhelming majority of them first- and second-generation immigrants. But most were not yet devotees of the anarchist cause when they arrived on American shores. Instead, a clear link existed between migration and the embrace of anarchist ideology. This study asks how and why thousands of migrants became anarchists, and how their embrace of an anti-nationalist and cosmopolitan ideology shaped their identities, experiences and actions.

Utilizing anarchist publications, government surveillance files, and archival materials, it focuses on Eastern European Jews and Italians—the two largest segments of the anarchist movement by the turn of the century—and the development of anarchism among these groups in three important centers of American anarchism: New York’s Lower East Side, Paterson, New Jersey, and San Francisco. It then follows the changing fortunes of the movement in the face of war, the Russian Revolution, the First Red Scare, and the birth of communism and fascism, and ends with an examination of immigrant American anarchist participation in the Spanish Civil War of 1936–39, and that conflict’s dramatic impact on the movement in the United States.

This study argues that it was American conditions that usually made immigrants into anarchists, rather than European ones, inextricably linking the histories of migration and American anarchism. Nevertheless, the phenomenon of post-migration radicalization defies categorization within most historiographical paradigms of European immigration that focus on the construction of “hyphenated” American identities or “hybrid” transnational ones. Anarchists chose an alternative: they embraced an ideology that opposed both Americanization and Old World nationalisms, severing their attachments to their states of origin while willfully resisting assimilation into their host society. They formulated a radical cosmopolitan outlook and identity that embraced diversity, rejected hierarchies, and extended solidarity across national, ethnic, and racial divides. This cosmopolitanism was ultimately unable to withstand the onslaught of competing nationalisms ranging from Americanism to fascism to Zionism, but it stands as an important example of a transnational collective identity delinked from nationalism, the nation-state and racial hierarchies.

I have incurred many debts while working on this dissertation. First and foremost I must thank Amanda Zeiders, my partner in crime (and life) throughout the years I was writing it. She has put up with more than I ever could have asked her to, and in return has kept me sane and never hesitated to remind me of what is important. As promised, she will receive two copies of this manuscript, one to read and one to burn. I hope she enjoys the first activity as much as the second.

I have been privileged to work with a number of wonderful mentors over the years. The prehistory of this project dates back to my classes with Derek Hutchinson and Jim Jennings at the Mendocino Community High School, where Derek exposed me to the writings of Howard Zinn and Jim introduced me to academic research and writing. At Bennington College my growing love of history and interest in radical politics were nurtured by Ron Cohen, Mansour Farhang, David Phillips, Miroslava Prazak, Eileen Scully, Susan Sgorbati, Carol Symes and Paul Voice, as well as outside of the classroom by my friends and fellow members of the Bennington Student Action Network, and through innumerable discussions back in California with Clay Hinson and Dan Young. A senior year Field Work Term internship at the Emma Goldman Papers under the guidance of Candace Falk, Jessica Moran and Barry Pateman cemented my continuing fascination with the history of anarchism. At the University of Pittsburgh I was fortunate to work with a number of inspiring and supportive professors including Kathy Blee, Alejandro de la Fuente, Patrick Manning, Lara Putnam, Marcus Rediker, Rob Ruck and Bruce Venarde. Richard Oestreicher and Donna Gabaccia, in particular, have been unflagging in their encouragement and assistance even as I subjected them to endless chapter drafts.

A number of other scholars have generously shared their time, thoughts, and materials with me. Marcella Bencivenni, Kirk Shaffer and Michael Miller Topp all offered extensive comments on conference presentations based on this dissertation, while Barry Pateman read drafts of multiple chapters and Bill Chase and Fraser Ottanelli provided valuable feedback on Chapter 7. Salvatore Salerno and Jennifer Guglielmo were both exceedingly generous in sharing their own research and thoughts on the Paterson anarchists, and Bob Helms, Barry Pateman and Nunzio Pernicone all answered obscure questions I posed to them. Fellow graduate students have also lent invaluable assistance. I was privileged to have been able to coordinate research trips with my friends and colleagues Matthew Casey, Bayete Henderson and Dave Struthers. Dave Struthers and Travis Tomchuk also gave me copies of important primary documents from their own research and helped to shape my thinking through hours of conversations. Tania Boster, Roland Clark, Isaac Curtis, Niklas Frykman, Marie Skoczylas and all of my friends in Pittsburgh have contributed to this project through innumerable formal and informal discussions—and, at times, welcome distractions. Olivia Cummings and Anna Torres also shared their own insightful work and thoughts on anarchism, ethnicity, and race with me.

The unsung heroes of any study are, of course, the staff of the various libraries and archives where the research is done. Above all others, the members of the Interlibrary Loan Department at the University of Pittsburgh’s Hillman Library have indulged my every whim and heroically tracked down the most obscure of sources. The personnel of Hillman’s Microforms Collection were also helpful and pleasant throughout the countless hours I spent in front of microfilm readers. I must additionally extend my thanks to the staff at the Archives of Labor and Urban Affairs at Wayne State University, the Archivio Centrale dello Stato in Rome, the Immigration History Research Center at the University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, the incomparable International Institute of Social History in Amsterdam, as well as to Julie Herrada and the friendly folks at the Joseph A. Labadie Collection at the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor and Gail Malmgreen and the staff of the Tamiment Library and Robert F. Wagner Labor Archives at New York University.

This project was made possible by the financial support of numerous institutions. The University of Pittsburgh kindly funded much of my research with a C. Y. Hsu Summer Research Fellowship, an Arts and Sciences Summer Fellowship, an Andrew Mellon Predoctoral Fellowship, a Samuel P. Hays Summer Research Grant and a Lillian B. Lawler Predoctoral Fellowship. The Yiddish research for this dissertation would have been impossible without a Steiner Summer Internship for Yiddish Studies at the National Yiddish Book Center, where I learned from wonderful teachers like Robert Adler Peckerar and Naomi Tencer, and the NYBC also granted me a Gildin Yiddish Book Scholarship. From the Immigration History Research Center I received a Grant-in-Aid enabling me to delve into their expansive collection of Italian newspapers, and special dispensations from the World History Center and Professor Alberta Sbragia of the European Union Center of Excellence and European Studies Center allowed me to present some of my findings at the 2010 European Social Science History Colloquium in Ghent.

Finally, special thanks are due to Christopher Daley and Sophie Feyder, who munificently opened their home to me when I was stranded for several days in Belgium while frantically finishing this dissertation, due to an Icelandic volcano with an unpronounceable name. Someday I hope to return the favor.

For Yiddish words I have followed the YIVO transliteration system. Yiddish names, however, are rendered more familiarly as they appear in the catalogs of the Library of Congress and the National Yiddish Book Center, with the YIVO transliteration of surnames appearing in parentheses with their first appearance in the text if they differ. Authors of newspaper articles, as well as names in the titles of books and articles, have been transliterated as they originally appeared. I have also taken the liberty of capitalizing the Yiddish and Italian names of organizations and periodicals according the English standards.

In memory of Paul Avrich and Howard Zinn

During his sojourn in the United States in 1895–96, the Italian lawyer and renowned anarchist poet and playwright Pietro Gori wrote Senza Patria (Without a Country), which went on to become one of his most popular plays. Gori’s drama follows a disillusioned peasant and veteran of the war for Italian unification as he immigrates to America and finds “not a homeland (patria)” but only “a little more bread.” At the end of the story he comes to realize that workers like himself “are foreigners of every country!….we are outcasts! we are bastards!” He therefore becomes a radical and a partisan of “the true, sacred ideal: one single patria: the world; one single family: humanity….”[1] The protagonist’s estrangement from the nation-state is depicted as painful and alienating, but ultimately emancipatory, as he realizes that to have no country of one’s own means that one is instead a citizen of the world. To be “i senza patria” (those without a country), as Italian-speaking anarchists commonly identified themselves, was to stand in solidarity with the members of all countries. In his popular Stornelli d’esilio (Songs of Exile), first published in 1904 in the United States, Gori declared, “The whole world is our country / liberty is our law” (Nostra patria è il mondo intero / nostra legge è la libertà).[2] Here was the anarchist program stripped to its bare essentials: freedom and cosmopolitanism taken to their logical extremes.

Significantly, migration to the United States was the precipitating factor in Gori’s tale. This reflected the fact that transatlantic migration was crucial to the formation of an anarchist movement in the United States. From the 1870s through the 1940s, American anarchism was overwhelmingly a movement of first- and second-generation immigrants. Nor should this be surprising, as by 1880 foreign-born migrants and their children composed the majority of the American working class. During the period of class recomposition that accompanied the Second Industrial Revolution, the migrant workers whose labor powered American capital drew on forms of resistance and ideologies from their native countries, while also adapting these to their changed circumstances and developing new ones.[3] This process of segmented class composition produced different forms and degrees of radicalism within separate ethnoracial groups,[4] which in turn influenced and were influenced by the ideas and actions of other such groups.

And, like the migrant Italian peasant of Senza Patria, most foreign-born anarchists in the United States were not yet devotees of the anarchist cause when they arrived on American shores. Instead, a clear causal link existed between migration to the United States and the embrace of anarchist ideology. As Louis Adamic observed, “While anarchism no doubt had foreign roots, it was an American growth in America, nurtured in American soil.”[5] This study asks how and why tens of thousands of migrants became anarchists, and how their embrace of an anti-nationalist and radically cosmopolitan ideology shaped their identities, experiences and actions. It is “a social history of politics,” combining the methodologies of social, cultural, and labor history, transnational studies, critical race theory, and discursive analysis to recover the worlds from which these anarchists emerged, the new social worlds they created, and the ideal world they sought to build.[6]

Anarchism emerged as an international mass movement in the last decades of the nineteenth century in reaction to the global expansion of capitalist modes of production and the rise of modern nation-states. Fusing anti-capitalism with anti-statism, anarchist ideology rejected the nation-state as a legitimate socio-political unit, an acceptable guarantor of rights, or a viable vehicle for systemic change. Anarchists instead envisioned a borderless world of freely constituted autonomous communities and federations, with economies based on collectivist or libertarian communist principles. By 1902, one journalist estimated that the movement’s adherents worldwide numbered one million.[7] In the United States they numbered in the tens of thousands—perhaps over a hundred thousand at the movement’s peak—and immigrants made up the overwhelming majority. Rather than attempt a general and therefore cursory overview of anarchism in the United States, I have chosen to focus on two major immigrant populations— Eastern European Jews and Italians—in three important centers of the anarchist movement: New York’s Lower East Side, Paterson, New Jersey, and San Francisco.

This study therefore begins by analyzing the growth of anarchism in each of these cities from the 1880s until the First World War. Chapter 2 explores the emergence of a Yiddishspeaking anarchist movement in New York’s Jewish ghetto, which brought together sweatshop workers and Russified Jewish intellectuals under the influence of the city’s German anarchists. In Paterson, the subject of Chapter 3, silk weavers and dyers from Northern Italy established a movement that dominated the Italian community and labor movement for nearly three decades. Chapter 4 traces the formation of a multiethnic anarchist movement in San Francisco’s North Beach neighborhood and its many interactions with a diverse array of other migrant workers and radicals. Chapter 5 follows the changing fortunes of the anarchist movement in the face of major national and international developments between 1914 and 1924—war, the Russian Revolution, the First Red Scare, and the birth of communism and fascism—and Chapter 6 chronicles anarchists’ ongoing campaigns against communism and fascism within their communities, and their attempts to forge an “international” English-speaking movement. Finally, Chapter 7 examines American anarchist participation in the Spanish Civil War of 1936–39 and this conflict’s dramatic impact on the movement in the United States, which collapsed in its aftermath.

Several considerations guided the choice of both the case studies and the timeframe used in this study. One is the existing scholarship on anarchism. The first wave of immigrant anarchism, which consisted primarily of Germans and Czechs and roughly coincided with the decade of the 1880s, has received by far the most historical attention and been ably documented by a number of scholars.[8] The historiography on anarchism among the “new immigrants” arriving from Eastern and Southern Europe between 1880 and 1920, however, is much less complete. Because Italians and Yiddish-speaking Eastern European Jews made up the largest segments of this second wave of immigrant anarchism, they constitute the core subjects of this study, although their interactions with workers and radicals of different ethnoracial backgrounds are also central to my analysis.

The Lower East Side was the center of Jewish politics and culture and in the United States, and it occupied the same position within the Jewish anarchist movement. Unlike the Italian-speaking movement, which produced at least eighty-three anarchist publications in twelve states, Yiddish-speaking anarchists established just twenty, all but three them published in New York City. Of these, the Lower East Side’s Fraye Arbayter Shtime (Free Voice of Labor) was the undisputed leader and, running from 1890–1977, the only Yiddish anarchist paper to last more than five years.[9] With a print run of around 30,000 at the outbreak of the First World War, the Fraye Arbayter Shtime was also the most widely circulating anarchist publication in American history, with a peak readership estimated by one journalist to top 150,000. To a large degree, the history of Yiddish anarchism in New York City is the history of Jewish anarchism in America.[10]

Paterson, meanwhile, was long known as the capital city of Italian American anarchism. Along with Barre, Vermont, Spring Valley, Illinois, and Tampa, Florida, it was one of a handful of communities in which a large local anarchist movement competed, sometimes successfully, for dominance among Italian immigrants.[11] Out of these communities, that of Paterson was by far the most important in terms of the influence it exercised locally, nationally, and internationally. Nevertheless, the historiography on the Paterson anarchism is sparse and fragmentary, especially in English.[12]

San Francisco is a less obvious choice for study. Cities like New York, Chicago, and Philadelphia had larger numbers of anarchists, and the Bay Area does not have a reputation as a significant historical center of anarchism.[13] However, San Francisco produced the third-most anarchist publications of any American city between 1880 and 1940, behind only New York and Chicago. As a Pacific port city, moreover, the city was home to a diverse population that gave rise to a uniquely diverse anarchist movement that included Asians and Latin Americans as well as Europeans and native-born Americans, linking the local movement to anarchist activities on four continents. The interactions between the different elements of the movement are also important examples of panethnic and interethnic working-class cooperation and solidarity in a region and period characterized by stark ethnoracial divides.

The persistence of significant anarchist activity in each of these locations through the 1920s and 1930s determined the chronological scope of this dissertation. This may surprise some readers, as historians have been strangely eager to pinpoint the supposed death of American anarchism at convenient historical markers such as the Haymarket Affair of 1886–87 or the Russian Revolution and Red Scare of 1917–20. Nevertheless, a plethora of evidence attests to the continuation of anarchist activity up until the outbreak of the Second World War. The movement’s high point in terms of participants and influence was from 1900 to 1914, and though it underwent a slow decline throughout the 1920s and early 1930s, it experienced a brief revival in the second half of the 1930s due to the Spanish Civil War. This is reflected in the circulation of the American anarchist press, which peaked at over 100,000 in 1910 and, after a period of decline, stabilized at between 20,000 and 40,000 from 1921 to 1940 (see Table 1). Both the ascent of communism and the government repression of the Red Scare depleted anarchist ranks, but to a much smaller degree than has been assumed. More important were the increasing isolation of anarchism from the labor movement and the rest of the Left due to its anticommunism, and the immigration restrictions imposed in 1921 and 1924. Nevertheless, the anarchist movement remained in the forefront of the anti-Fascist activity in the 1920s and 1930s, and it contributed at least 100–200 members to the fight against fascism in the Spanish Civil War.

I am interested not only in the prominent activists and writers who helped mobilize the movement, but also in the majority of largely anonymous individuals who constituted its base. The German-born anarchist intellectual Rudolf Rocker urged,
