author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Levantamento aponta um caso de violência política a cada 37 horas durante campanha de 2026
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando 

aqui

.













Noite de 12 de setembro de 2026, Jaraguá do Sul, Santa Catarina. Um grupo de militantes de esquerda se reúne em uma casa após uma atividade política na cidade. Integra o grupo a advogada 

Fernanda Klitzke

, candidata à suplente na chapa de Décio Lima (PT) ao Senado. Vizinhos chamam a Polícia Militar (PM), reclamando de barulho. 




A polícia chega e a candidata se apresenta como advogada aos policiais e questiona uma abordagem. Fernanda é agredida com um mata leão, derrubada no chão, chutada, baleada com tiros de borracha e levada presa. Ela foi liberada em seguida e teve que passar por atendimento médico. 




A partir desse caso, de 12 a 28 de setembro, um levantamento da 

Agência Pública

 compilou casos de violência política denunciados por candidatos nas eleições deste ano. 

Foram identificadas 11 ocorrências em quatro das cinco regiões do Brasil. Ao menos uma a cada 37h. O dado que mais chama a atenção é que dos 11 casos, 6 deles (54,5%) envolvem policiais ou agentes de segurança privada como os agressores. 




A frequência de casos de violência política levantados pela 

Pública

 nesses 17 dias de campanha para o primeiro turno é maior do que a aferida no mais recente estudo realizado pelas ONGs Justiça Global e Terra de Direitos, que há 10 anos compila dados de violência política. No período entre o final do 2º turno da eleição de 2024 e a véspera do início da campanha política de 2026, dia 15 de agosto, foram 354 casos, um a cada 44h. Esse foi o período pré-eleitoral mais violento da série histórica, afirmam as organizações autoras do estudo.




Os 354 casos de violência política do estudo das ONGs representam um aumento de 18,4% em relação aos 299 casos registrados no período pré-eleitoral da edição anterior da pesquisa, entre 1º de novembro de 2022 e 15 de agosto de 2024. O levantamento aponta que a violência política não desaparece fora do calendário eleitoral, tanto que em 2025, ano sem eleições, 225 casos foram registrados. 







PMs e seguranças contra a atividade política




O levantamento da 

Agência Pública

 encontrou três episódios em que não houve violência física, mas intimidação criminosa a candidatos durante suas atividades de campanha. Foram dois incidentes em São Paulo e um em Pernambuco, envolvendo dois candidatos homens e duas candidatas mulheres. 




No último dia 15, a deputada estadual Rosa Amorim (PT), candidata a deputada federal, e a vereadora Jô Cavalcanti (PSOL), candidata a uma vaga na Assembleia Legislativa de Pernambuco, 

faziam panfletagem

 em frente ao Instituto Federal de Pernambuco, no Recife. Ambas são negras. Seguranças de uma empresa que prestava serviço na organização da fila de um exame pré-Enem retiraram o material das mãos dos estudantes e jogavam no lixo. 




Em São Paulo, no Vale do Anhangabaú, o motoboy e candidato a deputado estadual pelo PSOL, Júnior Freitas, um homem negro, realizava uma atividade de campanha, no dia 19 de setembro, com bandeiras com um grupo de apoiadores quando foram abordados por um segurança dizendo que não era possível fazer campanha no local, que seria privado.

 O Vale do Anhangabaú é uma praça pública que passou por uma recente modernização e a gestão do espaço e segurança foram privatizados pela prefeitura de São Paulo.

 Depois da abordagem, questionada pelo candidato, a atividade prosseguiu. 




Já o vereador Nabil Bonduki (PT) comandava uma pedalada com apoiadores no Minhocão, no dia 20 de setembro, uma via elevada para carros na capital paulista que aos finais de semana e feriados é liberada para pedestres e bicicletas. Ele foi abordado três vezes durante a atividade, uma delas por uma policial militar que pediu o RG do candidato, perguntou quantas pessoas estavam reunidas com ele e o tempo que ficariam no local. 







Para o advogado Alberto Rollo, especialista em direito eleitoral, apesar de não-violentas, as três abordagens configuram o crime previsto no artigo 332 do código eleitoral: impedir propaganda, com pena de detenção de 1 a 6 meses de prisão e multa. Para o jurista, contudo, o que mais preocupa não é a abordagem em si, mas a presença da PM e um eventual direcionamento da polícia. 




“O que preocupa mais é, pode ser ignorância [da policial militar que abordou o candidato], ela não sabe, ou pode ser ordem de alguém? É isso que preocupa. A Polícia Militar, eu não vou falar de prefeitura, vou falar de Estado. Polícia Militar é do Estado. Será que existe algum tipo de ordem para dificultar a propaganda de adversários políticos?”, questionou Rollo. 




Em 

Prata, no Cariri paraibano

, um grupo de simpatizantes do PT organizou e informou as autoridades locais sobre uma atividade com som em apoio à reeleição do presidente Lula no dia 12 de setembro. PMs e policiais da reserva apareceram no local atirando para o alto e para o chão. Manifestantes foram chamados de baderneiros e vagabundos. O PT denunciou o caso à Corregedoria da PM. A corporação afirmou, entretanto, que houve resistência à abordagem e que, por isso, foi necessário um disparo de advertência. 







Ação suprapartidária contra abuso de autoridade




As ações violentas recentes contra candidaturas de esquerda chamaram a atenção do ex-senador Eduardo Suplicy, 85, fundador do PT e atualmente deputado estadual em busca da reeleição. Em 

vídeo publicado em seu Instagram

, ele compilou diversos episódios ocorridos recentemente e defendeu uma atuação conjunta das forças políticas. “É preciso uma ação suprapartidária e denunciar à corregedoria e à ouvidoria da PM e ao Ministério Público e à Justiça Eleitoral”, afirmou. 







De acordo com o jurista Alberto Rollo, 

o policial militar que impede ou atrapalha uma atividade de campanha política “pratica ato de abuso de autoridade, porque está impedindo alguma coisa que é lícita.

 Então, além do crime do Código Eleitoral, tem o crime de abuso de autoridade”. 




Para o advogado, os candidatos vítimas de violência ou de abordagens policiais atrapalhando suas atividades políticas, devem, além de denunciar os casos à Justiça Eleitoral, procurar também a Justiça comum para denunciar o abuso de autoridade. 




Segundo Gisele Barbieri, coordenadora de incidência política da Terra de Direitos, os casos de violência policial identificados na pesquisa “vem aumentando” e geralmente ocorrem durante manifestações em defesa de demandas populares e na forma de apreensão irregular de materiais de campanha.




“É preciso cobrar respostas quanto à apuração e responsabilização dos [agentes públicos] envolvidos por parte das corporações. São casos que nos preocupam e apontam para abuso de autoridade por agentes de segurança que deveriam proteger esses representantes políticos, principalmente, no período de campanha e no exercício de seus direitos políticos”, afirmou. 







Ameaça à democracia 




Para Glaucia Marinho, diretora-executiva da ONG Justiça Global, a participação de agentes de segurança pública na violência política é uma ameaça à democracia. “A pesquisa mostra que inclusive grupos criminosos e, até mesmo, policiais entre os responsáveis pelos atos de violência. 

Estamos diante de um cenário que ameaça não apenas a vida de representantes políticos, mas também o funcionamento das instituições democráticas.

 O Estado brasileiro precisa desenvolver e aperfeiçoar mecanismos eficazes de prevenção, proteção, investigação e responsabilização para enfrentar essa violência de forma contínua.”. 




A pesquisa realizada pelas ONGs indicou ainda que em 64 episódios (18,1% do total) o agressor também possuía mandato eletivo ou cargo público. Quando somados a policiais e outros agentes estatais, os ataques cometidos por representantes do próprio Estado chegam a quase um terço do total (29,9%).




Situação relatada pelo policial civil e deputado estadual Leonel Radde (PT) ilustra essa realidade. Ele participava de uma 

atividade política em Charqueadas (RS)

, no dia 20 de setembro, acompanhado de uma vereadora da cidade, quando passou a ser ameaçado de morte por um policial penal armado e que, o deputado afirma, estaria alcoolizado. 




No Rio de Janeiro, em 28 de setembro, o deputado estadual Flavio Serafini (PSOL) denunciou o colega de Alerj, Alexandre Knoploch (PL), por 

ameaça

 e invasão. Ambos disputam a reeleição. Em vídeo registrado por apoiadores de Serafini, Knoploch aparece mostrando uma arma na cintura. Em entrevistas, o candidato do PL admitiu ainda ter usado spray de pimenta contra os adversários políticos e afirmou ter sido intimidado. 







Ataques são racistas e machistas




A menção ao gênero e à identidade racial de alguns dos políticos vítimas dos casos de violência levantados pela 

Pública

 nessa reportagem não é aleatória. 

A pesquisa da ONG Justiça Global e da Terra de Direitos aponta que metade das vítimas de violência política no período analisado é mulher, apesar de as mulheres ocuparem apenas 18% dos cargos no legislativo, segundo dados do TSE.

 A violência política, aponta a pesquisa das ONGs, além de machista é racista. Uma a cada três vítimas mulheres de violência política é preta ou parda. 




Nos casos compilados pela 

Pública

 há 13 vítimas diretas, sendo cinco mulheres, três delas se autodeclaram negras. Entre os oito homens vítimas de violência política, um é negro. 




Uma das mulheres negras vítima de violência política é a vereadora Iza Lourença (PSOL), de Belo Horizonte. Candidata a deputada estadual, ela teve o 

comitê atacado

 por adolescentes com uma bomba caseira que explodiu no portão do imóvel. Dois funcionários do comitê foram agredidos. 




No local, afirma a vereadora, foi roubado um banner e outros materiais da candidata e deixado material de campanha do deputado federal e candidato à reeleição Nikolas Ferreira (PL). Imagens que ela obteve de câmeras de segurança mostram os menores correndo e entregando uma sacola com o banner furtado nas mãos de um homem, que se disse apoiador do PL e que foi detido. 




A pesquisa da Justiça Global e da Terra de Direitos encontrou ações assumidas inclusive por grupos ou perfis declaradamente neonazistas ou supremacistas.

 Foram quatro casos de ameaça, todos contra mulheres pretas, em quatro estados: a prefeita Professora Nilda, de Parnamirim (RN), e as vereadoras Alice Carvalho (Santa Maria, RS), Vivi Reis (Belém, PA) e Adriana Gerônimo (Fortaleza, CE). 




Em uma das ameaças, o grupo exigiu que a vítima renunciasse ao cargo para parar com as agressões. No caso de Belém, um grupo que se denomina “Nova Ordem Ariana”, ameaçou de estupro e morte a vereadora Vivi Reis e fez menção a um massacre. O caso de Fortaleza descreve as armas e um plano de dupla execução na casa da vereadora Adriana Gerônimo, alcançando também a esposa da parlamentar. 




O último incidente do levantamento da reportagem da 

Pública

 também aconteceu em Santa Catarina. Na noite de domingo (27), em Itajaí, a 

casa da mãe do candidato

 a senador pelo PT, Décio Lima, uma idosa de 88 anos, que tem Alzheimer, foi atacada a pedradas por uma pessoa em um carro. A pedra quebrou uma janela do imóvel e parte de uma estrutura em madeira. Havia três pessoas no local, mas ninguém se feriu. Na frente da casa havia banners do candidato.

author: Charlotte Reck & Joshua Carroll
title: US Politicians Vote Down Bid to Get Justice for Americans Killed by Israel
content:
US senators have blocked 

a resolution

 that would have forced the government to reveal what evidence it has relating to the killing of nine Americans by Israel.




The resolution, led by Democrat Chris Van Hollen, would have required the state department to report to congress on “all credible evidence” it had obtained about the deaths in the illegally occupied West Bank.




It highlighted the case of Omar Assad, a 78-year-old US citizen who “died of a stress-induced heart attack” in 2022 after Israeli soldiers dragged him from his car, bound his hands and left him gagged and blindfolded.  




It also named Aysenur Ezgi Eygi, 26, who was raised in Seattle. Eygi was “shot in the head by an Israeli soldier from a distance of 200 meters”, the resolution said. 




The killings have been “met by a lack of accountability from the Netanyahu government and an inability to secure justice by the United States government,” it added. 




“They have received no justice and no accountability. Their families – and the American people – deserve answers on their deaths,” Van Hollen said in a statement following Tuesday’s vote.




Fifty Republican senators voted against the resolution, along with Democrat John Fetterman (pictured, left), while 46 Democrats and one Republican supported it.




The resolution called on the US government to release any evidence on the identities of the killers and explain what steps it had taken to investigate them and to pressure Israel into holding them accountable. 




And it called for an official list of any US citizens held in 

Israeli detention

 and an assessment of whether 

Palestinian children in Israeli detention

 are being tortured. 




“Palestinian people have also borne the toll of this violence day in and day out,” Van Hollen added. “They, too, deserve justice and accountability. But again, Republicans blocked that today.” 




While Democrats almost unanimously supported the resolution, many of those same senators, such as 

New Jersey representative Cory Booker

, have backed Israel or opposed measures to disrupt its genocide in Gaza in the recent past. 




In 2025, 19 Democratic senators 

helped kill two resolutions

 to block arms sales to Israel amid its mass starvation campaign.

author: Unknown
title: E’ la bolla: quanta energia nelle mani dei padroni
content:
Stiamo entrando mani e piedi in un sistema di capitalismo finanziario in cui l’energia è la principale merce di scambio. 




Merce immateriale ma profondamente terrena: senza energia non c’è vita, l’energia è il motore per curarci, per mangiare, per scaldarci. Terrena come le miniere di uranio per produrre energia atomica, terrena come ettari di suolo che ospitano palazzi di server, terrena come scatole di metallo che se colpite da missili o droni possono fare saltare in aria centinaia di petabyte. Quel che salta in aria non è una fabbrica di armi o una ferrovia ma è il contenitore dentro il quale non vi è più alcun confine tra militare e civile. 




L’Italia è un teatrino grottesco. Il governo Meloni dall’inizio del suo mandato è passato dai proclami sull’hub del Mediterraneo per il gas e al Piano Mattei per poi voler dare seguito agli ultimi colpi di coda del Green New Deal europeo, per poi passare a encomiare la necessità delle trivellazioni di greggio – praticamente inesistente nella penisola – fino ad arrivare alla grande truffa del nucleare come soluzione finale. 




Il Ministro della Sicurezza energetica ha dunque ottenuto il consenso per il disegno di legge sul ritorno all’atomo. Questo disegno di legge delega dovrà essere sostanziato dai decreti legislativi di attuazione ma intanto traccia delle cosiddette “linee guida”, fumose e insensate, che possono essere riassunte così: si parla di nuovi “small modular reactor” senza parlare di deposito per le scorie passate né di decommissioning delle vecchie centrali; si parla di nucleare sostenibile senza parlare di salute degli abitanti dei territori contaminati né dei costi ambientali ed economici, oltre che di sicurezza. Se in questa fase di sicurezza si parla quotidianamente nei termini della necessità di “difendersi” da presunti attacchi russi alle nostre latitudini, non si fa alcun cenno alla sicurezza italiana in uno scenario in cui il territorio dovrebbe venire costellato da piccoli reattori. Piccoli reattori che saranno pronti non prima dei prossimi quindici anni e che aumenteranno la militarizzazione diffusa su tutto il territorio. Si parla di nuove centrali senza parlare dei costi enormi che prevedono ma quel che non si dice è che il budget previsto da questo disegno di legge è ridicolo a fronte dei costi previsti per un’operazione di questo tipo. 




Si parla però di nucleare per un motivo molto semplice: non è sicuramente quello ecologico e nemmeno perché abbiamo bisogno di energia. Ci sono dei limiti oggettivi che si fa finta di non vedere: la rete elettrica nazionale è vetusta e incompatibile a livello tecnico con un’iniezione di energia equivalente a quella che un reattore nucleare potrebbe immettere. Non si tiene minimamente conto del fatto che questa estate le temperature elevate hanno fatto sì che le centrali venissero spente in Francia e in altri paesi europei. Non si tiene conto dei limiti strutturalmente impossibili da superare rispetto alla fusione. La fusione nucleare, tanto propagandata come sola opzione per la fuoriuscita dal fossile, non esiste se non in laboratorio e non esisterà nella vita quotidiana a causa di un bilancio energetico sconveniente: nel processo di fusione si spende troppa energia rispetto a quanta se ne potrebbe guadagnare. Ma tutto questo evidentemente è fin troppo banale. Il motivo per cui si parla di nucleare è che insieme alle rinnovabili – o meglio, senza il nucleare non potremmo produrre tramite rinnovabili, quindi il nucleare è fondamentale per le rinnovabili – dovrà garantire energia a sufficienza per alimentare a spron battuto data center per l’intelligenza artificiale e per il piano di riarmo. 




Questo piano si basa su una proiezione nel futuro e non sulle necessità e possibilità del presente: è l’esempio del processo di finanziarizzazione della questione energetica e, dunque, delle nostre vite. Ciò che è molto reale è la riabilitazione nel dibattito pubblico di un’energia padrona come orizzonte al quale tendere, senza fare i conti con i tempi lunghissimi previsti e con lo scoglio di due referendum che, nonostante tutto, non possono essere sorpassati. Il disegno di legge apre così un ulteriore terreno di speculazione e profitto su qualcosa che ancora non c’è e chissà quando (e se) ci sarà. E’ in grande lo stesso meccanismo che vediamo all’opera da trent’anni in Val Susa: il treno non si farà, il tunnel non esisterà mai, ma intanto i piloni e il cemento oltre a distruggere un territorio producono minuto dopo minuto possibilità di profitto. Il nuovo nucleare probabilmente non esisterà mai ma intanto si mettano i piloni per aprire nuove società (vedasi Nuclitalia) in affari con aziende belliche come Leonardo per dare da mangiare all’apparato di manager che governano il nostro Paese e fare gli interessi di Confindustria; intanto si mettano i piloni per costruire mega centrali di dati che chissà come faranno a rimanere in vita vista la domanda energetica che esprimono; intanto svendiamo intere porzioni di territorio alle Big Tech americane e ai fondi di investimento come Blackrock che nelle città allungano i loro tentacoli dietro ai colossi immobiliari, tra i maggiori promotori di questi progetti; intanto si dia campo libero ai grandi capitali energetici di gestire in maniera totalmente proprietaria fonti, filiera e prodotto finale. 




In questo processo si inseriscono due ulteriori fattori: da un lato, la delega in bianco da parte del governo ad aziende monopolistiche private come ENI di gestire al suo posto il caro benzina sponsorizzando la questione come una prova di forza da parte del governo di essere ancora in grado di piegare le scelte di grandi società come ENI. Evidentemente una falsità, così come una falsità è il “sacrificio per il bene pubblico” del cane a sei zampe che con i profitti fatti negli ultimi tre anni sarebbe in capacità di sanare il debito italiano e invece diventa, in questo teatro dell’assurdo, il benefattore che soddisfa i consumatori agganciandoli alle proprie pompe di benzina. Questo implica non solo rientrare sullo sconto fatto, grazie all’aumento delle vendite, ma probabilmente anche guadagnare, perlomeno in termini di investimento di immagine e, dunque, investendo sul futuro, sul profitto che ci sarà. 




Dall’altro lato, la corsa all’intelligenza artificiale sta trasformando i meccanismi finanziari a livello strutturale dei colossi dell’energia, come dice Volpi, “un tempo caratterizzati da sterminati giacimenti di liquidità netta, in strutture ad alta intensità di capitale fortemente esposte all’indebitamento obbligazionario”

.

 Esiste al momento un debito societario accumulato di oltre 400 miliardi relativo ai colossi tecnologici dell’infrastruttura cloud. Il cuore dell’assorbimento di queste risorse risiede nella costruzione di data center a causa dei costi iperbolici di costruzione e di fornitura di hardware, si parla di 15-25 miliardi di dollari a trimestre per singola azienda, sostiene Volpi. Questo significa un esborso prima che i server entrino in funzione il che si aggiunge all’elevato ritmo di obsolescenza dei server che impone alle società di ricorrere a nuovi server prima di essere rientrate dagli investimenti precedenti. Questo, conclude Volpi, espone il settore a contrazione di liquidità e dunque a incertezza e al possibile scoppio di una bolla che investirà di conseguenza tutti i settori. 




Il tema è che oggi i profitti della banche e delle grandi società energetiche arrivano a livelli altissimi proprio perché non dipendono soltanto dal loro ciclo produttivo ma sono influenzati da eventi legati alla fase storica e, dunque, alla guerra. I profitti dipendono dalle dichiarazioni di Trump, dagli investimenti di Musk o della cricca di Epstein, dai data center colpiti in Medio Oriente, dal controllo sullo Stretto di Hormuz, dalle difese europee che gridano al lupo per gli attacchi russi. Non è solo che i soliti noti ci guadagnano dalla catastrofe è anche che l’immateriale assume valore materiale e quando la bolla scoppierà farà più male di una bomba. 




Energia padrona. Significa che la questione non è tecnica ma politica perché il nucleare per antonomasia non può che stare nelle mani dei padroni. Se negli anni 70 la critica al nucleare veniva fatta non tanto a partire da un presupposto ecologista quanto più perché l’energia nucleare in quanto tale rende più semplice una “gestione anti-operaia della crisi

1

”, anche oggi occorre guardare al dato materiale e porsi i problemi giusti. Stando all’interno del modo di produzione capitalistico non potrà essere il soluzionismo tecnologico a risolvere i nostri problemi, perché finché non ci sarà controllo del processo di estrazione, produzione e organizzazione del consumo energetico non ci sarà possibilità di contro-potere. In tal senso, l’energia nucleare per la sua specifica potenza olocaustica sposta in maniera drastica, rendendola remota, la possibilità di contendere il potere in un processo rivoluzionario. La delega pressoché totale all’ambito dei tecnici per quanto riguarda un’energia come questa è rappresentativa di un rapporto di dominio che difficilmente può ribaltarsi in favore della classe. La domanda da porsi oggi quindi non è solo come allontanare il rischio di un passaggio di questo tipo, ma anche impedire i processi di estrazione di valore che avvengono sin dalle fasi che precedono l’installazione effettiva di determinate opere energetiche considerate strategiche e che ne preparano insidiosamente il terreno.

At a campaign rally in Florida on Thursday, Vice President JD Vance discussed his desire to remove individuals from the United States based on their political views, saying that socialists “don’t belong in America.”

Vance was discussing Angie Nixon, the Democratic Party’s candidate for U.S. senator in Florida. Nixon is affiliated with the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA), a progressive political party that supports popular socialist ideals (including universal health care and reforms to government) being implemented through the democratic process.

Vance described Nixon, and anyone espousing her views, as un-American, suggesting they should leave the country rather than promote their political vision.

“When Angie Nixon calls herself a socialist, I think the right response is, ‘Get the hell out of here,'” Vance said during the rally. “You don’t belong in America, if those are your views.”

JD Vance on Angie Nixon: "Get the hell out of here. You don't belong in America"

Nixon responded to Vance’s rhetoric by citing unflattering memes about the vice president, and noting that her opponent, Sen. Ashley Moody (R-Florida), wasn’t even in attendance at the rally.

“I don’t wanna COUCH my words here: I know JD Vance, his eyeliner, and absent Ashley Moody, are used to running away from people when things get tough, because they care more about themselves and their billionaire buddies than the people they represent,” Nixon wrote on social media. “But this is my home.”

Notably, support for socialism in the U.S. is polling at its highest levels ever seen. According to a recent Gallup poll, 43 percent of Americans have a positive view of socialism, surpassing the 40 percent line for the first time since the polling organization started asking the question.

Nixon herself is polling well within the state. According to a recent Change Research survey, she is in a statistical tie with Moody, with Nixon garnering 47 percent of support among Florida voters and her Republican opponent receiving 48 percent support.

Notably, some Democrats have also been critical of democratic socialism, even going so far as to vote in favor of a measure in the U.S. House of Representatives condemning the ideology that Republicans have sought to make a political boogeyman this past year.

“It’s telling that some in our own party, alongside Republicans who have made their disdain for working people clear, would rather red-bait us than fight the corporate money corrupting our elections and making life unbearable for the people they claim to represent,” said Darializa Avila Chevalier, a democratic socialist running for Congress to represent a district in New York City, reacting to that bill’s passage in September.

“We don’t need a tent that shrinks from its own history. We need a unified party that takes on corporate power, gets money out of politics, and delivers for working people,” Chevalier added.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Burnham to Ban Airlines From Charging Parents to Sit With Their Children
content:
Andy Burnham has announced a ban on airlines charging people extra to sit next to their children on flights. 




The new rule, expected to come into force before next year’s summer holidays, will apply to parents or other accompanying adults travelling with under-14s. Passengers will also have the right to correct errors on their booking free of charge.




“Charging parents just to sit with their children is a rip-off, plain and simple,” Burnham said. “And being hit with a hefty fee for a simple spelling mistake on a booking form isn’t right either. People are fed up with these little charges that add up, so I’m putting a stop to them.”




Paying to select seats so that a parent and child can sit together cost up to an extra £104 on a return journey, 

according to

 the Department for Transport. 




On his first day as prime minister in July, Burnham 

promised to tackle the cost of living crisis

 and give people “breathing space”. 




“This is the latest example of the prime minister’s series of ‘everyday fixes’ to tackle the irritations that make life difficult and hit people’s wallets,” the government 

said in a statement

. 




It follows “action on rogue traders overcharging for home improvements, subscription traps that quietly drain bank accounts and rip-off school uniform costs,” the statement added. 




The new rules for airlines will also tighten restrictions on disruptive passengers, Burnham said: “We’re working with the industry to make sure that disruptive passengers who have been banned from one airline can be banned from flying with other airlines too.”

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Israel’s Supreme Court Pushes Palestinian Candidate to Withdraw From Elections
content:
Sami Abu Shehadeh, head of the left-wing Balad party, withdrew from Israel’s upcoming elections on Friday.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

On Friday, Sami Abu Shehadeh, head of the Balad party, withdrew from Israel’s upcoming elections, in a maneuver that will likely cost the left-wing party its relevancy in the Israeli parliament.

Israel’s Supreme Court heard appeals on Thursday against the decisions of Israel’s Central Elections Committee, which had voted last week to bar Palestinian parties and two individual candidates from running in Israel’s October 27 elections. The court advised Abu Shehadeh to withdraw.

The committee had voted to ban the two Palestinian-majority political lists: the United Arab List, also known as Ra’am, which represents the Islamic movement inside Israel, as well as the Joint List, which is a coalition of three parties: Hadash, or Jabha in Arabic, a left-wing Jewish and Palestinian party; Ta’al, an anti-Zionist Arab nationalist party; and Balad, a left-wing Palestinian party.

The committee had also voted to bar Ofer Cassif, a Jewish politician from the Hadash party, and Abu Shehadeh of Balad.

Israel’s Supreme Court will rule on Sunday on whether or not to push through with the bans of the parties and candidates. But it is the barring of Abu Shehadeh that is most likely to stick, Palestinian political analyst Diana Buttu told Truthout.

Israel’s Supreme Court indicated that they are likely to ban Abu Shehadeh, Buttu explained, but first gave him the option to withdraw, which he eventually decided to take.

While the Central Elections Committee is heavily represented by the far right Likud Party, and is pushing for the barring of all of the Palestinian-majority parties from the Israeli elections, it is unlikely that their complaints against the parties will meet the needed threshold previously set by the Israeli Supreme Court.

Israel’s parliamentary law allows for banning candidates for “denial of the existence of the State of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state,” “incitement to racism,” or “support for armed struggle by a hostile state or a terrorist organization against the State of Israel.”

“What’s fascinating is that over the course of the past three years, all we’ve heard is one racist statement after another,” Buttu told Truthout — but it has been from the Zionist parties, rather than from the Palestinian-majority parties or candidates.

“And yet what they’ve honed in on with Sami is that he wrote an article about October 7, which he wrote the very next day, on October 8, calling it an ‘important historical event.” While he has distanced himself from these comments, saying he did not realize the consequences of October 7, Israel’s parliament is using them as an excuse to ban him and further punish his left-wing party.

The consequences of banning him, Buttu says, “are huge.” It could lead to the indictment of Abu Shehadeh, as well as lower voter turnout from supporters of the Balad party, and significantly lower representation by the Balad party in the next parliament.

Because the Joint List had united the three left-wing parties — Hadash, Ta’al, and Balad — it was expected that they would get a higher number of seats in parliament in the October 27 elections, Buttu explained. But Abu Shehadeh’s ouster could mean his party may end up with just one or two seats, losing its political relevance.

Balad, Buttu says, “is the only party that says there should be equality between Palestinians and Israelis.”

Formed in 1995 by Palestinian intellectuals in Israel led by Azmi Bishara, the Balad party calls for transforming Israel into a secular “state of all its citizens,” with equal rights for Palestinians.

In 2015, the Joint List, which at the time represented all four Palestinian-majority parties — Ra’am, Ta’al, Hadash, and Balad — won more than a dozen seats in Israel’s Knesset, which saw the peak of its political representation in Israel’s parliament. While the parties had split up in recent years, the reunification of Ta’al, Hadash, and Balad brought about expectations for similarly high representation in the coming election.

Buttu also spoke about some of the issues faced by Palestinian residents of Israel, including high rates of violence in their neighborhoods, which incentivize Palestinians to vote in Israeli elections if just with the hope of improving the conditions of their day-to-day lives.

While there is a debate within Palestinian society inside Israel over whether or not to participate in the electoral system, many Palestinian residents of Israel are moved to vote in order to remove ministers like Itamar Ben Gvir, who has armed Zionist communities and further endangered Palestinian citizens of Israel.

“We know that liberation isn’t going to come through the ballot box – that’s a myth – but if there’s ways that we can still preserve ourselves, our identity, our families, our remaining [on the land], this is where people are looking for these very small things, but for many Palestinians, it becomes a big thing,” Buttu said.

title: Aram Tigran commemorated at Amed Book Fair
content:
The 10th Amed Book Fair, held at the Mesopotamia International Fair and Congress Center, continued on its seventh day. As part of the fair, a panel titled “Aram Tigran: Voice of Freedom and Symbol of Brotherhood” was held. Artists Dilovan, Delîl Dîlanar, Neşet Güçmen, and Kakşar Oremar, who knew Aram Tigran personally, spoke about his life, music, and the legacy he left to Kurdish music. Numerous artists and members of the public also attended the panel.




Ma Music Coordinator Şêrko Kanîwar announced that, in addition to commemorating Aram Tigran, the “Amida Concerts” initiative, which was launched during the pandemic, would be revived. He said the concerts would begin with the works of Aram Tigran and that other artists would subsequently be commemorated at historic sites.







‘I am devoted to the Kurdish language and Kurdish art’




Joining the panel online, Kakşar Oremar said that the third edition of his book about Aram Tigran, “Voice of Freedom, Symbol of Brotherhood,” had been published. The 670-page book covers Aram Tigran’s life and works, musical scores, and assessments by other artists.




Oremar said that Aram Tigran’s artistic vision was deeply intertwined with the language and culture of the people. He also recounted that Tigran had rejected offers from Turkey’s Ministry of Culture to sing in Turkish, saying, “I am devoted to serving the Kurdish language and Kurdish art.”




Oremar said that Aram Tigran’s works were much more than melodies alone: “The content and lyrics of his songs were profound. Each one, like ‘Ay Dilberê,’ had a story of its own.” Remarking that Aram Tigran remained faithful to his father’s final wish, he added: “Aram remained faithful until the very end to his father’s words, ‘Know their value and do not forget them.’ He stood by the Kurdish people until the end of his life.”




‘He traveled the world for the identity of his people’




Delîl Dîlanar said that Aram Tigran had undertaken an important mission for the identity and language of his people. Dîlanar said he met Aram Tigran in Yerevan and spent a great deal of time with him. He added: “We must recognize the value of our artists while they are alive. We must cherish figures like Aram Tigran.”




Dîlanar said that Aram Tigran’s art extended far beyond music: “He traveled the world and struggled for the identity of his people, serving as a bridge of friendship within his nation. He created such a distinctive style in the Kurdish language, with such clarity and simplicity, that people of all ages can listen to him for hours.”







‘Everything about him was Kurdish’




Artist Dilovan said that he first saw Aram Tigran in 1968, when he was just 15 years old. Stating that Aram Tigran made significant contributions to the dengbêj tradition, Dilovan said, “Aram contributed immensely to our art and to our dengbêjs. He was a master of his art.”




Referring to Aram Tigran’s devotion to the Kurdish language, Dilovan recalled his words, “If I were not Kurdish, I would not be who I am; if you were not Kurdish, you would not be who you are.” Speaking about Aram Tigran’s identity and language, he added: “Everything about him was Kurdish. His days, his ideas, his thoughts, even his dreams were in Kurdish.”




“Aram was a source of balance and color at Yerevan Radio. Every two weeks, he would record three or four ballads. With his artistry and knowledge, he was like a volcano at Yerevan Radio,” Dilovan said.




‘He earned a place in the hearts of Kurds’




Neşet Güçmen noted that Aram Tigran performed works in Kurdish, Armenian, Arabic, Syriac, Turkish, and Greek, saying that he built a bridge between peoples through music and language. “Aram Tigran played a very important role in the development of modern Kurdish music. With his voice, passion, and distinctive style, he brought his songs to the masses,” Güçmen said.




Güçmen added, “His works are part of our repertoire and our archives. With songs such as ‘Bilbilo,’ ‘Dilberim,’ and ‘Şev Çu,’ he earned a place in the hearts of Kurds everywhere through the Kurdish language. He left us 14 albums as his legacy. This is an immense treasure for us.”




The speakers at the panel emphasized that the legacy Aram Tigran left to Kurdish music should be preserved and carried forward by new generations.




The panel concluded with performances of Aram Tigran’s songs.

title: When will the architecture of war in North Kurdistan be dismantled?
content:
With the adoption of the framework law, the Peace and Democratic Society Process has acquired a legal foundation. However, the Turkish government’s hesitant approach to the steps that are now necessary has not dispelled doubts among the Kurdish population about the prospects for lasting peace. While the legal framework is changing in Ankara, the architecture of war in the mountains, valleys, and highlands of North Kurdistan remains largely unchanged: kalekols—gendarmerie stations expanded into fortified outposts—on the hilltops, dams in the valleys, and restricted zones across pastures and highland grazing areas. For the Kurdish population, peace will only become truly visible when this landscape changes as well.




On August 10, the Turkish National Assembly adopted the “Law on Strengthening National Solidarity and Social Cohesion” with 467 votes. This gave the Peace and Democratic Society Process, initiated by Abdullah Öcalan’s call, a legal foundation for the first time. The provisions of the law are to take effect once the National Security Council’s decision confirming and verifying disarmament and dissolution has been published in the Official Gazette.




Kalekols: Concrete alongside peace




Yet the people of Kurdistan do not measure peace by a vote in parliament alone, but also by what they see on the mountains above their own village. In many places, infrastructure that was significantly expanded during the so-called dialogue process between 2013 and 2015 still remains: fortified military outposts, so-called security dams, special security zones, and closed highland pastures. While one side is taking steps toward laying down its weapons, kalekols, military bases, and restricted zones remain in place. This is precisely where one of the most sensitive fault lines of the current process lies.




After Abdullah Öcalan called for the withdrawal of the guerrillas from Turkey during Newroz in 2013, the state began expanding the network of new military outposts and kalekols across the mountainous regions. According to a response issued at the time by the Ministry of Defense to a parliamentary inquiry, 78 new gendarmerie posts were already under construction at the beginning of 2013. Reports by the Human Rights Association’s (İHD) monitoring commission on the guerrilla withdrawal documented an even greater scale. In Hakkari alone, 189 police posts and kalekols were put out to tender through the state housing authority TOKİ. In Dersim (Tunceli), construction began on 22 of a total of 52 planned military bases. This was accompanied by a protocol for the construction of 820 kilometers of so-called security roads. While peace was being discussed, concrete was being poured.




This policy had deadly consequences early on. On June 28, 2013, military forces opened fire on people protesting against the expansion of a military base in the village of Kayacık near Lice. Eighteen-year-old Medeni Yıldırım was killed, and eight other people were injured.




A kalekol is not an ordinary military outpost. With stone walls up to 80 centimeters thick, reinforced concrete walls, and twelve-meter-high observation towers, these installations were designed to withstand even attacks involving rocket launchers. Their architecture was not based on the prospect of a permanent end to the armed conflict, but on the possibility of its return. This was the physical manifestation of the state’s peace policy at the time: while negotiations were taking place, military deterrence was being cast in concrete. By contrast, the concept of a democratic society requires conditions in which people themselves can determine how they live and shape their surroundings.




When even water is brought under control




During the first year of the peace process at the time, the İHD documented the construction of eleven so-called security dams in Şırnak, four dams along the Munzur River in Dersim, and another on the Botan River in Siirt. In Şırnak and Hakkari, a chain of installations was built along the border, including Silopi, Uludere, Çetintepe, Musatepe, Çocuktepe, Aslandağ, and Beyyurdu.




Officially, these projects were justified on the grounds of energy generation and irrigation. However, the fact that construction was concentrated specifically along the border with Iraq and accelerated during the peace process fueled the view, even at the time, that these were not merely energy policy investments. A dam does more than hold back water. It also creates control. It can reinforce a border through the use of water, cut off routes to highland pastures and villages, and submerge entire valleys along with their history. The flooding of 12,000-year-old Hasankeyf by the Ilısu Dam is the most drastic example.




In Abdullah Öcalan’s paradigm of a democratic, ecological, and women’s liberation-oriented society, nature is not a resource that can be exploited without limits, but a living environment whose liberation is connected to the liberation of society. A policy that forces rivers into concrete therefore cannot be separated from a logic that seeks to bring both society and nature under control.




Special Security Zones: Restrictions without continuing justification




Law No. 2565 on Military Prohibited and Security Zones allows for the establishment of “special security zones” around facilities of strategic importance. The decision to establish them rests with the president. Article 24 of the corresponding regulation generally allows property owners and residents within these areas to continue living there, farming, and carrying out their occupations. The reality in Kurdistan, however, is different. A de facto regime of restrictions has become established there, characterized by identity checks, permits, narrow access corridors, and regulations that in some cases change at short notice. What the law formally permits is once again restricted through administrative arbitrariness.




Even the existing legal framework provides a way to abolish such zones. A provincial administration can submit a corresponding file to the Interior Ministry requesting that the designation be lifted. The legal door is therefore open. What is lacking is the political will to walk through it. The fact that Turkey’s Constitutional Court found a violation of property rights in cases involving land whose use had been restricted for around 25 years because it was designated as a military security zone further demonstrates how deeply entrenched a system originally intended as an exceptional measure has become.




Why the restrictions must be lifted




There are several reasons for this. The first is the most obvious: the basis for the restrictions is disappearing. Special security zones are based on the assumption of an ongoing armed conflict. The further disarmament and dissolution progress and are officially confirmed, the harder it becomes to sustain that assumption.




Second, the restrictions curtail property rights, freedom of movement, and the economic livelihoods of the population. Third, continuing them under the banner of “security” would mean denying the population one of the most immediate consequences of peace.




And fourth, local democracy requires that people be able to make decisions about the places in which they live. It is difficult to speak of democratic self-determination as long as access to one’s own geography remains dependent on military authorization.




The objection: “Disarmament first”




Kalekols in their military dimension, dams in their ecological dimension, and restricted zones in their economic dimension are different manifestations of the same security paradigm. Land, water, and livelihoods are brought under control—and the population is turned into guests in its own geography. The government, however, has repeatedly argued: “Legal regulations can only be introduced after the PKK’s laying down of arms has been established and confirmed.” During the parliamentary process, the AKP and MHP maintained this position. The DEM Party, by contrast, called for the necessary regulations to be initiated without waiting for the disarmament process to be fully completed.




There are three responses to this objection.




First, the kalekols were not built only after waiting for developments to unfold. On the contrary, their construction was accelerated precisely during a period of ceasefire. Those who were unwilling to wait when pouring the concrete can hardly insist on patience when it comes to dismantling it.




Second, a significant proportion of the restrictions on highland pastures and grazing areas are based on administrative decisions and practical measures implemented locally, and lifting them does not require a new framework law. Many of these restrictions could be ended from one day to the next. Special security zones can also be abolished under existing law, while environmental permits for dam projects can likewise be revoked or annulled through existing legal mechanisms.




Third, lasting peace does not emerge simply because the parties place their trust in written texts. Trust is built through visible changes on the ground. For the population, the dismantling of a kalekol, the reopening of a highland pasture, and a stream flowing freely once again are the tangible translation of the Peace and Democratic Society Process into their everyday lives.




Peace begins on the ground




The steps that the government must take immediately in a peace process therefore concern not only the political and legal spheres. They must also become visible in people’s everyday lives. The construction of new military posts, kalekols, and bases must be halted. Existing installations require a public inventory and a timetable for their evacuation. Dams and hydroelectric power plants—particularly projects designed as “security dams”—should undergo new and independent environmental impact assessments with the participation of the affected population.




Provincial administrations can initiate procedures to abolish special security zones. Restrictions on highland pastures and grazing areas can be lifted, compensation can be provided for damages incurred, and privileges granted to the village guard system regarding access to grazing land can be ended. A monitoring commission established by parliament could explicitly include military infrastructure and existing restriction regimes within the scope of its work, while involving municipalities, professional associations, and residents of the affected villages in decision-making.




The village in the shadow of a kalekol, the river transformed by a dam, and the closed highland pasture symbolize the gap between the texts of the peace process in Ankara and the reality on the ground. The Kurdish population wants the silencing of the weapons to also bring an end to the control imposed over their living environment. Only when peace transforms not only the law but also the landscape will it truly have arrived in North Kurdistan.

author: Hudson Hongo
title: Victory! Court Rejects Government Effort to Dismiss Social Media Surveillance Lawsuit
content:
Judge Allows Social Media Surveillance Lawsuit Against Trump Administration to Move Forward

NEW YORK — A lawsuit filed by three labor unions against the Departments of State and Homeland Security for their viewpoint-based surveillance and suppression of protected expression online can move forward, a federal judge ruled yesterday.




On October 1, 2026, Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein of the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York rejected the government’s motion to dismiss the lawsuit. 

The case was filed in October 2025

 on behalf of the United Automobile Workers (UAW), Communications Workers of America (CWA), and American Federation of Teachers (AFT). The Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF), Muslim Advocates (MA), and the Media Freedom & Information Access Clinic (MFIA) represent the labor unions.




This decision is a victory: The Court held that claims that the government’s social media surveillance program is harming the unions’ members, as well as hampering the ability of the unions to associate with their members and potential members, can move forward.




The Court ruled that: "This threat of adverse immigration consequences, under a government whose harsh immigration crackdowns has been heavily publicized and reported on, is certainly enough to 'deter a person of ordinary firmness from the exercise of First Amendment rights.' It is objectively reasonable that noncitizens would limit their expression of disfavored viewpoints under the [Challenged Surveillance Program] given the credible threat of adverse immigration action from the Government."




"The freedom of Plaintiffs' members to speak, associate, and appear publicly is not incidental to union work, but rather is the mechanism through which unions recruit, organize, communicate, and bargain," the Court further explained. "A program alleged to silence members and drive them from the unions' rolls therefore strikes at the unions' representational function itself, which is the 'grounds that bring [their] membership together.'"




Since taking power, the Trump administration has created a mass surveillance program to monitor constitutionally protected speech by noncitizens lawfully present in the U.S. Using AI and other automated technologies, the program surveils the social media accounts of visa and green card holders with the goal of identifying and punishing those who express viewpoints the government disfavors. The surveillance program has been paired with a public intimidation campaign—silencing not just noncitizens with immigration status, but also the families, coworkers, and friends with whom their lives are integrated.




In October 2025, UAW, CWA, and AFT sued the Departments of State and Homeland Security, alleging that this viewpoint-based surveillance program violates the First Amendment and the Administrative Procedure Act.




"No one should have to fear government surveillance or retaliation against their immigration status for expressing their views or participating in their union. We're pleased the Court has allowed this challenge to move forward and will continue fighting to protect the rights of everyone to speak, organize, and advocate without fear," said 

UAW President Shawn Fain

.




"This is a victory for working people, for the labor movement, and for our democracy," said 

CWA President Claude Cummings Jr

. "Our very freedom is under attack by the Trump administration's online surveillance program, and today's decision is a critical first step toward affirming our freedom to speak, to protest, to organize without fear of government retaliation. These essential freedoms underpin our union rights to join together and fight to improve our working conditions. CWA is a fighting union, and our members remain ready to stand together to protect our rights and our freedoms."




"Today’s decision is a critical step toward vindicating our Constitutional right to freedom of speech and rejecting the Trump Administration’s cynical attempts to criminalize and punish those who disagree with them," said 

AFT President Randi Weingarten

. "Government surveillance to monitor the 'opposition' is a tool of dictators that erodes the democratic principles this country was founded on. We will continue to remain vigilant in defending our 250-year-old rights—not just for our members, but for all Americans."




"Our plaintiff-unions have members that have wholly changed the way they interact with social media—including limiting their engagement with union content—because of the government's social media surveillance program," said 

EFF Senior Staff Attorney Lisa Femia

. "Many have stopped posting online together, and have even stopped engaging in offline activities, for fear of being scrutinized or targeted related to immigration benefits. We are pleased that the Court has agreed to let the case proceed, and allow unions and their members to seek justice for infringement of their rights."




"Today’s ruling is an important step forward in holding the government accountable for its ever-expansive online surveillance program that silenced non-citizens, stoking fear that exercise of their protected First Amendment rights could result in unfavorable treatment on their immigration applications or worse." said 

Sadaf Hasan, Staff Attorney at Muslim Advocates

. "We will keep fighting until all non-citizens are able to freely associate, organize, and speak out without the looming threat of visa revocation and immigration enforcement simply because the government dislikes their views."




"Defendants' attempt to evade accountability on specious jurisdictional grounds was rightly rejected by the Court," said 

Nick Jones

, a student in the 

Media Freedom & Information Access Clinic

. "We are excited to see the case now proceed to the merits, where we expect to prevail as well.”




For the ruling:

title: Από τις ΗΠΑ μέχρι την Ισπανία και από τη Γερμανία μέχρι τη Γαλλία, η νεολαία επιλέγει τη ριζοσπαστική αριστερά!
content:
Του 

Γιώργου Μητραλιά




Δεν πρόκειται πια ούτε για μια εικασία ούτε για μια υπόθεση εργασίας. Εφεξής, υπάρχει όντως κάτι νεότερο στο δυτικό μέτωπο! Από τη Νέα Υόρκη μέχρι το Βερολίνο, και από τη Μαδρίτη μέχρι το Παρίσι, κινείται κάτι μεγάλο. Και μάλιστα, κινείται με μεγάλη ένταση. Σχεδόν ταυτόχρονα, η ριζοσπαστική αριστερά αναδεικνύει δικούς της στους δήμους μεγαπόλεων όπως η Νέα Υόρκη και το Βερολίνο. Και το πιο σημαντικό, η πλειοψηφία των νέων σε χώρες όπως οι Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες, η Ισπανία, η Γερμανία και η Γαλλία ριζοσπαστικοποιείται και εκφράζει τη συμπάθειά της, συχνά ενεργά, προς αυτές τις ίδιες ριζοσπαστικές αριστερές δυνάμεις! Πρέπει να είναι κανείς αδιάφορος, αναίσθητος ή απλά τυφλός για να μην παρατηρήσει και να μην λάβει υπόψη του ένα γεγονός σαν κι αυτό που βγάζει μάτια…




Καταρχήν στην Ισπανία, όπου οι διαδηλώσεις, οι καταλήψεις πλατειών και άλλες παραδειγματικές δράσεις των νεαρών αγωνιστών και αγωνιστριών του Συνδικάτου Ενοικιαστριών και Ενοικιαστών (Sindicato de Inquilinas y Inquilinos) ξανάδωσαν την πρωτοβουλία στους από κάτω, επαναφέροντας στην ημερήσια διάταξη ένα από τα πιο καυτά κοινωνικά ζητήματα, το δικαίωμα στη στέγαση! Υποστηρίζοντας και διαδίδοντας το αγωνιστικό κάλεσμα αυτής της θαυμαστής 87χρονης κυρίας που είναι η 

Μαρικάρμεν

 Αμπασκάλ

 (

«Το σπίτι μου ήταν όλη μου η ζωή και τώρα πρέπει να το αφήσω πίσω μου, αλλά αυτό δεν σημαίνει ότι θα σταματήσω να αγωνίζομαι. Δεν κατάφερα να υπερασπιστώ το σπίτι μου, αλλά πάλεψα για να μάθουν οι άλλοι να παλεύουν για το δικό τους. Αυτό που θέλω είναι να εξαλειφθεί αυτό το πρόβλημα των «ταμείων γύπες”…Παλέψτε, μην μένετε στο σπίτι »

), αυτοί οι χιλιάδες νέοι ακτιβιστές κατάφεραν μέσα σε λίγες μέρες ένα τρομερό κατόρθωμα: πρώτα να σταματήσουν πάραυτα την ξενοφοβική και ρατσιστική επίθεση της δεξιάς και της ακροδεξιάς με αφορμή την «εισβολή» στη Θέουτα Μαροκινών μεταναστών, πολλοί από τους οποίους, σύμφωνα με την Διεθνή Αμνηστία, βασανίζονται τώρα φρικτά από την ισπανική αστυνομία. Και κατόπιν, να επιβάλουν στον αριστερό συνασπισμό (PSOE+Sumar) να κάνει αυτό που δεν έχει κάνει εδώ και 8 χρόνια που βρίσκεται στην εξουσία: να θεσπίσει νόμο για την απαγόρευση των εξώσεων από τα αρπακτικά ταμεία-γύπες και να παγώσει τα νοίκια.




Προφανώς, δεν είναι τυχαίο που το ισπανικό συνδικάτο ενοικιαστών απαιτεί 

«πάγωμα των ισχύοντων ενοικίων, όπως το έκαναν στη Νέα Υόρκη («como se ha hecho en Nueva York»)

». Ή την απαλλοτρίωση των κατοικιών που βρίσκονται στα χέρια των αρπακτικών επενδυτικών κεφαλαίων, όπως υπόσχεται να κάνει η 

Ελίφ Εράλπ

, η θριαμβεύτρια των εκλογών στο Βερολίνο, η οποία, παρεμπιπτόντως, παραδέχεται δημοσίως ότι έχει μάθει πολλά από τον Ζοχράν Μαμντάνι, τον νεαρό δήμαρχο της Νέας Υόρκης και ηγέτη της νέας ριζοσπαστικής Αριστεράς που φέρνει τα πάνω κάτω στο πολιτικό τοπίο των Ηνωμένων Πολιτειών. Προφανώς, οι μεν επωφελούνται από τις επιτυχίες και τις εμπειρίες των δε, και ήδη δημιουργούνται δεσμοί μεταξύ αυτών των κινημάτων και των οργανώσεων της ριζοσπαστικής Αριστεράς. Άλλωστε, αυτό ακριβώς είναι που διευκρινίζει η εκπρόσωπος της Ένωσης Ενοικιαστών της Ισπανίας, Alicia del Rio, όταν δηλώνει ότι το κίνημα πρέπει 

«να επεκταθεί σε άλλες περιοχές μέσω περιφερειακών ή τοπικών, αλλά και εθνικών και διεθνών αντιπροσωπειών»

, πριν καταλήξει καλώντας σε γενική απεργία!




Αρκεί μια απλή ματιά στα αιτήματα και τα προγράμματα αυτής της νέας αριστεράς που νικάει για να καταλάβει κανείς ότι οι επιτυχίες της οφείλονται σε μεγάλο βαθμό στη ριζοσπαστικότητά της. Να λοιπόν γιατί η Ελίφ Εράλπ και το κόμμα της Die Linke, κατάφεραν να υπερδιπλασιάσουν το ποσοστό τους του 2023 (το οποίο, παρεμπιπτόντως, είχε επιτευχθεί πριν από την –αποτυχημένη– απόσχιση της δεξιότατης Ζάρα Βάγκενκνεχτ) χάρη στην δέσμευση τους να απαλλοτριώσουν τους μεγάλους ομίλους ακινήτων και λοιπά «ταμεία γύπες», και να μεταβιβάσουν τις σχεδόν 300.000 κατοικίες που αυτά κατέχουν στον δημόσιο τομέα. Όμως, δεν είναι μόνο αυτό. Είναι ότι 

αυτή η ριζοσπαστικότητα των προγραμμάτων τους, αλλά και των πρακτικών τους, προσελκύει, ενθουσιάζει και κινητοποιεί τα εντυπωσιακά και άνευ προηγουμένου πλήθη νέων ανθρώπων, χάρη στα οποία ο Μαμντάνι, η Εράλπ ή ακόμα και το ισπανικό Sindicato de Inquilinas καταφέρνουν εκλογικές και άλλες επιτυχίες που ήταν εντελώς αδιανόητες πριν από δύο χρόνια!




Πράγματι, το δεύτερο μεγάλο και πολύ ελπιδοφόρο χαρακτηριστικό όλων αυτών των αριστερών κινημάτων και σχηματισμών, τόσο στις Ηνωμένες Πολιτείες όσο και στην Ευρώπη, είναι η ικανότητά τους να εμπνέουν και να κινητοποιούν τους νέους. Πρόκειται εδώ για μια απόλυτη «καινοτομία» που είχαμε να δούμε εδώ και τουλάχιστον 40 χρόνια, και η οποία είναι πολλά υποσχόμενη για το μέλλον, καθώς διαπιστώνουμε ήδη πόσο μεγάλη είναι η δύναμη κρούσης και το αντικαπιταλιστικό δυναμικό αυτής της ριζοσπαστικοποιημένης νεολαίας και στις δύο πλευρές του Ατλαντικού. Έτσι, στο Βερολίνο, το κόμμα Die Linke θριάμβευσε στους νέους, συγκεντρώνοντας 43% στην ηλικιακή ομάδα 18-24 ετών και 49% στην ηλικιακή ομάδα 25-34 ετών! Και μάλιστα 55% στις νέες γυναίκες κάτω των 30 ετών!




Αυτά τα ήδη εξαιρετικά ποσοστά είναι, ωστόσο, χαμηλότερα από αυτά που συγκέντρωσε ο Μαμντάνι στη Νέα Υόρκη: 75% στους νέους ηλικίας 18 έως 29 ετών, και μάλιστα… 82% στις νεαρές γυναίκες! Προσωπική επιτυχία του Ζοχράν Μαμντάνι; Αναμφίβολα ναι, αλλά όχι μόνο. Σύμφωνα με πρόσφατη δημοσκόπηση της Gallup, το 57% των Αμερικανών ηλικίας 18 έως 34 ετών έχει θετική γνώμη για τον σοσιαλισμό, έναντι 43% για τον καπιταλισμό. Και σύμφωνα με δημοσκόπηση του CNBC, το 46% των Αμερικανών ηλικίας 18 έως 34 ετών έχει καλή ή πολύ καλή γνώμη για τους Δημοκρατικούς Σοσιαλιστές (DSA) του Μαμντάνι. Και για όσους πιστεύουν ότι η επιτυχία του Μαμντάνι και των DSA ή της Εράλπ και της Die Linke στους νέους οφείλεται στην «ιδιαιτερότητα των περιπτώσεών τους», υπάρχει, για να τους διαψεύσει, η καθόλου δευτερεύουσας σημασίας περίπτωση της Γαλλίας, όπου, σύμφωνα με τη Le Monde, ο Ζαν-Λυκ Μελανσόν, ηγέτης της μάλλον ριζοσπαστικής αριστεράς της «France Insoumise», «

συγκεντρώνει μεταξύ 40% και 45% των προθέσεων ψήφου στους 18-24χρονους εν όψει των προεδρικών εκλογών του 2027

».




Κατά συνέπεια, δεν αποτελεί καθόλου έκπληξη το γεγονός ότι ακριβώς αυτή η γαλλική νεολαία βρίσκεται αυτές τις μέρες στην πρώτη γραμμή των λαϊκών κινητοποιήσεων, που γίνονται όλο και πιο μαζικές και μαχητικές, ενάντια στις αντικοινωνικές πολιτικές δρακόντειας λιτότητας του προέδρου Μακρόν. Και δεν είναι επίσης έκπληξη το γεγονός ότι, η πανικόβλητη, η γαλλική δεξιά στην εξουσία, που σιγοντάρεται από την ακροδεξιά της Μαρίν Λε Πεν, επιτίθεται βίαια τόσο στον Μελανσόν και το κόμμα του όσο και στο ραγδαία αναπτυσσόμενο κίνημα των μαθητών λυκείου και των φοιτητών, φοβούμενη όλο και περισσότερο ότι η σπίθα της νεανικής εξέγερσης θα βάλει φωτιά σε μια γαλλική κοινωνία που είναι ήδη έτοιμη να εκραγεί.




Ποιος είπε ότι οι νέοι της τόσο σκοτεινής και εφιαλτικής εποχής μας, είναι τάχα καταδικασμένοι στη μοιρολατρεία, στην υποταγή και στην παθητικότητα;

www.contra-xreos.gr

title: Power shared is power supercharged: My reflections on being inducted into the National Women’s Hall of Fame
content:
2nd October 2026










Power shared is power supercharged: My reflections on being inducted into the National Women’s Hall of Fame
















7 min read



















From S. Mona Sinha – our CEO




North America


























































On September 24, I had the extraordinary honor of being inducted into the 

National Women’s Hall of Fame

 in Seneca Falls, New York. 

 As I reflected on the people and experiences that have shaped my understanding of leadership, I kept returning to a lesson my mother taught me as a child: that what we have becomes more powerful when we share it.




When I was growing up in Kolkata, my mother had a small ritual. Every morning, she would reach into our rice container, take out a fistful, and put it into a jute sack. Just one fistful. At the end of the month, when the sack was full, she gave it to someone who needed it more than we did.




There was no announcement, no drama, no expectation of gratitude. She simply did it quietly, day after day. As the youngest, I watched with a child’s curiosity and often copied her. It has taken me most of my life to understand what she was teaching me: you don’t have to have a lot to give something away. Small acts, repeated, can have an impact far greater than we imagine.




I sit with that lesson especially deeply at the moment, as she left us this June.




I have spent much of my life thinking about power. I’ve seen it on Wall Street, in business, in philanthropy, and in the fight for women’s equality, where power ultimately comes down to who has a voice, who has a choice, and who gets to shape our lives.




We are taught that power is finite: that if I give you some of mine, I will have less.




My life has taught me the opposite. Which is why I invest in documentaries about the most silenced voices, fund without questioning but believing in those doing the work, and double down on strengthening women’s rights movements especially during pushback from regressive regimes that promote sexual and gender-based violence against women and girls.




At the core, power shared is power supercharged.




I am standing here because so many people shared theirs with me. My advisor at Smith, Professor Taft-Morris, told me I could compete with any man on Wall Street. My chosen aunt Sally gave me a home during an internship in Washington and opened a world to me. And my dearest friend and co-conspirator, Gloria Steinem, kept pushing me into leadership and to light the torch for the next generation. Saying no to Gloria was never really a long-term strategy.




They saw possibility in me before I saw it in myself.




Perhaps that’s why I choose to mentor hundreds of young people. My children call it an inability to stop giving advice. I call it sharing power.




Sometimes sharing power is simply: You can do this. Let me help you. There’s someone you should meet.




Because power isn’t a zero-sum game. Nobody becomes smaller by helping someone else grow. Open a door, invest in an idea, hand her the microphone and watch power grow through her.




That is how power compounds.




I’ve learned this at home, too. My partner has never asked me to make my dreams smaller to fit more neatly into our lives. And our three children have taught me that loving someone means giving them the freedom to write their own story, not the one you would write for them. I’m still practicing.




Being inducted into the 

National Women’s Hall of Fame

, I know no one arrives at a moment like this alone. I am profoundly grateful to the Hall for giving me a permanent home in this sacred space, alongside women who have shaped America and opened the way for generations to come.




I am also carrying my mother and 

Gloria

 in my heart, the women and men who opened doors for me, my family who gave me the freedom to walk through them, and women around the world who encourage me every day to claim power and share it.




So, I don’t receive this extraordinary honor as mine alone.




I receive it as a fistful of rice, placed in my hands with a responsibility to pass it on.




So, I offer my fistful of rice to each of you.




Pass it on to someone who needs it. Someone whose voice hasn’t been heard. Someone who hasn’t been invited into the room. Someone who may not even know what you are placing in their hands or what it might make possible.




Because I didn’t know what my mother was placing in mine. I thought it was just rice. It took me a lifetime to understand that she was teaching me how to share power.




One small act. One open door. One opportunity. One fistful at a time.




Own your power. Share it with abundance. Watch it multiply.




And at a time when so much feels impossible, together, we might just turn the world on its head.
