author: winter oak
title: A rebel wild and free
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article 

here




Edward Abbey (1927-1989)

 was a writer, a defender of nature and an important inspiration for the radical environmentalist movement in the USA and beyond.




He was in many ways the embodiment of the idea of 

nature defending itself through people

, with his life and thinking being an eruption of undomesticated human nature.




Abbey’s writing features some nice evocations of landscapes, such as, in 

The Fool’s Progress

, of “the green and the vernal, the deep and haunted, the dark transpiring forests of the Appalachian hills”. [1]




And also in the same novel: “Ravens squawked at him from the rimrock. Hummingbirds throbbed before the scarlet monkeyflower of gardens hanging from seeps a hundred feet above the river. Winding tributary canyons like the corridors of a labyrinth led away from the river into the bowels of the plateau, gorges in the seamless stone that were so deep, so narrow that for hundreds of yards he could not see the sky”. [2]




He affirms: “It is an honor to be a visitor at the Grand Canyon of Colorado, as it is an honor and a privilege to be alive, however briefly, on this rare, sweet, delicate, one and one only planet we call Earth”. [3]










Abbey’s personal preference was less for the verdant than for the arid and austere – “the bright skies, the bracing air, the open space, the abundant wildlife, the desert plant life, the sheer physical delight of physical freedom”. [4]




All too often his descriptions come in the context of the threats facing beautiful places and their inhabitants, or of the debased state in which he now finds them, thanks to everything from overgrazing and tourism to mineral extraction and industrial development.




Take this scene from 

Hayduke Lives!

: “The Mitsubishis came grumbling close, snorting through their blowholes, tracks clacking, ‘dozer blades gleaming as they plowed the dirt, tore loose the living shrubs, crushed the homes and children of gopher, chipmunk, cottontail, vole, mole, bannertail mouse and kangaroo rat, ripped up the sod, scraped off the bunch grass and flowers, the wild buckwheat and the wild ricegrass”. [5]




Abbey’s characters want as little as possible to do with cities and think with horror of “Phoenix, Mesa, Tempe, Scottsdale, Tucson, Nogales, where the huddled masses endured their muddled lives amidst a welter of smog, crime, noise, drugs, police, traffic, disease, heart transplants, sphincter transplants, two-headed babies; hydrocephalic preemies, endless conflict, smouldering hatred, an ever-rising Irritability Level, enjoying the pleasures of Growth, Prosperity and Progress”. [6]




New York City was even worse: “Wherever he looked the view was the same: steel, cement, glass, iron, brick, asphalt, extending, as he knew from bitter experience, for miles, for leagues, for eternities in every direction, north to Boston, south to Baltimore, the world’s greatest labyrinth, full of Minotaurs”. [7]










He rejects the life of “an industrial serf” [8] and argues: “Our debased popular culture – television, rock music, home video, processed food, mechanical recreation, wallboard architecture – is the culture of slaves”. [9]




“How can humans endure this mad mechanical circus? No one should have to live this way”. [10]




Abbey sees the big picture and condemns the insane whirlpool which is dragging us ever deeper into industrial hell.




He writes: “Growth is good, they say, reciting like an incantation the prime article of faith of the official American religion. Bigger is better and best is biggest.




“Growth, they tell us, means more jobs, more bank accounts, more cars, more people, leading in turn to the demand for more jobs, more economic expansion, more industrial development. Where, when, and how is this spiraling process supposed to reach a rational end – a state of stability, sanity, and equilibrium?” [11]




“The religion of endless growth – like any religion based on blind faith rather than reason – is a kind of mania, a form of lunacy, indeed a disease.




“And the one disease to which the growth mania bears an exact analogical resemblance is cancer. Growth for the sake of growth is the ideology of the cancer cell. Cancer has no purpose but growth; but it does have another result – the death of the host”. [12]




As his character John Vogelin declares in 

Fire on the Mountain

: “I say, let’s turn back the clock. Why does progress have to progress over me and the coyotes?”. [13]










The author identifies the dark force behind all of this in his fiction, dubbing a $37m Giant Earth Mover known as GOLIATH, the world’s largest mobile machine, “Moloch the insatiable”. [14]




He writes: “The only purpose of freeway projects, highway building, river-damming, pro-development reasoning, and opposition to wilderness preservation, naming but a few measures, is to make possible, encourage and create the runaway growth that enriches a few and gradually impoverishes the rest of us”. [15]




And this massive ongoing theft is not random and spontaneous, but deliberately planned by a vast and malevolent entity.




Abbey describes “the oligarchy and oligopoly beyond: Peabody Coal only one arm of Anaconda Copper; Anaconda only a limb of United States Steel; US Steel intertwined in incestuous embrace with the Pentagon, TVA, Standard Oil, General Dynamics, Dutch Shell, I.G. Farben-industrie; the whole conglomerated cartel spread out upon half the planet Earth like a global kraken”. [16]




“The cheap false synthetic structures inspired by greed spread along the highways like mustard weed, like poison ivy, like the creeping kudzu vine. The vampires of real estate, the leeches of finance, the tapeworms of profit, have fastened themselves to the body of my nation”. [17]




“What happens to democracy when 2 percent of America’s families – according to Federal Reserve Board reports – control 40 percent of our national wealth?” [18]










Abbey also knows that the god of greed advances hand in hand with the power of the state, the means by which it can “legally” impose its rule on the victim population.




As Seldom Seen Smith tells fellow Monkey Wrench Gang member George Hayduke: “They own the guvmint, George, you know that. They own the politicians, the judges, the Tee Vee, the army, the 

po

-lice. They own ever’ damn thing they need to own”. [19]




Abbey aptly sums up the police: “The proud sensitive flunkies of the rich and powerful. Armed and dangerous”. [20]




“If I should object to force I will be arrested. If I object to arrest I will be clubbed. If I defend myself against clubbing I will be shot. These procedures are known as The Rule of Law”. [21]




Abbey sometimes finds hope by taking a very long-term view, looking beyond his own lifespan: “Nobody lives forever. Neither do civilizations. They come and they go, like you and me”. [22]




Vogelin reckons he was born forty years too late and is going to die forty years too soon.




Why the latter? “I figure in forty years civilization will collapse and everything will be back to normal. I wish I could live to see it”. [23]










But more often Abbey finds positivity in encouraging courageous resistance to the thing he calls the global kraken.




For Vogelin, this takes the form of a simple refusal to accept that the state wing of the military-industrial complex can “legally” dispossess him of his ranch so as to expand a missile base – declaring that he is following in the tradition of the Apaches who resisted the confiscation of their land by European colonialists.




“‘No!’ Grandfather thundered, cigar in hand. ‘No!’ he roared, as he did a thousand times that summer”. [24]




But the Monkey Wrench Gang resist joyfully with feisty and funny exploits of anti-industrial sabotage – illustrated in one edition by the artist 

Robert Crumb

, [25] who, as I have 

written

, continues his critique of the system to this day. [26]




The tone of the novel is nicely summed up by the words with which George Hayduke wakes fellow gang member Bonnie Abbzug.







“Back to work”, he growled, rousing her. “We got three bridges, a railroad, a strip mine, a power plant, two dams, a nuclear reactor, one computer data center, six highway projects and a BLM scenic overlook to take care of this week. Up, up, up”. [27]







When one of the gang asks why they are doing all this, Hayduke patiently explains, not for the first time: “Because somebody has to do it. That’s why”. [28]










Abbey writes: “One way or another they were going to slow if not halt the advance of Technocracy, the growth of Growth, the spread of the ideology of the cancer cell”. [29]




“The megamachine means slavery. Submission to slavery is the ultimate moral disgrace. Live free or die. Death before dishonor. Code of the eco-warrior, code of the free, motto of the noble in spirit… win or lose, the important thing is resistance. Defiance. Rebellion. Better to die on our feet than live on our knees”. [30]




“There’s one thing worse than being defeated and that’s not making any fight at all”. [31]




The Monkey Wrench Gang

 had a direct impact on the real world, as Eric Schlosser explains: “Fed up with the timidity of mainstream environmental groups and inspired by Abbey’s work, a group of activists founded Earth First!, vowing to monkey-wrench on behalf of the land”. [32]




In 

Hayduke Lives!

 Abbey describes an Earth First! gathering – “seven days of fun, frolic and anarchy” [33] attended by 

Earth First! Journal

 editor Dave Foreman, woke hecklers and a number of state spies (there may have been some overlap in those two categories, as we will see).




“Flags, pennants, T-shirts and buttons, clenched fists and flying monkey wrenches, the import might be construed as suggesting a certain vague dissatisfaction with the ‘oligarchic swine’ (as one wag put it) who ‘own and operate America’ (in the phrase of another)”. [34]










“It was that sense of life that cannot be expressed – or depressed – through mere words. It was the message of the wolf’s cry, the lion’s roar, the whispering of the forest, the thunder of a storm, the silence of the canyon, the wail of wind, the meaning of the moon. The fire of the blood. The drumming of the heart. The beating of the drums”. [35]




But, of course, “mere words” were the backbone of Abbey’s resistance, even if it seems he may well have participated in nocturnal activities of the kind his novels describe.




And he spells out the sense of duty, of 

necessity

 even, that pushed him to write what he did.




“The more freedom the writer possesses the greater the moral obligation to play the role of critic… When necessary the writer must be willing to undertake the dangerous, and often ridiculous, and sometimes martyrlike role of hero or heroine…




“I mean involvement, responsibility, commitment: the writer’s duty to speak the truth – especially unpopular truth. Especially truth that offends the powerful, the rich, the well-established, the traditional, the mythic, the sentimental. To attack, when the time makes it necessary, the sacred cows of his society”. [36]




Abbey was obviously guided by a powerful personal philosophy, which I would very much include under the organic radical banner, hence the 

addition

 of a version of this profile to that library of inspirations. [37]










He mentions in his writing several of those also featured there – on more than one occasion in the case of 

Henry David Thoreau

 [38] and 

Leo Tolstoy

 [39] – and his radicalism is combined, as is typical of that half-forgotten and now half-remembered current of thought, with “the conservative instinct to keep things not as they are but as they should be… to keep it like it was”. [40]




Abbey grew up in an Appalachian hillbilly family and was undoubtedly influenced by what W.D. James 

calls

 the “Organic Libertarianism” of that mountainous region. [41]




More specifically Abbey was, of course, an anarchist – he even researched the subject at the University of New Mexico. “His Master’s thesis was a study of Godwin, Proudhon, Kropotkin and Bakunin, among others, with the title ‘Anarchism and the Morality of Violence'”. [42]




He wrote an article for Earth First! called ‘Theory of Anarchy’ in which he explains: “Anarchism means maximum democracy: the maximum possible dispersal of political power, economic power, and force – military power.




“An anarchist society consists of a voluntary association of self-reliant, self-supporting, autonomous communities. The anarchist society would consist (as it did in preagricultural and preindustrial times) of a voluntary association of free and independent families, self-reliant and self-supporting but bound by kinship ties and a tradition of mutual aid”. [43]










Abbey, like the English green anarchist 

Richard Hunt

, [44] says this free society would be armed and prepared to defend itself: “A healthy community polices itself: a healthy society would do the same. Looters, thugs, criminals, may appear anywhere, anytime, but in nature such types are mutants, anomalies, a minority; the members of a truly democratic, anarchistic society would not require outside assistance in dealing with them”. [45]




“Like a bulldozer, government serves the caprice of any man or group who succeeds in seizing the controls. The purpose of anarchism is to dismantle such institutions and to prevent their reconstruction.




“Ten thousand years of human history demonstrate that our freedoms cannot be entrusted to those ambitious few who are drawn to power: we must learn – again – to govern ourselves.




“Anarchism does not mean ‘no rule’, it means ‘no rulers’. Difficult but not utopian, anarchy means and requires self-rule, self-discipline, probity, character”. [46]




It is not just the ideology of anarchism that inspires Abbey and his rebellious characters, but its vital spirit.




“Hayduke followed hard on his heels, sweating with excitement, fear, joy, the lust for action. For heroic and noble action. The urge to destroy that which is evil, said the anarchist Prince Bakunin, is a creative urge. How true. How bloody awful true”. [47]










However, as many of us have subsequently discovered, being a real organic anarchist – a rebel wild and free – does not go down at all well with the fake anarchists who seek to hijack, divert and undermine the movement and its thinking.




In the last few years of his life Abbey came under particular attack from Murray Bookchin, a Marxist turned “anarchist” who eventually abandoned that misleading label to peddle an insipid “Green Left” reformism he called “social ecology”.




Bookchin vehemently attacked Abbey and his friends in Earth First! for their so-called “eco-fascism” – an oft-used slur against deep ecology and nature-based spirituality that I thoroughly debunked in my 2018 article ‘

Organic radicalism: bringing down the fascist machine

‘. [48]




The main stick with which Bookchin attacked Abbey was an article in which the latter declared his opposition to ongoing mass immigration into the USA.




Abbey denied being “racist”, as Bookchin claimed him to be, conceding that “we are all the descendants of illegal aliens” [49] and clearly sourcing his stance in his opposition to industrialism, growth and exploitation.




He writes in ‘Immigration and Liberal Taboos’: “A large, cheap, frightened, docile, surplus labor force is exactly what the economy needs. Put some fear into the unions: tighten discipline, spur productivity, whip up the competition for jobs.




“The conservatives love their cheap labour, the liberals love their cheap cause… Both factions are supported by the cornucopian economists of the ever-expanding economy, who actually continue to believe that our basic resource is not land, air, water, but human bodies, more and more of them, the more the better in hive upon hive, world without end”. [50]










In truth, as the poet Gary Snyder 

told

 the 

Los Angeles Times

 in 1989, Bookchin (

pictured

) simply seized upon this issue in a desperate attempt to cling on to the ideological leadership that he wrongly imagined he had gained over the eco-anarchist scene.




“Murray launched an attack that I feel really misrepresents what deep ecology literature has been saying in a scandalous way,” Snyder said. “Although he claims to be an anarchist, he writes like a Stalinist thug”. [51]




In Abbey’s last novel, 

Hayduke Lives!

, he provides an entertaining account of the appearance at the aforementioned Earth First! wilderness gathering of a fictional character whose name alone suggests a strong resemblance to Bookchin.




“Bernie Mushkin took the microphone, red in the face and panting. A man of sixty or so, bald on top, flatfooted at bottom, wide-assed narrow-minded and slope-shouldered, he resembled in shape a child’s toy known as Mr. Potato-Head”. [52]










“Bernie Mushkin, old-time Marxist, sectarian revolutionary, tenured professor, academic writer, pedagogue, demagogue, ideologue, was drawn to political controversy as a moth to the flame – or a blowfly to a rotting hog. Inept and passionate, fiery-tempered and humorless, graceless but relentless”. [53]




Having delivered a Nazi salute and barked out “Sieg Heil!” two or three times to the bemused eco-crowd, Mushkin starts to read out a statement from a piece of paper in his hand.




“Earth First! eco-fascists… I congratulate you on setting back the cause of justice, decency, ecology and environmentalism by at least fifty years in America”. [54]




“Your well-publicized advocacy of sabotage and monkey-wrenching has made Earth First! a synonym for terrorism”. [55]




He says the deep ecologists have been revealed to be “nationalists and xenophobes, quite the opposite of the fun-loving anarchists you pretend to be… a hypocritical mob of creeping fascist hyenas and elitist Nazi racists. Sieg Heil!”. [56]




Abbey continues:







A fat little boy, wearing a T-shirt that argued “No Guts No Glory”, broke the silence by piping up. “Mister Mushkin”, he squeaked.

“Yes?”

“Wanta get rid of ten pounds of ugly fat?”

“What?”

“Cut your head off!” the boy squealed and broke down howling. Every child in the audience, and there were at least a hundred of them, listening intently when they heard the tip-off line, joined in the chorale of laughter. The contagion spread, the hilarity became general”. [57]













Mushkin’s three female supporters then “drove him to his hotel in nearby Las Vegas only three hundred miles away; in their eyes and in his the nearest outpost of proper civilization in the entire northern Arizona-Utah-Nevada region.




“At least there is a university in Las Vegas. Hospitals. A foreign-film cinema. Fern bars. Lesbian bookstores. And a synagogue or two or three…” [58]




I do not consider it irrelevant that Bookchin met his wife-to-be Beatrice Applestein 

while speaking to a zionist youth organization

 at City College, New York, [59] or that he 

enthused

 in print about the prospect of using sensing devices to automatically operate machines such as “a giant shovel in an open-strip mine” – the very industrial monsters that Abbey and Earth First! were resisting. [60]




As I have 

previously written

, [61] I strongly suspect him to have been an agent of ZIM, the zio-imperialist mafia which globally controls government and industry alike.




It is very telling that the real-life Bookchin, like the fictional Mushkin, 

used

 the very dangerous “terrorism” label to attack people who were supposedly fighting for the same broad cause as he was. [62]




Later the US authorities were to use the same term in the wave of repression against the Earth Liberation Front (ELF), a new generation of eco-activists inspired by Abbey’s work.










Despite the fact that the ELF was strictly opposed to violence against people or other living beings, in 2004 the FBI branded the network “America’s top domestic terrorist threat”. [63]




This is an obvious and odious inversion of real justice – throwing spanners into the cogs of the industrial monster is a desperate attempt to 

stop

 the very real terror that it is unleashing on our world.




We have seen the same inversion operating in the UK recently, with the unbelievable branding of people as “terrorists” for speaking out against the genocidal terror being inflicted by the criminal state of Israel.




I say “unbelievable” but it is utterly 

believable

 when you know that the British state is owned and controlled by those who own and control “Israel”.




And the elevation of resistance to both industrialism and zionism to “terrorism” status merely confirms what I have been saying for a while now – industrialism is a judeo-supremacist operation to pillage, enslave and exploit across the world.




Abbey points to the same criminocracy at work, albeit in a fictional context, in his description of an EF! action against strip mining.




He notes how comfortable liberal demonstrations in well-off American cities were both tolerated by the authorities and considered “newsworthy” by the media.










“But let a bunch of hairy redneck rabble in some wasteland western American state interpose their living bodies between the industrial megamachine and a little patch of free country, open space, old-growth forest, natural nature, wildland and wildlife, and the horror runs deep through the hierarchy of upper management.




“That kind of subversion (non-commercial) cannot be accepted; will not (anti-business) be tolerated; has to (pro-populist) be most severely punished both legally and – in so far as possible – illegally; and last but categorically imperative, shall not be encouraged through the power of example by publicity in any form.




“As in any well-ordered oligarchy, not only the event must be suppressed but all news of it as well. Therefore the ‘media’ did not appear”. [64]




The same supremacist mafia which owns the media, industry and finance – as well as an impressive track record in child-trafficking, warmongering and ethnic cleansing – also of course owns Hollywood.




So it is also less-than-unbelievable that, as Eric Schlosser explains: “Although the film rights to 

The Monkey Wrench Gang

 were optioned in 1975, repeated efforts to make a movie based on the book went nowhere”. [65]




To be honest, it is probably a good thing that they did not turn the book into a film – they would probably have completely ruined it and even inverted its morality to suit the needs of Abbey’s “global kraken” of which 

showbiz

 forms part.




But the fact that they did not want his voice to reach and inspire millions of young people confirms the potential power of that voice.




Let’s all keep reading Abbey, talking and writing about him, defending his memory, forgiving his failings as we forgive our own, following his example and battling to ensure that his message of joyful resistance is passed on from generation to generation until nature’s uprising at last succeeds in toppling the malignant megamachine!

author: Aaron Ernest Cruz
title: Seafarers demand end to US war
content:
eafarer groups along with migrant worker groups held a forum to condemn U.S war against countries, affecting their safe travel at sea. (Photo by Aaron Ernest Cruz/Bulatlat)

The Philippines is not just being exploited from their resources but it is also exposed to the enemies of the U.S.

Condrad Belasa, 28, witnessed military aircraft of Iran and the United States carrying out bombings while working as a seafarer. Although their route was far from the Strait of Hormuz, he said that he still felt afraid.

He recalled an incident on March 11, a month after the U.S started its attack on Iran, when their ship passed through the Green Zone. They saw military aircraft bombing one another in real time. Their crew could do nothing but hope that no missiles or ammunition would hit their ship.

“While we are sailing, we see in the radar that we are being followed by military aircraft. Some of my colleagues said it was a fighter jet but in my personal opinion, I think it was a drone,” Belasa told Bulatlat in an interview.

In his five years of working as a seafarer, this was the first time he found himself caught in the middle of a war. The experience worried him, especially because he has a two-year old child waiting for him to come home.

He and other seafarers gathered at Redemptorist Church, Baclaran for National Seafarer Day on September 25 and condemned the government’s lack of action to protect their welfare as well as its strong military ties with the U.S., which they said put them more at risk.

“I told my wife jokingly that she will be instantly rich when something bad happens [to me] because of the benefits that she will receive. But on a serious note, it is difficult for my family if something happens to me because the benefit they will receive is not for a lifetime,” Belasa told Bulatlat in Filipino.

There were reportedly five seafarers who died in the Strait of Hormuz.

“Whoever the enemy of the U.S will make the Philippines prone by their retaliation. Just when the U.S. bombed schools in Iraq, it retaliated and bombed US military facilities,” said Atty. Edwin Dela Cruz, president of International Seafarers Action Center (ISAC).

In terms of critical minerals, Dela Cruz said that the U.S. resorted to aggression, citing the kidnapping of former Venezuelan President Nicholas Maduro and the attacks on Iran to gain natural resources.

“That is why the Philippines is not just being exploited from their resources but it is also exposed to the enemies of the U.S. even though we don’t see them as the enemy,” Dela Cruz said.

Just like the other Filipino seafarers, Belasa hoped that the U.S should stop its aggression against any country as they only gained a little but lost a lot of innocent people’s lives. “We just want to make a living and to be with our family safe and sound.”

Xavier Bayoneta, chairperson of Concerned Seafarers of the Philippines (CSP), said that there has been a lack of protection for the seafarers whose lives were at risk every time they worked at the sea.

When the Magna Carta of Filipino Seafarers was signed on September 23, labor lawyers and seafarers groups criticized it.

Bayoneta pointed to the requirement to post a financial bond when a seafarer wins a labor dispute if the employer appeals the decision to a higher court. He also cited the bank “escrow” framework which he said prevents seafarers from immediately receiving medical or death benefits.

“If before we’re worried about pirates, now our worries doubled due to advanced military aircraft like drones. Instead of protecting our rights, the DMW [Department of Migrant Workers] is not doing anything or we don’t feel it if they are doing something,” Bayoneta said.

Belasa said that laws are meant to protect its constituents and not to suppress their rights. “There should be a proper consultation with us seafarers before they come up with laws that genuinely protect us instead.”

He also urged his co-seafarers to speak up despite the consequences of being blacklisted. (AMU, DAA)

author: Unknown
title: Эррико Малатеста - Наука и социальные преобразования
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Наука и социальные преобразования

Дата

: 27 декабря 1913

Источник

: Опубликовано в №29 журнала «Volontà» (Анкона)




 Великие научные открытия XIX века и победоносная критика, которую наука противопоставила лжи и заблуждениям религий, привели к тому, что прогрессивные умы стали восторженными поклонниками – если не разумными и терпеливыми исследователями – Науки, и, преувеличивая, приписали Науке способность всё понимать и всё разрешать: из Науки сделали новую Религию. 




 И сторонники социальных преобразований всех мастей, то есть все те, кто с какой-либо целью и какими-либо средствами намеревался изменить существующую общественную организацию, сочли себя обязанными обосновать свои стремления Наукой; тогда как с другой стороны консерваторы, увидев, что религиозная вера пошатнулась и уже недостаточна, чтобы держать народ в подчинении, также попытались оправдать существующий строй с помощью науки. 




 Это было подлинное опьянение (не рассеявшееся ещё и поныне), которое заставило утратить ясное понятие о природе, методах и пределах Науки, в полный ущерб научной истине и социальному действию. 




 Никто или почти никто не спасся; и если мы, анархисты, избежали нелепости называться анархистами научными, то, возможно, лишь потому, что эпитет «научный» был уже занят и стал отвратителен благодаря марксистскому социализму. 




 В самом деле, многие из наших товарищей, и среди наиболее заслуженных и известных, утверждали именно, что Анархия есть вывод из истин, установленных Наукой, что она не что иное, как применение механистической концепции вселенной к человеческим фактам. 




 Между тем, чтобы показать ошибочность этого их сциентизма, показать, что в действительности их анархизм проистекает из их чувств, а не из их научных убеждений, есть то обстоятельство, что они продолжают оставаться анархистами точно так же и тогда, когда науки прогрессируют и меняются; и, несмотря на исповедуемый ими объективизм, на практике они не допускают фактов и не принимают теорий, которые, казалось бы, противоречат их анархистским стремлениям. 




 И если бы у них не было случая заниматься научными исследованиями, или если бы наук не существовало, а человеческие знания оставались бы в том состоянии, в каком они находились века назад, они, вероятно, точно так же были бы анархистами, потому что, будучи людьми чувствительными и добрыми, они страдали бы от людского горя и желали бы его победить, а будучи людьми гордыми и справедливыми, восстали бы против угнетения и захотели бы полной свободы для себя и для всех. 




 Более того, они признают качество сознательных анархистов за огромным большинством товарищей, которые не знают науки; и когда они ведут пропаганду, то делают это точно так же, как мы, то есть стремятся пробудить в людях чувства личного достоинства и любви к другим, стараются возбудить страсть к свободе и справедливости, говорят об общем благе и человеческом братстве, выявляют социальные бедствия и пробуждают волю к их уничтожению, не дожидаясь, пока люди изучат математику, астрономию и химию. 




***




 Изучать науки – дело прекрасное, и далее мы скажем, для чего они служат. 




 Но утверждать, что анархизм (и то же самое следует сказать о социализме или любом другом человеческом стремлении) есть научный вывод, утверждать особенно, что он есть следствие одной из тех обширных космогонических гипотез, в которых находит удовольствие философия, – это вещь ложная сама по себе и, кроме того, вредная по последствиям, которые она может иметь для интеллектуального развития индивидов и для их способности быть революционерами. 




 Идея личного Бога, творца всех вещей, которая является самой древней, самой наивной и самой грубо абсурдной из тех гипотез, причинила огромный вред, потому что приучила людей верить, ничего не понимая в действительности, и, задушив дух любопытства и исследования, сформировала рабов сознания, хорошо подготовленных к тому, чтобы терпеть политическое и экономическое рабство. 




 Но разве не то же самое делают научные гипотезы, когда их представляют как неопровержимые истины и как мотив для действия тем, кто не знает науки и не способен судить о них? 




 Недостаточно того или иного смутного понятия о научных истинах, более или менее достоверных, и знания нескольких заумных слов, чтобы сделать человека мудрецом или, по крайней мере, человеком, который знает, что говорит, и может выбирать между вещами, которые ему говорят. 




 Для широкой публики Моисей и Геккель – фигуры одинаково мифические, и верить в монизм одного и не верить в генезис другого только потому, что это модно в нашей среде, не делает человека менее невежественным, менее суеверным, менее религиозным. И говорить профанам об атомах, ионах и электронах (которые в конечном счёте суть гипотезы для объяснения и соотнесения определённых категорий фактов, гипотезы удобные, гипотезы полезные для научного исследования, но гипотезы, простые мысленные построения, и ни в коем случае не позитивные открытия), говорить, повторяю, тем, кто их не знает, о вещах тайных и непостижимых без должной подготовки – это то же самое, что говорить им о Боге и Ангелах; то есть учить словам и заставлять верить, что это реально существующие вещи, приучать ум довольствоваться утверждениями, которых не понимаешь и не можешь ни доказать, ни определить. 




...

author: Craig Brittain
title: The story of the League of Revolutionary Black Workers
content:
Motown and the making of working-class revolutionaries: The story of the League of Revolutionary Black Workers By Jerome Scott and Walda Katz-Fishman University of Georgia Press. 2025

Of all the radical groups to emerge in the United States in the 1960s, one of the most interesting was the League of Revolutionary Black Workers, which began organising in the car industry in Detroit, Michigan.

Jerome Scott and Walda Katz-Fishman’s book, Motown and the making of working-class revolutionaries, is based on extensive interviews with the surviving members of the league.

Before and after World War II, large numbers of African Americans moved north from the southern states to escape segregation and police violence, and in search of the $5-a-day industrialist Henry Ford was promising in his car factories. They were used to earning about $6 a week.

However, what they discovered in the car plants was that white workers got the pick of the jobs and Black workers did the dirty work. Management was white and so was the union. Both were racist.

Those who went north might not have experienced the legally sanctioned discrimination they’d experienced in the south, but there was plenty of discrimination nonetheless; in housing, education and employment. And the police were just the same.

Things came to a head in what is known as the 1967 Detroit Rebellion, which the media naturally referred to as “race riots”. President Lyndon Johnson called in the National Guard and the military, which opened fire with machine guns, killing 45 people.

Black workers in Detroit had had enough. They started organising in their workplaces. A few student workers got together and created the Dodge Revolutionary Union Movement or DRUM, in May 1968, at the Chrysler Hamtramck car factory.

Later on, other Revolutionary Union Movements (RUMs) were set up in other plants and industries, such as FRUM at Ford, ELRUM at Chrysler Eldon Avenue and UPRUM at the United Postal Service.

At the time, the union traditionally representing car assembly workers, the United Auto Workers (UAW), had effectively become a branch of management. The UAW and the company had a convenient arrangement whereby the union would give advance notice of a strike. This enabled the company to prepare and plan around strike action, effectively undermining the strike. In return, the union got financial and other kickbacks.

The first thing DRUM members did was stage a wildcat strike over speedups on the car assembly line. They also protested the racist practices of the company and the union. Four-thousand workers walked off the job and stopped production. Wildcat strikes became their main tactic.

The league was established to bring the various RUMs together and coordinate their activity. Its leaders were Marxists. While most production-line workers didn’t start out that way, many became radicalised on the shop floor.

None of the white officials counted on Black workers having learned strategies and tactics through the Civil Rights movement, the Black Nationalist movement and a range of socialist groups that many belonged to.

They were experienced in mass meetings, collective decision-making and direct action, and believed strongly in grassroots leadership.

From the start, these revolutionaries set up newspapers to communicate with other workers and the Black community at large. The Inner City Voice and South End became major sources of information.

They were prepared to use whatever methods worked. It didn’t matter whether they’d originally come from the International Workers of the World, the Communist Party, anarcho-syndicalism or Maoism.

They held demonstrations and rallies, issued plant bulletins and leaflets, picketed union headquarters and forced union executives to listen to their demands. They also boycotted nearby bars that refused to hire Black workers.

Activists quickly moved pickets from one factory to another to outsmart the police. They studied Mao Zedong’s On Practice and On Contradiction, analysing situations dialectically in order to decide what to do next.

The league lasted from 1969–71, before it split. But it achieved a remarkable amount in just two years.

The split was primarily over a difference of opinion about priorities. Figures such as General Baker and Scott, the book’s co-author, felt that the league should stick with what it had set out to do: improve conditions for Black workers in the car industry. Others, such as Mike Hamlin and Ken Cockrel, wanted to broaden the league’s focus to include areas like education, healthcare, publishing and filmmaking.

By and large, organised production-line workers who belonged to DRUM raised concerns that its Executive Branch was separating itself from the rank and file and no longer listening to their grievances. They wanted more democracy; as it had been in DRUM at the beginning, when everyone had a say, and there wasn’t a gap between the “thinkers” (the Executive Branch) and the “workers” on the shop floor. Eventually, some of them, such as Ernie Allen, were expelled for raising complaints, and the organisation didn’t last long after that.

In spite of the organisational split, members of the league didn’t give up and become pro-capitalist or drop out, rather they, each in their own way, kept up the struggle.

Some leaders, such as Scott and Baker, joined the Communist Labor Party, which eventually became the League of Revolutionaries for a New America, along with die-hard radical Nelson Peery (1923–2015). They stuck with production workers in the factories and then, as automation and offshoring took over, increasingly concentrated on organising and educating unemployed and under-employed workers.

The Hamlin and Cockrel group went into community work, legal support, health work and local government.

Both groups have made long-standing contributions.

As one of the original league members, Luke Tripp, said in 2017, “The system in this country keeps me in a revolutionary orientation. The criminality and immorality of the system. Billionaires just sucking up all the wealth — super greedy, selfish and mean spirited. That’s what keeps me in a fighting spirit — a lot of outrage and anger. Revolutionaries are fighters.” (p155)

Another excellent book about the league is Dan Georgakas’ and Marvin Surkin’s Detroit: I do mind dying, originally published in 1975 and available at the Internet Archive, along with the documentary, Finally got the news, produced by the league in 1970.

author: La Zarzamora
title: Comunicado público ppm Caso Grollmus
content:
Frente a las exuberantes condenas y tras un viciado proceso declaramos:

Mari mari pu machi, pu lonko, pu werken, kom pu che. El día de hoy nos dirigimos a la sociedad en general, a todos y todas quienes nos han brindado su apoyo y respaldo en este proceso denominado “Caso Grollmus”.

Actualmente a nosotros como comuneros mapuche se nos ha condenado a penas que marcarán un precedente como obscenamente políticas, se nos condena por decisión política, por ser mapuche que vivimos y recuperamos nuestro territorio.

Tras el gigantesco despliegue comunicacional, y tras el espectáculo montado por el Ministerio Público y la PDI, la familia Grollmus demanda al estado en busca de indemnizaciones y reparaciones.

La fiscalía con el aval del tribunal logró su objetivo: condenar a una pena que ponderada resulta en 1055 años de prisión contra nosotros. La prensa vociferó la sentencia y el poder político respaldo, claridad absoluta.

Les decimos, su ocupación contra nuestro pueblo y su territorio apenas tiene 143 años. Nuestro pueblo resistió al imperio español casi 300 años.

Hoy Chile soberbio y republicano nos condena a más de 1000 años. Por el único motivo de luchar por nuestra soberanía, por nuestro buen vivir y dignidad. Lo anterior tendrá la más necesaria respuesta: continuar con el legado de nuestro pueblo, luchar por nuestra dignidad y libertad.

Los Grupos de Tarea y la BIPE de la PDI recorren los penales de forma morbosa buscando testigos a quienes poner corbata de protegido y sin rostro. Sólo por cuatro relatos de estos “testigos” se dictó sentencia y veredicto. Nuestro territorio se militariza y vuelven a saquear nuestros recursos naturales, vuelven las concesiones mineras, CMPC y Mininco cual mecenas entregan dinero y donaciones a Postas y Escuelas.

Queremos manifestar nuestro agradecimiento por todo el respaldo de nuestros hermanos y hermanas en otros territorios y ciudades. No renunciaremos jamás a la lucha por un debido y objetivo proceso.

Nos movilizaremos por nuestra libertad y juicio justo.

Finalmente los invitamos a sumarse a la próxima movilización articulada en distintos territorios para este 12 de octubre, Día de la resistencia de nuestros pueblos.

¡NULIDAD Y LIBERTAD! ¡NO MÁS TESTIGOS PROTEGIDOS! ¡UNIDAD EN EL WEYCHAN! ¡LIBERTAD A TODOS LOS PRESOS POLÍTICOS MAPUCHE!

Presos Políticos Mapuche del Caso Grollmus de la Franja Lavkenche, CP Biobio, CERECO Coronel, Cárcel Llancahue de Valdivia.

author: La Zarzamora
title: Detienen a ciberactivista Ola Bini en Ecuador
content:
Durante este 1 de octubre, el activista Ola Bini, fue nuevamente detenido tras ser interceptado por agentes de migración mientras se dirigía a comprar a un supermercado.

Carlos Soria, abogado de Ola Bini declaró durante esta tarde que la detención del activista es ilegal y lo calificó como un secuestro:

«Ola Bini se encuentra secuestrado en estos momentos, no le han dejado salir, no hay una orden de detención ni administrativa, peor judicial. Supuestamente esto viene de un informe secreto del Ministerio (del Interior), en donde no se rebelan las causas del porqué supuestamente Ola Bini ha sido considerado como una amenaza al Estado».

Ante el contexto actual de persecución a activistas digitales, distintas colectividades han mostrado preocupación y se mantienen atentas al estado de Ola Bini y al cumplimiento del debido proceso.

Carlos Soria también se refirió a la revocación de la visa que habría sido por «solicitud el Ministerio del Interior» ecuatoriano, supuestamente por actos que atentarían contra la seguridad del Estado.

Tras ser detenido se realizó una audiencia ante la directora de migración, en un acto calificado por el mismo abogado como totalmente ilegal, a la cual no permitieron el ingreso de observadores de DDHH, audiencia que posteriormente fue suspendida.

Esto sucede 7 años después de que fuera arrestado por el estado ecuatoriano el 2019 y pasara 70 días en prisión antes de poder llevar su proceso fuera de la cárcel, acusado de supuestas actividades ilícitas y ataque cibernético a sistemas del Estado, proceso en el cual fue declarado inocente, saliendo absuelto el año 2023.

Su abogado fue determinante en afirmar que Ola Bini no tiene ningún tema penal pendiente y que esto sólo responde a una arbitrariedad del estado ecuatoriano.-

author: anred
title: «Se vuelven a encender las calles» tras el fallo de la Corte que reactivó la extranjerización de la tierra
content:
El máximo tribunal dejó vigente la derogación de la Ley de Tierras impulsada por Milei mediante el DNU 70/2023. Organizaciones sociales, sindicales, campesinas, indígenas y políticas comenzaron a reunirse para responder en las calles. En Diputados, sectores de la oposición convocaron a una sesión especial para el 15 de octubre con el objetivo de rechazar el decreto. Por ANRed




La Corte Suprema de Justicia de la Nación volvió a poner en vigencia la derogación de la Ley 26.737 de Régimen de Protección al Dominio Nacional sobre la Propiedad, Posesión o Tenencia de Tierras Rurales, impulsada por Javier Milei a través del DNU 70/2023. El fallo, firmado por Horacio Rosatti, Carlos Rosenkrantz y Ricardo Lorenzetti, revocó la sentencia de la Cámara Federal de La Plata que había declarado inconstitucional el artículo 154 del megadecreto y había frenado la derogación de la denominada Ley de Tierras.




La decisión judicial no declaró constitucional el DNU ni resolvió el fondo de la discusión. La Corte fundamentó su resolución en una cuestión procesal: consideró que el Centro de Ex Combatientes Islas Malvinas (CECIM) La Plata, que había presentado la demanda, no tenía legitimación suficiente para llevar adelante esa acción colectiva. El propio tribunal aclaró que su decisión se limitó a la existencia de un caso judicial y a la legitimación de la organización demandante. Sin embargo, el efecto concreto es que vuelve a regir la derogación de la Ley de Tierras dispuesta por el artículo 154 del DNU 70/23.




La Ley 26.737 establecía, entre otras restricciones, un límite del 15% para la titularidad extranjera de tierras rurales. Con la derogación de esas disposiciones quedan sin efecto esas restricciones específicas.




El fallo llega además después de una jornada de movilización que, durante agosto, puso en el centro de la agenda la disputa por la tierra y la soberanía territorial.




La respuesta vuelve a las calles




El fallo produjo una rápida reacción. La CTA Autónoma y la CTA de las y los Trabajadores convocaron a movilizarse el 

martes 6 de octubre a las 15 frente a la Corte Suprema

, junto a sindicatos, organizaciones sociales y otros sectores. ATE también anunció su estado de alerta y movilización.




En paralelo, comenzaron a multiplicarse las reuniones para organizar la respuesta. El 

viernes 2 de octubre

, organizaciones que participaron de la denominada Marcha de la Bronca tienen previsto reunirse en Parque Lezama para discutir una movilización contra el fallo. Gabriel Solano anticipó esa convocatoria.




La reacción recupera así una consigna que ya recorrió el país durante agosto: 

“La tierra no se vende, no se quema ni se desaloja”

.







El antecedente del 6 de agosto: extranjerización frenada, desalojos aprobados




El conflicto tiene un antecedente inmediato. El 

6 de agosto

, mientras el Senado debatía la denominada Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, una jornada federal reunió a organizaciones campesinas, indígenas, ambientales, sociales, políticas, sindicales y de derechos humanos en distintos puntos del país.




La movilización central se realizó frente al Congreso, donde hubo radio abierta, festival cultural y un verdurazo. También se registraron acciones en numerosas ciudades y localidades del país. La consigna fue contundente: 

“La tierra no se vende, no se quema ni se desaloja”

.




La presión social se produjo mientras el oficialismo intentaba conseguir los votos para avanzar con el proyecto. Finalmente, el Gobierno tuvo que retirar del texto el capítulo referido a la extranjerización de tierras. Ese retroceso fue señalado por las organizaciones convocantes y dirigentes de izquierda como resultado de la movilización.







Represión en el Congreso: tres personas detenidas por defender la tierra




La masiva movilización contra el proyecto de Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, que busca ampliar la extranjerización de las tierras y profundizar su privatización, terminó con represión. 

pic.twitter.com/cRw7pDoUO8




— ANRed #30Años (@Red__Accion) 

August 6, 2026




  




Pero hubo una diferencia fundamental: 

la movilización logró frenar el capítulo de extranjerización, pero no consiguió impedir la aprobación de los artículos vinculados con los desalojos exprés

.




El Senado aprobó el proyecto de propiedad privada por 37 votos contra 33. La iniciativa estableció mecanismos destinados a agilizar los desalojos de inmuebles, viviendas, campos y terrenos considerados ocupados o usurpados.




Ese aspecto había sido advertido durante la campaña de movilización. Romina Del Plá había señalado antes de la sesión que, aunque había caído el capítulo de extranjerización, continuaban en pie los artículos que habilitaban 

“desalojos exprés violentos contra inquilinos y comunidades originarias”

.




En ese mismo sentido, ANRed había entrevistado al werken mapuche 

Mauro Millán

, quien había advertido sobre las consecuencias que podían tener los cambios en materia de desalojos para las comunidades indígenas y los territorios en conflicto.




Mauro Millán: “La presencia de las comunidades indígenas está garantizando seguir teniendo el agua gratuita y sana”







El antecedente resulta significativo para el escenario actual: mientras la movilización consiguió que el Gobierno retirara la modificación de la Ley de Tierras del proyecto, otra parte de la reforma vinculada directamente con los mecanismos de desalojo logró avanzar.




Ahora, con el fallo de la Corte, vuelve a abrirse por otra vía el capítulo que el Gobierno no consiguió aprobar en el Congreso durante agosto: la eliminación de los límites establecidos por la Ley de Tierras para la propiedad extranjera.




La izquierda cuestionó el fallo y agita respuesta en las calles




Las primeras reacciones de dirigentes de izquierda combinaron el rechazo al fallo con el reclamo de que Diputados avance sobre el DNU 70/23.




Myriam Bregman

 reclamó la anulación del decreto y señaló que el debate debe trasladarse a la Cámara de Diputados. La diputada del Frente de Izquierda sostuvo que desde ese espacio se pusieron a disposición para conseguir las firmas necesarias para convocar una sesión especial y planteó: 

“Sesión en mano, nos sentamos en el recinto y que se vea quién es quién”

.







Ya mismo hay que anular el decreto 70/23 y muchas de estas discusiones se resolverían. Falta hacerlo en la Cámara de Diputados, por eso integrantes del Frente de Izquierda nos hemos puesto a disposición reiteradamente para llamar a una sesión especial. Se necesitan 10 firmas, es…




— Myriam Bregman (@myriambregman) 

September 29, 2026







Por su parte, 

Romina Del Plá

 calificó como “gravísimo” el fallo y vinculó directamente la decisión judicial con el resultado de la movilización del 6 de agosto. “La entrega de tierras que el gobierno no pudo imponer con su nefasta Ley de Inviolabilidad de la Propiedad Privada, frenada por la enorme movilización popular del 6 de agosto, ahora pretende ser habilitada por un fallo de la Corte Suprema”, sostuvo.




La diputada del Partido Obrero reclamó además la derogación del DNU 70/23 y afirmó que su bloque impulsará una sesión especial para discutirlo. “Lo que el gobierno no pudo imponer por la movilización popular no puede ser impuesto ahora por la Corte Suprema”, señaló.




Gabriel Solano

, también dirigente del Partido Obrero, anticipó que las organizaciones que participaron de la Marcha de la Bronca se reunirían en Parque Lezama para organizar una movilización contra el fallo.




Las declaraciones se suman a las de otros sectores opositores. El diputado de Unión por la Patria 

Germán Martínez

 anunció que su bloque pedirá una sesión especial para rechazar el DNU 70/23. El planteo recibió también el respaldo de Esteban Paulón, Pablo Juliano, Maximiliano Ferraro y Romina Del Plá.




Diputados vuelve al centro de la disputa




El DNU 70/23 ya había sido rechazado por el Senado. Ahora distintos bloques opositores buscan que la Cámara de Diputados haga lo mismo. Para que el decreto pierda vigencia de manera definitiva, debe ser rechazado por ambas cámaras.




El pedido de sesión especial fue anunciado luego del fallo de la Corte. La fecha planteada es el 

15 de octubre

, con el DNU 70/23 entre los temas a tratar. La discusión parlamentaria aparece así como una de las vías abiertas para restablecer las restricciones que quedaron sin efecto con la derogación de la Ley de Tierras.




El oficialismo, por su parte, ya anticipó que la oposición deberá reunir el quórum necesario para abrir la sesión. El resultado dependerá, por lo tanto, de la composición del recinto y de las posiciones que adopten los distintos bloques.

author: Peter Boyle
title: Hunter Valley coal mine expansion approval bad for environment, jobs
content:
Steve O’Brien, the Socialist Alliance candidate for Newcastle in next year’s New South Wales election, said the September 30 decision of the NSW Independent Planning Commission to approve the Hunter Valley Operations (HVO) Mine Continuation Project, the largest coal mine expansion ever proposed in NSW, was a very bad decision.

“It is bad for our Pacific neighbours, who are already feeling the effects of rising sea levels,” O’Brien told Green Left. “It is bad for our environment because it will worsen the bushfires, floods and other catastrophic climate events. And it’s also bad for workers.

“We’ve been told by the Chris Minns Labor government that 1500 jobs have been saved by this decision, but that figure needs to be seriously interrogated.

“Who really trusts Glencore, which owns these mines, to keep 1500 jobs until 2045?

“Glencore will continue to cut jobs — the number left when the mine eventually closes in 2045 will be a lot less than 1500.

“Glencore is in the business of making profits for its owners. In the capitalist system, that invariably means cutting jobs.”

O’Brien said that NSW Labor is being duplicitous, deliberately lying to working people about climate change and the serious challenge that it poses for this country.

“To keep the capitalist class onside, Labor has to make sure that every last bit of coal is dug out of the Hunter Valley. Glencore’s boss actually said the last shovel full of coal that comes out anywhere in the world will come out of its HVO mines.”

Labor is totally pro-fossil fuels but pretends to be pro-climate action and pro-environment, he added.

“Governments can’t be serious about taking action on the climate while approving a huge coal mine expansion, which will add 800 million tonnes of carbon emissions [to the atmosphere].

“As The Climate Council has pointed out, this is more than seven times NSW’s annual climate pollution.”

O’Brien said the duplicity of the Labor party creates confusion and breeds cynicism in the working class about climate change.

“The climate crisis is real. People are facing fires, floods and other catastrophic climate disasters all the time. Yet, the Labor party acts like it doesn’t exist when it comes to pushing mine expansions like HVO.

“Greg Mullins, a former commissioner of Fire and Rescue NSW, has warned that this is a decision that every community in NSW will end up paying for — in the form of bushfires, floods, heatwaves and droughts. Just in the Hunter, more than 12,000 homes are already at high risk of becoming un-insurable.

“The billionaire class and the fossil fuel companies welcome the cynicism about the climate emergency. They love to see the working class divided and, in particular, they are very happy to see the Hunter Valley’s working class divided over this giant coal mine expansion.

“We need working-class unity if we are going to ensure that these communities have something left when the coal mines are gone,” O’Brien stressed.

“In the upper Hunter Valley, many problems need addressing, such as public transport between the different towns. They need schools and hospitals to keep up with the growing demand. In addition, there is the question of housing and tapping the full potential of renewable energy from solar and wind power.

“We all agree that the future needs to include jobs for these communities, so we should also agree that we need to tax the fossil fuel companies and the rest of the billionaire class, which doesn’t pay their fair share of tax. This is how we can fund a just transition to a post-coal future in the Hunter Valley.

“The fossil fuel companies, and the banks that are behind them, have made billions exploiting the working-class communities in the Hunter Valley over many years. They shouldn’t be allowed to extract the last bit of profit from the dying coal industry and take off scot-free.”

author: labor4pal
title: The Case for Replacing UAW Monitor Neil Barofsky (UAWD Daily Struggle)
content:
Understanding Layoffs Fighting Layoffs Boom and Bust BlueOval Closure

Daily Struggle Editorial Board October 1, 2026

In 2024, UAW Monitor Neil Barofsky carried out an effort to intervene in UAW policy decisions and overturn the UAW’s opposition to the Israeli genocide in Gaza. Barofsky should be replaced for attacking the political independence of the UAW and violating his duties under the consent decree.

This is a republished UAWD resolution, with a new introduction to provide context, being co-released with The Struggle for Class-Independent Unionism in the Face of State Intervention.

Over the summer, the conflict between UAW President Shawn Fain and the UAW’s federal court-appointed monitor Neil Barofsky was back in the news. On June 25, Barofsky released his latest report alleging that Fain abused his authority and retaliated against the UAW’s Secretary-Treasurer Margaret Mock and Vice President Rich Boyer.

Fain countered the Monitor’s attack by saying Barfosky was “playing political games and abusing his power.” Specifically, the Monitor was punishing Fain for the UAW’s public position in favor of a ceasefire in Gaza.

In the Daily Struggle article, “Standing Down: Reflections on Shawn Fain’s Presidency,” four members of the UAWD Steering Committee—Andrew Bergman, Jeremy Bunyaner, Nolan Tabb, and Judy Wraight—addressed Fain’s handling of past attacks by the Monitor:

“Barofsky launched an investigation of Fain in his search for a way to attack Fain after the UAW took a position in support of a ceasefire in Gaza that offended Barofsky. […] Fain could’ve himself gone public, in one of his well-watched Facebook Live appearances, and made the case to the rank and file, explaining that his actions weren’t self-serving but were to reinvigorate UAW militancy.”

“But Fain again took a risk-averse approach, believing that having a good argument and not “airing dirty laundry” from within the bureaucracy would insulate him. The result is that the UAW membership, rightfully, feels uninformed about a complex set of accusations and that Fain’s public silence has driven many to take the side of Mock, Boyer, and the Monitor, who support an apolitical, austere vision of unionism.”

In October of 2024 UAWD passed a resolution, available on our website and reproduced in full below below, that calls for the replacement of Barofsky.

This resolution was passed at the October 2024 Annual Membership Meeting on October 13, 2024.

Unite All Workers for Democracy calls for the replacement of federal monitor Neil Barofsky because of his illegal attempt to intervene in UAW policy decisions. These acts are an explicit violation of his duties under the consent decree. His acts must be seen as an example of the government and the billionaire class working to undermine our union’s political independence and our right as a union to take whatever political positions our membership and elected leadership decide on democratically.

Our union would never allow a monitor, a government official, or a corporate CEO to interfere with our union’s right to reject a bad offer during contract bargaining. In fact, we would call out that interference as a form of corruption and fight it in the courts and on the shop floor. UAWD sees our right to democratically adopt political positions as equally important. This right, for example, enabled us to put time and resources toward fighting against the Right to Work law in Michigan and ultimately defeating this political attack against the labor movement. Our political independence plays just as crucial a role in winning strong contracts for UAW members as our bargaining independence, and we must be just as committed to fight to defend it.

Extensive reporting has revealed that Barofsky has exhibited a clear bias against the UAW’s position in support of a ceasefire in Gaza, which was adopted last December by an overwhelming vote of the International Executive Board. This bias is based on the monitor’s political beliefs, which are affecting, or create a perception of affecting, his actions as monitor. According to the American Bar Association standards for monitors, where there exists any factor that could bias or impair, or be perceived to bias and impair, a monitor’s judgment, objectivity or independence this serves as the basis for removal of the monitor.

Monitor Barofsky twice tried to dissuade President Fain and the IEB from upholding the position on Palestine and Israel’s war on Gaza, which has now killed over 40,000 Gazans, including thousands of children. Some estimates, including by the peer-reviewed medical journal The Lancet, put the number of fatalities closer to 200,000. The monitor’s undue pressure had a chilling effect on the IEB and thus affected its future decisions and actions.

On December 13, 2023, Barofsky contacted President Fain and urged him to rethink the union’s position calling for a ceasefire. In the call, he conflated protests against the atrocities being committed in Gaza with antisemitism. President Fain correctly answered Barofsky that the union’s resolution was in no way antisemitic, but simply an expression of the union’s desire for peace.

Monitor Barofsky did not stop there. In February 2024 he contacted the IEB again to apply pressure in opposition to the union’s call for a ceasefire. Barofsky attached a letter from the Anti-Defamation League to his email to the IEB that once again incorrectly conflated support for the call for peace in Gaza with antisemitism.

When the union did not renege on its position for a ceasefire in Gaza, a position shared by labor and progressive organizations across the U.S. and worldwide, Barofsky escalated his demands on the union and began to accuse the UAW of noncompliance. He issued a demand that the union supply 116,000 documents, many of which dealt with collective bargaining and policy decisions outside the scope of the monitor’s authority.

Barofsky has also exploited divisions that have emerged in the IEB, weaponizing complaints filed by Secretary Treasurer Mock and Vice President Boyer and publicly announcing investigations into President Fain regarding those complaints. He did this despite the clear basis for President Fain’s actions in the UAW Constitution.

Barofsky’s overreach must be seen in the context of attacks on UAW members and locals across the country, by government officials nationwide and the monitor himself, based on a knowingly false and manipulative conflation of anti-Zionism with antisemitism:

UAW Local 2325 has been attacked by a congressional probe intended to scare them and mire them in legal procedures. The local has also been attacked in the press multiple times. Anti-Zionist Jewish 2325 members have pushed back.

UAW Local 4811’s Unfair Labor Practice strike was stopped by an illegal injunction and members and other University of California students were attacked by counter-protestors and police.

UAW Local 7902’s Palestine Solidarity statement was falsely cited by the Monitor and the Anti-Defamation League as “antisemitic.” The monitor’s act of passing on a false claim, through a formal channel, was an early attempt to silence UAW leaders and members.

While the current focus of these attacks is on the issue of the union’s opposition to the genocide in Gaza, this takes place within the context of growing hostility by corporations and the government to the rebirth of class struggle unionism signified by President Fain and the UAW reform movement.

For over 40 years, the corporations benefited from the UAW’s adoption of a line of cooperation with management, leading to disastrous consequences for workers. Under the former leadership of the UAW, our members were subjected to wage and benefits tiers, elimination of pensions, and a deterioration of working conditions. The corruption in the union was a direct product of that class collaboration with the billionaire class. And because of the influence of the UAW, these policies penetrated the entire U.S. labor movement.

The election of UAW President Shawn Fain, a UAWD member, and the other leaders on our UAWD Members United slate has enabled us to begin reviving the proud class struggle tradition of the UAW and advancing the cause of international working-class solidarity. This was not what the business class hoped for or counted on. The stand-up strikes, the organizing of Volkswagen and the broader movement by our union to organize the South, and the militancy of UAW workers against the system’s complicity with genocide in Palestine, are threats to their class interests.

We remember how Ron Carey, after being elected president of the Teamsters in a democratic election with the aid of a federal monitor, was run out of office the next year by the government following the militant strike he led in 1997 against United Parcel Service to end tiers and the abuse of part-time workers.

Our message is: We won’t allow the federal monitor or any other government or corporate entity tamp down militancy and activism in our union. We defend our movement to build a union run by and accountable to its rank-and-file members. We defend our union’s right to stand firmly for a ceasefire in Gaza.

It’s time to replace the federal monitor due to his illegal interference in our union’s affairs.

We will keep up the fight for a return to the UAW’s militant tradition of class struggle and the union’s rightful place in an emerging international working-class movement.

title: Husiler: Suudi Arabistan, başkent Sana ve diğer bazı kentlere hava saldırıları düzenliyor
content:
Fotoğraf: Felton Davis / Wikimedia Comons (CC BY 2.0)

Yemen'deki Husilere bağlı haber ajansı SABA'da yer alan haberde, Suudi Arabistan'a ait olduğu savaş uçaklarının Sana'nın yanı sıra Saada, Taiz ve Amran'daki bazı bölgeleri hedef aldığı belirtildi.

Haberde, saldırıların hedef aldığı noktalar ile can ve mal kaybına ilişkin ayrıntı verilmedi.

Öte yandan Başkanlık Konseyi güçleri ülkenin güneybatısındaki Taiz vilayetinde Husilere ait mevzi ve toplanma noktalarına 27 hava saldırısı düzenlendiğini açıkladı.

Sözcü Albay Macid Abdullah en-Nezili, yaptığı yazılı açıklamada, hava kuvvetlerinin Taiz'deki cephe hatları boyunca Husi hedeflerine "27 hassas ve yoğun hava saldırısı" gerçekleştirdiğini belirtti.

Nezili, saldırılarda füze deposu, komuta ve kontrol merkezleri, ikmal ve silahlandırma noktaları, Husi unsurlarının toplandığı bölgeler ile askeri araçların hedef alındığını kaydetti.

Nezili, hava saldırılarının hedefleri doğrudan vurduğunu, onlarca askeri araç ve kapasitenin imha edildiğini ve çok sayıda Husi unsurunun öldürüldüğünü veya yaralandığını belirtti.

Suudi Arabistan liderliğindeki Arap Koalisyonu Sözcüsü Tuğgeneral Turki el-Maliki, X sosyal medya platformundaki hesabından yaptığı açıklamada, Hamis Muşayt ve Cazan bölgelerine fırlatılan insansız hava araçları (İHA) ve balistik füzelerin hava savunma sistemleriyle imha edildiğini açıklamıştı.

Tuğgeneral Maliki daha önce yaptığı açıklamada da, Husilerin iki gün önce Suudi Arabistan'ın Medine kentindeki Taybe Elektrik Santralini İHA ile hedef aldıklarını duyurmuştu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Fransa'daki lise öğrencilerinin eylemleri Belçika'ya sıçradı
content:
Belçika basınında yer alan haberlere göre, Fransa'da yaklaşık bir haftadır devam eden lise protestoları Belçika'ya sıçradı.

Liege'deki çeşitli ortaöğretim kurumlarında öğrenciler sabah saatlerinde derslerin başlamasını engelleyen eylemler yaptı.

Eylemlerden "Athenee de Fragnee", "Athenee Royal de Montegnee", "Institut Maria Goretti", "College Saint-Barthelemy", "Saint-Laurent", "Saint-Sepulcre" ve "Institut Marie-Therese"in de aralarında bulunduğu çok sayıda okul etkilendi.

Liege'nin Hors-Chateau bölgesindeki Institut Marie-Therese önünde durum zaman zaman gerginleşti, okulun önünde ateş yakıldı ve bölgeye çok sayıda polis sevk edildi.

Polis, bazı okulların önünde havai fişek türü patlayıcılar, yumurta, elma ve bariyerlerin fırlatıldığını ve çeşitli noktalarda hasar meydana geldiğini iddia etti.

Esneux, Vise, Angleur ve Soumagne beldelerindeki bazı okullarda da eylemler görüldü. Vise, Angleur ve Soumagne'da öğrenciler kısa süre sonra okullara dönerken, diğer bazı kurumlarda ise öğrenciler ve öğretmenlerin okula girişini engellemek amacıyla gözcü hatları oluşturuldu.

Polis ve yerel kaynaklar, eylemlerin öğretmenler ya da sendikalar tarafından değil, öğrenciler tarafından başlatılan spontane bir hareket olduğunu aktardı.

Öğrenciler, sınıflardaki öğrenci sayısının azaltılmasını, yeterli sayıda öğretmen görevlendirilmesini, öğrenci ve velilerin karar süreçlerinde daha fazla dinlenmesini ve eğitimin herkes için erişilebilir olmasını talep ediyor.

Öğrenciler ayrıca eğitim alanında alınacak kararların geleceklerini olumsuz etkilememesi gerektiğini savunuyor.

Olaylara ilişkin soruşturma açılırken, polis Liege kentinde 6 kişinin gözaltına alındığını açıkladı.

Liege'de yetkililer, yarın eğitime ara verildiğini duyurdu.

Valonya-Brüksel Federasyonu hükümeti Eğitim Bakanı Valerie Glatigny, öğrencilerin "bir araç olarak kullanıldığı" iddiasında bulunarak, eğitimde hiçbir önlemin onlara sağlanan desteği azaltmadığını savundu.

Glatigny, herkesin kararlara itiraz etme hakkı olduğunu ancak işin şiddete dönüşmemesi gerektiğini öne sürerek"Öğrencilerin sınıfa girmesini engellemek, polislere cisim atmak, okul dışından gelen kişilerin baskısı altında tahribat yapmak kabul edilebilir değildir" ifadesini kullandı.

Fransa'da ilk olarak Paris ve çevresinde yoğunlaşan öğrenci eylemleri, daha sonra ülkenin diğer bölgelerine yayıldı.

29 Eylül'de yüzlerce lise, protesto ve blokajlardan etkilenirken, bazı kentlerde öğrencilerle güvenlik güçleri arasında gerginlik yaşandı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.
