Em 17 de novembro, a esposa de Ramagem e as filhas chegaram a Miami, onde também ficaram no apartamento dos Martins de Mello. Antes disso, Rebeca Ramagem, que hoje concorre a uma vaga de deputada federal (PL-RJ), chegou a ser parada pela PF no aeroporto do Galeão, no Rio de Janeiro, e teve o celular e computadores apreendidos, mas conseguiu seguir viagem.




Para a PF, Cataratas, Priscila e Celso desempenharam “papel de protagonismo na manutenção clandestina de Alexandre Ramagem em Miami/EUA, porquanto estão viabilizando a sua moradia em condomínio luxo, além de estarem auxiliando o foragido a ludibriar as autoridades americanas com documentos falsos a fim de obter a chamada driver license (carteira de motorista)”.




A revelação complica ainda mais o grupo ligado a Eduardo Bolsonaro nos Estados Unidos que atua em lobby na construção de ataques ao STF e contra a investigação sobre o 8 de janeiro de 2023. Desde que chegou aos EUA, Alexandre Ramagem tem apresentado o programa da Revista Timeline no Youtube, ao lado de Allan dos Santos, onde Eduardo é convidado frequente. Ramagem também tem participado de eventos com a extrema direita norte-americana junto com o filho 02 de Jair Bolsonaro.




O financiamento de Eduardo nos EUA tem sido investigado desde a revelação que ele teria orientado a captação e uso de recursos do filme Dark Horse, financiado por doação do ex-banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro através de uma empresa 

acusada

 de lavagem de dinheiro, a Entre Investimentos. 




Agora, a manutenção dos Ramagem na Flórida passa a estar associada a pessoa ligada a outro grupo criminoso, investigado por uma série de crimes ambientais.




Crimes contra os Yanomami e a Amazônia




Rodrigo Martins de Mello foi condenado em fevereiro deste ano a 16 anos e sete meses de prisão por liderar uma organização criminosa responsável pela mineração ilegal de cassiterita e ouro dentro da Terra Indígena Yanomami. Rodrigo Cataratas era responsável pela logística, com uma frota de helicópteros adulterados que faziam o trânsito do pessoal, de combustível e dos minerais. Seu filho Celso também foi condenado a oito anos de prisão por atuar na gestão financeira e logística do grupo. Ambos estão recorrendo em liberdade.




Cataratas foi também denunciado por financiar a destruição de uma caminhonete Hillux pertencente ao Ibama e por patrocinar a invasão da superintendência de Roraima na tentativa de queimar um helicóptero do órgão como retaliação a operações de combate ao garimpo em 2021. Além disso, ele também foi denunciado criminalmente e responde a uma ação civil pública que pede reparação de danos e multa, dentro da Operação Forja de Efestos, por conta da extração e comercialização de cassiterita proveniente de terra indígena.




Cataratas, Celso e Priscila também são investigados pelo STF por terem dado apoio à fuga de Ramagem para a Guiana. Celso chegou a ser preso em Manaus em dezembro do ano passado, mas hoje responde em liberdade, com uma tornozeleira eletrônica. Procurado, o STF afirmou que o caso está sob sigilo e não poderia passar mais detalhes. 




“O garimpo geralmente é uma organização criminosa que, em regra, trabalha com os familiares. O Cataratas trabalha também nesse sentido: os filhos trabalham junto”, explica o procurador Alisson Marugal, do Ministério Público Federal (MPF) de Roraima.




Ele detalha que a atuação da família Martins de Mello na exploração da terra Yanomami levou não apenas à destruição de grandes partes da floresta, mas também à deterioração da vida e da saúde dos indígenas. Aquelas cenas que o mundo todo acompanhou na TV, de crianças desnutridas sendo hospitalizadas em situação de emergência circularam pelo mundo. Este foi o fruto mais visível do garimpo ilegal, que inclui corrupção, aliciamento de indígenas, violação sexual de adolescentes e mulheres e a transmissão de doenças. Na época, 

reportagem

 do site Sumaúma mostrou que 570 crianças indígenas morreram por doenças evitáveis entre 2018 e 2022.




“O garimpo alcança pontos mais distantes do território, nessas comunidades ainda mais sensíveis, mais desprotegidas, de recente contato, mais vulneráveis do ponto de vista epidemiológico, e toma conta do território muito rápido”, explica Marugal. Para a exploração de cassiterita, na qual se especializaram os Martins de Mello, o garimpo desvia água dos rios e destroi suas encostas. “O garimpeiro, quando chega na terra indígena, paga para deixar que eles instalem o garimpo. E aí vem uma dependência também dos indígenas, que passam a trabalhar nos garimpos de cassiterita e deixam de cultivar a sua roça’’, diz.




“Destruíram todos os rios, corromperam os indígenas, fecharam postos de saúde. A situação de segurança pública se deteriora rapidamente, os profissionais de saúde não vão mais às comunidades. As crianças começam a ficar doentes… foi o caos nesse período entre 2021 e 2022”, lembra o procurador.




Atualmente, o MPF em Roraima investiga um potencial genocídio do povo indígena Yanomami a partir da invasão deliberada de suas terras e a ação do garimpo entre 2021 e 2022. Ao menos 23 aeronaves foram empregadas no esquema de extração ilegal de ouro e cassiterita no território.




Meses antes de ser condenado, Rodrigo Cataratas, que chegou a 

anunciar

 que concorreria ao Senado (PRD-RR), mudou-se para a Guiana, onde segue operando no garimpo. Na época, ele 

pagou um publieditorial

 no jornal Folha de Boa Vista anunciando que, “com coragem e ação”, estava levando sua retroescavadeira para o país vizinho. 

Segundo

 a Repórter Brasil, ele chegou a anunciar um projeto em parceria com o país, com investimento de 10 milhões de dólares, levando a 

um alerta

 da organização local Rede Anticorrupção na Guiana. 

Seu Instagram

 tem como foto de perfil uma imagem abraçado a Jair Bolsonaro com a mensagem “anistia já”. 




Apagando os rastros




Tanto Alexandre Ramagem quanto Rodrigo Martins de Mello admitem que se conhecem. Eles estiveram juntos em 31 de março de 2025, ocasião em que Cataratas postou uma 

imagem

 nas redes: “Tive a honra de receber em Boa Vista o deputado federal Alexandre Ramagem, grande aliado do presidente Jair Bolsonaro e defensor incansável da liberdade e da soberania nacional”, escreveu Cataratas.
















Post de 31 de março de 2025 em que Cataratas (à direita) celebra encontro com Ramagem em Boa Vista




Ele negou, entretanto, que a família tenha auxiliado na fuga. “Nos últimos dias, meu nome apareceu ligado ao caso do deputado Alexandre Ramagem”, 

escreveu

 em novembro do ano passado nas redes sociais, atribuindo a notícia à “perseguição” à direita. “Quando o Ramagem esteve comigo, ele não tinha qualquer condenação ou impedimento legal que o proibisse de sair do Brasil.”




Por sua vez, em vídeo 

postado

 no Instagram depois da prisão de Celso por facilitar a fuga, Ramagem afirmou que não conhecia “uma tal de” Priscila e nem Celso. “Prenderam um jovem, um rapaz, que só me conheceu quando eu já estava nos EUA. Eu não conhecia no Brasil. Inclusive esse rapaz é americano”.




Uma foto obtida pela 

Pública,

 que segundo investigadores estava no celular da Priscila, desmente a versão de Ramagem sobre não conhecer os familiares de Rodrigo Cataratas. Trata-se de uma imagem sua, sorridente, em um prédio público na Guiana em 10 de setembro de 2025, provavelmente em um posto de imigração. A foto foi tirada um dia depois de Ramagem chegar à Guiana e um dia antes de partir para os EUA, e segundo a PF teria sido tirada por Rodrigo Cataratas.




Celso de Mello tem cidadania dos Estados Unidos e tem, inclusive, registro de eleitor. Por conta disso, a família “notificou” o consulado dos EUA, 

segundo

 Rodrigo publicou em suas redes.
















Foto de Ramagem que, segundo os investigadores, estava no celular da filha de Cataratas




Ramagem e sua família tiveram que sair às pressas do apartamento de luxo da família de Cataratas em Miami no final de novembro de 2025. No dia 19 daquele mês, Rebeca e Alexandre foram flagrados 

pela coluna do jornalista Guilherme Amado

 caminhando tranquilamente no condomínio sob o sol da Flórida, trajando roupas esportivas.
















Foto publicada no site PlatôBR mostra Ramagem, foragido, e sua mulher Rebeca no condomínio em Miami




Dois dias depois, em 21 de novembro, Priscila teria enviado uma nova mensagem à gerente do La Sole Mia, desta vez tentando dissociar o nome do seu marido da família Ramagem. A anotação sobre a carta foi encontrada no bloco de notas do celular de Priscila.










 




“No meu apartamento localizado no Sole Mia, tem atualmente um visitante, Sr Alexandre Ramagem. No entanto, eu descobri através da imprensa que este indivíduo não tem permissão de deixar o Brasil por causa de questões judiciais. Não consegui contato com ele para pedir que ele saia do apartamento. Portanto, para evitar quaisquer problemas para o condomínio ou para mim mesmo, eu peço que o Condomínio notifique-o IMEDIATAMENTE da minha determinação de que ele deixe minha propriedade. Sinceramente, Rodrigo Martins de Mello”.













Desta vez, a carta foi assinada pelo próprio Rodrigo. As duas comunicações ao Sole Mia, contraditórias entre si, revelam um cuidado de Rodrigo Cataratas em relação ao condomínio e às autoridades norte-americanas. Afinal, pelos diálogos fica claro que seu filho Celso tinha acesso direto à Ramagem.




Para a PF, Rodrigo e Priscila redigiram o texto após a imprensa nacional vincular o seu apartamento à fuga de Ramagem como medida de precaução.




A vida da família de Cataratas na Flórida




Conforme apurou a 

Agência Pública

, a família de Rodrigo Martins de Mello está frequentemente na Flórida.




Na época em que Alexandre Ramagem chegou nos Estados Unidos, seu filho Celso e a esposa Mariana Poerschke de Mello estavam morando em Coral Bay, subúrbio a menos de uma hora de Miami. A mulher, que é influenciadora digital, chegou a promover eventos de consultoria em marketing nos EUA e conquistou o status de cidadã legal em fevereiro de 2025. 




A realidade mudou no final de 2025 – depois do apoio aos Ramagem. Em novembro, Rodrigo Cataratas 

anunciou

 que seu filho estava de volta ao Brasil. No mês seguinte, em 15 de dezembro, Celso foi preso em Manaus por facilitar a fuga do ex-diretor da Abin. Questionado, o STF não pode compartilhar informações sobre o pedido de prisão e o andamento das investigações, pois o inquérito está em sigilo.




Poucos dias antes, Mariana já havia anunciado a seus seguidores que a família estava se mudando de volta para o Brasil em uma publicação em parceria com uma consultoria de transporte internacional de animais de estimação, responsável pelo transporte do cachorro do casal, um pit bull caramelo, à Boa Vista.




Post da mulher de Celso, em dezembro, anuncia transporte do cachorro dos EUA para o Brasil




Até meados deste ano, no entanto, ficaram entre Miami e Boa Vista, segundo apurou a 

Pública

. A casa em que ambos moravam foi vendida por 519 mil dólares em maio (aproximadamente R$ 2,6 milhões na cotação da época), segundo 

classificados de imóveis

.




Hoje grávida do segundo filho, a influenciadora vive em uma mansão recém-reformada em Boa Vista enquanto o marido cumpre medidas cautelares – nas postagens no Instagram é possível ver fotos de Celso usando uma tornozeleira eletrônica.
















Durante chá revelação da gravidez de sua esposa em Boa Vista, Celso de Mello aparece com tornozeleira eletrônica




Nos EUA, Ramagem segue fazendo política com Bolsonaros




Mais do que fugir da lei brasileira, a ida de Alexandre Ramagem aos EUA representa a continuidade de seus atos contra a democracia do Brasil.




Condenado a 16 anos de prisão por tentativa de golpe de Estado, o ex-diretor da Abin segue disseminando desinformação sobre as eleições e ataques a instituições brasileiras do território americano.




Desde dezembro do ano passado, ele apresenta o programa Conversa TimeLine ao lado do também foragido Allan dos Santos. Nele, frequentemente Ramagem nega que tenha havido tentativa de golpe de estado no Brasil e 

afirma

 que o país vive em uma “ditadura da toga”.




A ofensiva não se limita a publicações nas redes sociais. Desde que chegou aos EUA, em setembro de 2025, Ramagem já se encontrou ao menos quatro vezes com Eduardo Bolsonaro e Paulo Figueiredo, neto do ditador João Figueiredo e ex-apresentador da Jovem Pan que tem liderado ao lado de Eduardo Bolsonaro o lobby por retaliações da Casa Branca contra o Brasil.




Em março, ele participou de evento fechado organizado pela think tank de extrema direita Heritage Foundation. O Miami Security Forum contou com a presença de políticos republicanos como a deputada 

Maria Elvira Salazar

, aliada de Figueiredo e Eduardo – Figueiredo chegou a fazer doação para sua campanha, 

segundo revelou

 a 

Pública

.




Na ocasião, o empresário participou de uma mesa intitulada “Realinhamento político das Américas: implicações para o futuro da segurança hemisférica”, ao lado de congressistas do Chile, Colômbia e Honduras. “Falamos de PCC, CV, narcoterrorismo e até Foro de São Paulo”, revelou em post no X. O evento 

influenciou

 a política externa de Donald Trump para países latino-americanos que levou à inclusão das facções brasileiras no rol de organizações terroristas.




No mesmo mês, Ramagem e Allan fizeram uma cobertura ao vivo do CPAC, sigla em inglês para Conferência de Ação Política Conservadora, evento que reuniu líderes da extrema direita mundial em Dallas, no Texas. O cadastro garantiu acesso dos influenciadores a palestrantes e organizadores do evento, entre eles o Eduardo Bolsonaro e o candidato à presidência Flávio Bolsonaro.







Em abril, depois de ser detido pelo ICE, serviço de imigração dos Estados Unidos, Alexandre Ramagem recebeu mais uma visita de Eduardo Bolsonaro em Miami. A detenção de Ramagem, que durou dois dias, foi motivada por uma infração de trânsito e foi revertida com 

ajuda direta da Casa Branca

.




Depois disso, Rebeca Ramagem foi anunciada como candidata a deputada federal pelo PL no Rio de Janeiro. Sua campanha tem como mote a anistia aos condenados pela tentativa de golpe de estado de 8 de janeiro, em especial, seu marido. No lançamento da candidatura de Flávio Bolsonaro à Presidência, na praia de Copacabana, a candidata enviou totens de papelão dela e do marido em tamanho real – exibidos pela esposa de Flávio Bolsonaro – e fez camisetas estampadas com a frase “Tragam a família Ramagem de volta, façam Justiça”, exibida pelo próprio candidato à Presidência.
















Mulher de Flávio Bolsonaro posa com totens da candidata Rebeca Ramagem e do marido




A campanha, que recebeu R$ 1,5 milhão do fundo partidário do PL, 

usou recursos para contratar associados de Alexandre Ramagem

, entre eles ex-funcionários de seu gabinete na Câmara dos Deputados que foram desligados após a cassação de seu mandato, e a irmã do influenciador Allan dos Santos, seu parceiro de bancada no canal Revista TimeLine.

author: Unknown
title: Ephéméride des luttes : 28 septembre
content:
Ce 28 septembre marque un jalon important de l'éphéméride des luttes : la constitution de la première internationale, qui engendrera plus ou moins logiquement et capillairement toutes les actions qui s'ensuivent.




1864 :

 A Londres, vers St. Martin's Hall, congrès constitutif de la Première Internationale.




1879 :

 A Marseille, naissance au 29 rue Navarin d'Alexandre Marius Jacob, cambrioleur anarchiste bien connu.




1883 :

 A Rüdesheim-sur-le-Rhin en Allemagne, attentat manqué des anarchistes Emil Küchler, Franz Reinhold Rupsch et August Reinsdorf contre l'empereur Guillaume et les princes qui inauguraient un monument à la gloire des armées allemandes.




1943 :

 - Au Danemark, les militant-e-s anti-nazis dans la clandestinité organisent le passage de la population juive vers la Suède.




 A Naples, c'est la deuxième journée de l'insurrection de Naples, qui au bout de 4 jours en fera la première grande ville à se libérer de l'occupant nazi, sans l'aide des Alliés.




1958 :

 En France, une nouvelle constitution est approuvée : c'est la naissance de la cinquième République.




1973 :

 Aux USA, le Weather Underground fait sauter la branche Amérique Latine de l'entreprise ITT pour son rôle dans le coup d'état au Chili 

17 jours plus tôt

.




 

 

 

 




1975 :

 A Caterham en Angleterre, une bombe de l'IRA explose, faisant quelques dégâts matériels.




1977 :

 - A Madrid, les GRAPO (Groupes de résistance antifasciste du premier octobre) abattent un capitaine de police.




 A Florence, des membres des Comités Communistes de Combat incendient trois agences immobilières qui spéculent en laissant des appartements vides pour faire monter les loyers à des prix exorbitants pour les pauvres.




1978 :

 - A Rome, un militant sympathisant communiste, Ivo Zini, est assassiné par un groupe néofasciste clandestin, les NAR.




 A Turin, les Brigades Rouges tirent dans les jambes du directeur de l'usine Lancia de Chivasso. Si l'intention n'était que de le blesser aux jambes, celui-ci mourra quelques heures plus tard de ses blessures.




1998 :

 A Londres, premier festival Queeruption, qui ramène des centaines d'anarcho-queers dans la ville.




1999 :

 A Plévin en Bretagne, un commando de huit militants d'ETA cambriole l'entreprise Titanite et repart avec plus de huit tonnes de dynamite et 6000 détonateurs.




2000 :

 A Jérusalem, la visite d'Ariel Sharon marque le début de la Seconde Intifada.




2014 :

 A Hong Kong, dans le cadre du mouvement Occupy, des milliers de personnes occupent les quartiers généraux du gouvernement. La police charge et fait usage de lacrymogènes mais énormément de gens restent sur place.




 

 

 

 




Voir aussi 

l'éphéméride anarchiste

 du 28 septembre.

author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: Imperial Nostalgia: History, Sovereignty, and the Unfinished Work of Decolonization in the Horn of Africa
content:
History in the Horn of Africa is rarely allowed to remain history. An ancient civilization becomes evidence of modern sovereignty. A medieval dynasty becomes proof of national continuity. Territory incorporated during one political era is later remembered as though it had always belonged to the state that governed it.




This habit has become especially visible as the Red Sea has returned to Ethiopian political discourse. Ethiopia is landlocked and has obvious economic reasons to seek dependable maritime trade. But there is a fundamental difference between negotiating the use of a port and claiming that a neighboring country possesses territory that properly belongs to Ethiopia. That distinction disappears when Assab is described as a “lost Ethiopian port.”




Ethiopia did not lose a sovereign port in 1993. Eritrea recovered sovereignty over territory that had been incorporated into Ethiopia after the violation and eventual termination of an internationally established federal arrangement. To describe this as Ethiopia “losing the sea” begins the story at the moment of Ethiopian possession and ignores how that possession came about.




This is what I mean by imperial nostalgia.




Imperial nostalgia is not merely admiration for emperors or attachment to an earlier age. It is a way of remembering political space. Territory once incorporated into an empire is remembered not simply as territory once governed, but as territory that naturally belonged there. Incorporation becomes ownership, ownership becomes entitlement, and independence can then be remembered as national loss.




Christopher Clapham’s notion of an Ethiopian “manifest destiny” is useful at the margins of this argument, although I invoke him cautiously and not to validate Ethiopian historical claims. The phrase captures a mentality in which expansion can stop looking like expansion when incorporation is presented as the fulfillment of history. Manifest destiny looks forward. Imperial nostalgia looks backward and imagines that a geography produced through expansion was the natural order all along.




The deeper problem is the projection of modern states backward into political worlds that did not organize themselves according to contemporary borders. Aksum is an obvious example. Its political and commercial world crossed territories that are now divided between Eritrea and Ethiopia and formed part of a much larger Red Sea system. 

UNESCO’s account of Aksum

 describes an ancient civilization. It does not describe a modern territorial state possessing a contemporary claim to the Red Sea.




Calling Aksum simply “ancient Ethiopia” imports the political geography of today into antiquity. Calling it “ancient Eritrea” would make the same mistake. Civilizations, languages, religions, trading networks, and archaeological landscapes regularly cross the boundaries of modern states. Shared history does not create shared sovereignty.




I explored this problem more fully in 

There Is No Timeless Eritrea or Ethiopia

. The point is not to diminish the history of either country. It is to stop asking ancient civilizations to perform the work of modern territorial law. Aksum should be studied as Aksum rather than recruited into a contemporary argument over Assab.




Richard Reid examined this problem directly in 

The Trans-Mereb Experience: Perceptions of the Historical Relationship between Eritrea and Ethiopia

. Reid is useful because he is skeptical of efforts on either side to recruit antiquity into modern nationalism. The same history can be arranged to prove a supposedly eternal Ethiopia or, in the opposite direction, an Eritrea with no meaningful historical relationship to communities south of the Mereb. Neither approach is good history.




Even the word Ethiopia should make us cautious. The Greek term 

Aithiopia

 did not refer neatly to the bounded territorial state called Ethiopia today. Recognizing this does not make modern Ethiopia less legitimate. It simply acknowledges that political names, communities, and territorial states change over time.




Eritrea should be approached in exactly the same way. Fred Halliday, writing in 1971 while the Eritrean war was still underway, acknowledged in 

“The Fighting in Eritrea”

 that Eritrea in its modern territorial form had been defined under European colonialism. That fact does not weaken Eritrean sovereignty. It places Eritrea within the history of modern Africa.




Most African states inherited territorial forms created or consolidated during European colonial rule. Political identities, institutions, and nationalisms subsequently developed within those territories. The colonial origin of a boundary does not give a neighboring state the right to erase it. Modern Eritrea did not exist from antiquity in its present territorial form. Neither did modern Ethiopia.




My late friend Professor 

Okbazghi Yohannes

 identified an important part of the problem in what he called the “mythical image of Ethiopia.” Adwa and Ethiopia’s resistance to European conquest gave the country an exceptional place in African and Black political consciousness. But that image also made it difficult for many outsiders to contemplate another possibility: that an African state celebrated for resisting European imperialism could itself exercise domination over another people.




John Markakis approached the question from another direction. In 

The Nationalist Revolution in Eritrea

, he took Eritrean nationalism seriously without pretending that an Eritrean state had existed eternally. Eritrean nationalism developed historically. The struggle over Eritrea’s political future after Italian rule and Ethiopia’s determination to absorb the territory helped accelerate that nationalism.




There is no reason for Eritreans to answer a mythology of eternal Ethiopia with a mythology of eternal Eritrea. Nations are not artificial simply because they have histories.




The late Elleni Centime Zeleke’s 

Ethiopia in Theory

 makes a similar point from within Ethiopian political history. Her account of the student movement shows young Ethiopians in the 1960s and early 1970s arguing not simply about how Ethiopia should be governed, but about what Ethiopia was, how its nationalities related to the state, and what self-determination meant. There was no single Ethiopia moving unchanged through history. There were competing ideas of Ethiopia.




This should also make us cautious about treating Tewodros, Yohannes, and Menelik as though they were successive emperors of a completed modern nation-state. Their authority was constructed through dynastic rivalry, warfare, negotiation, regional loyalties, and expansion. Under Menelik in particular, the state expanded substantially southward, southwestward, and eastward. The 

Kebra Nagast

 and the Solomonic tradition mattered enormously in legitimizing rulers and organizing political memory, but genealogy is not territorial law.




Federation, Annexation, and the Red Sea




The history of Eritrea’s federation with Ethiopia becomes much clearer when the language is precise. 

United Nations General Assembly Resolution 390(V)

 did not transfer Eritrea to Ethiopia as an ordinary province. It established an autonomous Eritrean unit federated with Ethiopia. Eritreans themselves disagreed sharply about their political future. Independence, union, federation, and partition all had supporters.




The federal arrangement was also shaped by the strategic interests of the United States and Britain. The American documentary record is unusually revealing. A 

1951 State Department document

 records Washington’s decision to give strong support to federation because the arrangement served American policy and American security interests in Eritrea. The United States helped develop the federation formula and secured British support for it.




One of the central American interests was Kagnew Station in Asmara. A 

1971 United States government study of the Horn of Africa

 described Kagnew as a major determinant of the scale of American involvement in Ethiopia. Washington’s relationship with Haile Selassie and its strategic presence in Eritrea were therefore part of the political environment in which the federation was created and later undermined.




The erosion of Eritrean autonomy was visible even to American officials. A 

United States policy paper from the late 1950s

 acknowledged that Eritrean autonomy had been gradually reduced. Eritreans understood where this process was heading, and armed resistance began in 

1961

, while the federal arrangement formally still existed.




That chronology matters. Eritreans did not suddenly take up arms after an ordinary Ethiopian province decided that it wanted to separate. Armed resistance began while the federal arrangement was being eroded and violated. In 1962, Haile Selassie completed the process by annexing Eritrea.




The terminology is not simply an Eritrean interpretation written after independence. A 

November 1962 memorandum by Robert Komer at the United States National Security Council

 referred directly to the “formal annexation of Eritrea.” Another 

State Department communication from November 1962

 stated that Washington could not commend Ethiopia for dissolving the federation.




The documentary trail matters because it strips away much of the later mythology. A political entity whose modern territorial boundaries had been defined during European colonial rule was placed in a federal relationship with Ethiopia. That arrangement was progressively violated. Eritrean armed resistance began in 1961. Ethiopia formally annexed Eritrea in 1962. The resistance continued for thirty devastating years.




John Franklin Campbell was already describing this as 

“Rumblings Along the Red Sea: The Eritrean Question”

 in 

Foreign Affairs

 in 1970, while Haile Selassie still ruled. Halliday’s 

“The Fighting in Eritrea”

, published the following year, is especially important because he was writing when nobody knew how the war would end. He examined the erosion of Eritrean autonomy, Ethiopian rule, armed resistance, and the strategic importance of Eritrea and the Red Sea to Ethiopia.




Halliday did not require Eritreans to prove that an Eritrean republic had existed in antiquity. The legitimacy of the Eritrean struggle did not depend on discovering an ancient Eritrean political entity whose borders resembled those that later became internationally recognized. That is an important corrective to the way the argument is often conducted today.




The Eritrean case was also being developed publicly during the liberation struggle itself. In 1978, the Association of Eritrean Students in North America and the Association of Eritrean Women in North America published 

In Defence of the Eritrean Revolution: Against Ethiopian Social Chauvinists

. Its Marxist language belongs unmistakably to its period, but the volume matters because it shows Eritreans constructing an extensive intellectual defense of independence while the military outcome remained uncertain.




After thirty years of devastating war, the entity incorporated into Ethiopia regained sovereignty. Ethiopia did not possess a timeless sovereign coastline that suddenly disappeared in 1993. Eritrea regained the territory that had been annexed, including Massawa, Assab, and its Red Sea coastline.




Ethiopia lost what it had annexed. It did not lose what it had legitimately owned.




Assab makes the contemporary problem particularly clear. Calling it Ethiopia’s “lost port” contains an entire historical argument in two words. It assumes that Ethiopia legitimately possessed Assab and that Eritrean independence took something Ethiopian away. But Ethiopia did not lose Assab in 1993. Eritrea recovered Assab together with the rest of the territory that had been incorporated into Ethiopia.




This is more than a disagreement over language. Once incorporation is treated as ownership, independence begins to look like dispossession.




The late Ethiopian international lawyer 

Dereje Zeleke Mekonnen

 understood the distinction. Dereje was not an Eritrean nationalist. He vigorously defended Ethiopian interests when he believed international law supported them. Yet in a 2019 interview published under the unusually direct headline 

“No way to make Assab part of Ethiopia”

, he rejected efforts to transform Ethiopia’s maritime interests into territorial ownership.




Assab can be enormously important to Ethiopia without belonging to Ethiopia. Commercial interest and sovereign title are different things.




The years immediately after Eritrean independence demonstrate the point particularly well. Ethiopia continued to use Assab extensively and also used Massawa. The 

1993 Transit and Port Services Agreement

 designated both ports for Ethiopian transit and exempted Ethiopian transit goods from Eritrean taxes and customs duties, although port and shipping services carried charges. The 

International Monetary Fund

 subsequently described Assab as a “free port for Ethiopia.”




Ethiopian use of Assab and Eritrean sovereignty were entirely compatible. What Ethiopia later lost was not sovereign territory. It lost a political relationship and commercial arrangements that had allowed extensive use of Eritrean ports. A country can lose favorable commercial arrangements without losing territory that belonged to it.




The experience of Bolivia and Chile provides a useful comparison precisely because the history is different. Bolivia actually possessed an internationally recognized Pacific coastline and lost it following the War of the Pacific. It eventually took the dispute to the 

International Court of Justice

, arguing that Chile had assumed a legal obligation to negotiate sovereign access to the ocean.




The Court rejected the claim in 2018. It did not deny Bolivia’s strong interest in reaching the Pacific. It found that the diplomatic history before it had not created the legal obligation Bolivia claimed. The comparison should not be pushed too far, but one distinction is illuminating. Bolivia actually lost internationally recognized sovereign coastline. Ethiopia did not lose Assab in that sense. Eritrea recovered territory that Ethiopia had annexed.




The legal settlement after the 1998–2000 Ethiopia–Eritrea war makes the point even stronger. Both governments submitted their boundary to binding international adjudication before the 

Eritrea–Ethiopia Boundary Commission

, whose members included some of the most distinguished international lawyers of their generation.




The Commission’s 

2002 boundary decision

 examined treaties, state conduct, and competing territorial claims in enormous detail. Badme was disputed. Zalambessa, Irob, Bure, and other areas were disputed. Assab was not.




Ethiopia did not present a claim to Assab to the Commission, nor did it ask the Commission to award it a sovereign corridor to the Red Sea. This deserves far more attention than it normally receives. After a devastating interstate war, Ethiopia contested comparatively small pieces of territory before some of the world’s most accomplished international jurists. It fought an international legal battle over Badme. It did not fight one over Assab.




The contemporary Prosperity Party narrative therefore has to be understood against this history. If Ethiopia were simply seeking cheaper and more dependable maritime trade, there would be little reason for alarm. Landlocked countries negotiate transit and port agreements throughout the world, and Ethiopia itself has extensive experience doing so.




The problem begins when a commercial question is transformed into a territorial story. Assab becomes a “lost port.” Ethiopia’s period of control over Eritrea is treated as evidence that the previous political geography was somehow more authentic than the sovereign order that followed Eritrean independence.




That reverses the history of annexation and resistance. Eritrean independence did not strip Ethiopia of territory it had legitimately possessed from time immemorial. It ended Ethiopian control over a political entity that had been federated with Ethiopia, progressively absorbed, formally annexed, and eventually regained after thirty years of resistance.




To describe that outcome as Ethiopia’s loss is to narrate Eritrean liberation from the perspective of the state that lost its empire.




The Prosperity Party does not need to declare openly that it wants to restore an empire for imperial nostalgia to become politically dangerous. The work can be done through political language. Annexation becomes ownership. Independence becomes loss. A neighboring coastline becomes an inheritance. Territorial revision can then be presented as restoration rather than expansion.




This also belongs to a broader political story. In 

The Messiah and the Crowd

, I examined the extraordinary investment in Abiy Ahmed as an individual and the dangers of substituting charismatic leadership for institutions.




The Red Sea narrative cannot be entirely separated from Ethiopia’s internal crisis. A government facing deep fragmentation at home can turn political attention outward and present territorial restoration as a national project. Meanwhile, the consequences are reshaping relationships throughout the Horn. In 

Tsimdo and the Changing Politics of the Horn

, I examined the striking cooperation emerging among former enemies whose differences remain profound but who increasingly regard Abiy’s government as a common threat.




Why Borders Matter




International law matters precisely because the history of the Horn can be mobilized almost without limit. Which period should determine sovereignty? Which kingdom counts? Which conquest produces legitimate title? Which emperor, language, migration, or previous political association should determine a modern boundary? There is no neutral historical answer to these questions.




African leaders understood this danger early. The 

OAU’s 1964 Cairo resolution

 did not preserve inherited boundaries because colonialism had produced fair borders. It preserved them because reopening every African frontier according to competing historical claims risked turning territorial conflict into a permanent feature of postcolonial politics.




Judge 

Abdulqawi Ahmed Yusuf

 has examined the particular African approach to inherited boundaries. The precise legal terminology matters to specialists, but the underlying political insight is straightforward. Decolonization could not produce a workable continental order if every historical empire, migration, kingdom, cultural relationship, or earlier period of administration could become grounds for reopening sovereignty.




That principle protects Eritrea, but it also protects Ethiopia. If ancient association, former imperial administration, or cultural affinity were enough to reopen sovereignty, modern Ethiopia itself would become vulnerable to historical claims arising from the many processes through which its territory was assembled. History cannot be decisive when it enlarges a state and suddenly become irrelevant when the same reasoning could fragment it.




This leads to a distinction between recognition and acceptance. Ethiopia legally recognizes Eritrea. The two countries have exchanged ambassadors, entered agreements, fought one another as sovereign states, and submitted their boundary to international adjudication. There is no serious legal uncertainty about Eritrean statehood.




Political acceptance asks for something more. It means accepting that a neighboring political community exists permanently and equally, whether or not one approves of its government, agrees with its historical narrative, or regards some part of its territory as economically desirable. A neighbor does not become provisional because its existence is inconvenient.




This may be part of the unfinished work of decolonization in the Horn. Decolonization is normally described as something European empires had to undergo. But European withdrawal did not automatically remove imperial habits of thought from African politics. A state can have resisted European conquest while also possessing its own history of expansion and incorporation. Those facts do not cancel one another.




The historical record therefore does not require us to choose between competing claims to antiquity. There were kingdoms, empires, political communities, colonial boundaries, federations, annexations, nationalist movements, wars, and eventually internationally recognized states. Modern sovereignty begins from that complicated history rather than pretending it never happened.




Rejecting imperial nostalgia does not require Eritreans to manufacture an ancient territorial claim of their own. Eritrea does not need an ancient republic to justify its sovereignty. Its modern territorial form developed through the same broad historical processes that produced much of contemporary Africa.




Nor does Ethiopia require its own coastline in order to prosper. Ethiopia needs dependable maritime trade. Eritrea needs economic opportunity. Djibouti depends heavily on regional commerce, while Somalia needs stability and investment. Ports can be used without being owned. Railways can cross sovereign boundaries without erasing them. Economic integration does not require territorial incorporation.




The alternative is an argument without a natural endpoint. One side invokes an ancient kingdom, another invokes an emperor, another points to cultural affinity, and another cites a period of previous rule. Nearly every society in the Horn can enter that contest, and none can settle modern sovereignty through it.




Africa’s postcolonial settlement offered a harder but more workable principle. It did not require Africans to forget history or pretend inherited boundaries were fair. It required them to stop treating history as an endless source of territorial title.




Historical attachment does not create ownership. Civilizational memory is not a deed.




The challenge is not to abandon history. It is to stop forcing history to perform political errands. We can study Aksum without turning it into a contemporary territorial claim. We can acknowledge that Europeans defined the territorial unit called Eritrea without pretending this makes Eritrean sovereignty provisional. We can examine Ethiopian expansion without denying the legitimacy of modern Ethiopia.




We can also acknowledge what the more recent historical record shows. In 1993, Eritrea regained the territorial entity that Ethiopia had annexed, including its Red Sea coastline. To describe that as Ethiopia “losing the sea” is to tell the history of liberation from the viewpoint of the power that lost its empire.




The Prosperity Party’s present rhetoric risks doing precisely that. It takes the political geography of an earlier imperial order and presents its restoration as historical entitlement. That is not simply nostalgia for the past. It is imperial nostalgia.




Answering it does not require historical amnesia. It requires sovereign acceptance.




–




This article was first published by Democracy in Africa

The post 

Imperial Nostalgia: History, Sovereignty, and the Unfinished Work of Decolonization in the Horn of Africa

 first appeared on 

The Elephant

.

author: Unknown
title: Rencontre avec Sandeep Bakshi sur Frontières queer
content:
Jeudi 15 octobre à 19h30, rencontre avec Sandeep Bakshi pour la sortie de son livre Frontières queer, sexualité, colonialité, décolonialité. La rencontre sera animée par Zaid du collectif sud-asiatique/Brown antiraciste.




 

 

 

 




Le queer est-il seulement occidental

 

? Conçu au cœur même des Empires, son lexique est-il utile loin des métropoles et logiques coloniales

 

? Dans cet ouvrage, Sandeep Bakshi remet en question les généalogies admises du queer pour échapper aux instrumentalisations et aux normalisations dont il est l'objet.




Partant de pratiques et d'analyses des Suds, ce livre montre que, si les études et le militantisme queer ont produit des formes de pensée radicales, elles ne sont pas immunisées contre les a priori culturels, sociaux et raciaux. Le queer, lui aussi, a sa colonialité. Dès lors, c'est en adoptant une perspective décoloniale que le queer retrouvera toute la vigueur de son insurrection initiale, pour semer à nouveau le trouble.

title: Sortie de la 16e édition du schéma de l'extrême droite française par la Horde
content:
Dans cette nouvelle édition (cela fait maintenant 14 ans que nous publions et mettons à jour notre schéma), nous avons, entre autres, particulièrement développé la partie consacrée aux influenceurs·euses et (enfin

 

!) accordé à Pierre-Édouard Stérin la place qu'il mérite.
















 



















 



















 

Schéma de l'extrême droite française - automne 2026

 







Le schéma peut être téléchargé au format 

PDF

 ou en version 

JPEG

 en cliquant sur l'image, et également être commandé sur notre site. N'hésitez pas à nous faire des remarques en nous écrivant à : materiel@lahorde.info.




Les électoralistes (1)




Le Rassemblement national
















 







Fondé en 1972 entre autres par des néofascistes, le Front National (

FN

) rassemblait à l'origine tous les courants de l'extrême droite sous l'autorité de son président incontesté pendant plus de 40 ans, Jean-Marie Le Pen. 

Une scission en 1998

 a affaibli le parti jusqu'en 2011 où Marine Le Pen a succédé à son père, avec la volonté de normaliser le parti, symboliser en 2018 par un changement de nom, l

e 

FN

 devenant le Rassemblement national

. Avec comme seul allié 

l'

UDR

, le 

RN

 dispose d'une base électorale solide : Marine Le Pen a été au second tour des présidentielles en 2017 et 2022 et le 

RN

 a obtenu 143 député·es aux législatives de 2024. Préparant sa candidature de 2027, Marine Le Pen a laissé la présidence du 

RN

 à 

un jeune ambitieux, Jordan Bardella

, au détriment de certains de ses plus fidèles soutiens (comme 

Steeve Briois

). Si Bardella se voyait déjà président de la République en 2027 suite à la 

condamnation de Marine Le Pen pour détournement de fonds publics

 en juillet 2026, celle-ci garde finalement la main sur le mouvement en maintenant sa candidature et en éloignant les proches de Bardella (comme François Durvye, conseiller de Bardella, ou l'ex-président du 

RNJ

 Pierre-Romain Thionney, remplacé cet été par 

Tony Bonalair

, venu pourtant de Reconquête). Le 

RN

, comme l'était le 

FN

, reste une entreprise familiale, et seuls les plus fidèles à la patronne, comme Sébastien Chenu ou Jean-Philippe Tanguy, parviennent à avoir de la visibilité.




Des concurrents marginalisés
















 







Plusieurs leaders de la droite dite «

 

de gouvernement

 

» 

continuent de se radicaliser sur les questions de sécurité, d'immigration et d'identité,

 comme l'ex-ministre de l'intérieur Bruno Retailleau et l'ex-porte-parole du gouvernement Laurent Wauquiez. Après la dissolution de l'assemblée nationale de 2024, Eric Ciotti, président des 

LR

, lance 

l'Union des Droites pour la République

 (

UDR

), pour s'allier électoralement au 

RN

, provoquant une crise au sein des 

LR

, enterrant au passage l'illusoire «

 

 ni droite ni gauche 

 

» du 

RN

.


Reconquête

 

! devait incarner une alternative au 

RN

 (jugé trop «

 

 socialiste 

 

» par certain·es

 

!) et le rassemblement à la droite de la droite : si son président Eric Zemmour reste en place, sa compagne 

Sarah Knafo a bien du mal à cacher ses ambitions

, bien que le mouvement soit au point mort. Marion Maréchal, après s'être rapprochée de Zemmour 

avant de le trahir

, a fondé son propre mouvement, Identité Libertés (dans lequel s'active également l'ancien leader identitaire 

Philippe Vardon

), et tente de retrouver les bonnes grâces de sa tante. Si l'

ISSEP

, son école de formation conservatrice, a mis la clé sous la porte à Lyon, 

l'Institut de Formation politique

 (

IFP

) lui se porte bien. D'autres personnalités politiques de la droite «

 

 hors les murs 

 

», comme Philippe de Villiers (fondateur du Puy-du-Fou) ou Jean Messiah (

spécialisé dans l'arnaque à la cagnotte en ligne

), sont invités dans les médias ou tentent d'exister sur les réseaux, sans pour autant peser électoralement.


Enfin, l'avenir semble toujours bouché pour les souverainistes de tout poil. Debout la France 

n'est qu'une coquille vide

 (ce qui n'empêche pas son président Nicolas Dupont-Aignan de se déclarer candidat pour les présidentielles de 2027

 

!), tandis que l'

UPR

 n'existe plus que dans les milieux complotistes. Les Patriotes de 

Florian Philippot

 (ex-numéro 2 du 

FN

 de Marine Le Pen dans les année 2010) s'activent principalement sur les réseaux sociaux, mais le mouvement organise malgré tout chaque année «

 

les Assises de la Souveraineté

 

» avec de nombreux invités issus pour la plupart de la fachosphère.




Les réactionnaires (2)













 







La guerre culturelle est menée par des revues (et leur extension sur internet), certains bénéficiant d'une large diffusion comme 

Frontières

 (qui dispose également 

d'une émission sur CNews

) ou Valeurs actuelles (dont le directeur adjoint, Charles Sapin, sévit également 

dans les médias du service public

). Ces réacs entendent prendre leur revanche sur l'hégémonie supposée de la gauche dans ce domaine, et saturer l'espace public de leurs obsessions patriarcales, islamophobes, et nationalistes. Tous étaient 

un temps derrière Zemmour

, mais depuis ses revers électoraux, sa capacités à rassembler s'est très largement effritée, et de nombreuses figures néoconservatrices lui préfèrent le jeune Bardella.


Tout ce petit monde peut en revanche compter sur le soutien sans faille de 

l'empire médiatique du milliardaire catho tradi Vincent Bolloré

 qui leur offre des heures d'expression débridée sur sa chaîne de télé (Cnews), sa radio (Europe 1), son journal (Le Journal du Dimanche) et une grande visibilité de leurs ouvrage dans son réseau de kiosques (Relais H), 

quand il ne les édite pas lui-même

.


Un autre milliardaire, 

Pierre-Édouard Stérin

, met également sa fortune au service de média d'extrême droite comme la très réac revue 

L'Incorrect

, à travers la collecte de fonds pour projets réactionnaires (

Les Nuits du Bien Commun

) et le financement de structures éducatives ou de formation (

académies Saint-Louis, Excellence Ruralités

).


Toujours du côté de la défense de la famille traditionnelle, la Manif pour Tous est devenue en 2023 le 

Syndicat de la Famille

 mais son activité est devenue plutôt confidentielle, malgré une mobilisation récente contre l'euthanasie.




Les nationaux-catholiques (3)













 







Les réseaux catholiques traditionnalistes sont denses car ils peuvent s'appuyer sur certaines paroisses et ils disposent de plusieurs médias (comme 

Radio Courtoisie

, dont le slogan est "toutes les droites, tous les talents"

 

!), de maisons d'édition (comme Renaissance catholique) et de sites internet (comme le Salon beige ou Media Presse Info).


Avec comme mot d'ordre «

 

Dieu, Famille, Patrie

 

», 

Civitas

, devenu depuis sa dissolution Civitas international était un parti politique voulant imposer sa foi à toute la société, à travers un discours discrètement antisémite, mais son activité se limite aux conférences de son leader Alain Escada.




L'Agrif, qui lutte contre le «

 

racisme anti-blanc

 

»

 et la «

 

christianophobie

 

» porte plainte et se constitue partie civile dans des procès, est désormais dirigé par Yann Baly, également président de Chrétienté Solidarité.


La lutte anti-

IVG

 est l'un des combats historiques des cathos tradis : 

les Marches pour la Vie

 rassemblent chaque année plusieurs milliers de gens et la Fondation Lejeune, depuis 1996, associe recherches scientifiques sur les maladies génétiques et engagement militant contre l'avortement. 

Academia Christiana

, fondée en 2013, est une structure de formation animée par Victor Aubert. Son réseau est assez étendu et a tendance à grossir : il va de mouvements traditionalistes (comme la Fraternité Saint-Pie-X) jusqu'aux activistes identitaires, en passant par la Nouvelle Droite. D'autres structures proposent également des formations comme Ichtus ou 

l'Institut Saint-Irénée

, a vu le jour cet été, à l'initiative entre autres de 

l'abbé Raffray

, par ailleurs influenceur masculiniste à ses heures perdues.




La fachosphère (4)




La présence de l'extrême droite sur internet, est composé de deux grands ensembles, qui se croisent mais ne se confondent pas tout à fait.
















 







D'une part, on trouve des médias qui traitent l'actualité avec tous les biais racistes et sexistes propres à la mouvance. Outre les médias mainstream qui servent de relais à leur propagande, sous l'impulsion de leur propriétaire comme le milliardaire catholique Vincent Bolloré avec Cnews, ou à l'initiative d'animateurs, comme André Bercoff de 

Sud Radio

, on trouve aussi quelques structures indépendantes de différentes natures. On trouve ainsi le pionnier 

FdeSouche

, un agrégateur d'articles qui sélectionne uniquement ceux qui lient immigration et insécurité, ou encore Occidentis, créé par David Alaime, qui propose un «

 

contenu dissident

 

». 

Breizh Info

, lui, est un site d'infos locales, tandis que 

TV

 Libertés

 est une webTV d'aspect professionnel ou encore Le Média pour Tous de 

Vincent Lapierre

 toujours au service de l'extrême droite.




Les influenceurs-euses (5)




D'autre part, on trouve une multitude de personnalités en lutte contre le «

 

 wokisme 

 

» et «

 

 l'islamisation de la Franc e 

 

» sur les réseaux sociaux, leur renommée et leur succès reposant sur leur capacité à créer des polémiques, à proposer des formations (douteuses) et à fidéliser suffisamment de followers pour monétiser leur activité et la pratiquer à plein temps.


Certain·es se spécialisent dans les discours antiféministes, par le biais de l'humour comme 

Papacito

, du coaching pour incels comme Alex Hitchens, de la glorification de la tradewife comme 

Thaïs d'Escufon

, d'un fémonationalisme bancal comme Alice Cordier ou d'une transphobie obsessionnelle comme

les terfs Stern ou Moutot

.


D'autres (parfois les mêmes

 

!) cultivent ad nauseam leur islamophobie, comme 

Damien Rieu

 spécialisé en fake news ou 

Mila Orriols

 qui multiplie les provocations pour renforcer son statut de victime.


D'autres encore rêvent d'associer leur propagande à de l'activisme sans y parvenir, comme le racialiste 

Daniel Conversano

 ou Égalité & Réconciliation, fan-club de l'antisémite invétéré 

Alain Soral

 qui apporte régulièrement son soutien à des négationnistes multi-condamnés.


Enfin, dernière tendance en date, des streameurs sous pseudo, dont certains ont percé grâce aux jeux vidéos comme 

Sardoche

 (présent à l'UdT de Reconquête

 

! cette année), proposent de longues vidéos dans lesquels ils s'invitent et se commentent les uns les autres (se clashent parfois) et traitent de l'actualité à travers un prisme raciste et sexiste, souvent ultra-libéral voire libertarien (comme 

LeGuiz

) mais indépendamment des partis politiques (même s'il y a des exceptions comme 

Lebracq

, revendiqué 

RN

), certains pratiquant une forme de confusionnisme en se revendiquant «

 

 de gauche 

 

» comme Greg Tabibian, animateur de la chaîne YouTube J'suis pas content 

TV

.




La Nouvelle Droite (6)




Pour réhabiliter la vision inégalitaire de l'extrême droite , le Groupement de Recherche et d'Étude pour la Civilisation Européenne (

GRECE

), inactif aujourd'hui, y a travaillé pendant des décennies. Alain de Benoist qui en est le représentant historique, se plaît à brouiller les cartes à travers la revue Éléments, dirigée par François Bousquet. La 

Nouvelle Droite

 dispose aussi d'un outil de formation, 

l'institut Iliade

, qui organise des conférences et des cycles de formation sur «

 

 le grand effacement 

 

», les «

 

 pensées non-conformes 

 

» ou la défense de la civilisation européenne. Polémia, un Think tank fondé par Jean-Yves Le Gallou, ex-idéologue du Front national, propose de son côté 

une 

IA

 raciste

, il fallait y penser

 

!




Les activistes (7)













 







L'

Action française

 (

AF

) est le plus vieux mouvement nationaliste en activité. Royaliste, historiquement école de formation, l'

AF

 organise des colloques mais aussi des actions de rue. Une scission en 2018 a éloigné les anciens restés fidèles à l'antisémitisme historique et à la nostalgie vichyste. L'

AF

 d'aujourd'hui se réfère toujours à Maurras, mais en concentrant ses attaques contre les musulmans.


La 

Cocarde étudiante

, un syndicat dont les militants n'hésitent pas à faire le coup de poing, roule aussi bien pour le 

RN

 que pour Reconquête

 

!. Il est en concurrence avec le syndicat historique de la droite, l'

UNI

, qui est plus proche de l'

UDR

 de Ciotti que des Républicains, alors qu'il était par le passé davantage rattaché à la droite dite «

 

de gouvernement

 

».


Le collectif 

Nemesis

 de son côté, sous couvert de «

 

 féminisme de droite 

 

», fait de l'agitation islamophobe, en particulier avec des happening visant à perturber des manifestations ou rassemblement véritablement féministes.


Les 

Identitaires

 ont tenté depuis leur création en 2002 de se démarquer de l'extrême droite traditionnelle, en misant tout sur la 

communication

. Dissout en 2021 alors qu'il était déjà en perte de vitesse, le mouvement tente régulièrement de se réinventer, mais semble avoir perdu sa créativité et tourne en rond, comme le montre sa dernière initiative, 

Objectif Remigration

. L'

ASLA

 (association de soutien aux lanceurs d'alerte), collecte de l'argent, mais pour quoi faire

 

?


Chaque année, les néofascistes de tout poil se retrouvent lors de la manifestation organisée par le 

Comité du 9 mai

 pour rendre hommage à un jeune militant mort en 1994, sous la direction de 

Gabriel Loustau

, fils d'Axel Loustau, un responsable du 

GUD

 (aujourd'hui dissout) des années 1990, devenu prestataire de service pour le 

RN

. On les retrouve également au sein des 

Active Clubs

, qui organisent des entraînements. Ces militants peuvent recevoir à l'occasion le renfort de hooligans venus du stade dont la seule expression politique est d'attaquer des militant·es de gauche.


Enfin, tout au fond du panier, on trouve le 

Parti de la France

, fondé en 2009 par Carl Lang, ex-n°2 du 

FN

, et aujourd'hui présidé par Thomas Joly, qui cherche à faire de l'agitation, tout en se présentant parfois à des élections, avec des résultats insignifiants ou encore les Nationalistes (ex-

PNF

) qui s'inscrivent dans la continuité de l'Œuvre française dissoute en 2013 et reste l'un des derniers mouvements à assumer ouvertement une filiation fasciste. Proche d'eux, un collectif de soutien aux nationalistes et aux négationnistes emprisonnés, le 

CLAN

, est animé par l'avocat 

Pierre-Marie Bonneau

, qui s'occupe également de la boutique du 

C9M

.




Les groupes locaux (8)




Des groupes implantés localement se revendiquent «

 

 enracinés 

 

» sans être affiliés à une organisation précise (nous avons réalisé 

une carte de France de l'implantation locale de l'extrême droite

 qui présentent les groupes réellement actifs). Certains se posent en héritiers du 

GUD

 (mouvement étudiant nationaliste-révolutionnaire), aujourd'hui dissout, mais la plupart sont en réalité de simples bandes affinitaires, à maintenir une activité militante, mais la plupart du temps basée sur la violence. Ils reçoivent à l'occasion le renfort de hooligans venus du stade et n'ont pas vraiment d'expression politique en dehors de leurs attaques contre des militant·es de gauche.




La Horde

author: Unknown
title: Soutien à Gino et aux antifas incarcéré·es : rassemblement place Mazagran mercredi à 18h30
content:
Le 19 août, la cour d'appel de Paris a rendu un avis favorable à l'extradition vers l'Allemagne de Gino, militant antifasciste interpellé 

pour s'être opposé aux néo-nazis hongrois à Budapest en février 2023

. Il y risque jusqu'à 10 ans de détention et surtout une extradition vers la Hongrie où la peine sera plus lourde encore. Suite à cette décision, un pourvoi en cassation a été déposé par les avocats de Gino, laissant un délai de 40 jours pour statuer définitivement.







Le 30 septembre, la justice française doit se prononcer sur la possible remise de Gino à l'Allemagne.




Zaid A. se trouve lui aussi en France et risque une extradition vers la Hongrie. C'est pourquoi le Comité Solidarité Budapest appelle à une mobilisation le 30, et notamment à un meeting antifasciste contre l'extradition de Gino à la Bourse du Travail de Paris.




À Lyon, l'attente de cette décision de justice résonne avec la repression des antifascistes dans le cadre de 

la mort du néo-nazi Deranque

, survenue en février dernier. le 24 septembre, 

8 nouvelles interpellations ont eu lieu

.




Le contexte, est partout le même : celui d'une criminalisation croissante de l'antifascisme, alors même qu'on assiste à une résurgence des forces fascistes et réactionnaires à travers l'Europe. Partout, les antifascistes sont poursuivis, réprimé·es, emprisonné·es parce qu'iels s'opposent de manière conséquente à cette situation.




En écho à la mobilisation à Paris contre l'extradition de Gino, et en soutien à tous·tes les antifas incarcéré·es, on se rassemble à Lyon

 

 Mercredi 30 septembre

 Place Mazagran

 À partir de 18h30




Retrouvons-nous pour échanger autour de la criminalisation de l'antifascisme. On vous propose de 

ramener de quoi boire un coup et grignoter

, mais aussi des feuilles et stylos, pour participer si vous le souhaitez à

 un atelier d'écriture

. On tentera aussi de 

créer ensemble une banderole

 en soutien à Gino et à tous·tes antifas incarcéré·es (n'hésitez pas à ramener peinture et bâches si vous en avez

 

!).

author: Markela Panegyres
title: Macklemore strikes a blow for the cultural intifada
content:
When United States rap artist Macklemore was dropped from pop singer Ed Sheeran’s US tour for saying “Free Palestine” during a concert, it sparked a global wave of support for Macklemore, and widespread condemnation of Sheeran’s refusal to take a stand on Palestine.

Billionaire Zionist Robert Kraft, owner of the Gillette Stadium where Macklemore was scheduled to perform, claimed the rapper had performed “hate speech” and pushed for his removal. The Israeli-American Council (IAC) petitioned against Macklemore, and pop singer PINK amplified social media posts by the Zionist StopAntisemitism group, claiming Macklemore had “accused Israel of a false ‘genocide’”, and “turned a mainstream event into a political nightmare against the Jewish state”.

Sheeran subsequently released a weak public response, playing down the genocide as a “conflict” and claiming he was trying to use his platform as a “sanctuary” outside politics. But as the Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) pointed out, Sheeran’s statement “both-sides Israel’s ongoing genocide against Palestinians in Gaza” and repeats “anti-Palestinian Israel lobby talking points that deny the genocide and want to whitewash apartheid”.

The attempt to silence Macklemore galvanised Palestinian and non-Palestinian artists and their supporters. It also brought to the fore the words of Paul Robeson, delivered at a rally during the Spanish Civil War, in 1937: “the artist must take sides. He must elect to fight for freedom or slavery.”

When faced with the ongoing genocide in Gaza, many artists have joined what can described as a cultural intifada — an uprising, or struggle within the cultural field for Palestine liberation.

Palestinian actor and director Juliano Mer-Khamis coined the term cultural intifada in 2006. Mer-Khamis argued that the “third Intifada will be a cultural intifada” and that artists must “join, by all means, the Palestinian struggle for liberation, which is our liberation struggle. We are not healers. We are not good Christians. We are freedom fighters.”

This concept has a long tradition in Palestinian art and literature. Following the 1948 Nakba (catastrophe), prominent figures such as writer, journalist and Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP) leader Ghassan Kanafani practised and advocated “Palestinian resistance poetry”, which expressed the lives and struggles of Palestinian refugees, peasants and workers and served the Palestinian collective struggle for liberation.

Kanafani believed that this could combat Zionist propaganda, because it transcended poetry’s traditional emotional and aesthetic concerns.“It is a closely welded literature based on reasoning and not on sheer emotion,” he said.

Kanafani was murdered by Mossad agents in 1972. Marwan Abd el-‘Al, a member of the Political Bureau of the PFLP, explained that Kanafani’s “martyrdom was part of a targeted campaign of erasure of those committed to political literature and political culture...”

Although the Zionist attempt to suppress Palestinian revolutionary cultural production existed before the Nakba, and never stopped, it intensified after October 7, 2023.

Macklemore’s cancellation is just the most recent example of the global crackdown on pro-Palestinian artists.

In Australia, Palestinian academic and writer Randa Abdel-Fattah, visual artist Khaled Sabsabi, and pianist Jason Gyllam were all censored for speaking out on Palestine. And while high profile artists such as Macklemore garner attention, there are many more unknown working-class artists refused work, opportunities and careers for taking a stance against genocide.

The global culture industry — including the commercial art market, music industry and elite art, cultural and educational institutions — works in the service of capitalism and imperialism; building social license for war, militarism, genocide, big banks, oil and gas companies, the destruction of the environment and more.

Although activists and artists have campaigned for many years for cultural institutions to remove big oil, gas and weapons companies as patrons and sponsors, and have had some modest success, the industry remains controlled by representatives of ruling class interests, such as CEOs and billionaires like Kraft, rather than cultural workers and artists.

So-called “apolitical artists” such as Sheeran are (often willingly) used by the culture industry to perpetuate the capitalist and imperialist status quo. But it is not possible to be apolitical in art under capitalism because, in the words of Surrealist poet Louis Aragon “apolitical works are really militant works for the benefit of the bourgeoisie in power”.

In the neoliberal era, art is also celebrated and promoted as an expression of liberal notions of “creativity and freedom”. A certain amount of cultural diversity, political and even anti-capitalist content is allowed, to give the illusion of a liberal and democratic cultural life.

Paradoxically, this strengthens the culture industry’s ability to provide social license and cover for the ruling class’s political agendas and ideology.

Pro-Palestine cultural production, like other truly revolutionary content, can’t be tolerated because it implicates the entire system. The risks to capitalist and imperial ideological hegemony are too great.

This is why the big capitalists running the culture industry have been on a mission to silence Palestinian and pro-Palestinian artists.

The case against Macklemore has unmasked this fact for all to see.

Since at least 2004, Palestinian groups such as Palestinian Campaign for the Academic and Cultural Boycott of Israel (PACBI) have advocated for an international intellectual and cultural boycott of Israel, “as a contribution to the struggle to end Israel's occupation, colonisation and system of apartheid”.

PACBI notes that “Israel overtly uses culture as a form of propaganda to whitewash, or artwash, its genocide in Gaza and underlying regime of settler-colonialism, apartheid, and military occupation over the Indigenous Palestinian people.”

To combat Sheeran’s role in Israel’s artwashing, the Boycott, Divestments and Sanctions movement is calling for a complete boycott of his current world tour.

Israel’s artwashing extends to its bi-yearly inclusion in the Venice Biennale — an international event often considered the pinnacle of international contemporary art scene. In May, thousands of pro-Palestine artists, artworkers and activists led an historic strike and protest against Israel’s inclusion, and a petition from the Art Not Genocide Alliance attracted hundreds of signatures.

In spite of the protests, the organisers of the Biennale allowed Israel to exhibit the work of Romanian-born Israeli artist Belu-Simion Fainaru. Fainaru’s artwork titled “The Rose of Nothingness” comprised a black pool of water that collects water droplets from a dripper array. The work alluded (in bad faith) to the poetry of Holocaust survivor Paul Celan, while celebrating Israeli drip-irrigation technology, promoting the myth that “Israel made the desert bloom”.

Israel’s participation in Eurovision is another example. Many artists and countries boycotted Eurovision 2026 in protest, but Israel was still allowed to compete. The moral bankruptcy and double standards of the European Broadcasting Union (EBU), the organising body behind the song contest, was clear when compared to Russia’s explusion from Eurovision in 2022, following its invasion of Ukraine.

Since October 7, Israel has murdered or maimed countless Gazan artists and their families. Poet Refaat Alareer was murdered by Israel in a targeted assassination, Hiba Abu Nada, a poet and novelist, was murdered along with her son in an air strike, painter Heba Zagout was killed in an air strike.

Even Gazan artists who escape the genocide as refugees face difficulties and hostility from authorities in their countries of refuge. Fayez Elhasani, former head of the Association of Palestinian Visual Artists in the Gaza Strip, was severely injured following the bombardment of his house by the Israeli Occupation Forces. The bombing killed many family members, and destroyed many of his paintings. But since being evacuated to Australia, he struggles to exhibit his artwork, due to Australian authorities and politicians labelling his work as “antisemitic”.

The Palestinian Ministry of Culture (PMC) reported in January 2024, just three months after the start of Israel’s genocidal war, that “all aspects of Palestinian culture have been systematically destroyed during the genocide war waged by the occupation state against our people”.

The PMC reported that many prominent artists, writers, musicians, dancers and cultural workers were killed along with their entire families and that their studios, archives and artistic works were completely destroyed.

The PMC also noted that Gaza had a thriving cultural and artistic scene prior to October 7 — an incredible feat of resilience given Israel’s ongoing siege and blockade of the Gaza strip.

The Institute for Palestinian Studies, as at October last year, reported at least 57 prominent cultural sector martyrs, who were targeted and killed, at least 36 destroyed cultural and art institutions, at least 21 destroyed archives and libraries and at least 49 destroyed archaeological sites and museums.

In August, the Palestine NGOs Network reported that 70% of Palestinian cultural heritage was damaged, and concluded that this destruction “can only be the result of a systemic and deliberate policy”.

Evidence for this included: “the scale of the attacks on cultural heritage sites, recurring patterns in the targeting and methods of destruction, including a number of sites being subjected to repeated and escalating attacks, and the fact that sites attacked were clearly identified as cultural or religious landmarks.”

Israel’s systematic attempt to extinguish living Palestinian cultural and artistic life and heritage constitutes a cultural genocide. This needs a cultural uprising in response, and it is up to all artists and cultural workers to take part and take a side.

Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions (BDS)

author: Franck Dick Rosete
title: ‘Trump not welcome’
content:
Trump is no ordinary foreign guest.

Should Filipinos welcome guests and express concerns another day?

Palace Press Officer Claire Castro thinks so in relation to the possible visit of United States President Donald Trump to the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit in November.

Bagong Alyansang Makabayan (Bayan) told Malacañang, “Trump is not welcome in the Philippines.”

“Trump is no ordinary foreign guest,” the group said in a statement. “His waterloo in Iran and West Asia, his continuing support for Israel’s genocide in Palestine, the proxy war in Ukraine, and his unprovoked interventions in Venezuela and Cuba, have made the entire world suffer.”

Castro made the request when asked by a reporter during a Palace press briefing on September 23 if there were additional security measures in place for the 49th ASEAN Summit in Metro Manila, considering what happened to the Luzon Economic Corridor (LEC) Investment Forum held at the Grand Hyatt Manila on September 10 where protesters barged to the venue. In this incident, five paralegals who responded to the protest were arrested but were eventually released.

The 1,600-hectare industrial hub under the U.S.-led Pax Silica initiative is planned to be built in New Clark City in Tarlac which is within the LEC.

Read: Why Pax Silica is bad for the Philippines

Malacañang declared November 16 to 18, as special non-working days in the National Capital Region (NCR) for the event. Other ASEAN-related meetings are also set to be held.

During the September 23 Malacañang press briefing, Castro did not confirm the attendance of Trump. But the Department of Foreign Affairs has been reportedly preparing for his possible visit, according to an Inquirer report.

Bayan stressed that the country is turning into a forward military base of the U.S. given the established military sites under agreements involving the U.S. and Philippine governments, such as the Enhanced Defense Cooperation Agreement (EDCA). It added that Pax Silica would support this alleged military agenda.

Read: Philippines as a US military base?

“Peaceful protests during an international summit are legitimate and effective means for our people to tell visiting leaders and our own government where they stand on issues that directly affect their lives, sovereignty and future,” the multisectoral group said.

It added that the Philippine National Police (PNP) should not use “security” as an excuse to establish protest-free zones. (DAA)

author: Jim McIlroy
title: Baird forced to resign over bid to privatise Big Bash League
content:
Former NSW Liberal Premier Mike Baird has resigned as chair of Cricket Australia (CA) as opposition grows to its proposed privatisation of the Big Bash League (BBL) — the Australian 20 over competition.

Former Australian Test batsman David Boon will take over as CA interim chair.

Baird has long been a privatisation crusader, particularly as NSW premier over 2014-2017, when he privatised and sold off the state-owned power facility Ausgrid and pushed to privatise huge swathes of public land, buildings and other assets.

He also rammed through major parts of the federal Coalition’s public sector cuts.

It should therefore come as no surprise that he played a key role in CA’s campaign to sell off major parts of the BBL to private investors.

Baird was told mid September that Cricket NSW, chaired by John Knox, had withdrawn support for him to take another three-year term. It also rejected a suggestion that Baird move into a recently-vacated independent director’s spot, until a new chair could be found.

Cricket NSW slammed CA’s decision to introduce private investment earlier this month. “This decision risks leaving cricket in NSW and Australia strategically and financially worse off, with direct consequences for our ability to invest in grassroots cricket,” it said on September 9.

CA, under Baird’s leadership, had earlier approved the partial and full privatisation of (BBL) and Women’s Big Bash League (WBBL) franchises in September, starting with a 100% sale process for the Melbourne Renegades ahead of the 2027-28 season.

Under the original plan, individual state associations could choose whether and when to sell stakes in their respective teams — the “opt-in” or “self-determination” model. It remains to be seen if some states attempt to move ahead with partial privatisation.

Even the pro-privatisation Australian Financial Review said in April that “there is no clear financial evidence for the claim that Cricket Australia must sell permanent equity in its best commercial asset to secure its future”.

CA had wanted to sell stakes in the eight BBL franchises, to raise about $600 million. The AFR argued that “the case for this particular sale doesn’t stack up” largely because of the “duty to steward the game”. It said “cricket is ... a key part of our cultural heritage [and] as the steward of that, Cricket Australia has the responsibility to nurture the game here, not to extract every last dollar from it.”

This fight over CA forms part of a worldwide fight over the future of sports competition under capitalism.

Most controversial has been the push led by Federation of International Football Association (FIFA) President Gianni Infantino’s to privatise world soccer. He wanted to create a commercial body, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), valued at up to $30 billion. FIFA intended to sell a 20-30% private equity stake to outside investors, including a consortium backed by Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Eternal and financial backing from JPMorgan Chase.

National member associations were offered a $20 million one-off payment and higher annual payouts to secure votes before a planned September deadline.

The Union of European Football Associations (UEFA), the Confederation of North, Central America and Caribbean Association Football and the Asian Football Confederation opposed the move, accusing FIFA of selling “football’s soul”.

UEFA threatened a complete boycott of FIFA tournaments, putting players’ careers and the international calendar at risk. Senior advisers and executives criticised the move’s lack of transparency and motives, leading to high-profile resignations.

This international backlash by soccer federations, players and fans forced Infantino to scrap the privatisation plan in just days.

While sport has been made a commodity under capitalism, the outcry over CA’s latest corporate plan is welcome. The struggle to maintain the co-operative and human basis of sports is a positive sign and shows that there is still fundamental public opposition to big business control of every aspect of social interaction.
